## Sūkta 184 — introductory matter (Anuvāka 24)

### Printed p. 2  (PDF 20)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184". The page opens with a paragraph on Agastya; the preceding title page, printed p. 1, is not part of this batch.)*

The greatness of Agastya is extraordinary; this is very well known in all the Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇas and the like. The very manner of his origin indicates his greatness.

> सत्रे ह जाताविषिता नमोभिः कुम्भे रेतः सिषिचतुः समानम् ।
> ततो ह मान उदियाय मध्यात्ततो जातमृषिमाहुर्वसिष्ठम् ॥
> उक्थभृतं सामभृतं बिभर्ति ग्रावाणं बिभ्रत्प्र वदात्यग्रे ।
> उपैनमाध्वं सुमनस्यमाना आ वो गच्छाति प्रतृदो वसिष्ठः ॥

> *satre ha jātāviṣitā namobhiḥ kumbhe retaḥ siṣicatuḥ samānam |*
> *tato ha māna udiyāya madhyāttato jātamṛṣimāhurvasiṣṭham ‖*
> *ukthabhṛtaṃ sāmabhṛtaṃ bibharti grāvāṇaṃ bibhratpra vadātyagre |*
> *upainamādhvaṃ sumanasyamānā ā vo gacchāti pratṛdo vasiṣṭhaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7. 37 [?] 13 to 14, as read.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "At the sacrificial session, the two, born, impelled by reverences, poured a common seed into the jar; from its midst Māna [Agastya] arose; from it, they say, the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha was born. He bears the bearer of hymns and the bearer of chants; bearing the pressing-stone he speaks first; approach him with kindly minds — Vasiṣṭha comes to you, O Pratṛds.")

> तेनैव तु मुहूर्तेन वीर्यवन्तौ तपस्विनौ ।
> अगस्त्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षी संबभूवतुः ॥

> *tenaiva tu muhūrtena vīryavantau tapasvinau |*
> *agastyaśca vasiṣṭhaśca tatrarṣī saṃbabhūvatuḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 5 [?]-150 [?].) (Gloss: "In that very moment the two vigorous ascetics, the ṛṣis Agastya and Vasiṣṭha, came into being there.")

Of the twelve Ādityas, the two, Mitra and Varuṇa, together, at the time of a sacrificial session (*satra*), saw the apsaras-woman Urvaśī and were infatuated. Then their seed fell and dropped into the jar called *vasatīvarī* that was there. At once the two ṛṣis called Vasiṣṭha and Agastya, ascetics and vigorous, were born. The great ascetic Agastya became one of only a span's (*śamyā*) measure, and Vasiṣṭha and Agastya both became possessed of the brilliance of the Sun — the section that narrates this episode is given elsewhere.

The portion of Mitra, who has the form of this world, and the portion of Varuṇa, who has the form of the heavenly world, joining together, were the cause of Agastya's origin. Mitra's brilliance-form, which is of the nature of food, and Varuṇa's great vigour-form (*ojas*) are fully mixed in Agastya. And as described in the sentences क्रतुदक्षौ ह वा अस्य मित्रावरुणौ (*kratudakṣau ha vā asya mitrāvaruṇau*) (Śa. Brā. 4. 1. 4. 1), of Mitra and Varuṇa, Mitra is of the form of resolve (*saṅkalpa*), Varuṇa is of the form of spiritual power. Both these, resolve and power, are Agastya's great qualities. Agastya is one who, like Mitra, makes the resolve for the accomplishment of a work, and, like Varuṇa, accomplishes it. Like Mitra he is of the form of *brahman*, and like Varuṇa of the form of *kratu*; therefore he is also of the form of the most excellent *kratu* and *dakṣa*.

> अगस्त्यः खनमानः खनित्रैः प्रजामपत्यं बलमिच्छमानः ।
> उभौ वर्णावृषिरुग्रः पुपोष सत्या देवेष्वाशिषो जगाम ॥

> *agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ khanitraiḥ prajāmapatyaṃ balamicchamānaḥ |*
> *ubhau varṇāvṛṣirugraḥ pupoṣa satyā deveṣvāśiṣo jagāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 179. 6) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Agastya, digging with spades, desiring offspring, progeny and strength, the mighty ṛṣi nourished both colours [classes]; he attained true blessings among the gods.")

In this ṛk all the special qualities of Agastya are described as stated above. Accomplishing what is desired by means such as sacrifice and praise; desirous of sons, servants, strength and the like; [beyond the senses …] *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 3  (PDF 21)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* …a seer of what is beyond the senses, and one who has passed beyond worldly existence (*saṃsāra*) and is free from sin — the ṛṣi Agastya has accomplished both the chief *puruṣārtha*s, desire (*kāma*) and austerity (*tapas*). Therefore he has obtained from the deities blessings with true fruits — thus Agastya's power is praised in this mantra.

The sūktas seen and composed by a ṛṣi so filled with power and so much a seer must also be of profound expression of feeling. When the purport of mantra-sentences such as कतरा पूर्वा कतरा परायोः (*katarā pūrvā katarā parāyoḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-185-1) and इदं द्यावा पृथिवी सत्यमस्तु (*idaṃ dyāvā pṛthivī satyamastu*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-185-11) is explained, the direct experience of the harmony of truth and beauty in Agastya's feelings will be made known. This Adhyāya begins with the mantra ता वामद्य तावपरम् (*tā vāmadya tāvaparam*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-184-1), which praises the Aśvin deities, who are the eyes of the world and have the form of the Sun and the Moon, as soon as the Dawn, which spreads light over the whole world, appears.

## Sūkta 184 — *tā vām adya* (Anuvāka 24, fifth Sūkta; 6 ṛks)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(printed p. 3; Sanskrit, transcribed; Anukramaṇikā wording as read)*

> तत्र ता वामितीदं प्रथममण्डलस्य चतुर्विंशेऽनुवाके पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । पूर्वसूक्ते षडित्युक्तत्वात् सूक्तसंख्यानुवर्तत इति परिभाषितत्वात् षडृचम् । ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादिति परिभाषयागस्त्यम् । तथाश्विनं वा इत्युक्तत्वात्तुह्यादिपरिभाषयेदमप्याश्विनम् । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रैष्टुभम् । ता वामित्यनुक्रान्तम् ॥ युवो रजांसीत्यादीनां पञ्च सूक्तानां तृतीयवर्जितानां प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोग उक्तः । तत्रेदं पञ्चमम् ॥

*Gist:* *tā vām* is the fifth sūkta of Anuvāka 24, of six ṛks, seen by Agastya, addressed to the Aśvins, in *triṣṭubh*; used, like the earlier sūktas from *yuvo rajāṃsi*, in the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, *tā vām adya*, is the fifth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka of the First Maṇḍala. There are six ṛks in this sūkta. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this sūkta; the Aśvin deities are the devatā; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. As stated earlier, for the five sūktas from the sūkta *yuvo rajāṃsi* onwards (except the third sūkta), the application is for the *triṣṭubh* mantras belonging to the Āśvina-śastra at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras; this sūkta, too, has the same application. Of those sūktas this is the fifth.

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)*

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—184
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 24 ‖ Sūkta 184 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 5 ‖ Varga 1 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 6 · Ṛṣi: Agastya · Devatā: the Aśvins · Chandas: *triṣṭubh*.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ता वामद्य तावपरं हुवेमोच्छन्त्यामुषसि वह्निरुक्थैः ।
> नासत्या कुह चित्सन्तावर्यो दिवो नपाता सुदास्तराय ॥ १ ॥

> *tā vāmadya tāvaparaṃ huvemocchantyāmuṣasi vahnirukthaiḥ |*
> *nāsatyā kuha citsantāvaryo divo napātā sudāstarāya ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ता । वाम् । अद्य । तौ । अपरम् । हुवेम । उच्छन्त्याम् । उषसि । वह्निः । उक्थैः ।
> नासत्या । कुह । चित् । सन्तौ । अर्यः । दिवः । नपाता । सुदाःऽतराय ॥ १ ॥

> *tā | vām | adya | tau | aparam | huvema | ucchantyām | uṣasi | vahniḥ | ukthaiḥ |*
> *nāsatyā | kuha | cit | santau | aryaḥ | divaḥ | napātā | sudāḥ 'tarāya ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(begins)*

> ता तौ रक्षकत्वेन प्रसिद्धौ वां युवामद्यास्मिन्यागदिने हुवेम । आह्वयाम इत्याशीः । तथापरमपरस्मिन्नपि दिने तौ युवां हुवेम । अपरमित्येतदपरस्मिन्नित्यर्थे समभिव्याहारात् अद्या च नो मृळयतापरं च । ऋ २-२९-२ । इत्यादिमन्त्रान्तरे तथा दर्शनाच्च । अपरयोगं प्रत्यपीति वा । कस्मिन्काले । उषस्युषोदेवतायामुच्छन्त्यां तमो विवासयन्त्यां सत्याम् । उषःकाले हि प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रे प्रयुज्येते । उक्ते काले हे नासत्यासत्यरहितौ दिवो नपाता द्युलोकस्य …

> *tā tau rakṣakatvena prasiddhau vāṃ yuvāmadyāsminyāgadine huvema | āhvayāma ityāśīḥ | tathāparamaparasminnapi dine tau yuvāṃ huvema | aparamityetadaparasminnityarthe samabhivyāhārāt adyā ca no mṛḷayatāparaṃ ca | ṛ 2-29-2 | ityādimantrāntare tathā darśanācca | aparayogaṃ pratyapīti vā | kasminkāle | uṣasyuṣodevatāyāmucchantyāṃ tamo vivāsayantyāṃ satyām | uṣaḥkāle hi prātaranuvākāśvinaśastre prayujyete | ukte kāle he nāsatyāsatyarahitau divo napātā dyulokasya …*

### Printed p. 5  (PDF 23)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* **Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (continued).**

> … नपातयितारौ नप्तृस्थानीयौ वा कुह चित्सन्तौ कुत्रचिद्देशे वर्तमानौ युवां वह्निः स्तुतेर्वोढार्य ईरयिता स्तुतेरीश्वरो वा ईदृशोऽहं होता सुदास्तरायात्यर्थं शोभनहविर्दात्रे यजमानाय तदर्थं ता युवामुक्थैः शस्त्रैर्हुवेमेति संबन्धः । अत्राख्यातं पदमेकवचनतया नेतव्यम् । वह्निरर्यशब्दौ वा बहुवचनत्वेन नेतव्यौ । अथवा वाक्यद्वयम् । यस्माद्वह्निरर्यो होतोक्तगुणकौ युवां शंसति तस्माद्वयं यजमानास्तौ युवामाह्वयाम इति ॥

> *… napātayitārau naptṛsthānīyau vā kuha citsantau kutraciddeśe vartamānau yuvāṃ vahniḥ stutervoḍhārya īrayitā stuterīśvaro vā īdṛśo 'haṃ hotā sudāstarāyātyarthaṃ śobhanahavirdātre yajamānāya tadarthaṃ tā yuvāmukthaiḥ śastrairhuvemeti saṃbandhaḥ | atrākhyātaṃ padamekavacanatayā netavyam | vahniraryaśabdau vā bahuvacanatvena netavyau | athavā vākyadvayam | yasmādvahniraryo hotoktaguṇakau yuvāṃ śaṃsati tasmādvayaṃ yajamānāstau yuvāmāhvayāma iti ‖*

*Gist:* We invoke you, Aśvins, famed as protectors, today and on other days, at dawn (when these śastras are used); wherever you are, I, the hotṛ, bearer and impeller of praise, call you with śastras for the generous sacrificer. The plural verb is to be taken as singular (or *vahni*, *arya* as plural); or two sentences: since the hotṛ praises you, we sacrificers invoke you. (*apara* = "on another day", as in अद्या च नो मृळयतापरं च (*adyā ca no mṛḷayatāparaṃ ca*), Ṛ 2-29-2.)

**Pratipadārtha.** *nāsatyā* — O Aśvin deities, free from untruth; *tā vām* — you, famed as protectors; *adya* — on this day of sacrifice; *uṣasi* — the Dawn-deity; *ucchantyām* — at the time when [she] dispels darkness; *huvema* — we call, praying (likewise); *aparam* — on other sacrificial days also; *tā* — you two (we call); *divaḥ napātā* — O Aśvin deities, grandsons of the heavenly world; *kuha cit santau* — in whatever region you may be; *vahniḥ* — [I,] the bearer of praise; *aryaḥ* — and the impeller of praise (the hotṛ); *sudāstarāya* — for the sacrificer who offers excellent oblation; *ukthaiḥ* — with śastra-mantras, praying, I call.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvin deities, grandsons of the heavenly world, free from untruth, famed as protectors: on this day of sacrifice, at the time when the Dawn-deity dispels darkness, and on other sacrificial days too, wherever you may be, I (the hotṛ), bearer of praise and impeller of praise, call you, praying with mantras in the form of śastras, for the sake of the sacrificer who offers excellent oblation.

**English Translation (as printed):** We invoke you two, (Ashwins), to-day; the same two on any other day: when the morning dawns. Nasatyas, grandsons of heaven, wherever you may be, the pious reciter (of the hymn) invokes you with praises on behalf of the liberal donor (of the offering).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** The nature of the Prātaranuvāka and śastra-mantras, the occasion for reciting them, who should recite them, the time at which they are to be recited, and such details, we have explained earlier, in Part 1 of the Ṛ. Saṃ. [volumes].

### Printed p. 6  (PDF 24)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* It is stated in the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya that the present sūkta has its application among the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra mantras. The story-context connected with the Āśvina-śastra is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa thus:

> प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे दुहितरं प्रायच्छत्सूर्यां सावित्रीं तस्यै सर्वे देवा वरा आगच्छंस्तस्या एतत्सहस्रं वहतुमन्वाकरोद्यदेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षतेऽनाश्विनं हैव तद्यदर्वाक्सहस्रं तस्मात्तत्सहस्रं वैव शंसेद्भूयो वा प्राश्य घृतं शंसेद्यथा ह वा इदमनो वा रथो वाक्तो वर्तत एवं हैवाक्तो वर्तते । शकुनिरिवोत्पतिष्यन्नाह्वयीत ।

> *prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchatsūryāṃ sāvitrīṃ tasyai sarve devā varā āgacchaṃstasyā etatsahasraṃ vahatumanvākarodyadetadāśvinamityācakṣate 'nāśvinaṃ haiva tadyadarvāksahasraṃ tasmāttatsahasraṃ vaiva śaṃsedbhūyo vā prāśya ghṛtaṃ śaṃsedyathā ha vā idamano vā ratho vākto vartata evaṃ haivākto vartate | śakunirivotpatiṣyannāhvayīta |*

(Ai. Brā. 16-1)

Formerly, when Prajāpati decided to give his daughter Sūryā to Soma in marriage, all the deities came, each wishing to wed her himself. Then Prajāpati made a rule that the thousand mantras known as the Āśvina-śastra must be recited, and that there must be no fewer than that. Just as in the world a chariot-wheel, after it has been smeared with oil, can move easily, so after drinking ghee one can recite the mantras easily; therefore one should first drink ghee and then recite. And, just as a bird about to fly makes its body light, so he said the bridegroom who would win her must have that quality.

> तस्मिन्देवा न समजानत ममेदमस्तु ममेदमस्त्विति ते संजानाना अब्रुवन्नाजिमस्यायामहै स यो न उज्जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति तेऽग्नेरेवाधि गृहपतेरादित्यं काष्ठामकुर्वत तस्मादाग्नेयी प्रतिपद्भवत्याश्विनस्याग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेति ।

> *tasmindevā na samajānata mamedamastu mamedamastviti te saṃjānānā abruvannājimasyāyāmahai sa yo na ujjeṣyati tasyedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti te 'gnerevādhi gṛhapaterādityaṃ kāṣṭhāmakurvata tasmādāgneyī pratipadbhavatyāśvinasyāgnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti |*

(Ai. Brā. 16-1)

Then the deities, not wishing to quarrel among themselves, all came to the agreement that they should take part together in a race, and that whoever won the race would be entitled to wed her. Then they ran, starting from Agni the householder (*gṛhapati*) as far as the Sun.

> तासां वै देवतानामाजिं धावन्तीनामभिसृष्टानामग्निर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यत तमश्विनावन्वागच्छतां तमब्रूतामपोदिह्यावां वा इदं जेष्याव इति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्तस्य वै ममेहाप्यस्त्विति तथेति तस्मा अप्यत्राकुरुतां तस्मादाग्नेयमाश्विने शस्यते ।

> *tāsāṃ vai devatānāmājiṃ dhāvantīnāmabhisṛṣṭānāmagnirmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyata tamaśvināvanvāgacchatāṃ tamabrūtāmapodihyāvāṃ vā idaṃ jeṣyāva iti sa tathetyabravīttasya vai mamehāpyastviti tatheti tasmā apyatrākurutāṃ tasmādāgneyamāśvine śasyate |*

(Ai. Brā. 16-2)

While all the deities were taking part in this race and running, Agni got ahead of everyone. Then the Aśvin deities came up to Agni and [said]: "Give us way; in this race we [shall] win …" *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 7  (PDF 25)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* …give us help", they asked. Then Agni agreed to it. But he asked that he too should be given a share in that victory. For that very reason he too has a share in the Āśvina-śastra mantras.

In this context another objection is stated and its answer also given:

> तदाहुर्यच्छस्यत आग्नेयं शस्यत उषस्यं शस्यत ऐन्द्रमथ कस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षत इत्यश्विनौ हि तदुदजयतामश्विनावाश्नुवातां यदश्विना उदजयतामश्विनावाश्नुवातां तस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षते ।

> *tadāhuryacchasyata āgneyaṃ śasyata uṣasyaṃ śasyata aindramatha kasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣata ityaśvinau hi tadudajayatāmaśvināvāśnuvātāṃ yadaśvinā udajayatāmaśvināvāśnuvātāṃ tasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣate |*

(Ai. Brā. 16-2)

In this context, since mantras are to be recited addressed to Agni, to Indra and to Dawn, if the objection arises how the name "Āśvina-śastra" came to all of them, the answer is that these mantras have this name because they are recited mainly with reference to the victory of the Aśvin deities.

In this context it is necessary to explain what the Prātaranuvāka is. When the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is performed, the day on which the Soma juice is pressed out is called the *sutyā*-day or *stutyā*-day [as printed]. In the morning of this day, before sunrise, as soon as the Adhvaryu recites the *praiṣa*-mantra देवेभ्यः प्रातर्यावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहि (*devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo hotaranubrūhi*) ("recite, O Hotṛ, for the gods who come early"), the Hotṛ recites certain mantras. These are called the Prātaranuvāka mantras. The Hotṛ must recite these Prātaranuvāka mantras. This is said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa itself: देवेभ्यः प्रातर्यावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः (*devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo hotaranubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2. 15.).

The order the Hotṛ follows when reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras is explained briefly. In the sacrifice the Adhvaryu, who holds the chief priestly role, has repeatedly to say to the other priests, "You must do such-and-such a work", and so on. Such sentences are called *praiṣa*s. In the present context the Adhvaryu, addressing the Hotṛ, says देवेभ्यः प्रातर्यावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहि (*devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo hotaranubrūhi*): "O Hotṛ, recite the Prātaranuvāka mantras addressed to the deities." Then the Hotṛ goes near the fire-pit called *āgnīdhra*, and there offers, with the prescribed mantras, one ghee-oblation for the purification of speech and two ghee-oblations in the Āhavanīya fire. Afterwards, entering by the eastern door the hall called *havirdhāna*, he sits near the yokes of the carts that are there and first recites this mantra:

> आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्वः क्रतुं च भद्रं बिभृथामृतं च ।
> रायश्च स्थ स्वपत्यस्य पत्नीः सरस्वती तद्गृणते वयो धात् ॥

> *āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasvaḥ kratuṃ ca bhadraṃ bibhṛthāmṛtaṃ ca |*
> *rāyaśca stha svapatyasya patnīḥ sarasvatī tadgṛṇate vayo dhāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 30. 12.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "O wealthy Waters, you rule over goods; you bear good intelligence and immortality; you are mistresses of riches and of good offspring; may Sarasvatī grant vigour to the singer.") *(Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 8  (PDF 26)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* Afterwards he recites the Prātaranuvāka mantras addressed to Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin deities. These are in three parts. The mantras said with reference to Agni are named the *Āgneya-kratu*; the mantras recited with reference to Uṣas, the *Uṣasya-kratu*; and the mantras recited with reference to the Aśvin deities, the *Āśvina-kratu*. To make known that the mantras addressed to each deity here must be in seven metres, there is the repetition (*vīpsā*) सप्तभिः सप्तभिः छन्दोभिः (*saptabhiḥ saptabhiḥ chandobhiḥ*) ("with seven, with seven metres") (it is said twice). Accordingly the account of these mantras is as follows.

> तान्येतान्याश्विने प्रातरनुवाके सप्तच्छन्दांसि ।

> *tānyetānyāśvine prātaranuvāke saptacchandāṃsi |*

("These are the seven metres in the Āśvina [part of the] Prātaranuvāka.") These seven are the Prātaranuvāka mantras addressed to the Aśvin deities and belonging to the Āśvina-kratu. The greatness of these Prātaranuvāka mantras, and its spiritual background, are made known in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as seen below.

> देवेभ्यः प्रातर्यावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः । एते वाव देवाः प्रातर्यावाणो यदग्निरुषा अश्विना त एते सप्तभिः सप्तभिश्छन्दोभिरागच्छन्ति । अस्य देवाः प्रातर्यावाणो हवं गच्छन्ति य एवं वेद । प्रजापतौ वै स्वयं होतरि प्रातरनुवाकमनुवक्ष्यत्युभये देवासुरा यज्ञमुपावसन्नस्मभ्यमनुवक्ष्यत्यस्मभ्यमिति स वै देवेभ्य एवान्वब्रवीत् । ततो वै देवा अभवन्परासुरा भवत्यात्मना परास्य द्विषन् पाप्मा भ्रातृव्यो भवति य एवं वेद । प्रातर्वै स तं देवेभ्योऽन्वब्रवीद्यत्प्रातरनुवाकस्य प्रातरनुवाकत्वम् । महति रात्र्या अनूच्यः सर्वस्यै वाचः सर्वस्य ब्रह्मणः परिगृहीत्यै यो वै भवति यः श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते तस्य वाचं प्रोदितामनुप्रवदन्ति तस्मान्महति रात्र्या अनूच्यः .... .... .... यदा वा अध्वर्युरुपाकरोति वाचैवोपाकरोति वाचा होतान्वाह वाग्घि ब्रह्म तत्र स काम उपाप्तो यो वाचि च ब्रह्मणि च ॥

> *devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo hotaranubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ | ete vāva devāḥ prātaryāvāṇo yadagniruṣā aśvinā ta ete saptabhiḥ saptabhiśchandobhirāgacchanti | asya devāḥ prātaryāvāṇo havaṃ gacchanti ya evaṃ veda | prajāpatau vai svayaṃ hotari prātaranuvākamanuvakṣyatyubhaye devāsurā yajñamupāvasannasmabhyamanuvakṣyatyasmabhyamiti sa vai devebhya evānvabravīt | tato vai devā abhavanparāsurā bhavatyātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda | prātarvai sa taṃ devebhyo 'nvabravīdyatprātaranuvākasya prātaranuvākatvam | mahati rātryā anūcyaḥ sarvasyai vācaḥ sarvasya brahmaṇaḥ parigṛhītyai yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatāmaśnute tasya vācaṃ proditāmanupravadanti tasmānmahati rātryā anūcyaḥ .... .... .... yadā vā adhvaryurupākaroti vācaivopākaroti vācā hotānvāha vāgghi brahma tatra sa kāma upāpto yo vāci ca brahmaṇi ca ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 7[?]-5, as read.)

Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin deities — these alone are the deities who move about in the early morning. Each one of these deities is possessed of seven metres. They come and join the man who knows this truth. Once, when Prajāpati himself was the Hotṛ, with the deities on one side and the asuras on the other consecrated for the sacrifice, both groups supposed that Prajāpati would recite the Prātaranuvāka for their own sacrifice. But Prajāpati recited it for the deities only. The deities won by this; the asuras were defeated. Because it was recited in the early morning it became known as the Prātaranuvāka; and if its effect is to appear in full, it must be recited after the deep midnight, before the light spreads. Since Speech is of the form of *brahman*, the desired object is obtained by reciting it.

> प्रजापतौ स्वयं होतरि प्रातरनुवाकमनुवक्ष्यति सर्वा देवता आशंसन्त मामभि प्रतिपत्स्यति मामभीति स प्रजाप्रतिरैक्षत [sic] यद्येकां देवतामादि[?] …

(Ai. Brā. 7-6.)

When Prajāpati, being the Hotṛ, was ready to recite the Prātaranuvāka, each one of the deities was watching with eagerness, [hoping] that he would recite it with reference to himself. Then Prajāpati [printed "Prajāprati"] fell into a state of doubt. Considering how, if he addressed only one deity, he would win another deity, at last, addressing the Waters (*ap*), which comprise all the deities, he recited the mantra

> आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्वः क्रतुं च भद्रं बिभृथामृतं च ।
> रायश्च स्थ स्वपत्यस्य पत्नीः सरस्वती तद्गृणते वयो धात् ॥

> *āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasvaḥ kratuṃ ca bhadraṃ bibhṛthāmṛtaṃ ca |*
> *rāyaśca stha svapatyasya patnīḥ sarasvatī tadgṛṇate vayo dhāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 30. 12) (gloss as on p. 7). By this all the deities were satisfied. Therefore the praiser who, knowing this truth, recites the Prātaranuvāka mantras becomes worthy of the grace of all the deities at once and obtains all that he desires.

> तिस्रो देवता अन्वाह त्रयो वा इमे त्रिवृतो लोका एषामेव लोकानामभिजित्यै ।

> *tisro devatā anvāha trayo vā ime trivṛto lokā eṣāmeva lokānāmabhijityai |*

(Ai. Brā. 7-8.) ("He recites [to] three deities; threefold indeed are these worlds; it is for the winning of these very worlds.")

Since Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin deities, these three, are the lords of the three worlds, the mantras recited with reference to them are means for attaining the three worlds. This being so, another doubt arises here. Anticipating that doubt, the answer to it is given thus:

> तदाहुः कथमनूच्यः प्रातरनुवाक इति । यथाछन्दसमनूच्यः प्रातरनुवाकः प्रजापतेर्वा एतान्यङ्गानि यच्छन्दांस्येष उ एव प्रजापतिर्यो यजते तद्यजमानाय हितम् । पच्छोऽनूच्यः प्रातरनुवाकश्चतुष्पादा वै पशवः पशूनामवरुद्ध्यै । . . . . . . . . . आहुतिभागा वा अन्या देवता अन्याः स्तोमभागाश्छन्दोभागास्ता या अग्नावाहुतयो हू- …

> … यन्ते ताभिराहुतिभागाः प्रीणात्यथ यत्स्तुवन्ति च शंसन्ति च तेन स्तोमभागाश्छन्दोभागाः । उभय्यो हास्यैता देवताः प्रीता अभीष्टा भवन्ति य एवं वेद ।

> *… yante tābhirāhutibhāgāḥ prīṇātyatha yatstuvanti ca śaṃsanti ca tena stomabhāgāśchandobhāgāḥ | ubhayyo hāsyaitā devatāḥ prītā abhīṣṭā bhavanti ya evaṃ veda |*

(Ai. Brā. 7-8.)

To the question, "What is the order of reciting the Prātaranuvāka?": the scriptural order is to recite it bound to metre and following the order of the prescribed metres. Why? Because the metres are the limbs of Prajāpati. Prajāpati himself is the performer of the sacrifice; and since animals go on feet, if one wishes to obtain them one must recite the Prātaranuvāka in the order of the *pāda*s (quarter-verse by quarter-verse). Having made known the order of recitation in this way, another doubt is anticipated. It is this:

> अभूदुषा रुशत्पशुरित्युत्तमया परिदधाति । तदाहुर्यत्त्रीन्क्रतूनन्वाहाग्नेयमुषस्यमाश्विनं कथमस्यैकयर्चा परिदधतः सर्वे त्रयः क्रतवः परिहिता भवन्तीति । अभूदुषा रुशत्पशुरित्युषसो रूपमाग्निरधाय्यृत्विय इत्यग्नेरयोजि वां वृषण्वसू रथो दस्रावमर्त्यो माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवमित्यश्विनोरेवमु हास्यैकयर्चा परिदधतः सर्वे त्रयः क्रतवः परिहिता भवन्ति भवन्ति ।

> *abhūduṣā ruśatpaśurityuttamayā paridadhāti | tadāhuryattrīnkratūnanvāhāgneyamuṣasyamāśvinaṃ kathamasyaikayarcā paridadhataḥ sarve trayaḥ kratavaḥ parihitā bhavantīti | abhūduṣā ruśatpaśurityuṣaso rūpamāgniradhāyyṛtviya ityagnerayoji vāṃ vṛṣaṇvasū ratho dasrāvamartyo mādhvī mama śrutaṃ havamityaśvinorevamu hāsyaikayarcā paridadhataḥ sarve trayaḥ kratavaḥ parihitā bhavanti bhavanti |*

(Ai. Brā. 7-8.)

Since the Prātaranuvāka must be recited with reference to all these deities — Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin deities — in the present case,

> अभूदुषा रुशत्पशुराग्निरधाय्यृत्वियः ।

> *abhūduṣā ruśatpaśurāgniradhāyyṛtviyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5. 75. 9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Dawn with her shining cattle has appeared; Agni, the timely one, has been set down.") — when the conclusion is made with this single mantra, if the question comes how all the rites addressed to all the deities become complete, it is explained and shown that the praise of the three deities is contained in this very mantra. This is the greatness of the Prātaranuvāka; and since the mantras endowed with this greatness must be recited at dawn, Sāyaṇa, in his explanation of the present ṛk, has stated उषःकाले हि प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रे प्रयुज्येते (*uṣaḥkāle hi prātaranuvākāśvinaśastre prayujyete*) ("for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra are used at the time of dawn").

By *uṣasi ucchantyām* ("when Dawn shines forth") the prayer addressed to the Aśvin deities is made known. Indicating the time of their journey to the place of sacrifice,

> अबोध्यग्निर्ज्म उदेति सूर्यो व्यु१षाश्चन्द्रा मह्यावो अर्चिषा ।
> आयुक्षातामश्विना यातवे रथं प्रासावीद्देवः सविता जगत्पृथक् ॥

> *abodhyagnirjma udeti sūryo vyu1ṣāścandrā mahyāvo arciṣā |*
> *āyukṣātāmaśvinā yātave rathaṃ prāsāvīddevaḥ savitā jagatpṛthak ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 157. 1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Agni has awoken; the Sun rises from the earth; the great bright Dawn has opened [the world] with her flame; the Aśvins have yoked their chariot to go; god Savitṛ has impelled the world, each in its own way.") *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 12  (PDF 30)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* In this ṛk the prayer is made thus: "Agni is blazing on the altar. The Āditya too is rising. The great-souled goddess Uṣas, with her radiance, is producing joy for the whole world. Therefore, O Aśvin deities, join your chariot with the horses and yoke it, to go to the place of sacrifice." Just as it is prayed there, so it is prayed in the present ṛk too. And in making known the time of their journey to the place of sacrifice, it has indicated the kindling of Agni, the appearance of Uṣas and the rising of the Sun. Making known this same point, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says:

> देवेभ्यः प्रातर्यावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः । एते वाव देवाः प्रातर्यावाणो यदग्निरुषा अश्विना त एते सप्तभिः सप्तभिश्छन्दोभिरागच्छन्ति ॥

> *devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo hotaranubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ | ete vāva devāḥ prātaryāvāṇo yadagniruṣā aśvinā ta ete saptabhiḥ saptabhiśchandobhirāgacchanti ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 7-5.)

In the mantra quoted above it is said that the Adhvaryu gives the Hotṛ the command that he must pray to Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin deities with the Prātaranuvāka mantras to come to the sacrificial house at the time of dawn. Describing this same point, the present ṛk has made known the appearance of Uṣas.

**उषसि उच्छन्ति (*uṣasi ucchanti*) [as printed].** For this word one meaning, "dispersing darkness and destroying it", and another meaning, "illumining with brilliance", are possible. The formation of the word *uṣā* too has come about only by way of *ucchati*. With the sentence उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*) ("Why *uṣās*? Because she shines forth; she is the later time of the night") the Niruktakāra has given this derivation (Ni. 2. 18). But with the sentence उषा वष्टेः कान्तिकर्मण उच्छतेरितरा माध्यमिका (*uṣā vaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇa ucchateritarā mādhyamikā*) (Ni. 12. 7[?]) the Niruktakāras have also made known that the word may be formed either from the root वश कान्तौ (*vaśa kāntau*) or from the root उच्छी विवासे (*ucchī vivāse*). In the present ṛk the words उषसि उच्छन्त्याम् (*uṣasi ucchantyām*) may mean either "Uṣas, who disperses darkness completely and appears outside" or "Uṣas, who is illumining with brilliance".

**दिवः नपाता (*divaḥ napātā*).** The word *napāt* means son and grandson. The Niruktakāras, with "नपादित्यनन्तरायाः प्रजायाः नामधेयम्" (*napādityanantarāyāḥ prajāyāḥ nāmadheyam*) ("*napāt* is a name of the offspring not immediately next"), have given this word the meaning "not the direct son", i.e. grandsons and the like (Ni. 8. 5). In the present case, for *divo napātā* Sāyaṇa has given the meaning द्युलोकस्य नप्तृस्थानीयौ (*dyulokasya naptṛsthānīyau*) ("standing in the place of grandsons of the heavenly world"). The origin and nature of the Aśvin deities are told in one way in one place and another way in another. For example,

### Printed p. 13  (PDF 31)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

> इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा३ नामभिः स्वैः ।
> जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥

> *iheha jātā samavāvaśītāmarepasā tanvā3 nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ |*
> *jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumakhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 181. 4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Born here and there, the two, spotless in body, have called out together by their own names; one of you is the victorious patron of the good sacrificer; the other is held to be the fortunate son of heaven.")

In this ṛk it is described that, of the Aśvin deities, one, as son of the middle world, in the form of the Moon, and the other, as son of the heavenly world, in the form of the Sun, are protectors of the world. That of these two, one deity is named Nāsatya and the other deity Dasra is known from some other contexts. This explanation was given earlier in the Special Topics of the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 181. 4.

**नासत्या (*nāsatyā*).**

> नासत्या चाश्विना । सत्या वेव नासत्यावित्यौर्णवाभः सत्यस्य प्रणेतारावित्याग्रायणः । नासिका प्रभवौ बभूवतुरिति वा ।

> *nāsatyā cāśvinā | satyā veva nāsatyāvityaurṇavābhaḥ satyasya praṇetārāvityāgrāyaṇaḥ | nāsikā prabhavau babhūvaturiti vā |*

(Ni. 6. 13.) According to Aurṇavābha's view, they who are of the nature of truth, not untrue, are the Nāsatyas; according to Āgrāyaṇa's view, they are Nāsatyas because they create truth and make it grow; or they are Nāsatyas because they were born from the nose — so the Niruktakāras have made known that the Aśvin deities have this epithet in one way according to each one's view.

**अर्यः (*aryaḥ*).** ईरयिता स्तुतेरीश्वरो वा (*īrayitā stuterīśvaro vā*): it has been explained as meaning "the impeller of praise" or "the one master of (able in) the making of praise". This is an epithet of the Hotṛ. Through this epithet the Hotṛ makes known his devotion and faith, [declaring] that he is one who praises most excellently.

The Niruktakāras have listed this word among the names of the Lord (*īśvara*) (Ni. 3. 11, as read), and, having quoted the ṛk that uses this word in the sense of "lord" —

> प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> तं त्वा गृणामि तवसमतव्यान्क्षयन्तमस्य रजसः पराके ॥

> *pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān |*
> *taṃ tvā gṛṇāmi tavasamatavyānkṣayantamasya rajasaḥ parāke ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7. 100. 5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, the lord [of praises], knowing the ways, proclaim that name of yours; I, the weaker, praise you, the strong, dwelling far beyond this region.")

— have explained it as "अर्योऽहमीश्वरः स्तोमानामर्यस्त्वमसीति वा" (*aryo 'hamīśvaraḥ stomānāmaryastvamasīti vā*) ("'I am the *arya*, master of praises', or 'you are the *arya*'") (Ni. 5. 9). Here the Vṛttikāra has explained: "यस्मादर्योऽहमस्मि ईश्वरः स्तुतीनामुदीरणे युष्मद्गुणाभिज्ञः अथवा अर्यस्त्वमसि अर्य ईश्वरः मदनुग्रहाय समर्थः" (*yasmādaryo 'hamasmi īśvaraḥ stutīnāmudīraṇe yuṣmadguṇābhijñaḥ athavā aryastvamasi arya īśvaraḥ madanugrahāya samarthaḥ*) — "I am able to know your qualities in order to praise [you]; or, you are able to show grace". The use of this word in the sense of "venerable" (*pūjya*) too occurs in many places. For example, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 14  (PDF 32)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* *(Ṛk 1 Special Topics continued: examples of* aryaḥ *in the sense "venerable".)*

> पृथू रथो दक्षिणाया अयोज्यैनं देवासो अमृतासो अस्थुः ।
> कृष्णादुदस्थादर्या३ विहायाश्चिकित्सन्ती मानुषाय क्षयाय ॥

> *pṛthū ratho dakṣiṇāyā ayojyainaṃ devāso amṛtāso asthuḥ |*
> *kṛṣṇādudasthādaryā3 vihāyāścikitsantī mānuṣāya kṣayāya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 123. 1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The broad chariot of Dakṣiṇā has been yoked; the immortal gods have mounted it; the noble, vast one has risen from the darkness, taking heed for the human dwelling.")

In this ṛk, describing the qualities of the Uṣas-deity, who is understood from the context, there is the epithet अर्या (*aryā*). For this word Sāyaṇa has given the meaning पूज्या (*pūjyā*) ("venerable"); and its use is most frequent in the sense of "the Lord of all" (*sarveśvara*).

**मघवाना (*maghavānā*).** For this epithet Sāyaṇa has given the meaning हविर्लक्षणान्नयुक्तौ (*havirlakṣaṇānnayuktau*): "(the Aśvin deities) endowed with food in the form of oblation". Although ordinarily the epithet *maghavan* refers to Indra, this epithet is used here and there in the Ṛksaṃhitā when the qualities of other deities too are described.

Or, since the word *magha* is read among the names of wealth (*dhana*) (Ni. 3. 9, as read), here it can be said to mean wealth in the form of food. The Niruktakāras, with मघमिति धननामधेयं मंहतेर्दानकर्मणः (*maghamiti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃhaterdānakarmaṇaḥ*) ("*magha* is a name of wealth, from *maṃh*, which means giving"), have made known the derivation of the word *magha* and explained the meaning of the word *maghonī* (Ni. 1. 7[?]). In the same way, in the present ṛk too, a derivation can be given for the epithet *maghavānā*. Or,

*maghavānā* may be taken to mean "the Aśvin deities joined with Viṣṇu", and that would not be wrong. For it has been made known earlier that in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and other texts the identity of Viṣṇu and *makha* (sacrifice) is stated (Śa. Brā. 14. 1. 1. 13). The association between the Aśvin deities and Viṣṇu, who has the form of *makha*, is also well known. This point too was made known earlier, in explaining the Special Topics of the ṛk

> तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विना क्रतुं संचत मारुतस्य वेधसः ।
> दधार दक्षमुत्तममहर्विदं व्रजं च विष्णुः सखिवाँ अपोर्णुते ॥

> *tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinā kratuṃ saṃcata mārutasya vedhasaḥ |*
> *dadhāra dakṣamuttamamaharvidaṃ vrajaṃ ca viṣṇuḥ sakhivā~ aporṇute ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 156. 4) (संचत (*saṃcata*) and दधार (*dadhāra*) as printed.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "King Varuṇa and the Aśvins attend on this resolve of the Marut-accompanied disposer; Viṣṇu holds the highest, day-finding skill, and, with his companion, opens the pen.") (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 11, pp. 656–657). Moreover, in the Ṛksaṃhitā too this same association is described thus:

> यदिन्द्रेण सरथं याथो अश्विना यद्वा वायुना भवथः समोकसा ।
> यदादित्येभिर्ऋभुभिः सजोषसा यद्वा विष्णोर्विक्रमणेषु तिष्ठथः ॥

> *yadindreṇa sarathaṃ yātho aśvinā yadvā vāyunā bhavathaḥ samokasā |*
> *yadādityebhirṛbhubhiḥ sajoṣasā yadvā viṣṇorvikramaṇeṣu tiṣṭhathaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8. 9. 12) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Whether, O Aśvins, you go on one chariot with Indra, or dwell in one abode with Vāyu, or are in accord with the Ādityas and Ṛbhus, or stand in the strides of Viṣṇu.") *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 15  (PDF 33)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* In ṛks such as these it is made known that the Aśvin deities have association with Viṣṇu. For this reason *maghavānā* may also be taken to mean "the Aśvin deities joined with Viṣṇu". But in the present context it appears more fitting to give the meaning, as Sāyaṇa has said, "those endowed with the wealth of food in the form of oblation".

**सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*).** सुष्ठु पापवर्जनं यथा भवति तथा । यद्वा । सुसमाप्ति (*suṣṭhu pāpavarjanaṃ yathā bhavati tathā | yadvā | susamāpti*) — the meaning is "having full release from sin", or "having a pure completion". This word is an epithet of the word *stoma* (praise). This epithet is used in one sense in one place and in another sense in another. The Niruktakāras, quoting the ṛk

> इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः ।
> पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥

> *iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ |*
> *pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6. 61. 2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "This [Sarasvatī], like one digging for lotus-fibres, has broken the ridges of the mountains with her strong, mighty waves; let us, for help, serve Sarasvatī, destroyer of the far-dwelling [foes], with fair praises and devout thoughts.")

— have given for the word *suvṛktibhiḥ* in it the meaning सुप्रवृत्ताभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिः (*supravṛttābhiḥ śobhanābhiḥ stutibhiḥ*), i.e. excellent praise. The word *vṛkti* is used in other places also in the sense of "avoiding". For example,

> कुविदङ्ग यवमन्तो यवं चिद्यथा दान्त्यनुपूर्वं वियूय ।
> इहेहैषां कृणुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमोवृक्तिं न जग्मुः ॥

> *kuvidaṅga yavamanto yavaṃ cidyathā dāntyanupūrvaṃ viyūya |*
> *ihehaiṣāṃ kṛṇuhi bhojanāni ye barhiṣo namovṛktiṃ na jagmuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 131. 2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "As men rich in barley reap the barley in due order, separating it, so here make provisions for those who have not given up the homage of the sacred grass.")

Here, with नमोवृक्तिं नमसः हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्य नमस्कारात्मकस्य स्तोत्रस्य वा वर्जनमकरणं न जग्मुः (*namovṛktiṃ namasaḥ havirlakṣaṇasyānnasya namaskārātmakasya stotrasya vā varjanamakaraṇaṃ na jagmuḥ*) ("*namovṛkti*: they have not come to the avoidance, the non-doing, of *namas* — food in the form of oblation, or praise in the form of homage"), Indra is prayed to [for those] who have not given up praise in the form of homage. Here the word *vṛkti* is used in the sense of avoiding. But its use in the sense of praise is by far the more frequent. For example,

> अस्मा इदु त्यमुपमं स्वर्षां भराम्याङ्गूषमास्येन ।
> मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ॥

> *asmā idu tyamupamaṃ svarṣāṃ bharāmyāṅgūṣamāsyena |*
> *maṃhiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 61. 3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "To him I bring with my mouth this highest, light-winning hymn, to strengthen the most bountiful patron with invocations and fair praises of thoughts.")

In all such places the meaning is "excellent praise".

**वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*).** वर्तनहेतुभूतं गृहम् (*vartanahetubhūtaṃ gṛham*): Sāyaṇa has given, in all places where this word comes, the meaning "the house that is the support for dwelling". But Skandasvāmin has generally, in all places, given the meaning "the well-known road (*mārga*)". For example, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 16  (PDF 34)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)*

> त्रिर्वर्तिर्यातं त्रिरनुव्रते जने त्रिः सुप्राव्ये त्रेधेव शिक्षतम् ।
> त्रिर्नान्द्यं वहतमश्विना युवं त्रिः पृक्षो अस्मे अक्षरेव पिन्वतम् ॥

> *trirvartiryātaṃ triranuvrate jane triḥ suprāvye tredheva śikṣatam |*
> *trirnāndyaṃ vahatamaśvinā yuvaṃ triḥ pṛkṣo asme akṣareva pinvatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 34. 4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Thrice come to the dwelling [or: along the course], thrice to the devoted man; thrice teach, as it were threefold, the one who is to be well protected; thrice, O Aśvins, bring us what gladdens; thrice swell for us nourishment, as [clouds] the waters.")

In all such ṛks Sāyaṇa has given for *varti* the meaning "house" (*gṛha*) and Skandasvāmin the meaning "path" (*patha*). It is a special point that all the sūktas containing ṛks in which the word *varti* is used in this way — *trir vartiḥ*, *aśvinā vartiḥ* and so on — such as 1. 1[?]6. 18; 1. 1[?]7[?]. 2; 1. 119[?]. 4, refer to the Aśvin deities (numerals as read; some digits are broken in the print). But in the ṛk

> इषं दुहन्त्सुदुघां विश्वधायसं यज्ञप्रिये यजमानाय सुक्रतो ।
> अग्ने घृतस्नुस्त्रिर्ऋतानि दीद्यद्वर्तिर्यज्ञं परियन्त्सुक्रतूयसे ॥

> *iṣaṃ duhantsudughāṃ viśvadhāyasaṃ yajñapriye yajamānāya sukrato |*
> *agne ghṛtasnustrirṛtāni dīdyadvartiryajñaṃ pariyantsukratūyase ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 122. 6) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Milking out, O wise Agni, for the sacrificer who loves sacrifice, nourishment that yields well and sustains all, you, dripping ghee, shining thrice upon the rites, going round the dwelling and the sacrifice, show yourself of good resolve.")

alone is the word used in a mantra addressed to Agni. Here it has been explained as "the sacrificial house". Sāyaṇa too has in some places given this word the meaning "path" (*mārga*). For example,

> यो ह स्य वां रथिरा वस्त उस्रा रथो युजानः परियाति वर्तिः ।

*(continues on the next page)*

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

> तेन नः शंयोरुषसो व्युष्टौ न्यश्विना वहतं यज्ञे अस्मिन् ॥

> *tena naḥ śaṃyoruṣaso vyuṣṭau nyaśvinā vahataṃ yajñe asmin ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7. 69. 5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "That chariot of yours, O charioteers, which clothes itself in the dawns and, being yoked, goes round the course — with it, O Aśvins, at the dawning of Uṣas, bring weal and welfare to us in this sacrifice.")

Here *vartiḥ* has been explained as मार्गम् (*mārgam*) ("the path"). This is a mantra prayed to with reference to the Aśvin deities themselves. In the present ṛk the meaning is "house". Generally it is a synonym for the sacrificial house.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as printed).** *tā* (*tad* with the dual ending *au*; *a*-substitution by *tyadādīnām aḥ*; *pararūpa* by *ato guṇe*; *ā* for the case-ending by *supāṃ suluk* … Pā. 7-1-39). *huvema* (root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *liṅ* 1st plural; *nighāta* accent as it follows a word that is not a verb [as printed "atiṅanta"]). *ucchantyām* (root *uchī vivāse*; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; *śa*-vikaraṇa by *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ*; feminine *ṅīp* by *ugitaś ca* Pā. 4-1-6; the vikaraṇa accent remains; locative singular). *vahniḥ* (root *vaha prāpaṇe*; suffix *ni* by *vahiśriśruyudru* … Uṇ. 4-51; initial acute as it is *nit*). *santau* (root *asa bhuvi*; *śatṛ*; *luk* of the vikaraṇa; elision of the root's *a* by *śnasor allopaḥ* Pā. 6-4-111; the suffix's initial acute; *num* augment as it is *ugit*, anusvāra and *parasavarṇa*). *aryaḥ* (root *ṛ gatau*; *yat* in the sense of "master" by *aryaḥ svāmivaiśyayoḥ* Pā. 3-1-103; guṇa with *r*). *sudāstarāya* (*śobhanaṃ dadātīti sudāḥ*; root *ḍudāñ dāne*; suffix *asun*; *kṛduttarapada-prakṛtisvara*; then *tarap* in the sense of excess, unaccented as it is *pit*; *rutva*, visarga, *satva* of the final *s*; dative singular). ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अस्मे ऊ षु वृषणा मादयेथामुत्पणीँर्हतमूर्म्या मदन्ता ।
> श्रुतं मे अच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनामेष्टा नरा निचेतारा च कर्णैः ॥ २ ॥

> *asme ū ṣu vṛṣaṇā mādayethāmutpaṇī~rhatamūrmyā madantā |*
> *śrutaṃ me acchoktibhirmatīnāmeṣṭā narā nicetārā ca karṇaiḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्मे इति । ऊं इति । सु । वृषणा । मादयेथाम् । उत् । पणीन् । हतम् । ऊर्म्या । मदन्ता ।
> श्रुतम् । मे । अच्छोक्तिऽभिः । मतीनाम् । एष्टा । नरा । निऽचेतारा । च । कर्णैः ॥ २ ॥

> *asme iti | ūṃ iti | su | vṛṣaṇā | mādayethām | ut | paṇīn | hatam | ūrmyā | madantā |*
> *śrutam | me | acchokti 'bhiḥ | matīnām | eṣṭā | narā | ni 'cetārā | ca | karṇaiḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(begins)*

> हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षकावश्विनौ युवामस्मे उ अस्मास्वेव सु मादयेथाम् । सुष्ठु तृप्यतम् । अस्मभ्यं तर्पयतमभिमतम् । तथा पणीन्वणिजो लुब्धकानयष्टॄनुदुत्कृष्य [?] हतम् । नाशयतम् । कीदृशौ युवाम् । ऊर्म्या रात्रिनामैतत् । रात्र्यां मदन्ता माद्यन्तौ । यद्वा । ऊर्मिरिति सोमनाम । ऊर्मिर्यस्ते पवित्र आ । ऋ. ९-६४-११ । इत्यादिषु तथा प्रयोगात् । अस्मदीयेन …

> *he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣakāvaśvinau yuvāmasme u asmāsveva su mādayethām | suṣṭhu tṛpyatam | asmabhyaṃ tarpayatamabhimatam | tathā paṇīnvaṇijo lubdhakānayaṣṭṝnudutkṛṣya [?] hatam | nāśayatam | kīdṛśau yuvām | ūrmyā rātrināmaitat | rātryāṃ madantā mādyantau | yadvā | ūrmiriti somanāma | ūrmiryaste pavitra ā | ṛ. 9-64-11 | ityādiṣu tathā prayogāt | asmadīyena …*

### Printed p. 18  (PDF 36)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* **Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (continued).**

> … सोमेन मदन्तौ । तादृशौ युवां मे ममाच्छोक्तिभिराभिमुख्यकरैर्निर्मलवेदवाक्यै रचिता मतीनाम् । कर्मणि षष्ठी । मननसाधनाः स्तुतीः कर्णैराकर्णनसाधनैः श्रोत्रैः श्रुतम् । शृणुतम् । हे नरा नेतारौ युवा[?] ऋष्वेष्ट्वन्वेष्टारावस्मत्स्तुतीनाम् [?] तथा निचेतारा लब्धानां तासां संचयकर्तारौ । निरित्येष समित्येतस्य स्थाने । यस्मादेवंविधौ तस्माच्छृणुतमिति ॥

> *… somena madantau | tādṛśau yuvāṃ me mamācchoktibhirābhimukhyakarairnirmalavedavākyai racitā matīnām | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | mananasādhanāḥ stutīḥ karṇairākarṇanasādhanaiḥ śrotraiḥ śrutam | śṛṇutam | he narā netārau yuvā[?] ṛṣveṣṭvanveṣṭārāvasmatstutīnām [?] tathā nicetārā labdhānāṃ tāsāṃ saṃcayakartārau | nirityeṣa samityetasya sthāne | yasmādevaṃvidhau tasmācchṛṇutamiti ‖*

*Gist:* O showerers of desires, take full delight among us; destroy the niggardly, non-sacrificing Paṇis; you who rejoice at night (*ūrmyā* = night) or with Soma, seekers and gatherers of our praises, hear with your ears the praises made by me with pure Vedic words. (*mati* in the genitive for the object; *ni-* stands for *sam-*.)

**Pratipadārtha.** *ūrmyā* — at the time of night (or, in the Somas offered by us); *madantā* — you who obtain satisfaction; *vṛṣaṇā* — O Aśvin deities, showerers of desires; *asme u* — among us alone (or, for our satisfaction alone); *su mādayethām* — you too obtain full satisfaction; *tathā* — (likewise); *paṇīn* — the misers who do not perform sacrifice; *ut hatam* — uproot and destroy; *narā* — O Aśvin deities, who are leaders; *eṣṭā* — you who look out for (our praises); *nicetārā ca* — and who gather (the praises obtained), you; *acchoktibhiḥ* — (to obtain your grace) made of Vedic words; *me* — my (composed by me); *matīnām* — praises in the form of meditation; *karṇaiḥ* — with your ears; *śrutam* — hear.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvin deities, who obtain satisfaction in the Soma juices offered by us and who shower desires: so as to give us satisfaction, you too obtain full satisfaction. Likewise uproot and destroy the misers who do not perform sacrifice. O Aśvin deities, who are leaders, you who look out for our praises and gather the praises obtained: to obtain your grace, hear with love my words of praise, made of Vedic words and of the nature of meditation.

**English Translation (as printed):** Showerers (of benefits), rejoicing in (our) libations, make us happy and destroy the niggard (withholder) of offerings; hear, leaders, with your ears, my praises addressed to you with pure words, for you are seekers (after praise), you are retentive (of laudation).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**ऊर्म्या (*ūrmyā*).** रात्रिनामैतत् । यद्वा । ऊर्मिरिति सोमनाम (*rātrināmaitat | yadvā | ūrmiriti somanāma*) ("this is a name of night; or, *ūrmi* is a name of Soma"). The Niruktakāras have read this word among the names of night (Ni. 2[?]-18, as read). Therefore here too the meaning "night" … *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 19  (PDF 37)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* … may be given: this is one alternative. Making known how the form of the word *ūrmi* is derived if this meaning is given, Sāyaṇa, where this word is used elsewhere, has explained it thus, pointing to that example:

> अस्मा उषास आतिरन्त याममिन्द्राय नक्तमूर्म्याः सुवाचः ।
> अस्मा आपो मातरः सप्त तस्थुर्नृभ्यस्तराय सिन्धवः सुपाराः ॥

> *asmā uṣāsa ātiranta yāmamindrāya naktamūrmyāḥ suvācaḥ |*
> *asmā āpo mātaraḥ sapta tasthurnṛbhyastarāya sindhavaḥ supārāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For him the dawns have prolonged their course, for Indra the nights with fair voices; for him the seven mother waters, the rivers easy to cross, have stood still, for men to cross.")

In giving the meaning of the word *ūrmi* in this ṛk [he says]: रात्रिनामैतत् । ऋ गतिप्रापणयोः । "अर्तेरूच" (उ. सू. ४-४४) इति 'मि' प्रत्ययः सर्वैरभिगन्तव्यः । रात्र्यां हि सर्वे स्वनिवासं गच्छन्ति । स्वनिलयप्राप्तिहेतुभूता रात्रयः [?] । (*rātrināmaitat | ṛ gatiprāpaṇayoḥ | "arterūca" (u. sū. 4-44) iti 'mi ' pratyayaḥ sarvairabhigantavyaḥ | rātryāṃ hi sarve svanivāsaṃ gacchanti | svanilayaprāptihetubhūtā rātrayaḥ [?] |*) ("This is a name of night. [Root] *ṛ*, 'to go, to reach'; by *arter ū ca* (Uṇ. 4-44) the suffix *mi*; [night is] that which is to be approached by all; for at night all go to their own dwellings; nights are the cause of reaching one's own abode.") — the word is formed from the root *ṛ*, which has the senses of going and reaching. At night all creatures go back each to its own dwelling and gather there. Because it brings all to their own places, night is well known by the name *ūrmi* — so he has explained. For this word in the present ṛk Sāyaṇa has given a second alternative, यद्वा ऊर्मिरिति सोमनाम (*yadvā ūrmiriti somanāma*): "or *ūrmi* may mean Soma". To support this explanation,

> ऊर्मिर्यस्ते पवित्र आ देवावीः पर्यक्षरत् । सीदन्नृतस्य योनिमा ॥

> *ūrmiryaste pavitra ā devāvīḥ paryakṣarat | sīdannṛtasya yonimā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-64-11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Your wave, which, gladdening the gods, has flowed round into the filter, settling in the seat of ṛta.")

— quoting this ṛk, in which *ūrmi* means Soma, he has made known that in the present ṛk too it may have the same meaning. Here one more point must be noted. *ūrmi* does not mean Soma; *ūrmi* means a wave of water. Since in the quoted ṛk Soma is prayed to, the meaning "Soma juice in the form of a wave" is understood. The Niruktakāras, quoting the ṛk in which this word is used in this very sense, that is, "wave of water",

> मा नः समस्य दूढ्य१ः [?] नि [?] परिद्वेषसो अंहतिः । ऊर्मिर्न नावमा वधीत् ॥

> *mā naḥ samasya dūḍhya1ḥ [?] ni [?] paridveṣaso aṃhatiḥ | ūrmirna nāvamā vadhīt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75-9) (the syllables after दूढ्य are unclear in the print; read roughly "ದೂಢ್ಯ೧ ಃ ನಿ"). (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Let not the distress of every ill-minded one, of the hater, strike us, as a wave a boat.")

— have explained ऊर्मिरूर्णोतेः (*ūrmirūrṇoteḥ*): it is derived from the root *ūrṇu*, which gives the sense of covering, concealing, enveloping (Ni. 5-23, as read). The meaning is "wave" or "mass of water". This word is used also in the sense of a collection or mass of water:

> धन्वन्स्रोतः कृणुते गातुमूर्मिं शुक्रैरूर्मिभिरभि नक्षति क्षाम् ।
> विश्वा सनानि जठरेषु धत्तेऽन्तर्नवासु चरति प्रसूषु ॥

> *dhanvansrotaḥ kṛṇute gātumūrmiṃ śukrairūrmibhirabhi nakṣati kṣām |*
> *viśvā sanāni jaṭhareṣu dhatte 'ntarnavāsu carati prasūṣu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-10) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "In the desert he makes a stream, a path, a wave; with bright waves he reaches the earth; he holds all old things in his bellies; he moves within the new, fresh shoots.") *(Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continue on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 20  (PDF 38)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* *(Ṛk 2 Special Topics continued.)* … where it says ऊर्मिं कृणुते (*ūrmiṃ kṛṇute*), ऊर्मिभिः अभिनक्षति (*ūrmibhiḥ abhinakṣati*). Here it is said that Agni makes the collection of water in the mid-region (*antarikṣa*) flow in the form of streams, and with the pure masses of water in the form of waves makes the earth soaked with water. In the present ṛk the meaning is either "night" or "Soma juice in the form of a wave".

**पणीन् (*paṇīn*).** For the word *paṇi* Sāyaṇa explained व्ययासहिष्णवो वणिजः (*vyayāsahiṣṇavo vaṇijaḥ*) — "merchants (traders) who shrink from spending", and then cited Yāska's view, पणिर्वणिग्भवतीति यास्कः (*paṇirvaṇigbhavatīti yāskaḥ*) ("*paṇi* is a merchant, says Yāska"). The Niruktakāras, when explaining the meaning of this word, quote the ṛk

> इन्द्रो विश्वान्बेकनाटाँ अहर्दृश उत क्रत्वा पणीँरभि ।

> *indro viśvānbekanāṭā~ ahardṛśa uta kratvā paṇī~rabhi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-66-10) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Indra [overcomes] all the usurers who look [only] to the day, and with his might the Paṇis.")

and give for the word *paṇi* in it the meaning वणिजः (*vaṇijaḥ*), "those who carry on trade" (Ni. 6-26, as read). Further, पणिः पणनात् । वणिक् पण्यं नेनेक्ति (*paṇiḥ paṇanāt | vaṇik paṇyaṃ nenekti*): because he trades, the vaiśya is called *paṇi*; and that trader always keeps his goods clean so that they are fit for trade — so they explain (Ni. 2-17, as read). Besides this, in some other places

Sāyaṇa has explained this word as पणय इति लुब्धका अबुध्यमाना यागादीनकुर्वाणा अदानशीला अस्मच्छत्रवः (*paṇaya iti lubdhakā abudhyamānā yāgādīnakurvāṇā adānaśīlā asmacchatravaḥ*) — "misers, those who do not perform sacrifices and the like, those devoid of acts of giving and the like: enemies". In the present ṛk he has given the meaning लुब्धकानयष्ट्वान् (*lubdhakānayaṣṭvān*) [?] (so printed here; the bhāṣya above has अयष्टॄन्). (The matter of the group of asuras called Paṇis will be made known later.)

**अस्मे उ (*asme u*).** For this word the meaning अस्मास्वेव (*asmāsveva*) ("among us alone") has been given. Although the word *asme* is of one form, the Niruktakāras have made known that this word is used in the senses of all the cases (Ni. 6-7). It was made known earlier that, like this word, the word *asmākam* too is used in all the cases.

Durgācārya, commenting in this context (Ni. 6-7), [says]:

> अस्मे इत्येतत्पदं सर्वविभक्त्यन्तम् । तस्मादनेकार्थम् । एकमेव ह्येतच्छब्दरूपं सप्तस्वपि विभक्त्यर्थेषु वर्तते । प्रकरणादिवशात् तस्य नियमो भवति । तद्यथा- प्रथमायास्तावत् अस्मे ते बन्धुः । वयमित्यर्थः ।

> *asme ityetatpadaṃ sarvavibhaktyantam | tasmādanekārtham | ekameva hyetacchabdarūpaṃ saptasvapi vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā- prathamāyāstāvat asme te bandhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ |*

("The word *asme* ends in all the case-endings; therefore it has many meanings. This one word-form serves in the senses of all seven cases; it is fixed by the context and so on. Thus, first, for the nominative: *asme te bandhuḥ* — the meaning is 'we'.")

He has made known that the word *asme*, used in all seven cases, must be interpreted according to each context. Among these, *asme te bandhuḥ* is the example for the nominative. And in the same way, *(continues on the next page)*

— quoting this ṛk, the Niruktakāras [say] for the word *asme* अस्मान् इत्यर्थः (*asmān ityarthaḥ*) ("the meaning is 'us'"): that here this word is used in the sense of the accusative (*dvitīyā*);

> भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः ।
> भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेन्द्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥

> *bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ |*
> *bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭhendra kratvā maruto yadvaśāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-7[?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Much have you done, O bull, with us your allies, with equal manly powers; much indeed shall we do, O mightiest Indra, by our resolve, we Maruts, when we will.")

— quoting this ṛk, [that it is] अस्माभिः (*asmābhiḥ*), the sense of the instrumental (*tṛtīyā*);

> अस्मे प्रयन्धि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निन्द्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः ।
> अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्छश्वत इन्द्र शिप्रिन् ॥

> *asme prayandhi maghavannṛjīṣinnindra rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ |*
> *asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāñchaśvata indra śiprin ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-10) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Bestow on us, O bounteous Indra, lord of the residue-drink, abundant wealth desired by all; grant us a hundred autumns to live; [give] us lasting heroes, O Indra of the fair jaws.")

— where अस्मभ्यम् (*asmabhyam*), "for us", is the sense of the dative (*caturthī*), so it is made known. And,

> तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम ।
> स सुत्रामा स्ववाँ इन्द्रो अस्मे अराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥

> *tasya vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma |*
> *sa sutrāmā svavā~ indro asme arācciddveṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-13) (अराच्चिद् as read, first vowel [?].) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May we be in the favour of him who is worthy of worship, and in his auspicious good will; may that good protector, the self-reliant Indra, keep hatred far away from us, even from afar.")

— where अस्मत् (*asmat*), "from our side", is the sense of the ablative (*pañcamī*);

> आ नो भर भगमिन्द्र द्युमन्तं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके ।
> ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनाम् ॥

> *ā no bhara bhagamindra dyumantaṃ ni te deṣṇasya dhīmahi prareke |*
> *ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tamā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-19) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Bring us, O Indra, a brilliant portion; may we partake of your gift in its overflow; our desire has spread wide like a reservoir; fill it, O lord of goods.")

— in which ṛk अस्माकम् (*asmākam*), "our", is the sense of the genitive (*ṣaṣṭhī*); likewise,

> अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो ।
> अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥

> *agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho |*
> *asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "O Agni, son of strength, lord of booty rich in cattle, bestow on us, O Jātavedas, great fame.")

— where it is also in the sense of the locative (*saptamī*); thus they have made known that the use of this one form is found in all the cases (Ni. 6-7).

**मतीनाम् (*matīnām*).** मननसाधनाः स्तुतीः (*mananasādhanāḥ stutīḥ*) — the meaning is "praise in the form of meditation". The genitive case is used in the sense of the accusative. The meaning is: "hear our praises in the form of meditation." *(continues on the next page)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as printed, small type).** *asme* (*asmad*; *śe* for the locative plural by *supāṃ suluk* … Pā. 7-1-39). *mādayethām* (root *mada tṛptiyoge*; *loṭ* 2nd dual; *nighāta* of the finite verb). *hatam* (root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *loṭ* 2nd dual *tam*; *luk* of the vikaraṇa; loss of the nasal by *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām* … Pā. 6-4-37[?]; *nighāta*). *ūrmyā* (*ā* for the locative singular by *supāṃ suluk*; *yaṇ*; the case-ending acute by *ekādeśa*). *madantā* (*śatṛ* for *laṭ*; *ā* for the dual; root accent kept as the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented by *tāsyanudāttet* …). *śrutam* (root *śru śravaṇe*; *loṭ* 2nd dual; *luk* of the vikaraṇa by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; no guṇa as the suffix is treated as *ṅit*; no *nighāta* at the head of the pāda; final acute). *matīnām* (acute on *nām* by *nāmanyatarasyām* Pā. 6-1-177[?]; genitive in the sense of the object). *eṣṭā* (root *iṣa gatau*; *tṛn* in the agent sense; guṇa of the light penultimate; *ṣṭutva*; initial acute as it is *nit*). *nicetārā* (root *ciñ cayane*; *tṛn*; guṇa by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*; *ni* by *vyatyaya* has the sense of the upasarga *sam*; *ā* for the dual by *supāṃ suluk*). ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> श्रिये पूषन्निषुकृतेव देवा नासत्या वहतुं सूर्यायाः ।
> वच्यन्ते वां ककुहा अप्सु जाता युगा जूर्णेव वरुणस्य भूरेः ॥ ३ ॥

> *śriye pūṣanniṣukṛteva devā nāsatyā vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ |*
> *vacyante vāṃ kakuhā apsu jātā yugā jūrṇeva varuṇasya bhūreḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> श्रिये । पूषन् । इषुकृताऽइव । देवा । नासत्या । वहतुम् । सूर्यायाः ।
> वच्यन्ते । वाम् । ककुहाः । अप्ऽसु । जाताः । युगा । जूर्णाऽइव । वरुणस्य । भूरेः ॥ ३ ॥

> *śriye | pūṣan | iṣukṛtā 'iva | devā | nāsatyā | vahatum | sūryāyāḥ |*
> *vacyante | vām | kakuhāḥ | ap 'su | jātāḥ | yugā | jūrṇā 'iva | varuṇasya | bhūreḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Savitṛ set a race for the gods to win his daughter Sūryā and the thousand-ṛk śastra; Agni won first, then the Aśvins beat him and placed Sūryā on their chariot (Ai. Brā. 4-7). *Pūṣan* here means the Aśvins (sun and moon, Ni. 12-1). Quick as arrows, they won Sūryā; therefore the hotṛs still praise them with śastras at sacrifices, as in former times.

> सविता सूर्यो दुहितरं सूर्याख्यां प्रदातुमना देवानाहूय सामर्थ्यसमीक्षणायाजिं परिकल्प्य य इमं जेष्यति स एषां कन्यकामृक्सहस्रक्लृप्तं स्तोत्रं च लभत इत्यकल्पयत् । तमग्निः प्रथममजयत् तमन्वश्विनावपि जित्वाग्निं प्रधृष्यर्क्सहस्रं कन्यकां चालभेताम् । तत इन्द्र उषाश्चाजयताम् । तौ च तैरग्न्यादिभिः प्रार्थितौ स्वशस्त्रस्य कंचित्कंचिद्भागं तेभ्यः परिकल्प्य सूर्यां स्वरथेऽधारयतामिति । अयमितिहासो ब्राह्मणे प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे । ऐ. ब्रा. ४-७ । इत्यत्राम्नातोऽस्माभिः प्रथमाष्टके आ वां पतित्वं सख्याय ( ऋ. १-११९-५ [?] ) इत्यत्र प्रपञ्चितः । अत्राह । हे पूषन् पोषक सूर्य । एतच्चन्द्रस्याप्युपलक्षणम् । सूर्याचन्द्रमसोरेवाश्वित्वात् । सूर्याचन्द्रमसावित्येके । नि. १२-१ । इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् । अतः पूषन्नित्युक्ते हे पोषकावश्विनावित्युक्तं भवति । हे पोषकौ हे नासत्यासत्यरहितौ देवा देवौ युवां श्रिये श्रेयसे । शस्त्रस्य कन्यायाश्च लाभायेत्यर्थः । इषुकृतेव । इवशब्द एवार्थे । आजिधावनायेषुवच्छीघ्रमृजुगामिनौ [?] कृतावेव संतौ सूर्याया एतन्नामिकायाः सवितुः पुत्र्याः ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ सूर्यां वहतुं रथे धारयितुम् । आजिमुदजयतामित्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं तस्मादप्सु जाताः कर्मसु संपादिताः ककुहाः शस्त्ररूपाः स्तुतयो भूरेरविच्छिन्नप्रवाहस्य वरुणस्य फलप्रतिबन्धकपापनिवारकस्य यागस्य सिद्ध्यर्थं तत्संबन्धिन्यो वां प्रति वच्यन्ते होत्रादिभिः । युवामेव शस्त्रगतमन्त्रैर्यागकाले च स्तुवन्तीत्यर्थः । युगा जूर्णेव जीर्णानि युगानीव । इवशब्दः संप्रत्यर्थः । पुरातना यागकाला यथा तद्वदद्यतना अपीत्यर्थः । पूर्वकाले यथा युवामेव स्तुवन्ति तद्वदिदानीमपीति तात्पर्यम् ॥

> *savitā sūryo duhitaraṃ sūryākhyāṃ pradātumanā devānāhūya sāmarthyasamīkṣaṇāyājiṃ parikalpya ya imaṃ jeṣyati sa eṣāṃ kanyakāmṛksahasraklṛptaṃ stotraṃ ca labhata ityakalpayat | tamagniḥ prathamamajayat tamanvaśvināvapi jitvāgniṃ pradhṛṣyarksahasraṃ kanyakāṃ cālabhetām | tata indra uṣāścājayatām | tau ca tairagnyādibhiḥ prārthitau svaśastrasya kaṃcitkaṃcidbhāgaṃ tebhyaḥ parikalpya sūryāṃ svarathe 'dhārayatāmiti | ayamitihāso brāhmaṇe prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe | ai. brā. 4-7 | ityatrāmnāto 'smābhiḥ prathamāṣṭake ā vāṃ patitvaṃ sakhyāya ( ṛ. 1-119-5 [?] ) ityatra prapañcitaḥ | atrāha | he pūṣan poṣaka sūrya | etaccandrasyāpyupalakṣaṇam | sūryācandramasorevāśvitvāt | sūryācandramasāvityeke | ni. 12-1 | iti yāskenoktatvāt | ataḥ pūṣannityukte he poṣakāvaśvināvityuktaṃ bhavati | he poṣakau he nāsatyāsatyarahitau devā devau yuvāṃ śriye śreyase | śastrasya kanyāyāśca lābhāyetyarthaḥ | iṣukṛteva | ivaśabda evārthe | ājidhāvanāyeṣuvacchīghramṛjugāminau [?] kṛtāveva saṃtau sūryāyā etannāmikāyāḥ savituḥ putryāḥ ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ sūryāṃ vahatuṃ rathe dhārayitum | ājimudajayatāmityarthaḥ | yasmādevaṃ tasmādapsu jātāḥ karmasu saṃpāditāḥ kakuhāḥ śastrarūpāḥ stutayo bhūreravicchinnapravāhasya varuṇasya phalapratibandhakapāpanivārakasya yāgasya siddhyarthaṃ tatsaṃbandhinyo vāṃ prati vacyante hotrādibhiḥ | yuvāmeva śastragatamantrairyāgakāle ca stuvantītyarthaḥ | yugā jūrṇeva jīrṇāni yugānīva | ivaśabdaḥ saṃpratyarthaḥ | purātanā yāgakālā yathā tadvadadyatanā apītyarthaḥ | pūrvakāle yathā yuvāmeva stuvanti tadvadidānīmapīti tātparyam ‖*

*(Ai. Brā. 4-7 read with the flat-footed glyph as 7; the second ref's last digit [?]; इवशब्दः संप्रत्यर्थः as printed.)*

### Printed p. 24  (PDF 42)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *nāsatyā* — free from untruth; *pūṣan* — (in the form of the Sun and the Moon) nourishers of the world; *devā* — O Aśvin deities, divine in nature; *śriye* — for glory in the form of śastra-mantras; (and) *sūryāyāḥ* — the daughter of Sūrya; *vahatum* — in order to seat [her] on the chariot and bring [her]; *iṣukṛtā iva* — swiftly like an arrow and straight, (you set out for the contest); *vām* — (such) you, with reference to; *apsu jātāḥ* — accomplished in rites such as sacrifice; *kakuhāḥ* — praises in the form of śastra-mantras; *bhūreḥ* — uninterrupted; *varuṇasya* — (that wards off the sin that obstructs the fruit), for the success of the sacrifice; *jūrṇā iva yugāḥ* [as printed] — just as in former sacrificial times they were recited praising you; *vacyante* — (now too) they are recited.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvin deities, free from untruth, nourishers of the world in the form of the Sun and the Moon, divine in nature: for glory in the form of śastra-mantras, and in order to seat the daughter of Sūrya on your chariot and bring her, you set out for the contest, swift as an arrow and straight. With reference to such as you, the praises in the form of śastra-mantras, accomplished in rites such as sacrifice, for the success of the uninterrupted sacrifice that wards off the sin which obstructs the fruit, are recited now too, just as in former sacrificial times they were recited praising you.

**English Translation (as printed):** Divine Ashwins, in whom is no untruth, (darting) like arrows to acquire glory, and to carry off Surya, to you are addressed the prayers that are recited at holy rites, for (the completion of) the uninterrupted, sin-removing (sacrifice), as ancient sages (offered them).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**पूषन् (*pūṣan*).** This word is used as an epithet of the Aśvin deities. Since they are nourishers of the world, their quality and their work are praised by this epithet. By the very derivation of this word the quality of the god Pūṣan, one of the twelve Ādityas, is also described.

> पूषा — यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत् पूषा भवति ।

> *pūṣā — yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tat pūṣā bhavati |*

(Ni. 12-16) — "because he nourishes with his rays, the Āditya has the name Pūṣan": this is the Niruktakāras' derivation. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 25  (PDF 43)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

> इयं वै पूषा पूषेयं हीदं सर्वं पुष्यति यदिदं किं च ।

> *iyaṃ vai pūṣā pūṣeyaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yadidaṃ kiṃ ca |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-4-2-25, as read) ("This [earth] indeed is Pūṣan; for she nourishes all this, whatever there is.") — it is said that this deity is called Pūṣan because he nourishes everything. A meaning of this kind may refer to Āditya. Or, since as the bearer of oblations he is the cause of the nourishment of all, gods, men and the rest, it may refer to Agni. Or, if Āditya is taken as one of the transformed forms of Agni, there is then no difficulty at all. Even so, if the doubt arises how this epithet is fitting for the Aśvin deities, in answer to it:

> सूर्याचन्द्रमसावित्येके ।

> *sūryācandramasāvityeke |*

(Ni. 12-1) ("Some [say they are] the Sun and the Moon.") — as this sentence of the Nirukta says, there is a view that the Aśvin deities are themselves the Sun and the Moon; therefore this epithet must naturally apply to them. Stating this same derivation,

> पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः ।
> तेनैनमस्तौत्पूषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पञ्चभिः ॥

> *puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ |*
> *tenainamastautpūṣeti bharadvājastu pañcabhiḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-63) ("Thriving, he nourishes the earth, dispelling darkness with his rays; therefore Bharadvāja praised him as Pūṣan in five [verses].") — "destroying darkness, because he nourishes the earth so that it attains growth, he has the name Pūṣan": this sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā too makes known the same intention. Besides,

> त्वं वातैररुणैर्यासि शंगयस्त्वं पूषा विधतः पासि नु त्मना ।

> *tvaṃ vātairaruṇairyāsi śaṃgayastvaṃ pūṣā vidhataḥ pāsi nu tmanā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-6) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You go with the ruddy winds, bringing weal to the household; you, as Pūṣan, protect by yourself the one who worships.")

> त्वमग्ने द्रविणोदा अरंकृते त्वं देवः सविता रत्नधा असि ।
> त्वं भगो नृपते वस्व ईशिषे त्वं पायुर्दमे यस्तेऽविधत् ॥

> *tvamagne draviṇodā araṃkṛte tvaṃ devaḥ savitā ratnadhā asi |*
> *tvaṃ bhago nṛpate vasva īśiṣe tvaṃ pāyurdame yaste 'vidhat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You, Agni, are the giver of wealth to the one who serves; you are god Savitṛ, bestower of treasure; you, as Bhaga, O lord of men, rule over goods; you are the protector in the home of him who has worshipped you.")

In such ṛks the identity of Pūṣan, Bhaga, Savitṛ and Āditya is stated. All the Ādityas have the nature of Agni, and the Aśvin deities have the form of the Ādityas. Therefore the epithet *pūṣan* makes known their being nourishers of the world. Besides,

> तत्कावश्विनौ द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके ।

> *tatkāvaśvinau dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke |*

(Ni. 12-1) ("Who then are the Aśvins? Heaven and Earth, say some.") — since there is a view that they are themselves Heaven and Earth, it can be said that in the form of Heaven and Earth they are nourishers of the world, and therefore this epithet is fitting. Therefore Sāyaṇa too has explained the meaning of this word in the present ṛk as हे पोषक सूर्य (*he poṣaka sūrya*) ("O nourishing Sun") and so on.

**सूर्यायाः वहतुम् (*sūryāyāḥ vahatum*).** सूर्यायाः एतन्नामिकायाः सवितुः पुत्र्याः रथे धारयितुम् (*sūryāyāḥ etannāmikāyāḥ savituḥ putryāḥ rathe dhārayitum*) — explaining the meaning "in order to seat on the chariot the maiden called Sūryā, the daughter of Savitṛ", Sāyaṇa has told the story of this context in this way *(quoted with variants from the bhāṣya on p. 23, as printed: स एतां for स एषां; च चालभेताम्; उषाश्चालभेताम् for उषाश्चाजयताम्; सूर्यः for सूर्यां)*:

> सविता सूर्यो दुहितरं सूर्याख्यां प्रदातुमनाः देवानाहूय सामर्थ्यसमीक्षणाय आजिं परिकल्प्य य इमं जेष्यति स एतां कन्यकामृक्सहस्रक्लृप्तं स्तोत्रं च लभते इत्यकल्पयत् । तमग्निः प्रथममजयत् । तमन्वश्विनावपि जित्वा अग्निं प्रधृष्य ऋक्सहस्रं कन्यकां च चालभेताम् । तत इन्द्र उषाश्चालभेताम् । तौ च तैरग्न्यादिभिः प्रार्थितौ स्वशस्त्रस्य कंचित्कंचिद्भागं तेभ्यः परिकल्प्य सूर्यः स्वरथे अधारयतां इति ।

> *savitā sūryo duhitaraṃ sūryākhyāṃ pradātumanāḥ devānāhūya sāmarthyasamīkṣaṇāya ājiṃ parikalpya ya imaṃ jeṣyati sa etāṃ kanyakāmṛksahasraklṛptaṃ stotraṃ ca labhate ityakalpayat | tamagniḥ prathamamajayat | tamanvaśvināvapi jitvā agniṃ pradhṛṣya ṛksahasraṃ kanyakāṃ ca cālabhetām | tata indra uṣāścālabhetām | tau ca tairagnyādibhiḥ prārthitau svaśastrasya kaṃcitkaṃcidbhāgaṃ tebhyaḥ parikalpya sūryaḥ svarathe adhārayatāṃ iti |*

Savitṛ, in order to give his daughter Sūryā in marriage, summoned the gods and, to learn their ability, arranged a contest. He announced that he would hand over his daughter, and the śastra measuring a thousand ṛks, to the one who won in it. Then, when Agni won it, the Aśvin deities challenged him and took both for themselves. Afterwards, when Indra and Uṣas too won that contest, being entreated by them and by Agni, they assigned to them too some portion in their śastra and seated Sūryā on their chariot — this is the story he has made known. This same matter was made known earlier in this same part, at Ṛk 1-184-1, when making known the greatness of the Āśvina śastra: quoting the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa's sentences "प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे (*prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe*)" (Ai. 4-7), the story narrated there was made known. In the Ṛksaṃhitā there is a separate sūkta describing the marriage of Sūryā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85; the second digit is the same glyph as the "5" of the headers' "Adhyāya 5"). Before understanding that description it is very necessary to know where and how the nature of the divine maiden, or deity, called Sūryā has been described. In the Bṛhaddevatā the nature of Sūryā is made known thus:

> तस्य मुख्यतमौ देवावश्विनौ सूर्यमाश्रितौ ।
> वृषाकपायी सूर्योषाः सूर्यस्यैव तु पत्नयः ॥
> अमुतोऽर्वाङ् निवर्तन्ते प्रतिलोमास्तदाश्रयाः ।
> पुरोदयात्तामुषसं सूर्यां मध्यंदिने स्थिते ॥
> वृषाकपायीं सूर्यस्य तामेवाहुस्तु निम्रुचि ।
> तस्याश्रये सरण्यूश्च भगः पूषा वृषाकपिः ॥

> *tasya mukhyatamau devāvaśvinau sūryamāśritau |*
> *vṛṣākapāyī sūryoṣāḥ sūryasyaiva tu patnayaḥ ‖*
> *amuto 'rvāṅ nivartante pratilomāstadāśrayāḥ |*
> *purodayāttāmuṣasaṃ sūryāṃ madhyaṃdine sthite ‖*
> *vṛṣākapāyīṃ sūryasya tāmevāhustu nimruci |*
> *tasyāśraye saraṇyūśca bhagaḥ pūṣā vṛṣākapiḥ ‖*

(Bṛhadde. 2[?]. 8 to 10; in अमुतोऽर्वाङ् the final consonant is [?]) ("Of him [the Sun] the two foremost gods, the Aśvins, are dependent on the Sun; Vṛṣākapāyī, Sūryā and Uṣas are the Sun's wives. Turning back from yonder towards here, in reverse order, they depend on him: before his rising [they call] her Uṣas, Sūryā when he stands at midday, and Vṛṣākapāyī that same one at the Sun's setting. In his shelter are Saraṇyū, Bhaga, Pūṣan and Vṛṣākapi.")

Both Aśvin deities are deities connected with the Sun. Vṛṣākapāyī, Sūryā and Uṣas — these three are the Sun's wives. Belonging to the antarikṣa-world, they, having obtained connection with the Sun, of this world *(continues on the next page)*

… turn back facing [it]. One and the same deity, in three forms, bears the name Uṣas before sunrise, Sūryā at midday, and Vṛṣākapāyī at the time of sunset — having said this, [the Bṛhaddevatā], when again making known the matter of the Sūryā-sūkta, describes it in this way:

> सावित्री चैव सूर्या च स्यैव पत्नी विवस्वतः ।
> स्तुता वृषाकपायीति उषा इति च योच्यते ।
> उषा एषा त्रिधात्मानं विभज्य प्रैति गोपतिम् ॥
> उषाः पुरोदयाद्भूत्वा सूर्या मध्यंदिने स्थिते ।
> भूत्वा वृषाकपायी च दिनान्तेष्ववगच्छति ॥

> *sāvitrī caiva sūryā ca syaiva patnī vivasvataḥ |*
> *stutā vṛṣākapāyīti uṣā iti ca yocyate |*
> *uṣā eṣā tridhātmānaṃ vibhajya praiti gopatim ‖*
> *uṣāḥ purodayādbhūtvā sūryā madhyaṃdine sthite |*
> *bhūtvā vṛṣākapāyī ca dinānteṣvavagacchati ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 7. 119 to 121; स्यैव as printed.) ("Sāvitrī and Sūryā [are] the wife of Vivasvat; she is praised as Vṛṣākapāyī, and she who is called Uṣas — this Uṣas, dividing herself threefold, goes to the lord of rays: having become Uṣas before his rising, Sūryā when he stands at midday, and Vṛṣākapāyī, she goes down at the ends of the days.")

Sāvitrī and Sūryā — both of these are wives of Vivasvān. Making known once more what was said before, that this same Sūryā is also called Vṛṣākapāyī and Uṣas, it praises the matter describing the marriage of Sūryā and the distinction of the Sūryā-sūkta. Thus, where there is a description of the maiden called Sūryā, it is necessary to know what her connection with the Sun is and what is meant by "she chose the Aśvin deities". In the ṛks quoted below from the Sūryā-sūkta, Sūryā's joining the Aśvin deities for marriage is described.

> यदश्विना पृच्छमानावयातं त्रिचक्रेण वहतुं सूर्यायाः ।
> विश्वे देवा अनु तद्वामजानन् पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा ॥

> *yadaśvinā pṛcchamānāvayātaṃ tricakreṇa vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ |*
> *viśve devā anu tadvāmajānan putraḥ pitarāvavṛṇīta pūṣā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 85. 14) — in this ṛk, "O Aśvin deities, when you came in your three-wheeled chariot to take Sūryā's hand, all the gods approved your marriage; and Pūṣan, your son, chose you as his parents" — the very words वहतुं सूर्यायाः (*vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ*) used in the present ṛk are used. Besides,

> स्तोमा आसन्प्रतिधयः कुरीरं छन्द ओपशः ।
> सूर्याया अश्विना वराग्निरासीत्पुरोगवः ॥

> *stomā āsanpratidhayaḥ kurīraṃ chanda opaśaḥ |*
> *sūryāyā aśvinā varāgnirāsītpurogavaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 85. 8) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The praises were the cross-pieces, the metre the head-ornament and plait; the Aśvins were Sūryā's wooers, Agni was the one who went before.")

> यदयातं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप ।
> क्वैकं चक्रं वामासीत्क्व देष्ट्राय तस्थथुः ॥

> *yadayātaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryāmupa |*
> *kvaikaṃ cakraṃ vāmāsītkva deṣṭrāya tasthathuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 85. 15) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When you came, lords of beauty, to Sūryā for the wooing, where was the one wheel of yours? Where did you stand for the giving?") — in these ṛks too the same description is found. Besides, *(continues on the next page)*
