#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः ।
> मृगाणां न हेतयो यंति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमाया अभि द्यून् ॥ ४ ॥

> *asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyāmatyo na yaṃsadyakṣabhṛdvicetāḥ |*
> *mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yaṃti cemā bṛhaspaterahimāyā abhi dyūn ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्य । श्लोकः । दिवि । ईयते । पृथिव्यां । अत्यः । न । यंसत् । यक्षऽभृत् । विऽचेताः ।
> मृगाणां । न । हेतयः । यंति । च । इमाः । बृहस्पतेः । अहिऽमायान् । अभि । द्यून् ॥ ४ ॥

> *asya | ślokaḥ | divi | īyate | pṛthivyāṃ | atyaḥ | na | yaṃsat | yakṣa 'bhṛt | vi 'cetāḥ |*
> *mṛgāṇāṃ | na | hetayaḥ | yaṃti | ca | imāḥ | bṛhaspateḥ | ahi 'māyān | abhi | dyūn ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed. Continues on p. 317 with the Pratipadārtha.)*

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati's fame spreads over heaven and earth; he grants fruit; his weapons, like hunters' missiles, go against Vṛtra and other demons day by day.

> अस्य बृहस्पतेः श्लोकः स्तुत्यात्मिका कीर्तिर्गर्जितना[?]ग्वा दिवि द्योतमाने द्युलोके पृथिव्यां ईयते । गच्छति । व्याप्नोति । यो बृहस्पतिरत्यो नातनशील [?] आदित्य इव यक्षभृत् पूजितं हविरादिकं दधानो विचेताः विविधं चेतयिता प्राणिनां विशिष्टप्रज्ञायुक्तो वा यंसत् नियच्छति फलं । किंच मृगाणां हंतुमिष्यतां हेतयो नायुधानीवास्य बृहस्पतेरिमा हेतयो हिंस्राण्यायुधानि यंति । गच्छंति च ॥ चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निघातः ॥ अहिमायानागत्य हंत्र्योऽंतरिक्षचारिण्यो वा माया येषां वृत्रादीनां तानसुरान् द्यून् दिवसान् ॥ कालाध्वनोः । पा. २-३-५ । इति द्वितीया ॥ तान्यायुधान्यभि लक्षयंति च । उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥

> *asya bṛhaspateḥ ślokaḥ stutyātmikā kīrtirgarjitanā[?]gvā divi dyotamāne dyuloke pṛthivyāṃ īyate | gacchati | vyāpnoti | yo bṛhaspatiratyo nātanaśīla [?] āditya iva yakṣabhṛt pūjitaṃ havirādikaṃ dadhāno vicetāḥ vividhaṃ cetayitā prāṇināṃ viśiṣṭaprajñāyukto vā yaṃsat niyacchati phalaṃ | kiṃca mṛgāṇāṃ haṃtumiṣyatāṃ hetayo nāyudhānīvāsya bṛhaspaterimā hetayo hiṃsrāṇyāyudhāni yaṃti | gacchaṃti ca ‖ cavāyoge prathameti na nighātaḥ ‖ ahimāyānāgatya haṃtryo 'ṃtarikṣacāriṇyo vā māyā yeṣāṃ vṛtrādīnāṃ tānasurān dyūn divasān ‖ kālādhvanoḥ | pā. 2-3-5 | iti dvitīyā ‖ tānyāyudhānyabhi lakṣayaṃti ca | upasargaśruteryogyakriyādhyāhāraḥ ‖*

### Printed p. 317 (PDF 337)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 12". Ṛk 4 continued.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** अस्य (*asya*) — of this Bṛhaspati; श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*) — fame in the nature of praise; दिवि (*divi*) — in the shining heaven-world; पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*) — in the earth too; ईयते (*īyate*) — (he) pervades; अत्यो न (*atyo na*) — like the sun who moves (everlastingly); यक्षभृत् (*yakṣabhṛt*) — bearing worshipful oblations; विचेताः (*vicetāḥ*) — endowed with wisdom, or making living beings endowed with consciousness; यंसत् (*yaṃsat*) — gives fruit; मृगाणां (*mṛgāṇāṃ*) — of the hunters of deer; हेतयः न (*hetayaḥ na*) — like (sharp) weapons; बृहस्पतेः (*bṛhaspateḥ*) — of Bṛhaspati; इमाः (*imāḥ*) — these cruel weapons; द्यून् (*dyūn*) — day by day; अहिमायान् अभि (*ahimāyān abhi*) — aiming at the deceitful asuras; यंति च (*yaṃti ca*) — go in pursuit of them.

**Bhāvārtha.** Bṛhaspati's fame, in the nature of praise, pervades the shining heaven-world and the earth. Like the sun that moves everlastingly, he bears worshipful oblations and, being endowed with wisdom, gives fruits. Like the sharp weapons of hunters of deer, Bṛhaspati's cruel weapons go day by day in pursuit of the deceitful asuras, aiming at them, and strike them down.

**English Translation (as printed):** The glory of this Brihaspati spreads through heaven and earth like the sun : receiving worship, and giving intelligence, he bestows (the rewards of sacrifice) ; like the weapons of the hunters, so these (weapons) of Brihas-pati fall daily upon the workers of guile· [sic, final mark]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** In this ṛk the author describes Bṛhaspati's fame as pervading earth and the heaven-world, his bearing of oblations, and his destroying with his weapons enemies, asuras and other evil ones. As an illustration of this matter, I give here the 6th maṇḍala's 73rd sūkta (numerals read from the strip), which describes Bṛhaspati's qualities just mentioned very well —

> यो अद्रिभित् प्रथमजा ऋतावा बृहस्पतिरांगिरसो हविष्मान् ।
> द्विबर्हजा प्राघर्मसत् पिता न आ रोदसी वृषभो रोरवीति ॥

> *yo adribhit prathamajā ṛtāvā bṛhaspatirāṃgiraso haviṣmān |*
> *dvibarhajā prāgharmasat pitā na ā rodasī vṛṣabho roravīti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-73-1) *(numeral agrees with the numerals file)*

### Printed p. 318 (PDF 338)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 190".)*

(The Special Topics continue.) "This Bṛhaspati breaks the mountains into pieces; the first-born of Prajāpati (Brahmā); one devoted to truth; of the line of the ṛṣi Aṅgiras; one who accepts the oblation, or who gives it to the gods; who can cross the two worlds (earth and heaven); who dwells in the shining place of light; who is like a father to us; who makes the rain pour; who thunders in heaven and earth (like a bull)."

> जनाय चिद्य ईवत उ लोकं बृहस्पतिर्देवहूतौ चकार ।
> घ्नन् वृत्राणि वि पुरो दर्दरीति जयंछ्त्रूरमित्रान् पृत्सु साहन् ॥ [?]

> *janāya cidya īvata u lokaṃ bṛhaspatirdevahūtau cakāra |*
> *ghnan vṛtrāṇi vi puro dardarīti jayaṃchtrūramitrān pṛtsu sāhan ‖ [?]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-73-2) *(numeral agrees with the file; 'jayaṃ… śatrūr' printed with a mark above the conjunct, reading doubtful)*

"This Bṛhaspati, called like a god, makes an excellent world for the sacrificer (the man) who praises him; he destroys obstacles and enemies. He conquers in battle the asuras and others who are not friends and demolishes their cities."

> बृहस्पतिः समजयद्वसूनि महो व्रजान् गोमतो देव एषः ।
> अपः सिषासन्त्स्व१रप्रतीतो बृहस्पतिर्हन्त्यमित्रमर्कैः ॥

> *bṛhaspatiḥ samajayadvasūni maho vrajān gomato deva eṣaḥ |*
> *apaḥ siṣāsantsva1rapratīto bṛhaspatirhantyamitramarkaiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-72-3) *(agrees with the file; the 'svar' syllable is printed with the digit 1 as shown)*

"This Bṛhaspati has won the wealth of enemies, and has subdued wide pastures and cow-herds; in order to obtain the waters of the cloud-region he destroys, with excellent praises, enemies such as Vṛtra who are in heaven (the atmosphere). In the sūkta cited above, all the chief qualities of Bṛhaspati are praised in detail."

**अहिमायान् (*ahimāyān*)** — आगत्य हंत्र्यः अंतरिक्षचारिण्यो वा माया येषां वृत्रादीनां तानसुरान् (*āgatya haṃtryaḥ aṃtarikṣacāriṇyo vā māyā yeṣāṃ vṛtrādīnāṃ tānasurān*) | (so printed; 'āgatya' as it looks). The Bhāṣyakāra explains the word *ahimāyān* as: asuras such as Vṛtra who come running or pursuing and kill by *māyā*, i.e. by crooked means, or who, moving in the atmosphere, cause trouble by *māyā* and the like. Though the word *ahimāya* is recited in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-7, 6-52-15, 10-63-4 (agree with the file), there, because it is used of gods, the meaning is explained differently.

Since this ṛk mentions Bṛhaspati's weapons, a little discussion on that subject is necessary. As said in the ṛk quoted above — बृहस्पतिर्हंत्यमित्रमर्कैः (*bṛhaspatirhaṃtyamitramarkaiḥ*) — "Bṛhaspati destroys enemies by mantras themselves"; for this statement there is support elsewhere too, in the Ṛgveda and other texts.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** **ईयते (*īyate*)** — root ईज् गतौ (*īj gatau*) (as it looks); *ātmanepada* since the *j* is an *it*; *laṭ* third person singular in another form; the *nighāta* accent comes because it stands before an *atiṅanta* word (as it looks). **अत्यः (*atyaḥ*)** — root अत सातत्यगमने (*ata sātatyagamane*); suffix *kyap*; being *pit*, initial-acute. **यक्षभृत् (*yakṣabhṛt*)** — यक्षं बिभर्ति (*yakṣaṃ bibharti*); root भृञ् भरणे (*bhṛñ bharaṇe*); suffix *kvip*; the accent of the stem of the final member (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*). **विचेताः (*vicetāḥ*)** — विविधं चेतः यस्य सः (*vividhaṃ cetaḥ yasya saḥ*); by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*) the accent of the first member remains; nominative singular in another form. **यंति (*yaṃti*)** — root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); *laṭ* third plural, suffix *jhi*; *anta* in place of *jh* by झोऽन्तः (*jho 'ntaḥ*); *yaṇ* for the *i* of the root; because च (*ca*) follows, the *nighāta* is barred by चवायोगे प्रथमा (*cavāyoge prathamā*); initial-acute by the accent of the suffix. **द्यून् (*dyūn*)** — since the days are connected without break with the action, the second case by कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे (*kālādhvanoratyantasaṃyoge*) (Pā. Sū. 2-3-5; agrees with the file). **अभि (*abhi*)** — an *upasarga*; the discussion on उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे (*upasargāḥ kriyāyoge*) begins: the name *upasarga* arises only in connection with a verb, so that even where no verb is stated here… *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

*(Header: "Maṃ. [blank]. A. 24. Sū. 190": the Maṇḍala numeral is not printed [sic]. Ṛk 4: grammar concluded; Ṛk 5: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya.)*

… because an upasarga is present, a suitable verb must be supplied (*adhyāhāra*); therefore the verb-word लक्षयन्ति (*lakṣayanti*) is understood here. *(End of the upasarga discussion and of Ṛk 4; a short rule closes it.)*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> ये त्वा देवोऽस्रिकं मन्यमानाः पापा भद्रमुपजीवन्ति पज्राः ।
> न दूढ्ये[?]ऽनु ददासि वामं बृहस्पते चयस इत्पियारुं ॥

> *ye tvā devo 'srikaṃ manyamānāḥ pāpā bhadramupajīvanti pajrāḥ |*
> *na dūḍhye[?] 'nu dadāsi vāmaṃ bṛhaspate cayasa itpiyāruṃ ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ये । त्वा । देव । उस्रिकं । मन्यमानाः । पापाः । भद्रं । उपऽजीवन्ति । पज्राः ।
> न । दुःऽढ्ये[?] । अनु । ददासि । वामं । बृहस्पते । चयसे । इत् । पियारुं ॥ ५ ॥

> *ye | tvā | deva | usrikaṃ | manyamānāḥ | pāpāḥ | bhadraṃ | upa 'jīvanti | pajrāḥ |*
> *na | duḥ 'ḍhye[?] | anu | dadāsi | vāmaṃ | bṛhaspate | cayase | it | piyāruṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati gives no desired wealth to evil-minded sinners who regard him as a worn-out cow, but he favours the sacrificer who offers soma, or destroys the enemy of the gods.

> हे देव बृहस्पते ये पापाः पापबुद्धयोऽल्पाः पज्रा हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्तः पापेन जीर्णा वा नरा भद्रं कल्याणं त्वा त्वामुस्रिकं । उस्रियेति गोनाम । कुत्सितामल्पक्षीरोत्स्राविणीं गां जीर्णमनड्वाहं वा मन्यमाना उपजीवन्ति उपेत्य प्राणन्ति । अल्पं याचन्ते इत्यर्थः । दूढ्ये[?] दुर्धिये ॥ वचनव्यत्ययः ॥ दुर्बुद्धिभ्यस्तेभ्यो वामं वननीयं धनं नानु ददासि । अनुकूलं न वितरसि । हे बृहस्पते देव पियारुं सोमपानशीलं सोमेन यष्टारं महाफलरिप्सुं तु चयसे इत् । गच्छस्येवानुगृहीतुं ॥ चय गताविति तस्येदं रूपं ॥ यद्वा । हे बृहस्पते पियारुं हिंसकं ॥ पीयतेर्हिंसाकर्मण इदं रूपं ॥ तं प्राणिहिंसकं चयसे इत् । हंस्येव । बृहस्पते यच्चातयसि देवपीयुमिति निरुक्तं । ४-२५ ॥

> *he deva bṛhaspate ye pāpāḥ pāpabuddhayo 'lpāḥ pajrā havirlakṣaṇānnavantaḥ pāpena jīrṇā vā narā bhadraṃ kalyāṇaṃ tvā tvāmusrikaṃ | usriyeti gonāma | kutsitāmalpakṣīrotsrāviṇīṃ gāṃ jīrṇamanaḍvāhaṃ vā manyamānā upajīvanti upetya prāṇanti | alpaṃ yācante ityarthaḥ | dūḍhye[?] durdhiye ‖ vacanavyatyayaḥ ‖ durbuddhibhyastebhyo vāmaṃ vananīyaṃ dhanaṃ nānu dadāsi | anukūlaṃ na vitarasi | he bṛhaspate deva piyāruṃ somapānaśīlaṃ somena yaṣṭāraṃ mahāphalaripsuṃ tu cayase it | gacchasyevānugṛhītuṃ ‖ caya gatāviti tasyedaṃ rūpaṃ ‖ yadvā | he bṛhaspate piyāruṃ hiṃsakaṃ ‖ pīyaterhiṃsākarmaṇa idaṃ rūpaṃ ‖ taṃ prāṇihiṃsakaṃ cayase it | haṃsyeva | bṛhaspate yaccātayasi devapīyumiti niruktaṃ | 4-25 ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** देव (*deva*) — O worshipful Bṛhaspati; ये पापाः (*ye pāpāḥ*) — which sinners; पज्राः (*pajrāḥ*) — possessed of food in the form of oblations (हविर्लक्षणान्नयुक्ताः (*havirlakṣaṇānnayuktāḥ*)); भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*) — the auspicious one; त्वा (*tvā*) — you; (not greatly useful) उस्रिकं (*usrikaṃ*) — as an old cow; मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*) — considering; उपजीवन्ति (*upajīvanti*) — live (by approaching you); दूढ्ये (*dūḍhye*)[?] — to those evil-minded sinners; वामं (*vāmaṃ*) — the desired wealth; न अनु ददासि (*na anu dadāsi*) — you do not give, as suits each; *(continued on p. 321)*

### Printed p. 321 (PDF 341)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 12." Ṛk 5: Pratipadārtha concluded; Bhāvārtha; printed English; Special Topics begun. Signature marks "[21]" and "Vol. 14" stand at the foot.)*

बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*) — O Bṛhaspati; पियारुं (*piyāruṃ*) — him who offers soma and performs the sacrifice; चयसे इत् (*cayase it*) — you certainly favour (positively).

**Bhāvārtha.** O worshipful Bṛhaspati, those sinners who, worn out by sin, regard you, the auspicious one, as an aged cow, as useless and a burden, and live by you: to such evil-minded sinners you give none of the wealth they desire. But the man who offers soma and performs the sacrifice you certainly favour.

**English Translation (as printed):**

Divine Brihaspati, you do not bestow desired (wealth) upon those stupid (men), who, sinful and mean, subsist, considering you, who are auspicious, as an old ox, but you favour him who offers (you) libations.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** In this ṛk the matter is described that Bṛhaspati gives nothing to those who do not praise him, and destroys such harmful men.

> सुनीतिभिर्नयसि त्रायसे जनं यस्तुभ्यं दाशान्न तमंहो अश्नवत् ।
> ब्रह्मद्विषस्तपनो मन्युमीरसि बृहस्पते मह तत्ते महित्वनम् ॥

> *sunītibhirnayasi trāyase janaṃ yastubhyaṃ dāśānna tamaṃho aśnavat |*
> *brahmadviṣastapano manyumīrasi bṛhaspate maha tatte mahitvanam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23-4) *(agrees with the file; the last words are as they look: 'mahi tatte mahitvanaṃ')*

In this ṛk it is said: you lead the man who pleases you (Bṛhaspati) with oblations and the like along the good path and protect him; sins cannot touch him; but those who hate you fall prey to your anger; O Bṛhaspati, is not this your greatness?

**उस्रिकं (*usrikaṃ*)** — उस्रियेति गोनाम । कुत्सिताल्पक्षीरोस्राविणीं गां जीर्णमनड्वाहं वा (*usriyeti gonāma | kutsitālpakṣīrosrāviṇīṃ gāṃ jīrṇamanaḍvāhaṃ vā*) (as printed; 'kṣīro-' as it looks). The word *usriyā* is recited among the names of the cow (Ni. [?]-9: the first numeral is undecided, not in the file); and उस्रियेति गोनाम उस्राविणोऽस्यां भोगाः उस्रेति च (*usriyeti gonāma usrāviṇo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ usreti ca*) (Ni. 4-19; agrees with the file), says Yāska: the cow that gives milk is called *usriyā*, because from such milk the enjoyments and the like arise; it is also called *usrā*. Here, since the word is *usrikaṃ*, the Bhāṣyakāra explains that the word means a cow that gives very little milk or none at all, that is barren, or an old ox unable to do any hard work. Nobody expects any return from such a milkless cow or a bullock unable to work. Likewise sinners, regarding

### Printed p. 322 (PDF 342)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190". Ṛk 5: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begun.)*

… him (Bṛhaspati) as a barren cow or an old ox, and knowing that nothing useful comes from you, do not worship you. To such wicked men you give nothing, that is, none of the wealth they need; and moreover you destroy them: this is the chief purport of the ṛk.

**उपजीवन्ति (*upajīvanti*)** — उपेत्य प्राणन्ति । अल्पं याचन्ते इत्यर्थः (*upetya prāṇanti | alpaṃ yācante ityarthaḥ*): they approach you and ask for hardly anything, do not heed you; this is the sense.

**पज्राः (*pajrāḥ*)** — Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning for this word: हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्तः (*havirlakṣaṇānnavantaḥ*), those having food in the form of oblations; or पापेन जीर्णा वा नराः (*pāpena jīrṇā vā narāḥ*), men who are sinners.

**बृहस्पते चयसे इत् पियारुं (*bṛhaspate cayase it piyāruṃ*)** — on these words Yāska says — बृहस्पते यच्चातयसि देवपीयुमिति (*bṛhaspate yaccātayasi devapīyumiti*) and देवपीयुः पीयतिर्हिंसाकर्मा (*devapīyuḥ pīyatirhiṃsākarmā*) (Ni. 4-25; agrees with the file), that is, *pīyati* is a verb of the sense of killing; from the root *pīyati* the word *piyāru* is formed. Therefore the word means the one who kills, that is, the destroyer of the gods: one who does not worship the gods but desires only his own enjoyment. You, Bṛhaspati, destroy such a destroyer of the gods: so the meaning is explained.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** **उस्रिकम् (*usrikam*)** — the word उस्रिया (*usriyā*); the suffix क (*ka*) in the sense of contempt, then the या (*yā*) at the end is dropped; accent on the last syllable by *vyatyaya*. **मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*)** — root मन ज्ञाने (*mana jñāne*); शानच् (*śānac*) for *laṭ*; श्यन् (*śyan*) as vikaraṇa; being *nit*, the initial-acute by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*) (as it looks). **पापाः (*pāpāḥ*)** — पापं येषामस्ति (*pāpaṃ yeṣāmasti*); the suffix अच् (*ac*) in the sense of possession by अर्शआदिभ्योऽच् (*arśaādibhyo 'c*); the preceding *a* drops by यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*); final-acute by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163; agrees with the file). **उपजीवन्ति (*upajīvanti*)** — root जीव प्राणधारणे (*jīva prāṇadhāraṇe*); *laṭ* third plural in another form; because यत् (*yat*) is in construction there is no *nighāta*; initial-acute by the root's accent; the preverb *upa* takes the low accent by तिङि चोदात्तम् (*tiṅi codāttam*) (as it looks) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-61; agrees with the file). **दूढ्ये (*dūḍhye*)** — [?] दुष्टं ध्यायन्ति इति दुर्धियः (*duṣṭaṃ dhyāyanti iti durdhiyaḥ*); root ध्यै चिन्तायां (*dhyai cintāyāṃ*); the suffix *kvip* by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*); through the force of the word *ca*, *samprasāraṇa*; since ध्यै (*dhyai*) is recited in the *pṛṣodarādi* group the desired form is obtained; by *vyatyaya* the seventh case stands for the fourth. *(Grammar continues on the next page; Ṛk 5 is still open.)*

### Printed p. 323 (PDF 343)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 13" (Aṣṭaka numeral prints like 'ಅ. ವ', as on pp. 285, 295); Varga 13 begins. Ṛk 5: grammar concluded; Ṛk 6: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya.)*

**चयसे (*cayase*)** — root चय गतौ (*caya gatau*); लट् (*laṭ*) second person singular in another form; because इत् (*it*) is in construction there is no *nighāta* accent. **पियारुं (*piyāruṃ*)** — root पीज् (*pīj*) (as it looks); since roots have many senses, it is used here in the sense of killing; the desired form is obtained by an Uṇādi suffix that is *nit*. *(Ṛk 5 ends.)*

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> सुप्रैतुः सूयवसो न पन्था दुर्नियन्तुः परिप्रीतो न मित्रः ।
> अनर्वाणो अभि ये चक्षते नोऽपीवृता अपोर्णुवन्तो अस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

> *supraituḥ sūyavaso na panthā durniyantuḥ pariprīto na mitraḥ |*
> *anarvāṇo abhi ye cakṣate no 'pīvṛtā aporṇuvanto asthuḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सुऽप्रैतुः । सुऽयवसः । न । पन्थाः । दुःऽनियन्तुः । परिऽप्रीतः । न । मित्रः ।
> अनर्वाणः । अभि । ये । चक्षते । नः । अपिऽवृताः । अपिऽऊर्णुवन्तः । अस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

> *su 'praituḥ | su 'yavasaḥ | na | panthāḥ | duḥ 'niyantuḥ | pari 'prītaḥ | na | mitraḥ |*
> *anarvāṇaḥ | abhi | ye | cakṣate | naḥ | api 'vṛtāḥ | api 'ūrṇuvantaḥ | asthuḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati, be pleasant like a good road and a trusted friend; may the sinless who instruct us, though enveloped in ignorance, stand uncovered.

> हे बृहस्पते त्वं सुप्रैतुः सुष्ठु गन्तुर्मनुष्यस्य सूयवसः शोभनान्नस्य पन्था न मार्ग इव सुष्ठु यज्ञमार्गगामिनो सूयवसः पन्था इव । सुखकारी भवेत्यर्थः । किंच दुर्नियन्तुर्दुःखेन नियमितो राज्ञः परिप्रीतः सर्वप्रकारेण सन्तुष्टो द्वेषादिरहितो मित्रो न सुहृन्मन्त्रीव । स यथा दुर्नयान्निवर्तयति तद्वत् त्वमपि तथास्मभ्यं कुर्वित्यर्थः । सखिवदनमार्गान्निवर्त्य[?] मार्गे यज्ञादिरूपे योजयित्वा तत्रापि फलप्रदो भवेत्यर्थः । किंचानर्वाणोऽपापा ये नरा नोऽस्मानभ्याभिमुख्येन चक्षते बोधयन्ति तेऽपीवृता अज्ञानेनावृता अस्य[?]पोर्णुवन्तोऽपगतावरणवन्तो ज्ञानवन्तोऽस्थुः । तिष्ठन्तु । यद्वा । अनर्वाणस्त्वमुप्राप्नुवन्तो येऽस्मद्विरोधिनो नोऽस्मानभि चक्षते अभिवदन्ति निन्दन्ति तेऽपीवृता आच्छादिता रक्षिता अप्यपोर्णुवन्तोऽपगतरक्षणा भवन्ति ॥

> *he bṛhaspate tvaṃ supraituḥ suṣṭhu ganturmanuṣyasya sūyavasaḥ śobhanānnasya panthā na mārga iva suṣṭhu yajñamārgagāmino sūyavasaḥ panthā iva | sukhakārī bhavetyarthaḥ | kiṃca durniyanturduḥkhena niyamito rājñaḥ pariprītaḥ sarvaprakāreṇa santuṣṭo dveṣādirahito mitro na suhṛnmantrīva | sa yathā durnayānnivartayati tadvat tvamapi tathāsmabhyaṃ kurvityarthaḥ | sakhivadanamārgānnivartya[?] mārge yajñādirūpe yojayitvā tatrāpi phalaprado bhavetyarthaḥ | kiṃcānarvāṇo 'pāpā ye narā no 'smānabhyābhimukhyena cakṣate bodhayanti te 'pīvṛtā ajñānenāvṛtā asya[?]porṇuvanto 'pagatāvaraṇavanto jñānavanto 'sthuḥ | tiṣṭhantu | yadvā | anarvāṇastvamuprāpnuvanto ye 'smadvirodhino no 'smānabhi cakṣate abhivadanti nindanti te 'pīvṛtā ācchāditā rakṣitā apyaporṇuvanto 'pagatarakṣaṇā bhavanti ‖*

### Printed p. 324 (PDF 344)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190". Ṛk 6: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** (O Bṛhaspati) सुयवसः (*suyavasaḥ*) — of sacrificial rites and the like that give excellent food; पन्थाः न (*panthāḥ na*) — as a road is pleasant; (and) दुर्नियन्तुः (*durniyantuḥ*) — to the king who restrains the wicked; परिप्रीतः (*pariprītaḥ*) — one who is fully affectionate; मित्रः न (*mitraḥ na*) — as a minister, being a good friend, is pleasant; सुप्रैतुः (*supraituḥ*) — to the sacrificer who walks in the good path and performs the rites, be a giver of happiness; ये (*ye*) — those who (printed यो (*yo*) in the Saṃhitā, Pada and Pratipadārtha as it looks); अनर्वाणः (*anarvāṇaḥ*) — being free of sin; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; अभि चक्षते (*abhi cakṣate*) — give instruction so that we become walkers in the good path; अपीवृताः (*apīvṛtāḥ*) — even though covered by ignorance; अपोर्णुवन्तः (*aporṇuvantaḥ*) — freed from the covering of ignorance; अस्थुः (*asthuḥ*) — let them be.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Bṛhaspati, be pleasant to the sacrificer who walks in the good path, as the road of sacrificial rites that give excellent food is pleasant, and as a minister who is a good friend and fully affectionate is pleasant to a king who restrains the wicked. And those who, being free from sin, teach us the good path: if they are covered by ignorance, remove their covering and make them wise. *(The Bhāvārtha runs over to the second strip of the page.)*

**English Translation (as printed):**

Be a (pleasant) way to him who goes well and makes good offerings, like the affectionate friend of (a ruler who) restrains the bad, and may those sinless men who instruct us, although yet enveloped (by ignorance), stand extricated from their covering· [sic: stray point after "covering"].

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** The matter stated in this ṛk is not clear, or it is entangled. Nevertheless the Bhāṣyakāra has explained it so that some sense is obtained; the sense given for the second half does not fit well.

**सुप्रैतुः (*supraituḥ*)** — सुष्ठु गन्तुर्मनुष्यस्य (*suṣṭhu ganturmanuṣyasya*): of the man who is a promoter of the good path; that is, here, of the man who worships Bṛhaspati with hymns and the like: this is the intention.

**सुयवसः (*suyavasaḥ*)** — the word *yuva* is recited among the names of food (Nighaṇṭu; the word printed as it looks 'paṭhita'). Therefore the meaning is: one who gives excellent food. Since food is obtained through sacrifices and the like, **यज्ञमार्गगामिनः (*yajñamārgagāminaḥ*)** *(continued on p. 325)*

### Printed p. 325 (PDF 345)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 13". Ṛk 6: Special Topics continued.)*

**पन्था इव (*panthā iva*)** — like the good path that one wishes to follow when desiring to perform sacrifices and the like, that is, like a pleasant road: this is the intention.

**दुर्नियन्तुः (*durniyantuḥ*)** — दुःखेन नियमितुः । अथवा दुर्नयान्निवर्तयति इति दुर्नियन्ता तस्य (*duḥkhena niyamituḥ | athavā durnayānnivartayati iti durniyantā tasya*): the king who rules with great difficulty, or who punishes those who go by evil paths and makes them walk in the good path: so the Bhāṣyakāra explains.

**परिप्रीतः मित्रः न (*pariprītaḥ mitraḥ na*)** — the sense is: like a friend who is satisfied in every way, that is, who has true love and trust. Although there are in this ṛk no words denoting a king or a minister, the Bhāṣyakāra explains the words दुर्नियन्तुः (*durniyantuḥ*) and मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) as having the senses king and minister. Or, without giving the senses king, minister and so on, one may take the words दुर्नियन्तुः मित्रो न (*durniyantuḥ mitro na*) to mean: as a friend who wishes him well brings back to the road one who has strayed from the good path.

**अनर्वाणः (*anarvāṇaḥ*)** — the Bhāṣyakāra explains this word as अपापाः (*apāpāḥ*), those free from sin. How the word has this sense he does not explain. Yāska in the Nirukta says:

अनर्वा प्रत्यृतोऽन्यस्मिन् (*anarvā pratyṛto 'nyasmin*) (as it looks) (Ni. 6-23; agrees with the file), and यः अन्यस्मिन् न आश्रितो भवति स्वप्रधान एव सः अनर्वा इत्युच्यते (*yaḥ anyasmin na āśrito bhavati svapradhāna eva saḥ anarvā ityucyate*) (as printed) — the man who takes no refuge in others but is himself the chief, that is, independent, is called *anarvā*. Hence, according to the Nirukta, the plural अनर्वाणः (*anarvāṇaḥ*) means independent men, those not subject to another.

**अपीवृताः, अपोर्णुवन्तः (*apīvṛtāḥ, aporṇuvantaḥ*)** — Sāyaṇa explains these words in order as अज्ञानेनावृताः (*ajñānenāvṛtāḥ*) and अपगतावरणवन्तः (*apagatāvaraṇavantaḥ*): that is, अपीवृताः (*apīvṛtāḥ*) means those covered by ignorance (overtaken by it), blinded by ignorance, without discernment; अपोर्णुवन्तः (*aporṇuvantaḥ*) means those freed from the covering of ignorance, without ignorance, the wise. There is doubt whether both these senses are right for these words. The Bhāṣyakāra himself, unable to explain the sense of the words properly, has given another kind of sense: यद्वा । अनर्वाणस्त्वमुप्राप्नुवन्तो येऽस्मद्विरोधिनो नोऽस्मानभि चक्षते अभिवदन्ति निन्दन्ति तेऽपीवृता आच्छादिता रक्षिता अप्यपोर्णुवन्तोऽपगतरक्षणा भवन्ति (*yadvā | anarvāṇastvamuprāpnuvanto ye 'smadvirodhino no 'smānabhi cakṣate abhivadanti nindanti te 'pīvṛtā ācchāditā rakṣitā apyaporṇuvanto 'pagatarakṣaṇā bhavanti*). That is: those of our adversaries who, taking refuge in you, revile us, even if they have their own protection, let that protection not remain with them (so he has said). This sense too is not quite fitting. In both these senses there is doubt, *(the passage continues on the next page; Ṛk 6 is still open.)*

### Printed p. 326 (PDF 346)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 190". Ṛk 6: Special Topics concluded; grammar; Ṛk 7: Saṃhitā begun.)*

*(Continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 6, from p. 325:)* …room for doubt remains. How? That those who are themselves covered by ignorance should give instruction to others does not seem right. Likewise the statement in the second sense, "even if those who do not take refuge in you have protection", is not right either, because for those who do not take refuge in you there is no protection at all. That being so, to say "destroy the protection they have" is also devoid of reason. In short, the correct sense of this ṛk, and in it especially the sense of the second half, remains clouded with doubt.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** Words treated: सुप्रैतुः (*supraituḥ*) (root इण् (*iṇ*), tṛn suffix; vṛddhi after *pra* by a sūtra beginning एत्येधत्यूठ्सु (*etyedhatyūṭhsu*) as it looks, no number printed; genitive singular), सुयवसः (*suyavasaḥ*) (bahuvrīhi; initial acute on the last member by क्रत्वादयश्च (*kratvādayaśca*), Pā. Sū. 6-2-118), अनर्वाणः (*anarvāṇaḥ*) (nañ-bahuvrīhi; no *tṛ* ending, because अर्वणस्त्रसावनञः (*arvaṇastrasāvanañaḥ*) forbids it when nañ precedes; final acute by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*), Pā. Sū. 6-2-172), चक्षते (*cakṣate*) (root चक्षिङ् (*cakṣiṅ*) in the sense of speaking, adādi; luk of śap; आत्मनेपदेष्वनतः (*ātmanepadeṣvanataḥ*); no nighāta accent because of the relative word; root accent), अपीवृताः (*apīvṛtāḥ*) (root वृञ् (*vṛñ*); suffix kta; no guṇa since it is kit; lengthening of the preceding member by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*), Pā. Sū. 6-3-139 as printed; गतिरनन्तरः (*gatiranantaraḥ*), Pā. Sū. 6-2-49, gives the prakṛti accent), अस्थुः (*asthuḥ*) (root ष्ठा (*ṣṭhā*); luṅ in the Veda; luk of sic by a sūtra beginning गातिस्थाघुपा (*gātisthāghupā*) …, Pā. Sū. 2-4-77; आतः (*ātaḥ*), Pā. Sū. 3-4-410 as printed, gives the ending उस् (*us*) with pūrvarūpa; nighāta accent because it follows a verb form).

### Printed p. 327 (PDF 347)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 13". Ṛk 7: Saṃhitā concluded, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha begun.)*

> स विद्वा उभयं चष्टे अन्तर्बृहस्पतिस्तर आपश्च गृध्रः ॥ ७ ॥

> *sa vidvā ubhayaṃ caṣṭe antarbṛhaspatistara āpaśca gṛdhraḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सं । यं । स्तुभः । अवनयः । न । यन्ति । समुद्रं । न । स्रवतः । रोधःऽचक्राः ।
> सः । विद्वान् । उभयं । चष्टे । अन्तः । बृहस्पतिः । तरः । आपः । च । गृध्रः ॥ ७ ॥

> *saṃ | yaṃ | stubhaḥ | avanayaḥ | na | yanti | samudraṃ | na | sravataḥ | rodhaḥ 'cakrāḥ |*
> *saḥ | vidvān | ubhayaṃ | caṣṭe | antaḥ | bṛhaspatiḥ | taraḥ | āpaḥ | ca | gṛdhraḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* As men go round their master and rivers run to the sea, so praises go to Bṛhaspati, who, standing in the midst, brings the increase of water.

> सं यं स्तुभ इत्येषा बार्हस्पत्ये पशौ पुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । सं यं स्तुभोऽवनयो न यन्त्येवा पित्रे । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥

> *saṃ yaṃ stubha ityeṣā bārhaspatye paśau puroḍāśasya yājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | saṃ yaṃ stubho 'vanayo na yantyevā pitre | ā. 3-7 | iti ‖*

> यं बृहस्पतिं स्तुभः स्तोत्राण्यवनयो न सर्वा अवनयो भूमयो मनुष्या यथा स्वामिनं कर्म प्रति वा सं यन्ति सङ्गच्छन्ति तद्वत् तथा समुद्रं रोधचक्राः । नदीनाम्नैतत् । रोधनशीलानि चक्राणि यासु तास्तादृश्यः कूलं क्रममाणा वा स्रवतः स्रवन्त्यो नद्यो यथा यन्ति तद्वत् सर्वा अपि स्तुतयो यमेव प्राप्नुवन्ति गृध्रो गर्धनशीलो वृष्टिमाकाङ्क्षमाणः स बृहस्पतिर्विद्वान् वक्ष्यमाणाभिज्ञस्तरस्तरणं जलाभिवृद्धिमापः उदकानि चोभयमन्तर्मध्ये स्थित्वा चष्टे पश्यति । करोतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *yaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ stubhaḥ stotrāṇyavanayo na sarvā avanayo bhūmayo manuṣyā yathā svāminaṃ karma prati vā saṃ yanti saṅgacchanti tadvat tathā samudraṃ rodhacakrāḥ | nadīnāmnaitat | rodhanaśīlāni cakrāṇi yāsu tāstādṛśyaḥ kūlaṃ kramamāṇā vā sravataḥ sravantyo nadyo yathā yanti tadvat sarvā api stutayo yameva prāpnuvanti gṛdhro gardhanaśīlo vṛṣṭimākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ sa bṛhaspatirvidvān vakṣyamāṇābhijñastarastaraṇaṃ jalābhivṛddhimāpaḥ udakāni cobhayamantarmadhye sthitvā caṣṭe paśyati | karotītyarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** अवनयः न (*avanayaḥ na*) — as men go round their sacrificers (and); रोधचक्राः (*rodhacakrāḥ*) — the rivers that flow between two banks; समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*) — toward the ocean; स्रवतः (*sravataḥ*) — as they flow (following one course alone); स्तुभः (*stubhaḥ*) — all the praises as well; यं (*yaṃ*) — whichever Bṛhaspati; सं यन्ति (*saṃ yanti*) — go and surround and join; सः बृहस्पतिः (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*) — that Bṛhaspati; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — being wise; गृध्रः (*gṛdhraḥ*) — and desirous of water; अन्तः (*antaḥ*) — standing in the middle; तरः (*taraḥ*) — the increase of water, or the manner of crossing; आपः (*āpaḥ*) — and the water; उभयं च (*ubhayaṃ ca*) — both these matters; चष्टे (*caṣṭe*) — contemplates (and brings about the increase of water).

**Bhāvārtha.** Just as men go round their sacrificers, and as rivers flowing between two banks run toward the ocean following one course, all praises go to whichever Bṛhaspati and surround him; that Bṛhaspati, being wise and desirous of water, *(the Bhāvārtha runs over to p. 328)*

### Printed p. 328 (PDF 348)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 190". Ṛk 7: Bhāvārtha concluded, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

*(Bhāvārtha, concluded:)* standing in the middle, contemplates the manner of crossing the lack of water and the water, and brings about the increase of water.

**English Translation (as printed):**

To whom praises (necessarily) proceed, as men (assemble round a master); as rivers, rolling between their banks, flow to the ocean : that wise Brihaspati, greedy (after rain), and stationary in the midst, contemplates both (the ferry and the water),

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra prescribes that this ṛk be used as the yājyā mantra in the purodāśa oblation of the animal sacrifice offered to Bṛhaspati, in the sūtra सं यं स्तुभोऽवनयो न यन्त्येवा पित्रे (*saṃ yaṃ stubho 'vanayo na yantyevā pitre*) (as quoted in the bhāṣya).

The sense of this ṛk too is not clear: in the first half the words अवनयो न (*avanayo na*) and in the second half the words उभयं (*ubhayaṃ*), अन्तः (*antaḥ*), तरः (*taraḥ*), आपः (*āpaḥ*) are not fitted well with the meaning.

**स्तुभः (*stubhaḥ*)** — स्तोभतीति स्तुतिः (*stobhatīti stutiḥ*): that which praises is *stuti*. The word स्तोभति (*stobhati*) is recited among the names of the verb "to worship" (Ni. 3-19; agrees with the file). Hence *stubhaḥ* means hymns of praise.

**अवनयः (*avanayaḥ*)** — भूमयो मनुष्याः (*bhūmayo manuṣyāḥ*) (men of the earth). The word *avanayaḥ* is recited among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5, as it looks), of rivers (Ni. 2-24; agrees with the file) and of fingers (Ni. 3-9; agrees with the file). Here the word *avani* is used in the sense of the earth, that is, men who dwell on the earth. For the words *avanayo na* in this ṛk Sāyaṇa's explanation is: as men approach their sacrificer. How this sense is possible for these words must be conjectured and made to fit. It is not possible to know for certain what the ṛṣi intended.

**रोधचक्राः (*rodhacakrāḥ*)** — this word is recited among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24). The constituent senses of the word are of three kinds: from the two roots रुधिर् आवरणे (*rudhir āvaraṇe*) and डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*) the words *rodha* and *cakra* are formed, and together they make *rodhacakra*.

(1) रोधस्य निरोधस्य चक्रं करणं कृतिरासां विद्यते इति रोधचक्राः । नद्यो वृष्ट्या प्राणिनां स्वैरसञ्चरणनिरोधकारिण्यः (*rodhasya nirodhasya cakraṃ karaṇaṃ kṛtirāsāṃ vidyate iti rodhacakrāḥ | nadyo vṛṣṭyā prāṇināṃ svairasañcaraṇanirodhakāriṇyaḥ*) — the rivers, by the water they hold, cause an obstruction to the movement of living beings; that is, living beings cannot cross a river full of flowing water. Hence rivers are called *rodhacakrāḥ*.

(2) यद्वा । रोधः तीरं तस्य करणं निर्माणमासां विद्यते तीरवत्यो हि नद्यः । सकारलोपश्छान्दसः (*yadvā | rodhaḥ tīraṃ tasya karaṇaṃ nirmāṇamāsāṃ vidyate tīravatyo hi nadyaḥ | sakāralopaśchāndasaḥ*) — or: *rodha* means a bank, shore; when rivers flow they build banks on both their sides. Hence, because they flow between two banks, rivers are called *rodhacakrāḥ*. *(Ṛk 7 remains open: the Special Topics continue on p. 329.)*

### Printed p. 329 (PDF 349)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 13". Ṛk 7: Special Topics continued; grammar begun.)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 7, continued — the third derivation of रोधचक्राः (*rodhacakrāḥ*):)*

(3) यद्वा । रुध्यतेऽनेन जलप्रवाह इति रोधः शब्दः करणं निर्माणमासां विद्यते । (*yadvā | rudhyate 'nena jalapravāha iti rodhaḥ śabdaḥ karaṇaṃ nirmāṇamāsāṃ vidyate |*) — or: the current of water flowing in a river is checked, so that it does not overflow and cease to flow, by the embankments on its sides; rivers build such embankments for themselves, and hence are called रोधचक्राः (*rodhacakrāḥ*).

In the ṛk before us, the simile in समुद्रं न स्रवतः रोधचक्राः (*samudraṃ na sravataḥ rodhacakrāḥ*) — "as the flowing rivers (reach) the ocean, so the hymns we make reach Bṛhaspati" — is quite fitting.

गृध्रः (*gṛdhraḥ*) — गर्धनशीलो वृष्टिमाकाङ्क्षमाणः सः बृहस्पतिः (*gardhanaśīlo vṛṣṭimākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*): Bṛhaspati, who desires rain. For the word गृध्रस्य (*gṛdhrasya*) in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-124-8 Sāyaṇa explains रसानभिकाङ्क्षतः (*rasānabhikāṅkṣataḥ*) (of one who desires the water), and for गृध्राः (*gṛdhrāḥ*) in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-88-4 he explains जलाभिकाङ्क्षायुक्तान् (*jalābhikāṅkṣāyuktān*) (those desirous of water).

तरः (*taraḥ*) — तरणं जलाभिवृद्धिं (*taraṇaṃ jalābhivṛddhiṃ*): the increase of water, says the bhāṣyakāra. *Taraṇa* means crossing; "Ferry" (printed in English) is the Western scholars' rendering.

उभयं चष्टे अन्तः (*ubhayaṃ caṣṭe antaḥ*) — "(both, that is, the water and the manner of crossing it) standing in the midst of the two, Bṛhaspati looks on or brings about." To explain उभयमन्तर्मध्ये (*ubhayamantarmadhye*) here as "between water and crossing" is not very fitting. उभयं अन्तः (*ubhayaṃ antaḥ*) is better understood as "in the antarikṣa, between the earth and the heaven"; for the lines of clouds filled with water stand in the antarikṣa, and the sense that Bṛhaspati, standing there, brought about both the mass of water and its crossing (that is, the order of rain) fits well here.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly).*

अवनयः (*avanayaḥ*) — root अव (*ava*) in the sense of protecting etc.; suffix असि (*asi*) by an Uṇādi sūtra beginning अर्ति… (*arti…*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-259 [partly read; the file gives 2-259]); nominative plural; the suffix's first syllable is acute. यन्ति (*yanti*) — root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), लट् (*laṭ*) third person plural; यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*) prevents the *nighāta* accent; the suffix's first syllable is acute. स्रवतः (*sravataḥ*) — root स्रु गतौ (*sru gatau*); by the vārttika सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यः क्विब्वा वक्तव्यः (*sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvibvā vaktavyaḥ*) and क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) the *kvip* suffix, and *tuk* is added; the word स्रवत् (*sravat*), final-acute by root accent; nominative plural.

### Printed p. 330 (PDF 350)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 190". Ṛk 7: grammar concluded. Ṛk 8, the last of the sūkta: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya begun.)*

रोधचक्राः (*rodhacakrāḥ*) — in the bahuvrīhi, by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*) the accent of the prior member remains. चष्टे (*caṣṭe*) — roots have many senses, so here the root चक्षिङ् (*cakṣiṅ*) is used in the sense of seeing; लट् (*laṭ*) third person singular; the *nighāta* accent of a *tiṅanta* occurs. गृध्रः (*gṛdhraḥ*) — root गृधु अभिकाङ्क्षायाम् (*gṛdhu abhikāṅkṣāyām*); the suffix क्रन् (*kran*) by सुसूधाञ्गृधिभ्यः क्रन् (*susūdhāñgṛdhibhyaḥ kran*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-600); since the suffix has a mute *n*, the first syllable is acute by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*) (the number of this sūtra is not printed).

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Ṛk 8)*

> एवा महस्तुविजातस्तुविष्मान्बृहस्पतिर्वृषभो धायि देवः ।
> स नः स्तुतो वीरवद्धातु गोमद्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ८ ॥

> *evā mahastuvijātastuviṣmānbṛhaspatirvṛṣabho dhāyi devaḥ |*
> *sa naḥ stuto vīravaddhātu gomadvidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एव । महः । तुविऽजातः । तुविष्मान् । बृहस्पतिः । वृषभः । धायि । देवः ।
> सः । नः । स्तुतः । वीरऽवत् । धातु । गोऽमत् । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरऽदानुं ॥ ८ ॥

> *eva | mahaḥ | tuvi 'jātaḥ | tuviṣmān | bṛhaspatiḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | dhāyi | devaḥ |*
> *saḥ | naḥ | stutaḥ | vīra 'vat | dhātu | go 'mat | vidyāma | iṣaṃ | vṛjanaṃ | jīra 'dānuṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati, the great showerer, has been praised thus; may he give us sons and cattle, and may we obtain food, strength and long life.

> महो महांस्तुविजातो बह्वर्थमुत्पन्नस्तुविष्मान् बलवान् वृषभोऽपां वर्षिता देवो बृहस्पतिरेव्यैवं [?] स्तुतिप्रकारेण धायि । धीयते । स्तूयते इत्यर्थः । स स्तुतो देवो नोऽस्माकं वीरवत्पुत्राद्युपेतं गोमद्गोभिर्युक्तं फलं धातु । करोत्वित्यर्थः । विद्यामेति गतम् ॥

> *maho mahāṃstuvijāto bahvarthamutpannastuviṣmān balavān vṛṣabho 'pāṃ varṣitā devo bṛhaspatirevyaivaṃ [?] stutiprakāreṇa dhāyi | dhīyate | stūyate ityarthaḥ | sa stuto devo no 'smākaṃ vīravatputrādyupetaṃ gomadgobhiryuktaṃ phalaṃ dhātu | karotvityarthaḥ | vidyāmeti gatam ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** महः (*mahaḥ*) — the great-souled; तुविजातः (*tuvijātaḥ*) — born for many purposes; तुविष्मान् (*tuviṣmān*) — the strong; वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) — able to shower water; देवः (*devaḥ*) — the divine; बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*) — Bṛhaspati; एव (*eva*) — in this manner; धायि (*dhāyi*) — is praised; स्तुतः सः (*stutaḥ saḥ*) — he thus praised, the god; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; वीरवत् (*vīravat*) — together with heroic sons and others; गोमत् (*gomat*) — together with cattle (this) fruit; धातु (*dhātu*) — let him bring about; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we *(printed in the Pratipadārtha; not in the ṛk)*; इषं (*iṣaṃ*) — food; वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*) — strength; जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*) — long life; विद्याम (*vidyāma*) — may we obtain.

### Printed p. 331 (PDF 351)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 13". Ṛk 8: Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics; grammar begun.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** Bṛhaspati, the great-souled, born for many purposes, strong, able to shower water, the divine, is praised in this manner. May the god thus praised give us heroic sons and others, and cattle. May we obtain food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed):**

So, Brihaspati, the mighty, the beneficent, the powerful, the showerer (of benefits), the divine, has been glorified : praised by us, may he make us possessed of progeny and cattle, that thence we may obtain food, strength and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** In this ṛk the ṛṣi, concluding the sūkta, prays to Bṛhaspati for the increase of sons and grandsons and for the wealth of cattle and other animals.

तुविजातः (*tuvijātaḥ*) — the word तुवि (*tuvi*) is recited among the names of "many" (Ni. 3-13). For the word तुविजात (*tuvijāta*) Yāska says बहुजातः (*bahujātaḥ*) — one born to bring about many benefits to men.

वीरवत्, गोमत् (*vīravat, gomat*) — these words are used as adjectives; a qualified noun must be supplied by adhyāhāra; or they may be applied as adjectives to the word इषं (*iṣaṃ*) as well. The chief intention is that Bṛhaspati should favour us with valiant sons and grandsons, servants and cattle.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly).*

एवा (*evā*) — by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) lengthening in the Saṃhitā. तुविजातः (*tuvijātaḥ*) — तुवि (*tuvi*) (as a *bhūnām*) + जातः (*jātaḥ*), a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa compound ("born in connection with benefit"); by समासस्य (*samāsasya*) the end of the compound is acute. *(The grammar continues on p. 332.)*

### Printed p. 332 (PDF 352)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 190". Sūkta 190, Ṛk 8: grammar concluded. Then the half-title of the next sūkta and its Pīṭhike begin.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly; continued from p. 331).*

धायि (*dhāyi*) — root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); the passive (*karmaṇi*) in the Vedic manner in the sense of the present, लुङ् (*luṅ*) [as printed: "luñ"]; a variant form of the third person singular. By बहुलं छन्दसि (*bahulaṃ chandasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75) the augment (printed "āḍāgama", as it looks) does not come; the *nighāta* accent of a *tiṅanta* occurs.

धातु (*dhātu*) — root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); लोट् (*loṭ*) third person singular; the suffix printed "āp" [?]; by एरुः (*eruḥ*) (the sūtra number is not printed) the *i* is replaced by *u*. In the Vedic manner the *śnu*-type infix (printed "śluvikaraṇa", as it looks) does not come; hence doubling and the like do not occur for the root. Because it stands before an *atiṅanta* word, the *nighāta* accent occurs.

**The hundred and ninety-first Sūkta** *(half-title printed in Kannada: "nūra toṃbhattoṃdaneyu sūktavu").*

*Pīṭhike (Sanskrit introduction):*

> कंकते इति षोडशर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं ऋषिरगस्त्यः अप्तृणसूर्यास्त्रयो देवताः त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । सूर्ये विषमित्याद्यास्तिस्रो महापंक्तयः । अष्टकौ सप्तकः षट्को दशको नवकश्च । अनु. १०-३ । इत्युक्तलक्षणोपेतत्वात् । नवानामि-
> त्येषा त्रयोदशी महाबृहती । चत्वारोऽष्टका जागतेश्च महाबृहती । अनु. ९-९ । इति ह्युक्तं । अत्र यद्यक्षराणि न्यूनानि तथापि व्यूहेन पूरणीयानि । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । कंकतेः षोळशोपनिषदानुष्टुभमप्तृणसौर्यं विषशंकावानगस्त्यः प्राब्रवीद्धश्प्याद्याश्च तिस्रो महापंक्तयो महाबृहती चेति । उपनिषदिति रहस्यमित्यर्थः । विषशंकायुक्तोऽगस्त्यस्तत्परिहारायेदमुक्तवान् ॥ श्रौतस्य विशेषविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ अत्र शौनकः । कंकतो नेति सूक्तं तु विषार्तः प्रयुतो जपेत् । विषं न क्रमते चास्य सर्पाद्दृष्टिविषादपि ॥ यत्कीटलूतासु विषं दंष्ट्रि वृश्चिकतश्च यत् । मूलं च कृत्रिमं चैव जपन्सर्वमपोहति । ऋग्वि. १-२८ । इति ॥

> *kaṃkate iti ṣoḍaśarcaṃ dvādaśaṃ sūktaṃ ṛṣiragastyaḥ aptṛṇasūryāstrayo devatāḥ triṣṭup chandaḥ | sūrye viṣamityādyāstisro mahāpaṃktayaḥ | aṣṭakau saptakaḥ ṣaṭko daśako navakaśca | anu. 10-3 | ityuktalakṣaṇopetatvāt | navānāmi-*
> *tyeṣā trayodaśī mahābṛhatī | catvāro 'ṣṭakā jāgateśca mahābṛhatī | anu. 9-9 | iti hyuktaṃ | atra yadyakṣarāṇi nyūnāni tathāpi vyūhena pūraṇīyāni | atrānukramaṇikā | kaṃkateḥ ṣoḷaśopaniṣadānuṣṭubhamaptṛṇasauryaṃ viṣaśaṃkāvānagastyaḥ prābravīddhaśpyādyāśca tisro mahāpaṃktayo mahābṛhatī ceti | upaniṣaditi rahasyamityarthaḥ | viṣaśaṃkāyukto 'gastyastatparihārāyedamuktavān ‖ śrautasya viśeṣaviniyogo laiṃgikaḥ ‖ atra śaunakaḥ | kaṃkato neti sūktaṃ tu viṣārtaḥ prayuto japet | viṣaṃ na kramate cāsya sarpāddṛṣṭiviṣādapi ‖ yatkīṭalūtāsu viṣaṃ daṃṣṭri vṛścikataśca yat | mūlaṃ ca kṛtrimaṃ caiva japansarvamapohati | ṛgvi. 1-28 | iti ‖*

*Gist:* The sūkta (Agastya; Apas, Tṛṇa and Sūrya; triṣṭubh, with three mahāpaṅktis and a mahābṛhatī) is a charm against poison; Śaunaka says one afflicted by poison should recite it.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning "kaṅkato na" is the twelfth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. It has sixteen ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi; the deities are the Apṛṇa-sūryas (water, grass, sun); the metre is triṣṭubh. The three ṛks beginning "sūrye viṣam" (the 10th, 11th and 12th ṛks, as printed) are in the mahābṛhatī metre [sic as printed: the Sanskrit calls them mahāpaṅkti]. The Anukramaṇikā says that in this metre the first two pādas have eight syllables each, the third seven, the fourth six, the fifth ten and the sixth nine (Anu. 10-3). The thirteenth ṛk, beginning "navānāṃ", is in the mahābṛhatī metre; in this metre there are four pādas of eight syllables and one pāda of twelve syllables… *(the sentence continues on p. 333.)*

### Printed p. 333 (PDF 353)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 14 ]" and "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Sūkta 191: Anuvāda concluded; heading block.)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada), continued from p. 332.** …"and one pāda of twelve syllables", so it is said in the Anukramaṇikā (Anu. 9-9). In general, even where in the metres some syllables are fewer, or where the syllables appear fewer by the processes of word-division (*padavibhāga*), *sandhi* and the like, it is to be supposed that in the total the syllables are of the prescribed number (*klṛpta-saṅkhyā*). In the Anukramaṇikā —

> कंकतेः षोळशोपनिषदानुष्टुभमप्तृणसौर्यं विषशंकावानगस्त्यः प्राब्रवीद्ध-
> शम्याद्याश्च तिस्रो महापंक्तयो महाबृहती चेति ।

> *kaṃkateḥ ṣoḷaśopaniṣadānuṣṭubhamaptṛṇasauryaṃ viṣaśaṃkāvānagastyaḥ prābravīddha-*
> *śamyādyāśca tisro mahāpaṃktayo mahābṛhatī ceti |*

— it is so stated *(the word printed "prābravīddha-śamyādyāśca" here is read as it looks [?]; on p. 332 the same passage was read "haśpyādyāśca"; here the printing is "-śamyādyāśca")*. Here *upaniṣad* means "secret" *(rahasya)*. Agastya, the ṛṣi, being in doubt whether the poison of a serpent's bite had touched him, is said to have uttered this sūkta for the removal of that poison. As to its śrauta application, the application of this sūkta is *laiṅgika*. The great sage Śaunaka, in his work called Ṛgvidhāna, speaks thus on the application of this sūkta —

> कंकतो नेति सूक्तं तु विषार्तः प्रयतो जपेत् ।
> विषं न क्रमते चास्य सर्पाद्दृष्टिविषादपि ॥
> यत्कीटलूतासु विषं दंष्ट्रि वृश्चिकजं च यत् ॥
> मूलं च कृत्रिमं चैव जपन् सर्वं व्यपोहति ।
> धर्मं बुद्धिं धनं पुत्रान् सौभाग्यं ब्रह्मवर्चसं ।
> आरोग्यं पुष्टिमायुष्यं पशून् विद्यां महद्यशः ।

> *kaṃkato neti sūktaṃ tu viṣārtaḥ prayato japet |*
> *viṣaṃ na kramate cāsya sarpāddṛṣṭiviṣādapi ‖*
> *yatkīṭalūtāsu viṣaṃ daṃṣṭri vṛścikajaṃ ca yat ‖*
> *mūlaṃ ca kṛtrimaṃ caiva japan sarvaṃ vyapohati |*
> *dharmaṃ buddhiṃ dhanaṃ putrān saubhāgyaṃ brahmavarcasaṃ |*
> *ārogyaṃ puṣṭimāyuṣyaṃ paśūn vidyāṃ mahadyaśaḥ |*

(Ṛgvidhāna 1-28; numeral agrees with the file, not zoomed)

*(Differences from the quotation on p. 332, as printed: here "prayato" for "prayuto" and "vṛścikajaṃ ca yat" for "vṛścikataśca yat"; "daṃṣṭri" in both.)*

The man who is tormented by the affliction of poison (the man who is racked, the poison having risen in him because a serpent has bitten him) should recite this sūkta beginning कंकतो न (*kaṃkato na*) with faith and devotion. If he does so, neither the poison that has spread in the body from a serpent's bite nor the poison that arises from the evil eye (*dṛṣṭidoṣa*) spreads further in the body. Moreover, the poison arising from creeping creatures, scorpions and other poisonous creatures is also removed. Whether that poison, bitten by a venomous creature, has spread in the body, or poisoned food and the like has entered the body, all these are removed by reciting this sūkta. Moreover, by reciting this sūkta, such fruits as righteous action, good understanding, wealth, sons and the rest, good fortune, *brahmavarcas*, health, nourishment, increase of life, wealth in cattle, learning and fame are all obtained.

### Printed p. 334 (PDF 354)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 191", running title "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā". Sūkta 191, Ṛk 1: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha.)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> कंकतो न कंकतोऽथो सतीनकंकतः ।
> द्वाविति प्लुषी इति न्यदृष्टा अलिप्सत ॥ १ ॥

> *kaṃkato na kaṃkato 'tho satīnakaṃkataḥ |*
> *dvāviti pluṣī iti nyadṛṣṭā alipsata ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कंकतः । न । कंकतः । अथो इति । सतीनऽकंकतः ।
> द्वौ । इति । प्लुषी इति । इति । नि । अदृष्टाः । अलिप्सत ॥ १ ॥

> *kaṃkataḥ | na | kaṃkataḥ | atho iti | satīna 'kaṃkataḥ |*
> *dvau | iti | pluṣī iti | iti | ni | adṛṣṭāḥ | alipsata ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* "Kaṅkata" is a small-venomed creature; its opposite is a great-venomed serpent; water-creatures too; two kinds, burning, and unseen ones have smeared me with poison.

> कंकतोऽल्पविषः कश्चित् न कंकतस्तद्विपरीतोऽनल्पविषो महोरगादिः ॥ तकतेर्गत्यर्थस्य वर्णव्यत्ययेन कंकत इति सरन् भवति ॥ अथो अपि च सतीनकंकतः । सतीनमित्युदकनामसु सतीनं गहनमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । उदकचार्यल्पविषवान् कश्चिद्दुंदुभादिः । एवं द्वाविति । अल्पविषमहाविषभेदेन जलस्थलभेदेन वा द्विप्रकाराविति । प्लुषी इति प्लोषणाविति । प्रकारद्वैविध्यदाहकत्वयोः प्रतिपादनायेतिकारद्वयं । तथादृष्टा अदृश्यमानरूपा एतत्संज्ञकाश्च केचिद्विषधरा एवमुक्तप्रकारा ये संति ते नूनं मां न्यलिप्सत विशेषेण लिंपंति । सर्वाण्यंगानि विषमावृणोति । केनैवं कृतमिति ज्ञायत इति भावः ॥

> *kaṃkato 'lpaviṣaḥ kaścit na kaṃkatastadviparīto 'nalpaviṣo mahoragādiḥ ‖ takatergatyarthasya varṇavyatyayena kaṃkata iti saran bhavati ‖ atho api ca satīnakaṃkataḥ | satīnamityudakanāmasu satīnaṃ gahanamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | udakacāryalpaviṣavān kaścidduṃdubhādiḥ | evaṃ dvāviti | alpaviṣamahāviṣabhedena jalasthalabhedena vā dviprakārāviti | pluṣī iti ploṣaṇāviti | prakāradvaividhyadāhakatvayoḥ pratipādanāyetikāradvayaṃ | tathādṛṣṭā adṛśyamānarūpā etatsaṃjñakāśca kecidviṣadharā evamuktaprakārā ye saṃti te nūnaṃ māṃ nyalipsata viśeṣeṇa liṃpaṃti | sarvāṇyaṃgāni viṣamāvṛṇoti | kenaivaṃ kṛtamiti jñāyata iti bhāvaḥ ‖*



**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**कंकतः (*kaṃkataḥ*)** — serpents and the like with little poison. **न कंकतः (*na kaṃkataḥ*)** — great serpents (*mahoraga*) and the like with exceeding poison. **अथो (*atho*)** — likewise. **सतीन कंकतः (*satīna kaṃkataḥ*)** — water-snakes (*nīruhāvu*) filled with poison. **द्वौ इति (*dvau iti*)** — two kinds: those that move on the earth and those that move in water; or those of little poison and those of great poison; in these two kinds. **प्लुषी इति (*pluṣī iti*)** — both causing harm, destroyers. **अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*)** — other poisonous creatures too that are not visible to the eye. **नि अलिप्सत (*ni alipsata*)** — make me filled with poison.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

Serpents and the like of little poison, serpents of great poison, likewise water-snakes full of poison; creatures of both these kinds of poison, and also those that are invisible to me, make me full of poison.

### Printed p. 335 (PDF 355)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 14 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 1: printed English, Special Topics; the Ṛk continues on p. 336.)*

**Printed English** *(the heading is printed "English Translatin" [sic])*

Some creature of little venom ; some creature of great venom ; or some venomous aquatic reptile ; creatures of two kinds, both destructive (of life), or (poisonous) unseen creatures, have anointed me with their poison.

**Special Topics (॥ विशेषविषयगळು ॥).** This is the last sūkta in the first Maṇḍala. In this sūkta the ṛṣi Agastya, having fallen into doubt that a serpent has bitten him, has treated that matter at length. In this matter there is no other such sūkta in the Ṛgveda apart from this one. That by reciting this sūkta the poison connected with serpents and other poisonous creatures is removed, as Śaunaka has said in his work called Ṛgvidhāna, has been shown in the Pīṭhike of this sūkta itself.

In this ṛk the matter of two kinds of serpents is suggested. Serpents of little poison and of great poison, thus two kinds; or serpents that move on the earth and water-serpents that live in water, thus also two kinds: so the ṛṣi has described.

**कंकतः (*kaṃkataḥ*)** — अल्पविषः (*alpaviṣaḥ*) । तकतेर्गत्यर्थस्य वर्णव्यत्ययेन कंकत इति सरन् भवति (*takatergatyarthasya varṇavyatyayena kaṃkata iti saran bhavati*) । The commentator's explanation is that the word *kaṃkataḥ* is formed by interchange of letters (*varṇa*, syllable) from the root *takati*, which indicates motion, and since this word gives the meaning *saran* (moving), it is a creature that crawls on the ground, and therefore the meaning "serpent" can be given to it. That there are many kinds of difference in the poison-power of serpents is well known. If some serpents bite, there is not much affliction; if some bite, the poison spreads and may cause affliction after some time and afterwards death. Again, some kinds of serpents, that is, the cobras (*nāgara-hāvu*), having much poison, death certainly occurs if they bite. Among these cobras too there are many divisions and subdivisions. Among these, if some bite, death occurs in some moments (instantly). Such serpents are spread in many ways in various countries. Some kinds of serpents are very large to look at and fearful, yet there is no poison in them. Instead of biting living beings they swallow them for food. Some kinds of serpents, if they touch, are enough: the body of the creatures begins to rot and afterwards death occurs. Yet again some kinds of serpents, as soon as they see creatures, squirt directly into their eyes a kind of poison-mixed liquid. By that creatures may lose their eyes and become blind. Thus, since there are various differences in serpents and in their poison, the ṛṣi Agastya here has described their nature as serpents of little poison, of great poison, and living in water.

### Printed p. 336 (PDF 356)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". Ṛk 1: Special Topics continued, then Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

**Special Topics, continued (word notes).**

**न कंकतः (na kaṃkataḥ (*na kaṃkataḥ*))** — तद्विपरीतोऽनल्पविषः महोरगादिः । Not of little poison, that is, cruel serpents such as the great cobra (*nāgarahāvu*) filled with great poison, is the sense.

**सतीनकंकतः (satīnakaṃkataḥ (*satīnakaṃkataḥ*))** — Because the word satīnam (*satīnam*) is read among the hundred and one names of water (Nirukta 2-24; numeral agrees with the file), the word satīnakaṃkataḥ (*satīnakaṃkataḥ*) means a water-snake, a snake living in water.

**द्वाविति प्लुषी (dvāviti pluṣī (*dvāviti pluṣī*))** — The two kinds of snakes spoken of before both do harm; they are destructive.

**अदृष्टाः (adṛṣṭāḥ (*adṛṣṭāḥ*))** — अदृश्यमानरूपा एतद्व्यंजकाश्च । "Unseen" means: either very small, or hiding in grass and the like or in bushes so as to be invisible to the eye. Because snakes are commonly in grass, in bushes and in holes, they do not at once come within people's sight; and when people have no such knowledge, they deceive them and bite, is the sense.

**अलिप्सत (alipsata (*alipsata*))** — विशेषण लिंपंति । सर्वाण्यंगानि विषमावृणोति । "They smear specially": they cover all the limbs with poison. That is, they bite so that the poison spreads over all the limbs; or: they bite and make the poison pervade the limbs.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

kaṃkataḥ (*kaṃkataḥ*): root taka (*taka*) in the sense of motion; the form arises by interchange of letters, and the initial-acute accent comes from the interchange itself. satīnakaṃkataḥ (*satīnakaṃkataḥ*): by the sūtra tatpuruṣe (*tatpuruṣe*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the first member keeps its natural accent; the word satīna (*satīna*) is final-acute by the accent of the nominal stem. adṛṣṭāḥ (*adṛṣṭāḥ*): na dṛṣṭāḥ (*na dṛṣṭāḥ*); by parādiśchandasi bahulam (*parādiśchandasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. printed "6 2-199", hyphen missing; the file reads 62.199) the last member has the initial acute. alipsata (*alipsata*): root lip upadehe (*lip upadehe*) (tudādi), Vedic luṅ (*luṅ*) in the present sense, ata (*ata*) substituted for the third plural, augment aṭ (*aṭ*); because it stands after a word ending in a tiṅ (*tiṅ*)-less word it takes the nighāta (*nighāta*) accent *(as it looks)*.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> अदृष्टान्हंत्यायत्यथो हंति परायती ।
> अथो अवघ्नती हंत्यथो पिनष्टि पिंषती ॥ २ ॥

> *adṛṣṭānhaṃtyāyatyatho haṃti parāyatī |*
> *atho avaghnatī haṃtyatho pinaṣṭi piṃṣatī ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अदृष्टान् । हंति । आयती । अथो इति । हंति । परायती ।
> अथो इति । अवघ्नती । हंति । अथो इति । पिनष्टि । पिंषती ॥ २ ॥

> *adṛṣṭān | haṃti | āyatī | atho iti | haṃti | parāyatī |*
> *atho iti | avaghnatī | haṃti | atho iti | pinaṣṭi | piṃṣatī ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* This ṛk praises the poison-destroying herb: coming, going away, being pounded or ground, it kills poisonous creatures, seen and unseen.

> अनेन विषघ्न्यौषधिः स्तूयते । आयती विषदष्टस्य सकाशमागच्छन्ती विषनिर्हरणसाधनौषधिरदृष्टानदृश्यमानान्विषधरान्हंति । हिनस्ति । अथो अपि च परायती परागच्छन्ती समार्जनसमये ऽर्वाक्प्रवृत्ता हंति । नाशयति जलचरविषधरान् । अथो अपि चावघ्नती ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृ प्रत्ययः ॥ अवहन्यमानौषधिः स्वगंधेन हंति बहुविषान् । यद्वा । काचिदोषधिर्दंशकान्मारयत्येव । अथो अपि च पिंषती पेषणकर्त्र्या दृषत्पिष्यमाणा वौषधिः पिनष्टि । चूर्णीकरोत्यल्पविषान् । अथवा सर्वेषु वाक्येष्वविशेषेण सर्वविषकारिणां नाश उक्तः ॥

> *anena viṣaghnyauṣadhiḥ stūyate | āyatī viṣadaṣṭasya sakāśamāgacchantī viṣanirharaṇasādhanauṣadhiradṛṣṭānadṛśyamānānviṣadharānhaṃti | hinasti | atho api ca parāyatī parāgacchantī samārjanasamaye 'rvākpravṛttā haṃti | nāśayati jalacaraviṣadharān | atho api cāvaghnatī ‖ karmaṇi kartṛ pratyayaḥ ‖ avahanyamānauṣadhiḥ svagaṃdhena haṃti bahuviṣān | yadvā | kācidoṣadhirdaṃśakānmārayatyeva | atho api ca piṃṣatī peṣaṇakartryā dṛṣatpiṣyamāṇā vauṣadhiḥ pinaṣṭi | cūrṇīkarotyalpaviṣān | athavā sarveṣu vākyeṣvaviśeṣeṇa sarvaviṣakāriṇāṃ nāśa uktaḥ ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**आयती (āyatī (*āyatī*))** — (the herb) at once when it comes near one bitten by a poisonous creature. **अदृष्टान् (adṛṣṭān (*adṛṣṭān*))** — poisonous creatures not visible to the eye. **हंति (haṃti (*haṃti*))** — it kills. **अथो (atho (*atho*))** — afterwards. **परायती (parāyatī (*parāyatī*))** — (at the time of washing, as the poison) goes out of the body. **हंति (haṃti (*haṃti*))** — it destroys them. **अथो (atho (*atho*))** — and besides. **अवघ्नती (avaghnatī (*avaghnatī*))** — the herb that destroys by its own (smell). **हंति (haṃti (*haṃti*))** — it destroys the poison-bearers. **अथो (atho (*atho*))** — along with that. **पिंषती (piṃṣatī (*piṃṣatī*))** — the herb in powdered form. **पिनष्टि (pinaṣṭi (*pinaṣṭi*))** — it grinds the poison-worms to powder (destroys them).

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

The herb, the moment it comes near one bitten by a poisonous creature, destroys some poison-bearers. Likewise, at the time it passes out of the body, it destroys some poison-worms. There are also herbs that destroy by their own smell. The herb in powdered form grinds the worms to powder and destroys them.

### Printed p. 338 (PDF 358)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". Ṛk 2: printed English, Special Topics; the Ṛk continues on p. 339.)*

**Printed English** *(heading "English Translation")*

(The antidote), coming (to the bitten person), destroys the unseen (venomous creatures) ; departing, (it destroys them) ; deprived (of substance), it destroys them (by its odour) ; being ground, it pulverises them·

*(Stray point after "them" as printed [sic].)*

**Special Topics (॥ विशेषविषयगळು ॥).** In this ṛk the nature of herbs that can destroy or counteract poison is described.

**अदृष्टान् हंति आयती (adṛṣṭān haṃti āyatī (*adṛṣṭān haṃti āyatī*))** — As soon as the poison-removing herb comes, it kills the poisonous creatures that are hiding so as not to be seen. That is, by the power of the herb the poisonous creatures are destroyed at once.

**अथो हंति परायती (atho haṃti parāyatī (*atho haṃti parāyatī*))** — परागच्छन्ती समार्जनसमये ऽर्वाक्प्रवृत्ता हंति । The commentator has given this sentence the meaning: the herb, at the time of washing the wound the snake has bitten, destroys the poison that goes out of the body. This does not appear very smooth. The word parāyatī (*parāyatī*) means going backwards. Therefore the meaning is quite fitting here: the herb destroys the serpents and the like that, having bitten men, flee backwards out of sight, escaping for fear that they will be killed somewhere.

**अथो अवघ्नती हंति (atho avaghnatī haṃti (*atho avaghnatī haṃti*))** — The herb kills snakes by its own sharp smell. Snakes cannot endure the smell of some roots (nāgadāḷīsappu and the like); therefore they leave the place where such herbs are and go away. The word avaghnatī (*avaghnatī*), if taken as formed from the root ghrā (*ghrā*) (jighra (*jighra*)), smell, with the prefix ava (*ava*), gives the sense stated above. Or, if taken as formed from hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*) "kill", avaghnatī (*avaghnatī*) may mean poisonous creatures that bite (men) and kill; the herb kills (destroys) such poisonous creatures: a second meaning may be given in this way.

**अथो पिनष्टि पिंषती (atho pinaṣṭi piṃṣatī (*atho pinaṣṭi piṃṣatī*))** — Some roots used for medicines are reduced to powder and used. Such powder grinds (crushes) the poisonous creatures and kills, that is, destroys them.

The sense stated in the four pādas of this ṛk is all of one kind, with slight differences. For these sentences — that herbs destroy the poisons spread in the wound — thus is said [… the sentence continues on p. 339]

### Printed p. 339 (PDF 359)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 14 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 2: Special Topics concluded, Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā. Ṛk 3: Saṃhitā, Pada, beginning of the bhāṣya, which continues on p. 340.)*

**Special Topics, concluded.** … can be [said]; or it may also be said that it destroys poisonous serpents and the like filled with poison — thus the commentator has explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

हंति (*haṃti*): root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*), adādi class; लट् (*laṭ*), third person singular; the तिङन्त (*tiṅanta*) nighāta accent comes. आयती (*āyatī*): root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), शतृ (*śatṛ*) suffix, ङीप् (*ṅīp*) when the feminine is intended; by शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (*śaturanumo nadyajādī*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173; agrees with the numerals file) it is final-acute; so also परायती (*parāyatī*) and अवघ्नती (*avaghnatī*). अवघ्नती (*avaghnatī*): root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*), शतृ (*śatṛ*) in the sense of लट् (*laṭ*); by व्यत्यय (*vyatyaya*) an agent-suffix has come here in the passive; for the sense "being pounded" the form would have to be अवहन्यमानाः (*avahanyamānāḥ*), so the शतृ (*śatṛ*) suffix itself expresses the object. पिनष्टि (*pinaṣṭi*): root पिषल् संचूर्णने (*piṣal saṃcūrṇane*) [?], rudhādi class; लट् (*laṭ*), third person singular, तिप् (*tip*); the श्नम् (*śnam*) (as it looks) vikaraṇa, being an *m*-marked element, comes after the last vowel; by ṣṭutva the suffix gets *ṭ* (as printed); because it stands after an अतिङन्त (*atiṅanta*) the nighāta accent comes.

*(Ṛk 2 ends here.)*

*Gist:* The ṛk names further places of venom: śara, kuśara, darbha, sairya, muñja and vīraṇa grasses, where unseen venomous creatures dwell.

> अन्यांश्च विषहेतूनाह । शरासः शरा वेणुदंडसदृशा अंतश्छिद्रास्तृणविशेषाः । कुशरासः कुत्सितशरा अंतश्छिद्राः शरसदृशास्तृणविशेषाः । दर्भासो दर्भाः कुशाः । सैर्यास्तटाकादिप्रांतोद्भवास्तृणविशेषा अश्ववाला इति प्रसिद्धाः । मौंजा मुंजाः

### Printed p. 340 (PDF 360)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". Ṛk 3: bhāṣya concluded, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun; the Ṛk continues on p. 341.)*

> प्रसिद्धाः । वैरिणा वीरणप्रकाराः । एतेषु वर्तमाना अदृष्टा उक्तरूपाः सर्वे विषधराः साकं मिलित्वा न्यलिप्सत । निलंपंति स्म ॥

> *prasiddhāḥ | vairiṇā vīraṇaprakārāḥ | eteṣu vartamānā adṛṣṭā uktarūpāḥ sarve viṣadharāḥ sākaṃ militvā nyalipsata | nilaṃpaṃti sma ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**शरासः (*śarāsaḥ*)** — dwelling in the śarā grass. **कुशरासः (*kuśarāsaḥ*)** — dwelling in the kuśa grass. **दर्भासः (*darbhāsaḥ*)** — in the darbhas. **सैर्याः (*sairyāḥ*)** — in the sairya, a kind of reed-grass. **मौंजाः (*mauṃjāḥ*)** — in thickets of muñja. **वैरिणाः (*vairiṇāḥ*)** — in vīraṇa; being so, **अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*)** — unseen by the eye, **सर्वे (*sarve*)** — all poison-bearers too, **साकं (*sākaṃ*)** — joining together, **न्यलिप्सत (*nyalipsata*)** — make me filled with poison.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

All the poison-bearers that hide in grasses such as śarā, kuśa, sairya, muñja and vīraṇa, and that are not visible to the eye, join together, bite us, and make our whole body pervaded with poison.

**Printed English** *(the heading is printed "Englih Tranlation" [sic])*

(Blades of) shara grass, (of) kushara, (of) darbha, (of) sourya, (of) munja, (of) virana, all (the haunt) of unseen (venomous creatures), have together anointed me (with their venom)·

*(Stray point at the end as printed [sic].)*

**Special Topics (॥ विशेषविषयगळು ॥).** In this ṛk the various kinds of grass and darbha in which snakes lie hidden out of sight are named.

**शरासः (*śarāsaḥ*)** — वेणुदंडसदृशा अंतश्छिद्रास्तृणविशेषाः (*veṇudaṃḍasadṛśā aṃtaśchidrāstṛṇaviśeṣāḥ*). A kind of grass or darbha (Saccharum Sara) that is tall and straight like a bamboo staff, and hollow in the middle as if cut across. This kind of darbha grows densely, and in places where water stands. Since it is about waist-high (as printed), one cannot tell what is at its foot. The sense is that snakes lie hidden in such places unseen by the eye.

**कुशरासः (*kuśarāsaḥ*)** — कुत्सितशरा अंतश्छिद्राः शरसदृशास्तृणविशेषाः (*kutsitaśarā aṃtaśchidrāḥ śarasadṛśāstṛṇaviśeṣāḥ*). The darbha called kuśara also is like the śara spoken of above, that is, belongs to the same class, but does not grow so tall.

**दर्भासः (*darbhāsaḥ*)** — the grass called darbha that is used in sacrifices and in household rites. It grows only as thick as a "heñcī-stick" [?] (word unclear). (Poa cynosuroides).

### Printed p. 341 (PDF 361)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 14 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 3: Special Topics concluded, Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā. Ṛk 4: Saṃhitā, Pada; the bhāṣya follows on p. 342.)*

**सैर्याः (*sairyāḥ*)** — सैर्यास्तटाकादिप्रांतोद्भवास्तृणविशेषा अश्ववाला इति प्रसिद्धाः (*sairyāstaṭākādiprāṃtodbhavāstṛṇaviśeṣā aśvavālā iti prasiddhāḥ*). Sairya means a kind of reed-grass that grows near tanks, lakes or rivers, that is, in places where still water stands. It has the popular name "horse's tail" (aśvavāla). Elephants use it as food. (Saccharum spontaneum)

**मौंजाः (*mauṃjāḥ*)** — मौंजाः मुंजाः प्रसिद्धाः (*mauṃjāḥ muṃjāḥ prasiddhāḥ*). Muñja is a grass that grows straight up like a stick. It is used for plaiting mats. (Saccharum munja)

**वैरिणाः (*vairiṇāḥ*)** — वीरणप्रकाराः (*vīraṇaprakārāḥ*). It is not known what kind of grass the vīraṇa is. (Andropogon muricatum)

Besides these grasses there are many other kinds of grass; only some are mentioned here. The idea is that snakes lie hidden in these, out of the sight of people, and bite those who come near.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

शरासः (*śarāsaḥ*): first case plural, जस् (*jas*); by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (no number printed) it gets the augment असुक् (*asuk*); by the single-substitute accent the middle syllable is acute. कुशरासः (*kuśarāsaḥ*): कुत्सिताः शराः कुशरासः (*kutsitāḥ śarāḥ kuśarāsaḥ*); as before जस् (*jas*) gets असुक् (*asuk*); by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ… (*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2; agrees with the numerals file) the first member keeps its natural accent; there it is read अव्ययेन [?]कु निपातानाम् (*avyayena [?]ku nipātānām*) (the middle of this quotation unclear). न्यलिप्सत (*nyalipsata*): नि (*ni*) prefix; root लिप उपदेहे (*lipa upadehe*), लुङ् (*luṅ*), third person plural, अतादेश (*atādeśa*) [?] (as it looks); च्लि (*cli*) is replaced by सिच् (*sic*); because it stands after an अतिङन्त (*atiṅanta*) the nighāta accent comes.

*(Ṛk 3 ends here; ornament line.)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> नि गावो गोष्ठे असदन्नि मृगासो अविक्षत ।
> नि केतवो जनानां न्य१दृष्टा अलिप्सत ॥ ४ ॥

> *ni gāvo goṣṭhe asadanni mṛgāso avikṣata |*
> *ni ketavo janānāṃ nya1dṛṣṭā alipsata ‖ 4 ‖*

*(In the second line a small mark like the digit 1 is printed after न्य (*nya*), as printed.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> नि । केतवः । जनानां । नि । अदृष्टाः । अलिप्सत ॥ ४ ॥

> *ni | gāvaḥ | go 'sthe | asadan | ni | mṛgāsaḥ | avikṣata |*

### Printed p. 342 (PDF 362)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191" (the Maṇḍala numeral as it looks). Ṛk 4: bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The cows lay in the stall, the beasts rested in their places, men's faculties were stilled; the unseen venomous creatures then anointed me.

> गावो गोष्ठे न्यसदन् । निषीदंति । मृगासो मृगा न्यविक्षत । निविष्टाः । स्वस्वस्थाने उपरताः । जनानां प्राणिनां केतवः प्रज्ञानानि नि ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । नीचान्यभवन् । एतेऽस्मिन्समये ऽदृष्टा अदृश्यमानरूपाः संतो न्यलिप्सत । निलिंपंति विशेषेण ॥

> *gāvo goṣṭhe nyasadan | niṣīdaṃti | mṛgāso mṛgā nyavikṣata | niviṣṭāḥ | svasvasthāne uparatāḥ | janānāṃ prāṇināṃ ketavaḥ prajñānāni ni ‖ upasargaśruteryogyakriyādhyāhāraḥ | nīcānyabhavan | ete 'sminsamaye 'dṛṣṭā adṛśyamānarūpāḥ saṃto nyalipsata | niliṃpaṃti viśeṣeṇa ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**गावः (*gāvaḥ*)** — the cows. **गोष्ठे (*goṣṭhe*)** — in the cowshed. **न्यसदन् (*nyasadan*)** — they were tied up (in the stall), taking rest. **मृगासः (*mṛgāsaḥ*)** — the beasts. **न्यविक्षत (*nyavikṣata*)** — taking rest, each in its own place. **जनानां (*janānāṃ*)** — of living beings. **केतवः (*ketavaḥ*)** — the faculties of knowledge. **नि (*ni*)** — were quiet (at such a time). **अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*)** — the venomous creatures not visible to the eye. **न्यलिप्सत (*nyalipsata*)** — bit me and made the venom pervade my body.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

Make me thus: the venomous creatures that are invisible to the eye bit me and made my body pervaded with venom. At that time the cows were tied up in the cowshed, the beasts lay in their own places, and the faculties of living beings were quiet.

**Printed English** *(heading "English Translation")*

The cows had lain down in their stalls; the wild beasts had retreated (to their lairs); the senses of men were at rest; when the unseen (venomous creatures) anointed me (with their venom).

**Special Topics** *(the heading is printed in garbled type; the sense is the usual "Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu")*

This ṛk describes that snakes generally move about at night. For the cattle (at night) lie in their cowsheds, that is, resting without movement, they chew the cud. The wild beasts also enter their own caves and sleep. People too, having finished their daily business and doing no work, sleep at night for rest. At such a time snakes come unseen and bite people: this is the sense.

It is not right to say here that wild beasts remain in their caves at night; for they sleep all day in their caves and go about at night for food. But since this ṛk says only मृगासः (*mṛgāsaḥ*), it need not be understood as wild beasts; they may be domestic animals (printed in English: "Domestic Animals") such as horses. Or again, there is no word in this ṛk giving the sense "at night". But since it indicates the time when people, doing no work, are devoid of awareness (are sleeping), it appears as night. The main point is: whether night or day, when people and animals have finished their work and are taking rest, these evil snakes come unseen and bite them.

### Printed p. 343 (PDF 363)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 14 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 4: Special Topics concluded, Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

(Special Topics continued from p. 342.) In the first sentence of this ṛk there is the verb नि असदन् (*ni asadan*). In the remaining sentences there is no verb, but because the upasarga नि (*ni*) is used, a verb has to be supplied for each sentence. Such ṛks are met with in the Ṛgveda. To press the sense in sentences (printed "Emphasis"), an upasarga is used in this way, for instance:

> मा नो महांतमुत मा नो अर्भकं मा न उक्षंतमुत मा न उक्षितं ।
> मा नो वधीः पितरं नोत मातरं मा नः प्रियास्तन्वो [?] रुद्र रीरिषः ॥

> *mā no mahāṃtamuta mā no arbhakaṃ mā na ukṣaṃtamuta mā na ukṣitaṃ |*
> *mā no vadhīḥ pitaraṃ nota mātaraṃ mā naḥ priyāstanvo [?] rudra rīriṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-7, as given by the file and the strip.) *(The syllable after प्रिय (*priya*) in the second line is doubtful as printed; kept as it looks. Gloss, mine and tentative: "Do not harm our elder, nor our child, nor the one who is growing, nor the one begotten; do not slay our father nor our mother; do not injure our dear bodies, Rudra.")*

In this ṛk, though the verbs वधीः (*vadhīḥ*) and रीरिषः (*rīriṣaḥ*) occur only once, the prohibitive word मा (*mā*) is used in every sentence. Such usages give grace, depth and clarity (*prasāda*) to the poet's skill in composition.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

गोष्ठे (*goṣṭhe*): root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); by सुपि स्थः (*supi sthaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-4) the affix ka after the upapada गो (*go*); by the sūtra अंबांबगोभूमि… (*aṃbāṃbagobhūmi…*) (number doubtful: Pā. Sū. 8-3-[?]) the s of the root becomes ṣ; आतो लोप इटि च (*āto lopa iṭi ca*) (no number printed) drops the ā; the kṛdutta-uttarapada keeps its natural accent; locative singular form.

असदन् (*asadan*): root षदॢ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*); by Vedic usage luṅ in the sense of the present; पुषादिद्युताद्यॢदितः… (*puṣādidyutādyḷditaḥ…*) (as printed; no number) replaces cli by aṅ; the plural ending jhi gets ant; augment aṭ; tiṅanta-nighāta accent. अविक्षत (*avikṣata*): root विश प्रवेशने (*viśa praveśane*), luṅ, third person plural, same pattern. नि (*ni*): since it is fixed as an upasarga in connexion with a verb, the bare नि (*ni*) heard here requires a suitable verb to be supplied.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> एत उ त्ये प्रत्यदृश्रन्प्रदोषं तस्करा इव ।
> अदृष्टा विश्वदृष्टाः प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन ॥ ५ ॥

> *eta u tye pratyadṛśranpradoṣaṃ taskarā iva |*
> *adṛṣṭā viśvadṛṣṭāḥ pratibuddhā abhūtana ‖ 5 ‖*

*(After न् (*n*) in the first line an extra small sign is printed, and the following प्र (*pra*) looks compressed; kept as it looks [?].)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एते । ऊं इति । त्ये । प्रति । अदृश्रन् । प्रऽदोषं । तस्कराः ऽइव ।
> अदृष्टाः । विश्वऽदृष्टाः । प्रतिऽबुद्धाः । अभूतन ॥ ५ ॥

> *ete | ūṃ iti | tye | prati | adṛśran | pra 'doṣaṃ | taskarāḥ 'iva |*
> *adṛṣṭāḥ | viśva 'dṛṣṭāḥ | prati 'buddhāḥ | abhūtana ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* These snakes are detected at night by their breathing, like thieves at dusk; unseen, they see all; so, men, be vigilant.

> त्ये ते एते सर्पाः प्रत्यदृश्रन् । प्रतिदृश्यंते रात्रौ श्वासादिलिंगेन । यद्वा । ते रात्रौ हंतारो दिव्येते [?] प्रतिदृश्यंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । प्रदोषं । रात्रिदोषा । रात्रिं प्रति तमसाभिभूतासु रात्रिषु तस्करा इव हिंसकाश्चोरा दृश्यंते यथा तद्वत् । कीदृशास्ते । अदृष्टा अपरिदृश्यमानाः विश्वदृष्टा विश्वं दृष्टं यैस्ते तादृशाः प्रतिदृश्यंते । अतो हे नराः प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन । भवत ॥

> *tye te ete sarpāḥ pratyadṛśran | pratidṛśyaṃte rātrau śvāsādiliṃgena | yadvā | te rātrau haṃtāro divyete [?] pratidṛśyaṃte | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | pradoṣaṃ | rātridoṣā | rātriṃ prati tamasābhibhūtāsu rātriṣu taskarā iva hiṃsakāścorā dṛśyaṃte yathā tadvat | kīdṛśāste | adṛṣṭā aparidṛśyamānāḥ viśvadṛṣṭā viśvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yaiste tādṛśāḥ pratidṛśyaṃte | ato he narāḥ pratibuddhā abhūtana | bhavata ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**त्ये ते (*tye te*)** — these venomous creatures described above. **प्रदोषं (*pradoṣaṃ*)** — in the pradoṣa time, accompanied by darkness. **तस्करा इव (*taskarā iva*)** — as thieves make themselves seen. **प्रत्यदृश्रन् (*pratyadṛśran*)** — (at night) they are known (by their breathing and the like); or, though not seen at night, they are seen in daytime. **अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*)** — though not looked at by others. **विश्वदृष्टाः (*viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*)** — all the rest they see too (therefore, O men). **प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन (*pratibuddhā abhūtana*)** — be very watchful.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

The venomous creatures described above are known at night, in the dusk full of darkness, by their breathing and the like, as thieves make themselves seen. Though it is not possible for others to see them, they themselves can see all the rest. Therefore, O men, all of you be watchful.

**Printed English** *(heading "English Translation")*

Or they may be discovered (in the dark), as thieves in the (dusk of) evening; for although they be unseen, yet all are seen by them; therefore, men, be vigilant.

*(Ṛk 5 is left open: Special Topics etc. follow on p. 345.)*
