जातवेदसं—जातानां वेदितारं जातधनं जातप्रज्ञं वा (*jātavedasaṃ—jātānāṃ veditāraṃ jātadhanaṃ jātaprajñaṃ vā*) —

(Kannada:) "Sāyaṇa explains this word in three ways: one who knows all that is produced; one who produces wealth (dhana); one who produces and increases knowledge and understanding."

(Kannada:) "The Nirukta-writer says: जातवेदाः कस्मात्, जातानि वेद, जातानि वैनं विदुः, जाते जाते विद्यते इति वा, जातवित्तो जातधनः, जातविद्यो जातप्रज्ञानः (*jātavedāḥ kasmāt, jātāni veda, jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ, jāte jāte vidyate iti vā, jātavitto jātadhanaḥ, jātavidyo jātaprajñānaḥ*). That is, he is omniscient because all that is produced in this world is known to him; he is called Jātavedas because all produced beings know him; because he is not absent in what is produced, he is in all produced things; he produces wealth; and he has by nature unsurpassed knowledge: thus four ways of meaning are explained. Durgācārya explains the derivation, saying that the word जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*) is formed from the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*) and from the root विद (*vida*), and cites the Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa sentence यत्त्रज्ञातः [?] पशूनविंदत तज्ज्ञातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वं (*yattrajñātaḥ [?] paśūnaviṃdata tajjñātavedaso jātavedastvaṃ*) (not translated in the source)."

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒भि त्वा॒ नक्ती॑रु॒षसो॑ ववाशि॒रेऽग्ने॑ व॒त्सं न स्वस॑रेषु धे॒नवः॑ ।
> दि॒व इ॒वेद॑र॒तिर्मानु॑षा यु॒गा क्षपो॑ भासि पुरुवार सं॒यतः॑ ॥ २ ॥

> *abhi tvā naktīruṣaso vavāśire 'gne vatsaṃ na svasareṣu dhenavaḥ |*
> *diva ivedaratirmānuṣā yugā kṣapo bhāsi puruvāra saṃyataḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अभि । त्वा । नक्तीः । उषसः । ववाशिरे । अग्ने । वत्सं । न । स्वसरेषु । धेनवः ।
> दिवः इव । इत् । अरतिः । मानुषा । युगा । आ । क्षपः । भासि । पुरुवार । संयतः ॥ २ ॥

> *abhi | tvā | naktīḥ | uṣasaḥ | vavāśire | agne | vatsaṃ | na | svasareṣu | dhenavaḥ |*
> *divaḥ iva | it | aratiḥ | mānuṣā | yugā | ā | kṣapaḥ | bhāsi | puruvāra | saṃyataḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Day and night, or evening and morning, or the days and nights themselves, long for Agni as cows long for their calves; the bhāṣya goes on to explain "pervading like heaven".

> हे अग्ने त्वा त्वामभि प्रति नक्तीः रात्रीरुषसोऽहानि । सर्वासु रात्रिषु सर्वेष्वप्यहस्सु । यद्वा नक्तशब्दः सायंकालं लक्षयति सायं प्रातरग्निहोत्रस्य सद्भावात् । सर्वेषु कालेषु सायंप्रातःकालेषु वा ववाशिरे । आकांक्षते यजमाना युष्टं [?] । यद्वा अहानि रात्रयश्च त्वामेव कामयंते होतुं । काले कर्मणश्चोदनात् कालानां कामनमुपचर्यते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । स्वसरेषु स्वयंसरणशीलेष्वहस्सु स्वसरणाधिकरणेषु गोष्ठेषु वा धेनवो वत्सं न । वत्समिव । किंच हे

> *he agne tvā tvāmabhi prati naktīḥ rātrīruṣaso 'hāni | sarvāsu rātriṣu sarveṣvapyahassu | yadvā naktaśabdaḥ sāyaṃkālaṃ lakṣayati sāyaṃ prātaragnihotrasya sadbhāvāt | sarveṣu kāleṣu sāyaṃprātaḥkāleṣu vā vavāśire | ākāṃkṣate yajamānā yuṣṭaṃ [?] | yadvā ahāni rātrayaśca tvāmeva kāmayaṃte hotuṃ | kāle karmaṇaścodanāt kālānāṃ kāmanamupacaryate | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | svasareṣu svayaṃsaraṇaśīleṣvahassu svasaraṇādhikaraṇeṣu goṣṭheṣu vā dhenavo vatsaṃ na | vatsamiva | kiṃca he*

*(The bhāṣya breaks off at किंच हे (*kiṃca he*) at the foot of the page and continues on p. 432. The word युष्टं (*yuṣṭaṃ*) after यजमाना (*yajamānā*) is read letter by letter from the strip, not zoomed. In the strip the compound before गोष्ठेषु (*goṣṭheṣu*) reads स्वसरणाधिकरणेषु (*svasaraṇādhikaraṇeṣu*); on p. 433 the quotation reads सुखसरणाधिकरणेषु (*sukhasaraṇādhikaraṇeṣu*), as printed.)*

### Printed p. 432 (PDF 453)

*(Header: "432", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. [?]" (the sūkta numeral looks like "೧" in the strip, although the sūkta is 2; not zoomed). Ṛk 2: bhāṣya concluded, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(continued)*

*Gist:* Agni, desired by many and self-controlled, pervades like heaven, to give oblations to the gods there; he shines in all human rites and all nights.

> पुरुवार बहुभिर्वरणीयाग्ने संयतो नियतस्त्वं दिव इव द्युलोकस्येवारतिः । व्याप्तो विस्तृतः । तत्रत्यानां देवानां हविःप्रदानायैव सर्वत्र व्याप्त इत्यर्थः । मानुषा मनुष्याणां यजमानानां संबंधीनि युगा युगानि । युगशब्दः कालोपलक्षकः । प्रातरादिसवनानि । सर्वेषु सवनेषु ॥ अत्यंतसंयोगे द्वितीया ॥ क्षपो रात्रीः । सर्वासु रात्रिष्वप्याभासि । समंताद्दीप्यसे ॥

> *puruvāra bahubhirvaraṇīyāgne saṃyato niyatastvaṃ diva iva dyulokasyevāratiḥ | vyāpto vistṛtaḥ | tatratyānāṃ devānāṃ haviḥpradānāyaiva sarvatra vyāpta ityarthaḥ | mānuṣā manuṣyāṇāṃ yajamānānāṃ saṃbaṃdhīni yugā yugāni | yugaśabdaḥ kālopalakṣakaḥ | prātarādisavanāni | sarveṣu savaneṣu ‖ atyaṃtasaṃyoge dvitīyā ‖ kṣapo rātrīḥ | sarvāsu rātriṣvapyābhāsi | samaṃtāddīpyase ‖*

*(Its tail, the remark अत्यंतसंयोगे द्वितीया (*atyaṃtasaṃyoge dvitīyā*) (the second case in the sense of continuous connection), is grammatical: characterized, not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वा अभि (*tvā abhi*) — [aiming at you; the Kannada prints ದ್ವೇಶಿಸಿ "having hated" [sic], evidently a misprint for ಉದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ "having aimed at", the word used in the Bhāvārtha]; नक्तीः (*naktīḥ*) — in the nights; उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*) — in the days too; स्वसरेषु (*svasareṣu*) — in the cow-stalls; धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) — cows; वत्सं न (*vatsaṃ na*) — as they love the calf and wish for its nearness; ववाशिरे (*vavāśire*) — (the sacrificers) seek your presence in order to perform the sacrifice; पुरुवार (*puruvāra*) — you who are desired by many people; संयतः (*saṃyataḥ*) — you who have a regulated conduct; दिव इव (*diva iva*) — like the heavenly world; अरतिः (*aratiḥ*) — you who are extensive; मानुषा (*mānuṣā*) — of men; युगा (*yugā*) — in the (sacrifice) times; क्षपः (*kṣapaḥ*) — in the nights; आ भासि (*ā bhāsi*) — you shine exceedingly.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, aiming at you, the sacrificers seek your presence in order to perform sacrifice, both in the nights and in the days, as cows in their stalls love the calf and wish for its nearness. You, who are desired by many people, who have a regulated conduct, and who are extensive like the heavenly world, shine exceedingly in the sacrifice-times of men and in the night-times."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

The mornings and evenings, Agni, are desirous (of worshipping) you, as cows in their stalls long for their calves: adored of many, you self-controlled, are verily spread through the sky: you (are present at all) the sacred rites of men, and shine brightly by night.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

नक्तीः—रात्रीः (*naktīḥ—rātrīḥ*) | उषसः—अहानि (*uṣasaḥ—ahāni*) | Agni — सर्वासु रात्रिषु सर्वेष्वप्यहस्सु (*sarvāsu rātriṣu sarveṣvapyahassu*) —

(Kannada:) "The first meaning is that Agni is desired and wished to be worshipped by the sacrificers in all nights and in all days; this has been set out in the sentence अभित्वा रात्रीरुषसो ववाशिरे (*abhitvā rātrīruṣaso vavāśire*) (as printed)."

(Kannada:) "In the second meaning: यद्वा नक्तशब्दः सायंकालं लक्षयति । सायं प्रातरग्निहोत्रस्य सद्भावात् (*yadvā naktaśabdaḥ sāyaṃkālaṃ lakṣayati | sāyaṃ prātaragnihotrasya sadbhāvāt*) — the meaning 'evening time' is given for the word नक्त (*nakta*). Those who perform the sacrifice, every" *(the sentence runs over to p. 433)*

### Printed p. 433 (PDF 454)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 20" as read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; "433". Ṛk 2 Special Topics continued and concluded. Numeral file: three rows, "Ni. 2-21", "Ni. 5-4" and "Ni. 3-13", all agreeing with the strip. At the foot: the signature mark "[28]" and "Vol. 14".)*

(Kannada, continued:) "…evening and morning, seek Agni in order to perform the homa: thus it is explained."

यद्वा अहानि रात्रयश्च त्वामेव कामयंते होतुं काले कर्मणश्चोदनात् कालानां कामनमुपचर्यते (*yadvā ahāni rātrayaśca tvāmeva kāmayaṃte hotuṃ kāle karmaṇaścodanāt kālānāṃ kāmanamupacaryate*) —

(Kannada:) "Even the insentient nights and days, following the injunction that agnihotra must be performed at the respective times, of their own accord seek Agni in order to worship him: thus the third meaning is explained. The injunction सायंप्रातेरग्निहोत्रं जुहुयोत् (*sāyaṃprāteragnihotraṃ juhuyot*) [?] (as read letter by letter from the strip, not zoomed; the last word may be the printing of जुहुयात् (*juhuyāt*)) teaches an indispensable duty in the matter of performing agnihotra; the seer of the mantra has expressed this very intention."

स्वसरेषु धेनवः वत्सं न (*svasareṣu dhenavaḥ vatsaṃ na*) —

(Kannada:) "In this sentence the word न (*na*) expresses comparison (upamāna). For the word स्वसर (*svasara*) the bhāṣya gives two kinds of meaning: स्वयं सरणशीलेषु अहस्सु (*svayaṃ saraṇaśīleṣu ahassu*), 'days that pass by of themselves'; or सुखसरणाधिकरणेषु गोष्ठेषु वा (*sukhasaraṇādhikaraṇeṣu goṣṭheṣu vā*) [as printed here], 'places for tying cows, fit for moving about comfortably'."

(Kannada:) "Yāska reads the word स्वसर (*svasara*) among the names of days (Ni. २-२१ (*2-21*) (*2-21*)) and explains the meaning: स्वसराण्यहानि भवन्ति स्वयं सारीण्यपि वा (*svasarāṇyahāni bhavanti svayaṃ sārīṇyapi vā*), and gives as example उस्रा इव स्वसराणि (*usrā iva svasarāṇi*) (Ni. ५-४ (*5-4*) (*5-4*)). The word स्वसर (*svasara*) is also read among the names of houses (Ni. ३-१३ (*3-13*) (*3-13*)). Just as milk-giving cows, at day and at night, long for their calves in order to suckle them, the sacrificers long for Agni, for the offering of oblations, at the evening and morning times: this is said by way of comparison."

(Kannada:) "Sāyaṇa explains the word अरतिः (*aratiḥ*) as 'pervading'. Agni, praised by many people and being regulated in manner, like the antarikṣa [as printed] pervades all regions: तत्रत्यानां देवानां हविः प्रदानायैव सर्वत्र व्याप्तिः (*tatratyānāṃ devānāṃ haviḥ pradānāyaiva sarvatra vyāptiḥ*) — to give oblations to the deities who are in the sky he pervades everywhere, and he shines abundantly at all times in the savanas beginning with the morning one, in the sacrifices performed by the sacrificers: this meaning is described by the sentence मानुषा युगा क्षपः आ भासि (*mānuṣā yugā kṣapaḥ ā bhāsi*)."

युगा युगानि । युगशब्दः कालोपलक्षकः । प्रातरादि सवनानि सर्वेषु सवनेषु (*yugā yugāni | yugaśabdaḥ kālopalakṣakaḥ | prātarādi savanāni sarveṣu savaneṣu*) —

(Kannada:) "That the word युग (*yuga*) denotes time, and that by it the morning, midday and third savanas are meant: this is the meaning explained."

(Kannada:) "By the word पुरुवार (*puruvāra*) the meaning that Agni is praised in many ways by many people is explained."

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तं दे॒वा बु॒ध्ने रज॑सः सु॒दंस॑सं दि॒वस्पृ॑थि॒व्योर॑र॒तिं न्ये॑रिरे ।
> रथ॑मिव॒ वेद्यं॑ शु॒क्रशो॑चिषम॒ग्निं मि॒त्रं न क्षि॒तिषु॑ प्र॒शंस्य॑म् ॥ ३ ॥

> *taṃ devā budhne rajasaḥ sudaṃsasaṃ divaspṛthivyoraratiṃ nyerire |*
> *rathamiva vedyaṃ śukraśociṣamagniṃ mitraṃ na kṣitiṣu praśaṃsyam ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तं । देवाः । बुध्ने । रजसः । सुऽदंससं । दिवःपृथिव्योः । अरतिं । नि । एरिरे ।
> रथंऽइव । वेद्यं । शुक्रऽशोचिषं । अग्निं । मित्रं । न । क्षितिषु । प्रऽशंस्यं ॥ ३ ॥

> *taṃ | devāḥ | budhne | rajasaḥ | su 'daṃsasaṃ | divaḥpṛthivyoḥ | aratiṃ | ni | erire |*
> *rathaṃ 'iva | vedyaṃ | śukra 'śociṣaṃ | agniṃ | mitraṃ | na | kṣitiṣu | pra 'śaṃsyaṃ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The gods, or the priests, establish the well-known Agni at the root of the earth, that is, on the altar; the bhāṣya then explains his epithets.

> तं प्रसिद्धमुक्तगुणविशिष्टमग्निं देवाः प्रसिद्धा व्यवहर्तार ऋत्विजो वा रजसो रंजनात्मकस्य लोकस्य बुध्ने मूले । पृथिव्यां वेद्यामित्यर्थः । तत्र न्येरिरे । नितरामीरयंति । व्यापारयंति स्वस्वहविर्लाभाय । ऋत्विक्पक्षे स्तोत्रादिना नितरां गच्छंति । भजंते । कीदृशमित्याह । सुदंससं शोभनदर्शनं दिवस्पृथिव्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योररतिं । ईश्वरं गंतारं व्याप्तं वा । वेद्यं । वेदो धनं । तस्मै हितं । रथमिव । रथं यथा स्वाभिमतलाभायाश्रयंते तद्वत् । यद्वा रथमिव प्राप्तिसाधनत्वेन वर्तमानं । वेद्यं वेदितव्यं । शुक्रशोचिषं दीप्तवर्णमग्निं मित्रं न सखिवत्कार्यसाधकं । यद्वा आदित्यमिव । क्षितिषु योगभूमिषु मनुष्येषु वा प्रशंस्यं । प्रकर्षेण स्तुत्यं । एवं महानुभावमग्निं न्येरिर इति ॥

> *taṃ prasiddhamuktaguṇaviśiṣṭamagniṃ devāḥ prasiddhā vyavahartāra ṛtvijo vā rajaso raṃjanātmakasya lokasya budhne mūle | pṛthivyāṃ vedyāmityarthaḥ | tatra nyerire | nitarāmīrayaṃti | vyāpārayaṃti svasvahavirlābhāya | ṛtvikpakṣe stotrādinā nitarāṃ gacchaṃti | bhajaṃte | kīdṛśamityāha | sudaṃsasaṃ śobhanadarśanaṃ divaspṛthivyordyāvāpṛthivyoraratiṃ | īśvaraṃ gaṃtāraṃ vyāptaṃ vā | vedyaṃ | vedo dhanaṃ | tasmai hitaṃ | rathamiva | rathaṃ yathā svābhimatalābhāyāśrayaṃte tadvat | yadvā rathamiva prāptisādhanatvena vartamānaṃ | vedyaṃ veditavyaṃ | śukraśociṣaṃ dīptavarṇamagniṃ mitraṃ na sakhivatkāryasādhakaṃ | yadvā ādityamiva | kṣitiṣu yogabhūmiṣu manuṣyeṣu vā praśaṃsyaṃ | prakarṣeṇa stutyaṃ | evaṃ mahānubhāvamagniṃ nyerira iti ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सुदंससं (सुदंससं (*sudaṃsasaṃ*)) — one of beautiful appearance (lit. having a beautiful sight); दिवस्पृथिव्योः (दिवस्पृथिव्योः (*divaspṛthivyoḥ*)) — between heaven and earth, throughout (being the lord); अरतिं (अरतिं (*aratiṃ*)) — one who pervades and moves about; रथमिव (रथमिव (*rathamiva*)) — (because he bears the oblation) like a chariot bearing a load; वेद्यं (वेद्यं (*vedyaṃ*)) — one who is to be known; शुक्रशोचिषं (शुक्रशोचिषं (*śukraśociṣaṃ*)) — one of shining lustre; क्षितिषु (क्षितिषु (*kṣitiṣu*)) — among men; प्रशंस्यं (प्रशंस्यं (*praśaṃsyaṃ*)) — highly praiseworthy; मित्रं न (मित्रं न (*mitraṃ na*)) — like a friend; तं अग्निं (तं अग्निं (*taṃ agniṃ*)) — that well-known Agni; देवाः (देवाः (*devāḥ*)) — the gods; रजसः (रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)) — of the earth, which is of the nature of delighting (रंजनात्मक (*raṃjanātmaka*)); बुध्ने (बुध्ने (*budhne*)) — at the root (in the altar); न्येरिरे (न्येरिरे (*nyerire*)) — establish.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "The one of beautiful appearance, the lord of heaven and earth who pervades and moves about everywhere, the one who is known like a chariot that bears a load, because he bears the oblation, the one of shining radiance," *(the sentence runs over to p. 435)*

### Printed p. 435 (PDF 456)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 20" as read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; "435". Ṛk 3: Bhāvārtha concluded, printed English, Special Topics. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

(Kannada, continued:) "…the one who is like a most praiseworthy friend among men, and who is well known — that Agni the gods established on the altar, the root-part of the earth, which is of the nature of delighting."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

The gods have stationed at the root of the world, that Agni who is of goodly appearance ; the pervader of heaven and earth ; who is to be known as a car (to convey men to their wishes), who shines with pure radiance, and who is to be honoured as a friend amongst mankind.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

देवाः रजसः बुध्ने तं न्येरिरे (*devāḥ rajasaḥ budhne taṃ nyerire*) —

(Kannada:) "In this sentence Sāyaṇa has explained, for the word deva, the words व्यवहर्तारः ऋत्विजो वा (*vyavahartāraḥ ṛtvijo vā*): that the well-known gods praise Agni abundantly, on the altar that is the earth, in order to obtain their respective shares of the oblations — one kind of meaning. When he gives another kind of meaning for the word deva, 'priests', he says स्तोत्रादिना नितरां गच्छंति भजंते (*stotrādinā nitarāṃ gacchaṃti bhajaṃte*): the priests serve Agni, who has great glory, with hymns. Thus he has explained the second meaning also."

दिवस्पृथिव्योः अरतिं (*divaspṛthivyoḥ aratiṃ*) — द्यावापृथिव्योः ईश्वरं गंतारं व्याप्तं वा (*dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ īśvaraṃ gaṃtāraṃ vyāptaṃ vā*) —

(Kannada:) "Agni is the lord of earth and antarikṣa (भूम्यंतरिक्ष); he moves in earth and antarikṣa; he pervades heaven and earth. Since three kinds of meaning have been explained, the greatness of Agni is described."

रथमिव वेद्यं (*rathamiva vedyaṃ*) —

(Kannada:) "In this sentence the word veda has been explained as 'wealth'. स्वाभिमतलाभाय रथं यथा आश्रयंते (*svābhimatalābhāya rathaṃ yathā āśrayaṃte*): as a chariot is a support for men for obtaining what they desire, Agni is the giver of wealth — the meaning is expanded by showing this comparison. यद्वा रथमिव प्राप्तिसाधनत्वेन वेद्यं (*yadvā rathamiva prāptisādhanatvena vedyaṃ*): as a chariot is a means of accomplishing benefit for men, so Agni too is known by men as the accomplisher of benefit. Thus two kinds of meaning are described."

मित्रं न शुक्रशोचिषं (*mitraṃ na śukraśociṣaṃ*) —

(Kannada:) "It is explained that Agni accomplishes the work for the sacrificers like a friend."

मित्रं न क्षितिषु प्रशंस्यं (*mitraṃ na kṣitiṣu praśaṃsyaṃ*) —

(Kannada:) "In this sentence the word mitra is used in the sense of Āditya; having explained the meaning thus, and having said that Agni, like Āditya, is worthy of unsurpassed praise in the sacrificial grounds (on earth) or among men, Sāyaṇa has established the comparison of Agni with a friend or with Āditya. The greatness of Agni is explained to be of this kind." *(This Special Topic runs over to p. 436.)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तमु॒क्षमा॑णं॒ रज॑सि॒ स्व आ दमे॑ चं॒द्रमि॑व सु॒रुचं॑ ह्वा॒र आ द॑धुः ।
> पृश्न्याः॑ पत॒रं चि॒तयं॑तम॒क्षभिः॑ पा॒थो न पा॒युं जन॑सी उ॒भे अनु॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> *tamukṣamāṇaṃ rajasi sva ā dame caṃdramiva surucaṃ hvāra ā dadhuḥ |*
> *pṛśnyāḥ pataraṃ citayaṃtamakṣabhiḥ pātho na pāyuṃ janasī ubhe anu ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तं । उक्षमाणं । रजसि । स्वे । आ । दमे । चंद्रंऽइव । सुऽरुचं । ह्वारे । आ । दधुः ।
> पृश्न्याः । पतरं । चितयंतं । अक्षऽभिः । पाथः । न । पायुं । जनसी इति । उभे इति । अनु ॥

> *taṃ | ukṣamāṇaṃ | rajasi | sve | ā | dame | caṃdraṃ 'iva | su 'rucaṃ | hvāre | ā | dadhuḥ |*
> *pṛśnyāḥ | pataraṃ | citayaṃtaṃ | akṣa 'bhiḥ | pāthaḥ | na | pāyuṃ | janasī iti | ubhe iti | anu ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The priests place Agni, who is sprinkled with ghee and shines like gold, in the sacrificial house; he moves in the sky, protects like water, and pervades heaven and earth.

> तं स्तुत्यतरं रजस्यंतरिक्ष आ उक्षमाणं सर्वतः सिंचंतं वृष्टिजलं रजसि पृथिव्यां वेद्यां घृतादिनासिच्यमानं वा । स्वे स्वकीये ह्वारे विजने दमे यागगृह आदधुः । आदधते । कीदृशं तं । चंद्रमिव सुरुचं । चंद्रमिति हिरण्यनाम । हिरण्यमिव शोभनदीप्तिं । सश्चात्स्पृद्धावस्थायां [?] पृश्न्याः पतरं । द्युलोकस्यांतरिक्षस्य गंतारं । अक्षभिः स्वकीयैर्ज्वालारूपैरवयवैश्चितयंतं चेतयमानं । पाथो न पायुं । उदकमिव रक्षकं । उभे जनसी सर्वस्य जनयित्र्यौ द्यावापृथिव्यावनु व्याप्तं । भूम्यां होमाधारत्वेन स्थित्वा हविष्प्रेषणाय द्युलोकगामिनमिति भावः । एवंरूपमग्निमादधते ॥

> *taṃ stutyataraṃ rajasyaṃtarikṣa ā ukṣamāṇaṃ sarvataḥ siṃcaṃtaṃ vṛṣṭijalaṃ rajasi pṛthivyāṃ vedyāṃ ghṛtādināsicyamānaṃ vā | sve svakīye hvāre vijane dame yāgagṛha ādadhuḥ | ādadhate | kīdṛśaṃ taṃ | caṃdramiva surucaṃ | caṃdramiti hiraṇyanāma | hiraṇyamiva śobhanadīptiṃ | saścātspṛddhāvasthāyāṃ [?] pṛśnyāḥ pataraṃ | dyulokasyāṃtarikṣasya gaṃtāraṃ | akṣabhiḥ svakīyairjvālārūpairavayavaiścitayaṃtaṃ cetayamānaṃ | pātho na pāyuṃ | udakamiva rakṣakaṃ | ubhe janasī sarvasya janayitryau dyāvāpṛthivyāvanu vyāptaṃ | bhūmyāṃ homādhāratvena sthitvā haviṣpreṣaṇāya dyulokagāminamiti bhāvaḥ | evaṃrūpamagnimādadhate ‖*

*(The word सश्चात्स्पृद्धावस्थायां (सश्चात्स्पृद्धावस्थायां (*saścātspṛddhāvasthāyāṃ*)) is given as read letter by letter, not zoomed; the first letter looks like स (*sa*) and the sense is unclear to me [?].)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

चंद्रमिव (चंद्रमिव (*caṃdramiva*)) — like gold; सुरुचं (सुरुचं (*surucaṃ*)) — one of excellent radiance; पृश्न्याः (पृश्न्याः (*pṛśnyāḥ*)) — in the antarikṣa; पतरं (पतरं (*pataraṃ*)) — one who moves about; अक्षभिः (अक्षभिः (*akṣabhiḥ*)) — with his limbs in the form of flames; चितयंतं (चितयंतं (*citayaṃtaṃ*)) — *(the entry breaks off at the foot of the page and continues on p. 437; Ṛk 4 is left open at its Pratipadārtha)*

### Printed p. 437 (PDF 458)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 20" as read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; "437". Ṛk 4: Pratipadārtha concluded, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics. Numeral file: four rows, "Ni. 2-10", "Ni. 2-18", "Ni. 3-22" and "Ni. 2-13", all agreeing with the strip.)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued from p. 436:)* चितयंतं (*citayaṃtaṃ*) — one who gives animation (चैतन्य); पाथो न (*pātho na*) — like water; पायुं (*pāyuṃ*) — a protector; उभे जनसी (*ubhe janasī*) — both heaven and earth, the mothers of all; अनु (*anu*) — one who pervades; रजसि (*rajasi*) — in the antarikṣa; आ उक्षमाणं (*ā ukṣamāṇaṃ*) — one who pours down rain everywhere; तं (*taṃ*) — that venerable Agni; स्वे ह्वारे (*sve hvāre*) — in his own solitary; दमे (*dame*) — in the sacrificial house; आ दधुः (*ā dadhuḥ*) — they establish.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "Of the one whose radiance is as excellent as gold, who moves in the antarikṣa, who gives animation with his limbs in the form of flames, who protects like water, who pervades heaven and earth, the mothers of all, who pours rain everywhere in the antarikṣa, the venerable one — that Agni they establish in the sacrificial house, which is his own and solitary."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

They have placed him in his solitary dwelling, who is shedding moisture upon the earth ; resplendent as gold, traversing the firmament, animate with flames ; and pervading the two parents (of all things, heaven and earth) like refreshing water.

*(The scan has small blemishes in the words "parents" and "things" on the last printed line; no misprint is intended by the source. The English sentence runs to the top of the next strip, "like refreshing water.")*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

चंद्रमिव सुरुचं उक्षमाणं तं दमे आ दधुः (चंद्रमिव सुरुचं उक्षमाणं तं दमे आ दधुः (*caṃdramiva surucaṃ ukṣamāṇaṃ taṃ dame ā dadhuḥ*)) —

(Kannada:) "In this sentence, since the word candra (चंद्र (*caṃdra*)) is read among the fifteen names of hiraṇya (Ni. २-१० (*2-10*)), Agni is very radiant, like hiraṇya (gold). And, being in the antarikṣa, he pours down rain-water everywhere; or, on the sacrificial altar, which is of the nature of the earth, he obtains satisfaction from the homa-substances beginning with ājya: thus two kinds of meaning are described. For the word रजसि (रजसि (*rajasi*)) Yāska has given the meaning 'night' (Ni. २-१८ (*2-18*)) and also 'heaven and earth' (Ni. ३-२२ (*3-22*)). Sāyaṇa here has given this word the meaning 'heaven and earth' [as printed; the bhāṣya above reads it as antarikṣa]."

पाथो न पायुं (पाथो न पायुं (*pātho na pāyuṃ*)) —

(Kannada:) "On the sacrificial altar Agni grows with his limbs in the form of flames, and, pervading the antarikṣa, protects everyone as water does. This is set out in the words भूम्यां होमाधारत्वेन स्थित्वा हविष्प्रेषणाय द्युलोकगामिनं (भूम्यां होमाधारत्वेन स्थित्वा हविष्प्रेषणाय द्युलोकगामिनं (*bhūmyāṃ homādhāratvena sthitvā haviṣpreṣaṇāya dyulokagāminaṃ*)): standing on the earth as the support of the homa, and moving in the antarikṣa in order to carry the oblations to the deities, he pervades both earth and antarikṣa and protects everyone."

पृश्न्याः पतरं (पृश्न्याः पतरं (*pṛśnyāḥ pataraṃ*)) —

(Kannada:) "The word pṛśni (पृश्नि (*pṛśni*)) is read among the six common names beginning with स्वः (स्वः (*svaḥ*)) (Ni. २-१३ (*2-13*)). Here Sāyaṇa explains पृश्न्याः पतरं द्युलोकस्यांतरिक्षस्य गंतारं (पृश्न्याः पतरं द्युलोकस्यांतरिक्षस्य गंतारं (*pṛśnyāḥ pataraṃ dyulokasyāṃtarikṣasya gaṃtāraṃ*)): Agni pervades the antarikṣa and moves about in it."

*(The Special Topic on the word दमे continues on p. 438.)*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स होता॒ विश्वं॒ परि॑ भूत्वध्व॒रं तमु॑ ह॒व्यैर्मनु॑ष ऋंजते गि॒रा ।

> *sa hotā viśvaṃ pari bhūtvadhvaraṃ tamu havyairmanuṣa ṛṃjate girā |*
> *hiriśipro vṛdhasānāsu jarbhuraddyaurna stṛbhiścitayadrodasī anu ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(In the print the bar between अध्वरं and तं is absent: "अध्वरं तं"; in स्तृभिः a small subscript mark stands between the syllables, as in the compound हिरिऽशिप्रः; I give स्तृभिः without it.)*

> सः । होता । विश्वं । परि । भूतु । अध्वरं तं । ऊं इति । हव्यैः । मनुषः । ऋंजते । गिरा ।
> हिरिऽशिप्रः । वृधसानासु । जर्भुरत् । द्यौः । न । स्तृभिः । चितयत् । रोदसी इति । अनु ॥ ५ ॥

> *saḥ | hotā | viśvaṃ | pari | bhūtu | adhvaraṃ taṃ | ūṃ iti | havyaiḥ | manuṣaḥ | ṛṃjate | girā |*
> *hiri 'śipraḥ | vṛdhasānāsu | jarbhurat | dyauḥ | na | stṛbhiḥ | citayat | rodasī iti | anu ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* May Agni, accomplisher of the homa, encompass every sacrifice; men adorn him with oblations and praise; he consumes the growing plants and, like the sky with stars, enlivens heaven and earth with flames and sparks.

> सोऽग्निर्होता होमनिष्पादकः सन् विश्वं सर्वमध्वरं यागं परिभूतु । परितो भवतु । तमु तमेवाग्निं हव्यैर्हविर्भिर्गिरा स्तुत्या च मनुषो मनुष्या ऋंजते । प्रसाधयंति ॥ ऋंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा ॥ हिरिशिप्रो हरणशीलहनुर्दीप्तोष्णीषो वा । शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः । ५.५४-११ । इत्यादिमंत्रांतरात् । वृधसानासु प्रवर्धमानास्वोषधीषु ज्वालासु वा जर्भुरत् । पूर्यमाणो यज्ञं गंता ॥ शत्रंतं [?] पदं । यद्वा द्वितीयार्थे सप्तमी ॥ वर्धमाना ओषधीर्जर्भुरत् । पुनः पुनर्दहन्नित्यर्थः । द्यौर्द्युलोकांतरिक्षं स्तृभिर्नक्षत्रैरिव रोदसी अनु द्यावापृथिव्यावनु चितयत् । चेतयति । ज्वालाभिर्विस्फुलिंगैश्च भुवमंतरिक्षं च व्याप्नोतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *so 'gnirhotā homaniṣpādakaḥ san viśvaṃ sarvamadhvaraṃ yāgaṃ paribhūtu | parito bhavatu | tamu tamevāgniṃ havyairhavirbhirgirā stutyā ca manuṣo manuṣyā ṛṃjate | prasādhayaṃti ‖ ṛṃjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā ‖ hiriśipro haraṇaśīlahanurdīptoṣṇīṣo vā | śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayīḥ | 5.54-11 | ityādimaṃtrāṃtarāt | vṛdhasānāsu pravardhamānāsvoṣadhīṣu jvālāsu vā jarbhurat | pūryamāṇo yajñaṃ gaṃtā ‖ śatraṃtaṃ [?] padaṃ | yadvā dvitīyārthe saptamī ‖ vardhamānā oṣadhīrjarbhurat | punaḥ punardahannityarthaḥ | dyaurdyulokāṃtarikṣaṃ stṛbhirnakṣatrairiva rodasī anu dyāvāpṛthivyāvanu citayat | cetayati | jvālābhirvisphuliṃgaiśca bhuvamaṃtarikṣaṃ ca vyāpnotītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read letter by letter from the strip, not zoomed: the grammatical remark शत्रंतं [?] पदं may be the printing of शतृंतं, "a word ending in the śatṛ suffix"; the sentence ends with "…चितयत् । चेतयति" as printed, and the Kannada Special Topics on p. 439 explain the passage. The bhāṣya reading हरणशीलहनुर्दीप्तोष्णीषो is as read here; the Special Topics on p. 439 quote it without हनुः.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सः (*saḥ*) — Agni; होता (*hotā*) — as the accomplisher of the homa; विश्वं अध्वरं (*viśvaṃ adhvaraṃ*) — all sacrifices; परि भूतु (*pari bhūtu*) — may he stand encompassing them; तमु (*tamu*) — that same Agni; हव्यैः (*havyaiḥ*) — with oblations; गिरा (*girā*) — and with praise as well; मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*) — men; ऋंजते (*ṛṃjate*) — adorn; हिरिशिप्रः (*hiriśipraḥ*) — the Agni with a radiant flame *(the entry continues on p. 439)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued:)* वृधसानासु (*vṛdhasānāsu*) — in the thicket of densely grown plants; जर्भुरत् (*jarbhurat*) — burning; स्तृभिः (*stṛbhiḥ*) — with the stars; द्यौः न (*dyauḥ na*) — as one makes the antarikṣa radiant; रोदसी अनु (*rodasī anu*) — both heaven and earth; चितयत् (*citayat*) — he makes them endowed with animation.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "May Agni, the accomplisher of the homa, stand encompassing all the sacrifices. Men adorn that same Agni with oblations and with praise. Agni, with his radiant flame, burning the thicket of densely grown plants, makes heaven and earth endowed with animation, as one makes the antarikṣa radiant with stars."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

May he, the presenter of oblations (to the gods), be around all sacrifices ; men propitiate him with oblations and with praises, when blazing with radiant tresses amongst the growing plants, and enlivening heaven and earth (with his sparks), like the sky with stars.

*(The scan blurs the word "his" in "his sparks"; no misprint is certain.)*

(Kannada:) "Agni is one among the priests (ṛtvij), called the hotṛ; the meaning that he is the one denoted by the word hotṛ, which indicates this priest, has been given here for the word होता (होता (*hotā*)). The meaning 'accomplisher of homa' has also been explained. It is described that men worship this Agni with हव्यैः गिरा ऋंजते (हव्यैः गिरा ऋंजते (*havyaiḥ girā ṛṃjate*)), 'with oblations and with praise', so that he may be pleased."

(Kannada:) "It is explained that Agni, pleasing to the mind, wears a very radiant uṣṇīṣa (turban). Here, for the word शिप्र (शिप्र (*śipra*)), the meaning uṣṇīṣa (a turban, 'rumāl') is given, and the use of this word in this meaning is shown by the following —"

अंसेषु वा ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षस्सु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः ।
अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ॥

वृधसानासु जर्भुरत् (वृधसानासु जर्भुरत् (*vṛdhasānāsu jarbhurat*)) — प्रवर्धमानास्वोषधीषु ज्वालासु वा पूर्यमाणो यज्ञं गंता । यद्वा द्वितीयार्थे सप्तमी । वर्धमाना ओषधीः पुनः पुनः दर्ह (दर्ह (*darha*) — as printed) —

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स नो॑ रे॒वत्स॑मिधा॒नः स्व॒स्तये॑ संदद॒स्वान्र॒यिम॒स्मासु॑ दीदिहि ।
> आ नः॑ कृणुष्व सुवि॒ताय॒ रोद॑सी॒ अग्ने॑ ह॒व्या मनु॑षो देव वी॒तये॑ ॥ ६ ॥

> *sa no revatsamidhānaḥ svastaye saṃdadasvānrayimasmāsu dīdihi |*
> *ā naḥ kṛṇuṣva suvitāya rodasī agne havyā manuṣo deva vītaye ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । नः । रेवत् । संऽइधानः । स्वस्तये । संऽददस्वान् । रयिं । अस्मासु । दीदिहि ।
> आ । नः । कृणुष्व । सुविताय । रोदसी इति । अग्ने । हव्या । मनुषः । देव । वीतये ॥ ६ ॥

> *saḥ | naḥ | revat | saṃ 'idhānaḥ | svastaye | saṃ 'dadasvān | rayiṃ | asmāsu | dīdihi |*
> *ā | naḥ | kṛṇuṣva | suvitāya | rodasī iti | agne | havyā | manuṣaḥ | deva | vītaye ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, kindled by us, is asked to give wealth fit for giving and shine; to make heaven and earth bestowers of enjoyment, so that the sacrificer's oblations reach the gods.

> हे अग्ने स तादृशस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं स्वस्तये । स्वस्तीत्यविनाशनाम । क्षेमाय रेवद्रयिमद्रयिं धनं उपर्युपरिवृद्धिमद्दानयोग्यं वा धनमस्मासु संददस्वान् सम्यक् प्रयच्छन् समिधानोऽस्माभिः सम्यगिध्यमानः सन् दीदिहि । दीप्यस्व । यद्वा रेवदिति क्रियाविशेषणं । रा धनं समृद्धिमद्यथा तथा दीप्यस्वेति । तथाभूतः सन् नोऽस्मभ्यं सुविताय सुहिताय शोभनफलाय रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावाकृणुष्व । सर्वतः कुरुष्व । उभौ लोकौ भोगप्रदौ कुर्वित्यर्थः । किमर्थमिति तदुच्यते । हे देवाग्ने मनुषो मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य मम संबंधीनि हव्या हवींषि वीतये देवेभ्यो भक्षणाय । पुनःपुनर्यागाद्यनुष्ठानायेत्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne sa tādṛśastvaṃ no 'smākaṃ svastaye | svastītyavināśanāma | kṣemāya revadrayimadrayiṃ dhanaṃ uparyuparivṛddhimaddānayogyaṃ vā dhanamasmāsu saṃdadasvān samyak prayacchan samidhāno 'smābhiḥ samyagidhyamānaḥ san dīdihi | dīpyasva | yadvā revaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ | rā dhanaṃ samṛddhimadyathā tathā dīpyasveti | tathābhūtaḥ san no 'smabhyaṃ suvitāya suhitāya śobhanaphalāya rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyāvākṛṇuṣva | sarvataḥ kuruṣva | ubhau lokau bhogapradau kurvityarthaḥ | kimarthamiti taducyate | he devāgne manuṣo manuṣyasya yajamānasya mama saṃbaṃdhīni havyā havīṃṣi vītaye devebhyo bhakṣaṇāya | punaḥpunaryāgādyanuṣṭhānāyetyarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सः (*saḥ*) — (O Agni) one who has the qualities described above; नः (*naḥ*) — our; स्वस्तये (*svastaye*) — for welfare; रेवत् रयिं (*revat rayiṃ*) — wealth that has increased and is fit for giving; अस्मासु (*asmāsu*) — to us; संददस्वान् (*saṃdadasvān*) — while giving; समिधानः (*samidhānaḥ*) — (kindled by us) blazing; दीदिहि (*dīdihi*) — shine.

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 21" as read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; "441". The numeral file has no rows. Ṛk 6: Pratipadārtha concluded, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued from p. 440:)* नः (*naḥ*) — to us; सुविताय (*suvitāya*) — for giving an excellent fruit; रोदसी (*rodasī*) — heaven and earth; आ कृणुष्व (*ā kṛṇuṣva*) — make them bestowers of enjoyment; देव (*deva*) — O shining; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*) — offered by the sacrificer; हव्या (*havyā*) — the oblations; वीतये (*vītaye*) — for the eating of the deities — make them fit for it.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, of the nature of a deity, for our welfare may you, attaining increase and giving us wealth fit for giving, shine, kindled by us. For giving us an excellent fruit, make heaven and earth bestowers of enjoyment, and make the oblations offered by the sacrificer fit for the eating of the deities."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

You, Agni, are he who, for our good, is possessed of riches ; kindled by us, blaze as the liberal donor of wealth to us : render heaven earth [sic, no "and"] propitious to us, so that divine Agni, (the gods) may partake of the oblations of the institutor of the rite.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) "The wish of the ṛtvijs, 'May Agni, for their welfare, be one who favours (grants) wealth increasing from day to day, and one abundantly served by them, and may he prosper', is described. In this meaning the word रेवत् (*revat*) is an adjective of the word रयिं (*rayiṃ*). Taking the word रेवत् (*revat*) as an adverb in सः नः स्वस्तये रेवत् दीदिहि (*saḥ naḥ svastaye revat dīdihi*) and रा धनं समृद्धिमत् यथा तथा दीप्यस्व (*rā dhanaṃ samṛddhimat yathā tathā dīpyasva*), a second meaning is also described: 'for the welfare of us the ṛtvijs, may Agni, who brings his favour to light so that wealth is abundant, prosper well.'"

नः सुविताय रोदसी कृणुष्व (*naḥ suvitāya rodasī kṛṇuṣva*) — अस्मभ्यं सुविताय शोभनफलाय द्यावापृथिव्यौ उभौ लोकौ भोगप्रदौ कुर्विन्त्यर्थः (*asmabhyaṃ suvitāya śobhanaphalāya dyāvāpṛthivyau ubhau lokau bhogapradau kurvintyarthaḥ*) —

*(The last word of the quotation is as read from the strip: कुर्विन्त्यर्थः as printed in the Special Topics, against कुर्वित्यर्थः in the bhāṣya above; not zoomed.)*

(Kannada:) "The wish of the ṛtvijs and the sacrificers, 'May Agni favour so that the two worlds, earth and antarikṣa, be agreeable for our welfare and for other excellent good', is described here. And Agni's subjugation (vaśīkāra) of heaven and earth, in the form of favour, —"

मनुषः हव्या वीतये (*manuṣaḥ havyā vītaye*) — मनुष्यस्य मम यजमानस्य संबंधीनि हवींषि देवेभ्यो भक्षणाय (*manuṣyasya mama yajamānasya saṃbaṃdhīni havīṃṣi devebhyo bhakṣaṇāya*) —

(Kannada:) "— the wish that the sacrificer, a man, may attain fulfilment (caritārtha) through oblations offered by him and directed to the deities, is explained."

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> दा नो॑ अग्ने बृह॒तो दाः स॑ह॒स्रिणो॑ दु॒रो न वाजं॒ श्रुत्या॒ अपा॑ वृधि ।
> प्राची॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ब्रह्म॑णा कृधि॒ स्व१॒॑र्ण शु॒क्रमु॒षसो॒ वि दि॑द्युतः ॥ ७ ॥

> *dā no agne bṛhato dāḥ sahasriṇo duro na vājaṃ śrutyā apā vṛdhi |*
> *prācī dyāvāpṛthivī brahmaṇā kṛdhi svarṇa śukramuṣaso vi didyutaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> दाः । नः । अग्ने । बृहतः । दाः । सहस्रिणः । दुरः । न । वाजं । श्रुत्यै । अप । वृधि ।
> प्राची इति । द्यावापृथिवी इति । ब्रह्मणा । कृधि । स्वः । न । शुक्रं । उषसः । वि । दिद्युतः ॥ ७ ॥

> *dāḥ | naḥ | agne | bṛhataḥ | dāḥ | sahasriṇaḥ | duraḥ | na | vājaṃ | śrutyai | apa | vṛdhi |*
> *prācī iti | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | brahmaṇā | kṛdhi | svaḥ | na | śukraṃ | uṣasaḥ | vi | didyutaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

*(The Saṃhitā reads श्रुत्या अपा; the Pada reads श्रुत्यै । अप, as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni is asked to give abundant wealth and thousands of sons and servants; to open the doors of food and fame; to make heaven and earth favourable by sacrifice; the dawns kindle him, shining like the sun.

*(Two places in the bhāṣya are doubtful letter by letter, not zoomed: लुजि [?] (*luji [?]*) in the grammatical remark, and the word उषःकालाः [?] (*uṣaḥkālāḥ [?]*) near the end.)*

> हे अग्ने नोऽस्मभ्यं बृहतो महतः प्रभूतान् गवाश्वादिधनविशेषान् दाः । देहि । तथा सहस्रिणः सहस्रसंख्योपेतान्पुत्रभृत्यादीन्दाः देहि ॥ ददातेश्छांदसे लुजि [?] रूपं । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥ श्रुत्यै कीर्त्यै वाजमन्नं दुरो न तस्य द्वाराण्यपि ॥ नशब्दश्चार्थे ॥ अपावृधि आपवृणु । प्रेरयेत्यर्थः । यद्वा द्वाराणीव । तत्प्राप्त्युपायान्विशदयति । तदर्थं द्यावापृथिवी ब्रह्मणा परिवृद्धेन कर्मणा प्राची प्रकृष्टांचने । अस्मदनुकूले कृधि । कुरु । स्वर्ण आदित्य इव । स यथा जगत्प्रकाशयति तद्वत् । शुक्रं दीप्तं त्वामुषस उषःकालाः [?] विदिद्युतः । विद्योतयंति । उषःकाले ह्यग्नयः प्रज्वाल्यंते ॥

> *he agne no 'smabhyaṃ bṛhato mahataḥ prabhūtān gavāśvādidhanaviśeṣān dāḥ | dehi | tathā sahasriṇaḥ sahasrasaṃkhyopetānputrabhṛtyādīndāḥ dehi ‖ dadāteśchāṃdase luji [?] rūpaṃ | vākyabhedādanighātaḥ ‖ śrutyai kīrtyai vājamannaṃ duro na tasya dvārāṇyapi ‖ naśabdaścārthe ‖ apāvṛdhi āpavṛṇu | prerayetyarthaḥ | yadvā dvārāṇīva | tatprāptyupāyānviśadayati | tadarthaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī brahmaṇā parivṛddhena karmaṇā prācī prakṛṣṭāṃcane | asmadanukūle kṛdhi | kuru | svarṇa āditya iva | sa yathā jagatprakāśayati tadvat | śukraṃ dīptaṃ tvāmuṣasa uṣaḥkālāḥ [?] vididyutaḥ | vidyotayaṃti | uṣaḥkāle hyagnayaḥ prajvālyaṃte ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*) — abundant cattle, horses and the like; दाः (*dāḥ*) — give; सहस्रिणः (*sahasriṇaḥ*) — of the number of a thousand; sons, servants and the like; दाः (*dāḥ*) — give; श्रुत्यै (*śrutyai*) — for bringing fame; अन्नं (*annaṃ*) — of food; दुरो न (*duro na*) — the doors as well; अपा वृधि (*apā vṛdhi*) — open (for that); द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*) — heaven and earth; ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*) — by sacrificial and other rites; प्राची (*prācī*) — so that they may be favourable to us; कृधि (*kṛdhi*) — make; स्वर्ण (*svarṇa*) — as the Sun illumines the world; शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*) — you who are radiant; उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*) — the dawns; वि दिद्युतः (*vi didyutaḥ*) — cause to shine.

*(Ṛk 7 is left open: Bhāvārtha, printed English and Special Topics follow on p. 443.)*

### Printed p. 443 (PDF 464)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 21" as read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; "443". The numeral file has no rows for this page. Ṛk 7 concludes: Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, give us abundant cattle, horses and the like. Give us sons, servants and the like, thousands in number. Open the door of food for fame. By rites that bring abundant merit, make heaven and earth favourable to us. As the Sun makes the world shine, the dawns make you, radiant, shine."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Bestow upon us, Agni, infinite possessions : grant us thousands (of cattle and dopendants [sic]) : open to us, for your reputation, the doors of abundance : make heaven and earth, propitiated by sacred prayer, favourable to us, and may the mornings light you up like the sun.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) "In this Ṛk, the words बृहतः—महतः प्रभूतान् गवाश्वादिधनविशेषान् (*bṛhataḥ—mahataḥ prabhūtān gavāśvādidhanaviśeṣān*) are given. For the word बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*) the meaning 'abundant cattle, horses and the like, wealth' is described, and the wish is expressed that Agni may bestow this kind of wealth in thousands (सहस्र (*sahasra*))."

श्रुत्यै वाजं दुरो न अपावृधि (*śrutyai vājaṃ duro na apāvṛdhi*) — कीर्त्यै अन्नं तस्य द्वाराण्यपि अपवृणु । यद्वा द्वाराणीव तत्प्राप्त्युपायान् विशदय । (*kīrtyai annaṃ tasya dvārāṇyapi apavṛṇu | yadvā dvārāṇīva tatprāptyupāyān viśadaya |*)

(Kannada:) "In this sentence, giving the word न (*na*) the senses of 'and' (samuccaya) and 'like' (upamā), one meaning is described: may Agni favour food for fame, or the means by which food is obtained. Then, 'the ways by which food is obtained, that is, the means by which it is obtained (show), may he favour so that they become clear to the understanding' is also described."

द्यावापृथिवी ब्रह्मणा प्राची कृधि (*dyāvāpṛthivī brahmaṇā prācī kṛdhi*) — (Kannada:) "In this sentence, for the word ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*) the meaning is explained as परिवृढेन कर्मणा (*parivṛḍhena karmaṇā*) [as printed in the bold heading; the bhāṣya above has परिवृद्धेन (*parivṛddhena*)], an abundant rite that brings merit; and the wish is expressed that Agni may make earth and antarikṣa favourable to us by our performance of rites."

स्वर्ण शुक्रमुषसो विदिद्युतः (*svarṇa śukramuṣaso vididyutaḥ*) — उषःकालाः दीप्तं त्वा आदित्य इव विद्योतयंति । उषःकाले ह्यग्नयः प्रज्वाल्यंते । (*uṣaḥkālāḥ dīptaṃ tvā āditya iva vidyotayaṃti | uṣaḥkāle hyagnayaḥ prajvālyaṃte |*)

(Kannada:) "For the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) the meaning Āditya is explained. As the Sun shines at the dawns with his own rays, so the dawn makes Agni shine with his rays, it is described."

*(Rule line.)*

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स इ॑धा॒न उ॒षसो॒ राम्या॒ अनु॒ स्व१॒॑र्ण दी॑देदरु॒षेण॑ भा॒नुना॑ ।
> होत्रा॑भिर॒ग्निर्मनु॑षः स्वध्व॒रो राजा॑ वि॒शामति॑थि॒श्चारु॑रा॒यवे॑ ॥ ८ ॥

> *sa idhāna uṣaso rāmyā anu svarṇa dīdedaruṣeṇa bhānunā |*
> *hotrābhiragnirmanuṣaḥ svadhvaro rājā viśāmatithiścārurāyave ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । इधानः । उषसः । राम्याः । अनु । स्वः । न । दीदेत् । अरुषेण । भानुना ।
> होत्राभिः । अग्निः । मनुषः । सुऽअध्वरः । राजा । विशां । अतिथिः । चारुः । आयवे ॥ ८ ॥

> *saḥ | idhānaḥ | uṣasaḥ | rāmyāḥ | anu | svaḥ | na | dīdet | aruṣeṇa | bhānunā |*
> *hotrābhiḥ | agniḥ | manuṣaḥ | su 'adhvaraḥ | rājā | viśāṃ | atithiḥ | cāruḥ | āyave ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, kindled at the dawns, shines like the sun; praised with hymns, he is lord of the people and a pleasing guest to the sacrificer.

*(The first word of the bhāṣya is printed सोऽग्नी (*so 'gnī*) [?] as read; not zoomed.)*

> सोऽग्नी [?] राम्या रमणहेतुभूता उषसोऽनु अनुलक्ष्येधान इध्यमानो दीपितः सन् अरुषेण रोचमानेन भानुना तेजसा स्वर्ण आदित्य इव दीदेत् । दीप्यते ।
> सोऽग्निर्मनुषो मनुष्यस्य होतुर्होत्राभिः । होत्रेति वाङ्नाम । होमसाधनभूताभिः स्तुतिभिः स्तूयमानः स्वध्वरः शोभनयागो विशां प्रजानां राजा राजमानः स्वाम्यायुवे मनुष्याय यजमानाय तदर्थं चारुश्चरणशीलोऽतिथिरतिथिवत्पूज्यो भवति ॥

> *so 'gnī [?] rāmyā ramaṇahetubhūtā uṣaso 'nu anulakṣyedhāna idhyamāno dīpitaḥ san aruṣeṇa rocamānena bhānunā tejasā svarṇa āditya iva dīdet | dīpyate |*
> *so 'gnirmanuṣo manuṣyasya hoturhotrābhiḥ | hotreti vāṅnāma | homasādhanabhūtābhiḥ stutibhiḥ stūyamānaḥ svadhvaraḥ śobhanayāgo viśāṃ prajānāṃ rājā rājamānaḥ svāmyāyuve manuṣyāya yajamānāya tadarthaṃ cāruścaraṇaśīlo 'tithiratithivatpūjyo bhavati ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सः (सः (*saḥ*)) — Agni; राम्याः (राम्याः (*rāmyāḥ*)) — of the delightful; उषसः अनु (उषसः अनु (*uṣasaḥ anu*)) — upon the rising of the Dawn; इधानः (इधानः (*idhānaḥ*)) — kindled; अरुषेण (अरुषेण (*aruṣeṇa*)) — with radiant; भानुना (भानुना (*bhānunā*)) — brilliance; स्वर्ण (स्वर्ण (*svarṇa*)) — like the Sun; दीदेत् (दीदेत् (*dīdet*)) — he shines; (सः) अग्निः (अग्निः (*agniḥ*)) — that same Agni; मनुषः (मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)) — of the human hotṛ; होत्राभिः (होत्राभिः (*hotrābhiḥ*)) — praised by the hymns; स्वध्वरः (स्वध्वरः (*svadhvaraḥ*)) — having an excellent sacrifice; विशां (विशां (*viśāṃ*)) — for the people; राजा (राजा (*rājā*)) — as lord; आयवे (आयवे (*āyave*)) — for man; चारुः (चारुः (*cāruḥ*)) — come; अतिथिः (अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)) — worshipful like a guest.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "Agni, kindled at the very rising of the delightful Dawn, shines like the Sun with a radiant brilliance. That same Agni, praised by the hymns of the human hotṛ, is one who has an excellent sacrifice, is lord of the people, and is worshipful like a guest who has arrived."

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Among the splendid gods, first-born Agni, our praise or rite swells him. Like a milch cow, he yields countless wealth of many forms to the praiser.

*(Doubtful: दोग्ध्री (*dogdhrī*) is printed with an unclear vowel sign, read दोग्ध्री [?]. The word पूर्वभाविनग्ने (*pūrvabhāvinagne*) is read as printed across the line break.)*

> बृहद्दिवेषु प्रभूतद्युतिष्वमृतेषु देवेषु मध्ये हे पूर्व्य पूर्वभाविनग्ने त्वां मानुषा मनुष्याणां मध्ये नोऽस्मदीया धीर्बुद्धिः स्तुतिः कर्म वा एव एवं पीपाय । प्याययति । यद्वा मानुषा मनुष्यान् धीस्त्वदीया बुद्धिः कर्म वा प्याययतु । तथा त्वदीया धीर्वृजनेषु यज्ञेषु कारवे स्तोत्रे दुहाना धेनुः । दोग्ध्री [?] धेनुरिव । लुप्तोपममेतत् । त्मनात्मनैवेषण्येषणायां सत्यां शतिनमपरिमितसंख्याकं पुरुरूपं गवाश्वादिरूपेण नानारूपं धनसमूहं दुहाना भवति ॥

> *bṛhaddiveṣu prabhūtadyutiṣvamṛteṣu deveṣu madhye he pūrvya pūrvabhāvinagne tvāṃ mānuṣā manuṣyāṇāṃ madhye no 'smadīyā dhīrbuddhiḥ stutiḥ karma vā eva evaṃ pīpāya | pyāyayati | yadvā mānuṣā manuṣyān dhīstvadīyā buddhiḥ karma vā pyāyayatu | tathā tvadīyā dhīrvṛjaneṣu yajñeṣu kārave stotre duhānā dhenuḥ | dogdhrī [?] dhenuriva | luptopamametat | tmanātmanaiveṣaṇyeṣaṇāyāṃ satyāṃ śatinamaparimitasaṃkhyākaṃ pururūpaṃ gavāśvādirūpeṇa nānārūpaṃ dhanasamūhaṃ duhānā bhavati ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada:) बृहद्दिवेषु (*bṛhaddiveṣu*) — among those who shine exceedingly; अमृतेषु (*amṛteṣu*) — among the gods; पूर्व्य (*pūrvya*) — O first one; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; मानुषा (*mānuṣā*) — of human beings; नः (*naḥ*) — our; धीः (*dhīḥ*) — rite or praise; एव (*eva*) — in this manner; पीपाय (*pīpāya*) — it exalts (in the same way your intelligence too); वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*) — at sacrifices; कारवे (*kārave*) — to the praiser; दुहाना धेनुः (*duhānā dhenuḥ*) — like a cow that yields when milked; त्मना (*tmanā*) — by his own impulse; इषणि (*iṣaṇi*) — at the time of desired objects; शतिनं (*śatinaṃ*) — without limit; पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*) — he gives many kinds of desired objects, in the form of cattle, horses and the like.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, first among the gods who shine exceedingly, our praise, as men, exalts you in many ways. As a cow that is milked yields abundant milk of her own will, so your intelligence too fulfils our desired objects at the times of our sacrifices."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Amongst men our praise, Agni, celebrtaes [sic] you, who are first amongst the greatly-splendid immortals ; (may it be to us) as a milch cow spontaneously yielding at sacrifices to the worshipper, infinite and multiform (blessings according to his) desire.

### Printed p. 447 (PDF 468)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 21", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "447", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) Agni is addressed as

> बृहद्दिवेषु अमृतेषु पूर्व्य

> *bṛhaddiveṣu amṛteṣu pūrvya*

— "the very ancient one among the gods who shine with abundant lustres".

> नः धीः पीपाय—अस्मदीया बुद्धिः स्तुतिः कर्म वा एवं प्याययति । यद्वा (मानुषा) मनुष्यान् [?] धीः त्वदीयो बुद्धिः कर्म वा प्याययतु ।

> *naḥ dhīḥ pīpāya—asmadīyā buddhiḥ stutiḥ karma vā evaṃ pyāyayati | yadvā (mānuṣā) manuṣyān [?] dhīḥ tvadīyo buddhiḥ karma vā pyāyayatu |*

(Kannada:) "Two kinds of meaning are explained for this sentence. By taking the word धी (*dhī*) to mean praise or rite, one meaning is: among men, the praise or rite of us the sacrificers swells in the same way in regard to Agni. In the second meaning, the intelligence or rite of Agni, who accepts worship, is explained as making the sacrificers prosper."

> त्वदीयो धीः वृजनेषु कारवे दुहाना धेनुः

> *tvadīyo dhīḥ vṛjaneṣu kārave duhānā dhenuḥ*

(Kannada:) "By this sentence it is described that Agni's intelligence, in regard to the sacrificers who praise at the sacrifices, nourishes or protects, like a cow giving milk. This same idea is expressed in the sentence

> इषिणि [?] त्मना शतिनं पुरुरूपं—आत्मनैव एषणायां सत्यां अपरिमितसंख्याकं गवाश्वादिरूपेण नानारूपं धनसमूहं दुहाना भवति ।

> *iṣiṇi [?] tmanā śatinaṃ pururūpaṃ—ātmanaiva eṣaṇāyāṃ satyāṃ aparimitasaṃkhyākaṃ gavāśvādirūpeṇa nānārūpaṃ dhanasamūhaṃ duhānā bhavati |*

(printed इषिणि (*iṣiṇi*) here, with the इषणि (*iṣaṇi*) of the Ṛk; read as printed), and it is elaborated that Agni's benevolent wish is to give, by the thousand, wealth of many kinds, such as cow and horse. Here, though there is no word of comparison, the meaning 'like a cow' is explained for the word धेनु (*dhenu*)."

### Printed p. 448 (PDF 469)

*(Header: "448", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 2", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Pada of Ṛk 10 concludes.)*

> अस्माकं । द्युम्नं । अधि । पंच । कृष्टिषु । उच्चा । स्वः । न । शुशुचीत । दुस्तरं ॥ १० ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* May we, with the horse or food you gave, outshine the people around us, and may our unsurpassed wealth shine like the sun among the five peoples.

*(Doubtful: पंच पंचसु (*paṃca paṃcasu*) in the second line of the bhāṣya is printed पंचे पंचेसु (*paṃce paṃcesu*) [sic?], not zoomed. The bhāṣya has शुशुचीते (*śuśucīte*) where the Saṃhitā has शुशुचीत (*śuśucīta*), as printed.)*

> *he agne vayaṃ yajamānāḥ suvīryaṃ śobhanasāmarthyopetaṃ yathā tathārvatā vā raṇakuśalenāśvena ‖ vāśabdaścārthe | brahmaṇā vānyena ca tvaddattena janānasmatsamānānati citayema | atikramya jñāyemahi ‖ karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ ‖ yadvā tvaddattenāśvenānnena ca suvīryaṃ citayema | prakāśayema | tadarthamasmākaṃ paṃce [?] paṃcesu [?] kṛṣṭiṣu janeṣu niṣādapaṃcameṣu caturṣu varṇeṣūccairatiprabhūtaṃ dustaramanyenāprāptaṃ dyumnaṃ dhanaṃ svarṇa sūrya ivādhikaṃ śuśucīte | dīpyatām | adhītyayamanarthako vā ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada:) अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we, the sacrificers; सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*) — so as to be endowed with excellent strength; अर्वता वा (*arvatā vā*) — with a horse (given by you); ब्रह्मणा वा (*brahmaṇā vā*) — with food; जनान् (*janān*) — the people around us; अति चितयेम (*ati citayema*) — may we shine, surpassing them; अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*) — our; उच्चा (*uccā*) — exceedingly abundant; दुस्तरं (*dustaraṃ*) — not possible to be obtained by others; द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*) — wealth; पंच कृष्टिषु (*paṃca kṛṣṭiṣu*) — among the people of the five classes beginning with the Niṣādas; स्वर्ण (*svarṇa*) — like the Sun; शुशुचीते (*śuśucīte*) — may it shine.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, may we the sacrificers, with a horse and with food given by you, which make us endowed with excellent strength, shine surpassing the people around us. May our exceedingly abundant wealth, which others cannot obtain, shine like the Sun among the people of the five classes beginning with the Niṣādas."

**English Translation** *(as printed; the heading is printed "English Trnslation" [sic])*

May we manifest vigour among other men, Agni, through the steed and the food (which you have given) : and may our unsurpassed wealth shine like the sun over (that of) the five clases [sic] of beings.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

> वयं अर्वता वा ब्रह्मणा वा जनान् [?] अति चितयेम

> *vayaṃ arvatā vā brahmaṇā vā janān [?] ati citayema*

(Kannada:) "Two kinds of meaning are given for this sentence. In the first meaning, वयं यजमानाः अरणकुशलेन अश्वेन त्वद्- (*vayaṃ yajamānāḥ araṇakuśalena aśvena tvad-*) [as printed अरणकुशलेन (*araṇakuśalena*) here, against रणकुशलेन (*raṇakuśalena*) in the bhāṣya]" (the passage continues on p. 449).

### Printed p. 449 (PDF 470)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 21", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "449", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Special Topics of Ṛk 10 continue from p. 448.)*

*(The page opens in mid-word, continuing त्वद्- (*tvad-*) from p. 448. The first visible letters are printed "ತ್ತ್ರೇನ", read …त्तेन (*…ttena*) [?]. The next word is read अन्नेन (*annena*) [?] as printed, though the bhāṣya has अन्येन (*anyena*) in the corresponding place.)*

(Kannada, continuing:) ……त्तेन [?] अन्नेन च अस्मत्समानान् अतिक्रम्य ज्ञायेमहि (*…ttena [?] annena ca asmatsamānān atikramya jñāyemahi*) — "We the sacrificers know ourselves to be surpassing those who are equal to us, through wealth such as a horse, favoured by Agni and moving swiftly, and also through food. This is the sense." In the second meaning, यद्वा त्वद्दत्तेनान्नेन च सुवीर्यं प्रकाशयेम (*yadvā tvaddattenānnena ca suvīryaṃ prakāśayema*) (as printed, without अश्वेन (*aśvena*)): "Agni's favour is also described: we the sacrificers, through horses favoured by Agni and through food, will also be strong."

(Kannada:) पंचे कृष्टिषु (*paṃce kṛṣṭiṣu*) (printed पंचे (*paṃce*), as in the bhāṣya on p. 448) means the "five peoples": Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas, five kinds of people, some say. Others hold, as Upamanyu and others do, that the four varṇas beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, together with the people of the hunter caste called Niṣāda, make five kinds of people. (Sāyaṇa has approved this very view; the letters of Sāyaṇa (*Sāyaṇa*) are partly damaged in print.) Niṣādas are "killers of living beings", or, because sin is abundant in them, the Nairuktakāras have called them Niṣādas. Besides, at that time there may have been five main tribes (printed in English "tribes"). The poet may have said पंचे कृष्टिषु (*paṃce kṛṣṭiṣu*) with this idea. In any case it is clear that, on this question, a difference of view existed even in the time of Yāska, the author of the Nirukta.

*(Rule line.)*

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Saṃhitā reads यस्मिन्त्सुजाता (*yasmintsujātā*); the sign after स (*sa*) is not wholly clear, read सु (*su*) as in the Pada. Ṛk number printed ೧೧, read 11, not zoomed.)*

> स नो॑ बोधि सहस्य प्र॒शंस्यो॒ यस्मि॑न्त्सुजा॒ता इ॒षयं॑त सू॒रयः॑ ।

> *sa no bodhi sahasya praśaṃsyo yasmintsujātā iṣayaṃta sūrayaḥ |*
> *yamagne yajñamupayaṃti vājino nitye toke dīdivāṃsaṃ sve dame ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । नः । बोधि । सहस्य । प्रऽशंस्यः । यस्मिन् । सुऽजाताः । इषयंत । सूरयः ।
> यं । अग्ने । यज्ञं । उपऽयंति । वाजिनः । नित्ये । तोके । दीदिऽवांसं । स्वे । दमे ॥ ११ ॥

> *saḥ | naḥ | bodhi | sahasya | pra 'śaṃsyaḥ | yasmin | su 'jātāḥ | iṣayaṃta | sūrayaḥ |*
> *yaṃ | agne | yajñaṃ | upa 'yaṃti | vājinaḥ | nitye | toke | dīdi 'vāṃsaṃ | sve | dame ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Powerful, praiseworthy Agni, take note of our hymns; for in you the well-born priests offer praises, and sacrificers approach you in their own sacrificial houses for lasting offspring.

> हे अग्ने सहस्य शत्रूणामभिभवितर्बलप्रभव वा प्रशंस्यः स्तुत्यः स त्वं नोऽस्मदीयं स्तोत्रादिकं बोधि । बुध्यस्व । स इत्युक्तं क इत्याह । यस्मिन्नग्नौ

> *he agne sahasya śatrūṇāmabhibhavitarbalaprabhava vā praśaṃsyaḥ stutyaḥ sa tvaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ stotrādikaṃ bodhi | budhyasva | sa ityuktaṃ ka ityāha | yasminnagnau*

*(No grammatical tail.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada:) अग्ने (agne (*agne*)) — O Agni; यज्ञं (yajñaṃ (*yajñaṃ*)) — worthy of worship; दीदिवांसं (dīdivāṃsaṃ (*dīdivāṃsaṃ*)) — shining; यं (yaṃ (*yaṃ*)) — whom, you; वाजिनः (vājinaḥ (*vājinaḥ*)) — sacrificers possessing food; नित्ये तोके (nitye toke (*nitye toke*)) — for the sake of eternal sons and other wealth; स्वे दमे (sve dame (*sve dame*)) — in their own sacrificial house; उपयंति (upayaṃti (*upayaṃti*)) — approach (with hymns and the like); and यस्मिन् (yasmin (*yasmin*)) — in whom, you; सुजाताः (sujātāḥ (*sujātāḥ*)) — of excellent birth; सूरयः (sūrayaḥ (*sūrayaḥ*)) — praisers; इषयंते (iṣayaṃte (*iṣayaṃte*)) — offer their praises; सहस्य (sahasya (*sahasya*)) — O Agni endowed with strength; प्रशंस्यः सः (praśaṃsyaḥ saḥ (*praśaṃsyaḥ saḥ*)) — you who are worthy of praise; नः (naḥ (*naḥ*)) — our hymns and the like; बोधि (bodhi (*bodhi*)) — know.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, endowed with strength, worthy of worship and shining, you whom the sacrificers, possessing food, approach with hymns and the like in their own sacrificial houses for the sake of eternal offspring and other wealth; and in whom the praisers, born of excellent birth, offer their praises: you, worthy of praise, know our hymns and the like."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Vigorous Agni, hear (our prayers); for you are he who is to be lauded ; to whom the well-born priests address (their hymns) ; and whom, entitled to worship, and radiant in your own abode, the offerers of the oblation approach, for the sake of never-failing posterity.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) "Agni is शत्रूणामभिभवितः बलप्रभव वा (*śatrūṇāmabhibhavitaḥ balaprabhava vā*): one who overcomes enemies, or one who, churned in the araṇi by the strength of the priests' arms, has come into being; thus the meaning of the word सहस्य (*sahasya*) has been given. And may this Agni-deva know the hymns and the like made by us, the priests and sacrificers. The prayer of the priests is also expressed: may the hymns and the like offered by the priests, who were born on earth and have attained the qualification to worship this Agni-deva endowed with abundant splendour, reach this very god."

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(Ṛk number printed ೧೨, read 12, not zoomed.)*

> उ॒भया॑सो जातवेदः स्याम ते स्तो॒तारो॑ अग्ने सू॒रय॑श्च॒ शर्म॑णि ।
> वस्वो॑ रा॒यः पु॑रुश्चं॒द्रस्य॒ भूय॑सः प्र॒जाव॑तः स्वप॒त्यस्य॑ शग्धि नः ॥ १२ ॥

> *ubhayāso jātavedaḥ syāma te stotāro agne sūrayaśca śarmaṇi |*
> *vasvo rāyaḥ puruścaṃdrasya bhūyasaḥ prajāvataḥ svapatyasya śagdhi naḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उभयासः । जातऽवेदः । स्याम । ते । स्तोतारः । अग्ने । सूरयः । च । शर्मणि ।
> वस्वः । रायः । पुरुऽचंद्रस्य । भूयसः । प्रजाऽवतः । सुऽअपत्यस्य । शग्धि । नः ॥ १२ ॥

> *ubhayāsaḥ | jāta 'vedaḥ | syāma | te | stotāraḥ | agne | sūrayaḥ | ca | śarmaṇi |*
> *vasvaḥ | rāyaḥ | puru 'caṃdrasya | bhūyasaḥ | prajā 'vataḥ | su 'apatyasya | śagdhi | naḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, we, both priests and wise patrons, would be yours in your shelter; give us abundant, delightful wealth with servants, progeny and good sons.

*(Doubtful: उभयासः (*ubhayāsaḥ*) near the beginning is printed with a sign that looks like उभयोसः (*ubhayosaḥ*); read उभयासः (*ubhayāsaḥ*) [?]. वसिष्ठस्य (*vasiṣṭhasya*) and बहुहिरण्योपेतस्य (*bahuhiraṇyopetasya*) are read as printed, not zoomed [?].)*

> हे जातवेदो जातानां वेदितरग्ने स्तोतारस्त्वां स्तुवंत ऋत्विजः सूरयो मेधाविनो यजमानाश्चेत्युभयासः [?] । उभये वयं शर्मणि सुखे निमित्तभूते सति ते त्वत्संबंधिनः स्याम । भवेम । यद्वा ते शर्मणि स्याम । त्वं च नोऽस्माकं वस्वो निवासहेतोर्वसिष्ठस्य [?] रायो गवादिधनस्य पुरुश्चंद्रस्यातिशयेनाह्लादकस्य बहुहिरण्योपेतस्य [?] वा भूयसः प्रभूतस्य प्रजावतो भृत्याद्युपेतस्य पुत्रादिभोगपर्याप्तस्य वा स्वपत्यस्य शोभनपुत्रस्य । ईदृग्रूपं धनं नोऽस्मभ्यं शग्धि । देहि । दातुं शक्तो भवसि ॥

> *he jātavedo jātānāṃ veditaragne stotārastvāṃ stuvaṃta ṛtvijaḥ sūrayo medhāvino yajamānāścetyubhayāsaḥ [?] | ubhaye vayaṃ śarmaṇi sukhe nimittabhūte sati te tvatsaṃbaṃdhinaḥ syāma | bhavema | yadvā te śarmaṇi syāma | tvaṃ ca no 'smākaṃ vasvo nivāsahetorvasiṣṭhasya [?] rāyo gavādidhanasya puruścaṃdrasyātiśayenāhlādakasya bahuhiraṇyopetasya [?] vā bhūyasaḥ prabhūtasya prajāvato bhṛtyādyupetasya putrādibhogaparyāptasya vā svapatyasya śobhanaputrasya | īdṛgrūpaṃ dhanaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ śagdhi | dehi | dātuṃ śakto bhavasi ‖*

*(The rest of Ṛk 12, from the Pratipadārtha onward, follows on p. 452.)*

### Printed p. 452 (PDF 473)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 2", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "452", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. Ṛk 12 continues from p. 451.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada:) जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*) — O one of born knowledge (all-knowing); अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; स्तोतारः (*stotāraḥ*) — the priests, fit to praise; सूरयश्च (*sūrayaśca*) — and the wise sacrificers; उभयासः (*ubhayāsaḥ*) — both together; शर्मणि (*śarmaṇi*) — for the sake of obtaining happiness; ते (*te*) — in your service; स्याम (*syāma*) — may we be (for us); वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*) — suited for dwelling; रायः (*rāyaḥ*) — endowed with wealth of cattle and the like; पुरुश्चंद्रस्य (*puruścaṃdrasya*) — exceedingly delightful; भूयसः (*bhūyasaḥ*) — abundant; प्रजावतः (*prajāvataḥ*) — endowed with servants and the like; स्वपत्यस्य (*svapatyasya*) — excellent, endowed with sons; of such wealth, नः (*naḥ*) — to us; शग्धि (*śagdhi*) — give.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O all-knowing Agni, the praising priests and the wise sacrificers, together, shall be in your service for the sake of obtaining happiness. Give us wealth that is suited for dwelling, endowed with cattle and the like, exceedingly delightful, endowed with servants and the like, and excellent, with sons."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Agni, knowing all that is born, may we, both adorers and priests, be yours for the sake of felicity ; and do you bestow upon us wealth of dwellings of cattle, of much gold, of many dependants, and virtuous offspring.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) "Here Agni is addressed by the word जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*). The meaning of the word jātavedas has been explained in many places."

> (हे) जातवेदः अग्ने स्तोतारः सूरयश्च उभयासः

> *(he) jātavedaḥ agne stotāraḥ sūrayaśca ubhayāsaḥ*

(Kannada:) "We have already explained the meaning of the word जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*). Two kinds of meaning are possible for this word. One meaning: Agni who knows all beings that are born or will be born (or the matter concerning those beings); another meaning: all beings that are born know Agni. For the word स्तोतारः (*stotāraḥ*) the bhāṣyakāra has explained the meaning as priests who recite praise, and for the word सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) as wise sacrificers. But there is no rule that those fit to praise Agni must be priests only. Likewise there is no rule that the wise people (men of intelligence) indicated by the word सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) must be sacrificers only. But there is no fault at all in the bhāṣyakāra's explanation, in which he says 'priests, sacrificers' and fits one kind of meaning to each."

#### Ṛk 13

*(Ṛk number printed as ೧೩, read 13, not zoomed. At the beginning of the Saṃhitā the vowel sign of the first word is read ये (*ye*) (printed ए/ओ-sign ambiguous); the plural verb उपसृजंति (*upasṛjaṃti*) and the Pratipadārtha support ये (*ye*) [?].)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ये स्तो॒तृभ्यो॒ गोअ॑ग्रा॒मश्व॑पेशस॒मग्ने॑ रा॒तिमु॑पसृ॒जंति॑ सू॒रयः॑ ।
> अ॒स्माञ्च॒ तांश्च॒ प्र हि नेषि॒ वस्य॒ आ बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥ १३ ॥

> *ye stotṛbhyo goagrāmaśvapeśasamagne rātimupasṛjaṃti sūrayaḥ |*
> *asmāñca tāṃśca pra hi neṣi vasya ā bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ये । स्तोतृऽभ्यः । गोऽअग्रां । अश्वऽपेशसं । अग्ने । रातिं । उपऽसृजंति । सूरयः ।
> अस्मान् । च । तान् । च । प्र । हि । नेषि । वस्यः । आ । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुऽवीराः ॥ १३ ॥

> *ye | stotṛ 'bhyaḥ | go 'agrāṃ | aśva 'peśasaṃ | agne | rātiṃ | upa 'sṛjaṃti | sūrayaḥ |*
> *asmān | ca | tān | ca | pra | hi | neṣi | vasyaḥ | ā | bṛhat | vadema | vidathe | su 'vīrāḥ ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* With this Ṛk the Hotṛ asks, under cover of praise, for what he wants: gifts of cow and horse to praisers, and Agni's leading us to the best abode.

> अनया होता स्तुतिनिगमव्याजेनाभिमतमाशास्ते । हे अग्ने सूरयो मेधाविनः प्रेरयितारो वा यजमानाः स्तोतृभ्यः स्तुतिकर्तृभ्यो गोअग्रां गावोऽग्रगामिन्यो यस्यास्तादृशीं गोप्रमुखामश्वपेशसं ॥ पेश इति रूपनाम ॥ अश्वेन निरूपणीयां । एतद्द्वयप्राधान्याभिप्रायं । गौश्चाश्वश्चाजश्चेति दक्षिणापरिगणनेषु गवाश्वयोः प्राथम्यात् । तादृशीं रातिमुपसृजंति । ददते । तान्यजमानानस्मांश्चर्त्विजो [?] वस्यो वसीयः श्रेष्ठं स्वर्गादिस्थानं आ सर्वतः प्र हि नेषि । प्रकर्षेण नयसि खलु । नयेत्यर्थः । हि प्रसिद्धा । वयं च सुवीराः शोभनपुत्रादिसहिताः विदथे यज्ञे बृहन्महन्मंत्रजातं वदेम । उच्चारयामः । स्तुमः इत्यर्थः ॥

> *anayā hotā stutinigamavyājenābhimatamāśāste | he agne sūrayo medhāvinaḥ prerayitāro vā yajamānāḥ stotṛbhyaḥ stutikartṛbhyo goagrāṃ gāvo 'gragāminyo yasyāstādṛśīṃ gopramukhāmaśvapeśasaṃ ‖ peśa iti rūpanāma ‖ aśvena nirūpaṇīyāṃ | etaddvayaprādhānyābhiprāyaṃ | gauścāśvaścājaśceti dakṣiṇāparigaṇaneṣu gavāśvayoḥ prāthamyāt | tādṛśīṃ rātimupasṛjaṃti | dadate | tānyajamānānasmāṃścartvijo [?] vasyo vasīyaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ svargādisthānaṃ ā sarvataḥ pra hi neṣi | prakarṣeṇa nayasi khalu | nayetyarthaḥ | hi prasiddhā | vayaṃ ca suvīrāḥ śobhanaputrādisahitāḥ vidathe yajñe bṛhanmahanmaṃtrajātaṃ vadema | uccārayāmaḥ | stumaḥ ityarthaḥ ‖*

*(The word चर्त्विजो (*cartvijo*) is printed with the ऋ combined with the preceding श्च (*śca*) in a contracted way; read as printed [?]. No grammatical tail.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada:) अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; ये (*ye*) — who; सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) — such sacrificers as are impelled by good intelligence; स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*) — to the praisers; गोअग्रां (*goagrāṃ*) — having cows as the chief; अश्वपेशसं (*aśvapeśasaṃ*) — to be defined by horses; रातिं (*rātiṃ*) — the gift; उपसृजंति (*upasṛjaṃti*) — give; तांश्च (*tāṃśca*) — those sacrificers also; अस्मांश्च (*asmāṃśca*) — and us, the priests; वस्यः (*vasyaḥ*) — to the superior place, heaven and the like; आ प्र हि नेषि (*ā pra hi neṣi*) — lead us in an excellent manner; सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*) — we, endowed with excellent sons and the like; विदथे (*vidathe*) — in the sacrifice; बृहत् (*bṛhat*) — a mantra filled with greatness; वदेम (*vadema*) — may we recite.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, the sacrificers impelled by good intelligence give to the praisers a gift consisting of cows and horses. Lead those sacrificers and us, the priests, in an excellent manner to the best place, heaven and the like. We, endowed with excellent sons and the like, will recite a mantra filled with greatness at the sacrifice."

## Sūkta 3 (Third Sūkta, ೩) — "ಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು"

(Kannada:) "The third sūkta, beginning समिद्धो अग्निः (*samiddho agniḥ*), is the Āprī sūkta of this Maṇḍala. Concerning the deities of the Āprī sūktas we have written a detailed explanation in the Special Topics of the 188th sūkta of the first Maṇḍala (the 188th sūkta is itself an Āprī sūkta) (page 227–273). Since those same explanations apply to the deities in the 11 Ṛks of this sūkta, it is not explained again here. Therefore readers should read it as if what was explained in the 188th sūkta had been written here concerning the deities of this sūkta."

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Sūkta 3 has eleven Ṛks, by Gṛtsamada, in Triṣṭubh (the seventh Ṛk Jagatī); the deities are the eleven Prayāja deities.

*(Doubtful: in नराशंसतनूनपादादय (*narāśaṃsatanūnapādādaya*) the letters after शंस (*śaṃsa*) are printed ತೇನೂನ…; read तनूनपाद (*tanūnapāda*) with the reading of the letter after नूनप (*nūnapa*) as पा (*pā*) not certain [?]. The page ends in mid-word, at समिद्ध् (*samiddh*).)*

### Printed p. 455 (PDF 476)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 21", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "455", read from the strip. The numeral file has three rows for this page: "3-2" twice (both agree with the print, Āśvalāyana reference "आ. ३-२") and "1-6" in the metre line (agrees, see below). The bhāṣya of Sūkta 3 continues from p. 454, where it broke off at "समिद्ध्-".)*

*Gist:* The Anukramaṇikā gives eleven Ṛks, the seventh in Jagatī. The sūkta is the Āprī sūkta of the Śunaka line in the animal sacrifice, because Gṛtsamada also belonged to that line.

*(Joined with the end of p. 454, the Anukramaṇikā words read समिद्ध् + एकादशाप्रं. After the शा of the first word a small sign is printed that looks like an avagraha; the Kannada explanation prints the word without it. Read as printed [?].)*

> एकादशाप्रं सप्तमी जगतीत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ पशौ शुनकानामिदमाप्रीसूक्तं । गृत्समदस्यापि शुनकत्वात् । समिद्धो अग्निरिति शुनकानामिति हि सूत्रितं । आ. ३-२ ॥

> *ekādaśāpraṃ saptamī jagatītyanukramaṇikā ‖ paśau śunakānāmidamāprīsūktaṃ | gṛtsamadasyāpi śunakatvāt | samiddho agniriti śunakānāmiti hi sūtritaṃ | ā. 3-2 ‖*

**अनुवादः (Anuvāda — Kannada, translated)**

"The sūkta beginning समिद्धो अग्निः (*samiddho agniḥ*) is the third sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the ṛṣi; the metre is Triṣṭubh, and only the seventh Ṛk is in Jagatī metre. Since it is an Āprī sūkta, the eleven Prayāja deities beginning with समिद्धः अग्निः (*samiddhaḥ agniḥ*) are the deities of this sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said समिद्ध एकादशाप्रं सप्तमी जगती (*samiddha ekādaśāpraṃ saptamī jagatī*). In the animal sacrifice this is the Āprī sūkta for those of the Śunaka line of ṛṣis, because Gṛtsamada too belonged to that line, and because the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra has the sūtra समिद्धो अग्निरिति शुनकानामिति हि (*samiddho agniriti śunakānāmiti hi*) (Ā. 3-2). Those of Śunaka descent also use this Āprī sūkta."

### Printed p. 456 (PDF 477)

*(Header: "456", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 3", read from the strip. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Saṃhitā and Pada of Ṛk 1 stand on p. 455 and at the top of this page.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The well-kindled Agni, placed on the altar of earth, stands in sight of all beings; he is Hotṛ, purifier, ancient, wise, divine, and being worthy of worship he is to offer to the gods.

> पृथिव्यां वेदिलक्षणायां समिद्धः सम्यक् दीप्त एतन्नामकोऽग्निर्निहितः स्थापितः सन् विश्वानि सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि प्रत्यज् अभिमुखः सन् अस्थात् । तिष्ठति । यथा सर्वे जनाः पश्यंति तथा प्रवृद्धोऽभवदित्यर्थः । किंच सोऽग्निर्होता होमनिष्पादको देवानामाह्वाता वा पावकः शोधकः प्रदिवः पुराणः सुमेधाः शोभनप्रज्ञो देवो द्योतमानः । एवं महानुभावोऽग्निरर्हन् यागयोग्यः सन् देवान्यजतु । अत्र यष्टव्यानिंद्रादीन्पूजयतु ॥

> *pṛthivyāṃ vedilakṣaṇāyāṃ samiddhaḥ samyak dīpta etannāmako 'gnirnihitaḥ sthāpitaḥ san viśvāni sarvāṇi bhuvanāni bhūtajātāni pratyaj abhimukhaḥ san asthāt | tiṣṭhati | yathā sarve janāḥ paśyaṃti tathā pravṛddho 'bhavadityarthaḥ | kiṃca so 'gnirhotā homaniṣpādako devānāmāhvātā vā pāvakaḥ śodhakaḥ pradivaḥ purāṇaḥ sumedhāḥ śobhanaprajño devo dyotamānaḥ | evaṃ mahānubhāvo 'gnirarhan yāgayogyaḥ san devānyajatu | atra yaṣṭavyāniṃdrādīnpūjayatu ‖*

*(No grammatical tail. In the last word the letters are printed पूजयतु, the ya with the usual hook.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) होता (*hotā*) — the performer of the homa; पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*) — the purifier; प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*) — the ancient one; सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*) — one of excellent wisdom; देवः (*devaḥ*) — the shining one; पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*) — on the earth in the form of the altar; समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*) — well kindled (samiddha); अग्निः (*agniḥ*) — Agni; निहितः (*nihitaḥ*) — being established; विश्वानि (*viśvāni*) — all; भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*) — the beings; प्रत्यज् (*pratyaj*) — keeping in front of him; अस्थात् (*asthāt*) — stands; अग्निः (*agniḥ*) — Agni with such great qualities; अर्हन् (*arhan*) — worthy of the sacrifice (to be honoured); देवान् (*devān*) — the gods; यजतु (*yajatu*) — let him sacrifice (to).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "Agni, the performer of the homa, the purifier, the ancient, one of excellent wisdom, kindled well on the earth in the form of the altar, is established and stands keeping all beings before him. May this Agni, with such great qualities, being worthy of the sacrifice, sacrifice to the gods."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Agni, the well-kindled, placed upon (the altar of) the earth, stands in the presence of all beings; the invoker (of the gods), the purifier, the ancient the intelligent [sic, no comma], the divine: Let the venerable Agni minister to the gods.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> नरा॒शंसः॒ प्रति॒ धामा॑न्यं॒जन् ति॒स्रो दिवः॒ प्रति॑ म॒ह्ना स्व॒र्चिः ।
> घृ॒त॒प्रुषा॒ मन॑सा ह॒व्यमुं॒दन् मू॒र्धन्य॒ज्ञस्य॒ सम॑नक्तु दे॒वान् ॥ २ ॥

> *narāśaṃsaḥ prati dhāmānyaṃjan tisro divaḥ prati mahnā svarciḥ |*
> *ghṛtapruṣā manasā havyamuṃdan mūrdhanyajñasya samanaktu devān ‖ 2 ‖*

*(In मह्ना the conjunct ह्न is printed as in the Pratipadārtha.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> नराशंसः । प्रति । धामानि । अंजन् । तिस्रः । दिवः । प्रति । मह्ना । सुऽअर्चिः ।
> घृतऽप्रुषा । मनसा । हव्यं । उंदन् । मूर्धन् । यज्ञस्य । सं । अनक्तु । देवान् ॥ २ ॥

> *narāśaṃsaḥ | prati | dhāmāni | aṃjan | tisraḥ | divaḥ | prati | mahnā | su 'arciḥ |*
> *ghṛta 'pruṣā | manasā | havyaṃ | uṃdan | mūrdhan | yajñasya | saṃ | anaktu | devān ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Narāśaṃsa, with bright flames, makes his greatness shine at each place of the oblation and in the three worlds; may he gratify the gods to be worshipped at the head of the sacrifice.

> नराशंसो नरैर्नेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः शंसनीय एतन्नामकोऽग्निः स्वर्चिः
> शोभनज्वालः सन् धामानि स्थानान्याहुत्यधिकरणानि तेजांसि प्रति प्रत्येकं मह्ना स्वमहिम्नांजन् व्यक्तीकुर्वन् तिस्रो दिवो द्योतमानांस्त्रीन् भूम्यादिलोकांश्च प्रति प्रत्येकमंजन् । स्थित्या भूमिं प्रकाशेनांतरिक्षं हविष्प्रापणेन दिवमित्यभिप्रायः । यद्वा लोकानां प्रत्येकं त्रित्वोपेतत्वात् तिस्रो दिव इत्यविरुद्धं । तिस्रो दिवः पृथिवीस्तिस्रः । ४-५३-५ । इत्यादिमंत्रवर्णात् त्रयो वा इमे त्रिवृतो लोका इति ब्राह्मणाच्च । तथा घृतप्रुषा घृतं सिंचता मनसा हव्यमुंदन् क्लेदयन् स्निग्धीकुर्वन् यज्ञस्य मूर्धन् मूर्धनि मुखे होमसमये देवान्यष्टव्यान् समनक्तु । सम्यक् व्यक्तीकरोतु । तर्पयत्वित्यर्थः ॥

> *narāśaṃso narairnetṛbhirṛtvigbhiḥ śaṃsanīya etannāmako 'gniḥ svarciḥ*
> *śobhanajvālaḥ san dhāmāni sthānānyāhutyadhikaraṇāni tejāṃsi prati pratyekaṃ mahnā svamahimnāṃjan vyaktīkurvan tisro divo dyotamānāṃstrīn bhūmyādilokāṃśca prati pratyekamaṃjan | sthityā bhūmiṃ prakāśenāṃtarikṣaṃ haviṣprāpaṇena divamityabhiprāyaḥ | yadvā lokānāṃ pratyekaṃ tritvopetatvāt tisro diva ityaviruddhaṃ | tisro divaḥ pṛthivīstisraḥ | 4-53-5 | ityādimaṃtravarṇāt trayo vā ime trivṛto lokā iti brāhmaṇācca | tathā ghṛtapruṣā ghṛtaṃ siṃcatā manasā havyamuṃdan kledayan snigdhīkurvan yajñasya mūrdhan mūrdhani mukhe homasamaye devānyaṣṭavyān samanaktu | samyak vyaktīkarotu | tarpayatvityarthaḥ ‖*

*(No grammatical tail. In मह्ना the Kannada print is ಮಹ್ನಾ, written as printed; the word नरैः is read from ನರೈರ್.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*) — Agni, praised by the priests, who is Narāśaṃsa by name; स्वर्चिः (*svarciḥ*) — together with excellent flames; धामानि (*dhāmāni*) — the vessels of oblation; प्रति (*prati*) — one by one; मह्ना (*mahnā*) — by his greatness; अंजन् (*aṃjan*) — making them shine; तिस्रः दिवः (*tisraḥ divaḥ*) — the three worlds beginning with earth; प्रति (*prati*) — each one, making it shine; घृतप्रुषा (*ghṛtapruṣā*) — that which sprinkles ghee (that which makes for well-being); मनसा (*manasā*) — with the mind; हव्यं (*havyaṃ*) — the oblation; उंदन् (*uṃdan*) — making it moist; यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*) — of the sacrifice; मूर्धन् (*mūrdhan*) — at the time of the homa; देवान् (*devān*) — the gods; समनक्तु (*samanaktu*) — let him satisfy.

*(The Bhāvārtha, printed English and Special Topics of Ṛk 2 follow on p. 458.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) "May Agni, Narāśaṃsa by name, joined with excellent flames, by his greatness make shine each of the oblations (receptacles of the oblation) and the three worlds beginning with the earth. May the bright Narashansa, illumining the receptacles (of the offering) making manifest by his greatness the three radiant (regions), and diffusing the oblation at the season of sacrifice with butter-dispensing purpose, satisfy the gods

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ई॒ळि॒तो अ॑ग्ने॒ मन॑सा नो॒ अर्ह॑न्दे॒वान्य॑क्षि॒ मानु॑षा॒त्पूर्वो॑ अ॒द्य ।
> स आ व॑ह म॒रुतां॒ शर्धो॒ अच्यु॑त॒मिंद्रं॑ नरो बर्हि॒षदं॑ यजध्वं ॥ ३ ॥

> *īḷito agne manasā no arhandevānyakṣi mānuṣātpūrvo adya |*
> *sa ā vaha marutāṃ śardho acyutamiṃdraṃ naro barhiṣadaṃ yajadhvaṃ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ईळितः । अग्ने । मनसा । नः । अर्हन् । देवान् । यक्षि । मानुषात् । पूर्वः । अद्य ।
> सः । आ । वह । मरुतां । शर्धः । अच्युतं । इंद्रं । नरः । बर्हिःऽसदं । यजध्वं ॥ ३ ॥

> *īḷitaḥ | agne | manasā | naḥ | arhan | devān | yakṣi | mānuṣāt | pūrvaḥ | adya |*
> *saḥ | ā | vaha | marutāṃ | śardhaḥ | acyutaṃ | iṃdraṃ | naraḥ | barhiḥ 'sadaṃ | yajadhvaṃ ‖ 3 ‖*

*(In the Pada the compound बर्हिःऽसदं is printed with the usual small compound stroke.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, praised by us and worthy of the sacrifice, is asked to sacrifice today to the gods before the human Hotṛ, to bring the Maruts' host and the undecaying Indra; the priests are to worship Indra seated on the grass.

> हे अग्ने ईळितोऽस्माभिः स्तुतः सन् मनसास्मदनुरक्तेन देवानां यागबुद्ध्या वार्हन् यागयोग्यः सन् मानुषाद्धोतुः पूर्वः पूर्वभावी नोऽस्मदर्थमद्यास्मिन्दिने देवान् यष्टव्यान् यक्षि । त्वमेव यजसि । स तादृशो यष्टा त्वमावह । आकारय । कान् । मरुतां शर्धो गणं । अच्युतमक्षीणमिंद्रं तदविनाभूतमिंद्रमपि । यद्वा मरुद्बलोपेतमिंद्रं । अनंतरं हे नरो नेतार ऋत्विजो बर्हिषदं बर्हिषि सीदंतं तमिंद्रं यजध्वं । पूजयध्वं ॥

> *he agne īḷito 'smābhiḥ stutaḥ san manasāsmadanuraktena devānāṃ yāgabuddhyā vārhan yāgayogyaḥ san mānuṣāddhotuḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvabhāvī no 'smadarthamadyāsmindine devān yaṣṭavyān yakṣi | tvameva yajasi | sa tādṛśo yaṣṭā tvamāvaha | ākāraya | kān | marutāṃ śardho gaṇaṃ | acyutamakṣīṇamiṃdraṃ tadavinābhūtamiṃdramapi | yadvā marudbalopetamiṃdraṃ | anaṃtaraṃ he naro netāra ṛtvijo barhiṣadaṃ barhiṣi sīdaṃtaṃ tamiṃdraṃ yajadhvaṃ | pūjayadhvaṃ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; ईळितः (*īḷitaḥ*) — praised by us; मनसा (*manasā*) — with a mind attached to us; अर्हन् (*arhan*) — being worthy of the sacrifice; मानुषात् (*mānuṣāt*) — than the human Hotṛ; पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*) — as the one who comes before; नः (*naḥ*) — for us; अद्य (*adya*) — today; देवान् (*devān*) — with reference to the gods worthy of sacrifice; यक्षि (*yakṣi*) — perform the sacrifice;

*(The Pratipadārtha continues on p. 459.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3, continued)**

(Kannada, translated:) सः (*saḥ*) — you, the revered one of that kind; मरुतां शर्धः (*marutāṃ śardhaḥ*) — the host in the form of an assembly of the Maruts; अच्युतं (*acyutaṃ*) — free from decay; इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*) — Indra; आ वह (*ā vaha*) — bring, having called (afterwards); नरः (*naraḥ*) — O priests, leaders of the sacrifice; बर्हिषदं (*barhiṣadaṃ*) — Indra, who sits on the seat of darbha grass; यजध्वं (*yajadhvaṃ*) — worship.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "O Agni, you who are praised by us, with a mind attached to us, worthy of the sacrifice, before the human Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice today for us, addressing the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice [the print has ಯುಗಾರ್ಹರಾದ *yugārhar-*, probably a misprint for *yāgārha-*, [sic?]]. You, the revered one, come bringing the host of the Maruts and the undecaying Indra. Then, O priests, leaders of the sacrifice, worship Indra, who sits on the seat of darbha grass."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Agni, you are the venerable Ilita ; do you, with mind favourably disposed towards us, offer to-day sacrifice to the gods, before the human (ministrant priest) ; as such, bring hither the company of the Maruts, the undecaying Indra, to whom, seated on the sacred grass, do you priests, offer worship.

*(No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 3.)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> देव॑ बर्हि॒र्वर्ध॑मानं सु॒वीरं॑ स्ती॒र्णं रा॒ये सु॒भरं॒ वेद्य॒स्यां ।
> घृ॒तेना॒क्तं व॑सवः सीदते॒दं विश्वे॑ देवा आदित्या य॒ज्ञिया॑सः ॥ ४ ॥

> *deva barhirvardhamānaṃ suvīraṃ stīrṇaṃ rāye subharaṃ vedyasyāṃ |*
> *ghṛtenāktaṃ vasavaḥ sīdatedaṃ viśve devā ādityā yajñiyāsaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> देव । बर्हिः । वर्धमानं । सुऽवीरं । स्तीर्णं । राये । सुऽभरं । वेदी इति । अस्यां ।
> घृतेन । अक्तं । वसवः । सीदत । इदं । विश्वे । देवाः । आदित्याः । यज्ञियासः ॥ ४ ॥

> *deva | barhiḥ | vardhamānaṃ | su 'vīraṃ | stīrṇaṃ | rāye | su 'bharaṃ | vedī iti | asyāṃ |*
> *ghṛtena | aktaṃ | vasavaḥ | sīdata | idaṃ | viśve | devāḥ | ādityāḥ | yajñiyāsaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Divine Barhis is asked to be strewn by our priests on this altar for wealth, and the Vasus, Viśvedevas and Ādityas are asked to sit on this ghee-sprinkled grass.

> हे बर्हिर्देव एतदभिमानिन्नग्ने वर्धमानं सुवीरं शोभनवीरसंपादकं सुभरं सुपूर्णं स्तीर्णमस्मदीयैर्ऋत्विग्भिरास्तृतं भव । किमर्थं । रा-

> *he barhirdeva etadabhimāninnagne vardhamānaṃ suvīraṃ śobhanavīrasaṃpādakaṃ subharaṃ supūrṇaṃ stīrṇamasmadīyairṛtvigbhirāstṛtaṃ bhava | kimarthaṃ | rā-*

*(The bhāṣya continues on p. 460, from the last word रा(ये).)*
