### Sūkta 5

*(A short rule is printed here, then the title "ಐದನೆಯು ಸೂಕ್ತವು" ("The fifth sūkta"), then another short rule.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The fifth sūkta, "hotājaniṣṭa", has eight Ṛks, ṛṣi Somāhuti, deity Agni, metre Anuṣṭubh. Its application is in the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra, and in the ājya offerings of certain days.

*(The sūtra "अग्नायो होताजनिष्ट (*agnāyo hotājaniṣṭa*)" is printed ಅಗ्नಾಯೋ in the bhāṣya and ಆಗ್ನಾಯೋ in the Kannada exposition. It is written as in the bhāṣya [?]. The references Ā. 4-13, Ā. 7-2 and Ā. 7-6 (Aśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, as printed) are read from the strip, not zoomed [?].)*

> होताजनिष्टेत्यष्टर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं सोमाहुतेरार्षमाग्नेयमानुष्टुभं । होताष्टावानुष्टुभमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोराग्नेये क्रतावस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । अग्नायो [?] होताजनिष्ट । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥ चतुर्विंशेऽहन्यपीदमेवाज्यं । चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्टेत्याज्यं । आ. ७-२ [?] । इति ॥ अभिप्लविके द्वितीयेऽहनीदमेवाज्यं । द्वितीयस्य चतुर्विंशेनाज्यं । आ. ७-६ [?] । इत्यतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

> *hotājaniṣṭetyaṣṭarcaṃ paṃcamaṃ sūktaṃ somāhuterārṣamāgneyamānuṣṭubhaṃ | hotāṣṭāvānuṣṭubhamityanukrāṃtaṃ ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorāgneye kratāvasya viniyogaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | agnāyo [?] hotājaniṣṭa | ā. 4-13 | iti ‖ caturviṃśe 'hanyapīdamevājyaṃ | caturviṃśe hotājaniṣṭetyājyaṃ | ā. 7-2 [?] | iti ‖ abhiplavike dvitīye 'hanīdamevājyaṃ | dvitīyasya caturviṃśenājyaṃ | ā. 7-6 [?] | ityatidiṣṭatvāt ‖*

**अनुवाद (Anuvāda)**

(Kannada, translated:) This sūkta, "hotājaniṣṭa", is the fifth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Somāhuti; the deity is Agni; the metre is Anuṣṭup. The Anukramaṇikā says "होताष्टावानुष्टुभं (*hotāṣṭāvānuṣṭubhaṃ*)". The use of this sūkta for the Ṛks of the Āgneya-kratu, at the recital of the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras, is told by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "अग्नायो होताजनिष्ट (*agnāyo hotājaniṣṭa*)" (Ā. 4-13). In the special sacrifice lasting up to twenty-four days, its use for the ājya-homa on the twenty-fourth day is told by the sūtra "चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्टेत्याज्यं (*caturviṃśe hotājaniṣṭetyājyaṃ*)" (Ā. 7-2). On the second day of the Abhiplava sacrifice this sūkta is also to be recited for the ājya-homa, as the sūtra "द्वितीयस्य चतुर्विंशेनाज्यं (*dvitīyasya caturviṃśenājyaṃ*)" (Ā. 7-6) tells.

### Printed p. 491 (PDF 512)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 26 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "491", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. Ṛk 1 continues from p. 490, where its Saṃhitā and Pada were written.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, the Hotā who makes our rite effective and guards our sacrifice, has been born to protect the patrons. We, having oblation-food, ask to win worshipful, conquerable and controllable wealth.

*(The grammatical tail is printed as "षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी" (dative in the sense of the genitive, for पितृभ्यः); no sūtra is quoted.)*

> होता होमनिष्पादकश्चेतनश्चेतयिताऽस्मदनुष्ठितस्य । पिता पालकोऽस्मद्यज्ञस्य ईदृशोऽग्निरजनिष्ट । उत्पन्नः । किमर्थं । पितृभ्यः पालकेभ्यो यजमानेभ्यः ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी ॥ तेषामूतये रक्षणाय च । वयं च वाजिनो हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतः संतः प्रयक्षं प्रकर्षेण पूज्यं जेन्यं जेतव्यं यमं यमयितव्यं वसु धनं शकेम । शक्ता भूयास्म लब्धुमिति शेषः । यद्वा वाजिनोऽन्नस्य यमं यमनं कर्तुं शकेम । प्रयक्षं जेन्यं वसु धनमित्युपमानं । उक्तलक्षणं धनमिव । तद्यथावरोद्धुं शक्नुमस्तद्वत् ॥

> *hotā homaniṣpādakaścetanaścetayitā 'smadanuṣṭhitasya | pitā pālako 'smadyajñasya īdṛśo 'gnirajaniṣṭa | utpannaḥ | kimarthaṃ | pitṛbhyaḥ pālakebhyo yajamānebhyaḥ ‖ ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī ‖ teṣāmūtaye rakṣaṇāya ca | vayaṃ ca vājino havirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaḥ saṃtaḥ prayakṣaṃ prakarṣeṇa pūjyaṃ jenyaṃ jetavyaṃ yamaṃ yamayitavyaṃ vasu dhanaṃ śakema | śaktā bhūyāsma labdhumiti śeṣaḥ | yadvā vājino 'nnasya yamaṃ yamanaṃ kartuṃ śakema | prayakṣaṃ jenyaṃ vasu dhanamityupamānaṃ | uktalakṣaṇaṃ dhanamiva | tadyathāvaroddhuṃ śaknumastadvat ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) होता (*hotā*) — the accomplisher of the homa; चेतनः (*cetanaḥ*) — the one who gives (our rites) consciousness (the inspirer); पिता (*pitā*) — Agni, the protector of our sacrifice; पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) — of the performers of the sacrifice; ऊतये (*ūtaye*) — for protection; अजनिष्ट (*ajaniṣṭa*) — has been born. (वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we too.) वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) — possessed of food in the form of the oblation; प्रयक्षं (*prayakṣaṃ*) — exceedingly worshipful; जेन्यं (*jenyaṃ*) — fit to be conquered; यमं (*yamaṃ*) — fit to be held in our own control; वसु (*vasu*) — wealth; शकेम (*śakema*) — may we be able to obtain.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) Agni, the accomplisher of the homa, the giver of consciousness to us, the protector of our sacrifice, has been born for the protection of the performers of the sacrifice. We too, as possessors of Agni in the form of the oblation, worshipping Agni, may obtain wealth that is exceedingly worshipful, fit to be conquered, and within our control.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 1)*

An invoker (of the gods), our instructor and protector, has heen [sic] born for the preservation of our patrons ; may we, possessed of (sacrificial} [sic] food be able to acquire worshipful, conquerable, and manageable riches.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

> चेतनः—चेतयिता अस्मदनुष्ठितस्य ।

> *cetanaḥ—cetayitā asmadanuṣṭhitasya |*

He who prompts the sacrificial and other rites that we perform or are performing; that is, he who gives us the strength and capacity to carry them out, is the meaning.

> पिता—

> *pitā—*

The word is formed from the root पा (*pā*) "to protect"; Sāyaṇa has explained it as "protector". Yāska — *(the Kannada continues on the next page)*

> उत्तानयोश्चम्वो३र्योनिरंतरत्रा पिता दुहितुर्गर्भमाधात् ॥

Citing this Ṛk, he has explained the word पिता (*pitā*) in it as "protector or guardian, or preserver": पाता वा पालयिता वा (*pātā vā pālayitā vā*) (Ni. 4-21, as printed), and, with another Ṛk:

*(The gloss is mine and tentative: "Let the lower, the higher and the middle Fathers, worthy of Soma, rise up; those harmless Fathers who went to life, knowers of the truth, may those Fathers help us in the invocations".)*

> उदीरतामवर उत्परास उन्मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्यासः ।
> असुं य ईयुरवृका ऋतज्ञास्ते नोऽवंतु पितरो हवेषु ॥

> *udīratāmavara utparāsa unmadhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ |*
> *asuṃ ya īyuravṛkā ṛtajñāste no 'vaṃtu pitaro haveṣu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-15-1, as printed.)

citing this Ṛk, he has said that the word पितरः (*pitaraḥ*) in it means "the deities of the fathers (pitṛ-devatās)" (Ni. 11-18, as printed). Sāyaṇa, in the Ṛk before us, gives the sense "protector" to both words पिता (*pitā*) and पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*). He construes पिता (*pitā*) "protector" with Agni, and पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) "for the protecting sacrificers" with the yajamānas. The sense "protector" that Sāyaṇa gives to पिता (*pitā*) here does suit Agni. But for पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) there is no objection to giving the sense "(for the protection) of the deities of the fathers" in place of "for the sacrificers". The scholar Wilson has accepted the sense "deities of the fathers" only.

> वाजिनः—हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतः ।

> *vājinaḥ—havirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaḥ |*

The word वाजः (*vājaḥ*) is read among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 3-9, as printed). वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) means those who are accompanied by food, or those who have prepared food in the form of oblations in order to offer it to Agni.

> जेन्यं वसु—

> *jenyaṃ vasu—*

वसु (*vasu*) means wealth. This wealth must be worthy of being won by us. That is, we must be able to subdue enemies, win the wealth and other things they hold, and bring them under our control. Agni is prayed to that we may be able to obtain such wealth.

In this Ṛk and in the following Ṛks, Agni is addressed and praised as the ṛtvijs who take part in the sacrifice: Hotā, Netā, Praśāstā, Neṣṭā, Adhvaryu and the rest. In the Ṛk before us, Agni is praised as होता (*hotā*), the one who invokes the deities in the sacrifice, or as होमनिष्पादकः (*homaniṣpādakaḥ*), the one who accomplishes the homa; and it is described that Agni of such greatness has been born (in the araṇis, for the sake of our sacrifice).

*(A short rule is printed here, ending the Special Topics of Ṛk 1.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ यस्मि॑न्त्स॒प्त र॒श्मय॑स्त॒ता य॒ज्ञस्य॑ ने॒तरि॑ ।
> म॒नु॒ष्वद्दैव्य॑मष्ट॒मं पोता॒ विश्वं॒ तदि॑न्वति ॥ २ ॥

> *ā yasmintsapta raśmayastatā yajñasya netari |*
> *manuṣvaddaivyamaṣṭamaṃ potā viśvaṃ tadinvati ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । यस्मिन् । सप्त । रश्मयः । ततासः । यज्ञस्य । नेतरि ।
> मनुष्वत् । दैव्यं । अष्टमं । पोता । विश्वं । तत् । इन्वति ॥ २ ॥

> *ā | yasmin | sapta | raśmayaḥ | tatāsaḥ | yajñasya | netari |*
> *manuṣvat | daivyaṃ | aṣṭamaṃ | potā | viśvaṃ | tat | invati ‖ 2 ‖*

*(In the Pada the second word of the first line is printed ತತಾಃ, i.e. ततासः is not what is printed; it is written as printed: तताः. Correction of the line above:)*

> आ । यस्मिन् । सप्त । रश्मयः । तताः । यज्ञस्य । नेतरि ।
> मनुष्वत् । दैव्यं । अष्टमं । पोता । विश्वं । तत् । इन्वति ॥ २ ॥

> *ā | yasmin | sapta | raśmayaḥ | tatāḥ | yajñasya | netari |*
> *manuṣvat | daivyaṃ | aṣṭamaṃ | potā | viśvaṃ | tat | invati ‖ 2 ‖*

*(The first of the two Pada lines above is wrong in its fifth word (ततासः); the second Pada block, with तताः, is the printed reading. The Saṃhitā likewise has ततता in my block; the printed Saṃhitā word is ततता? No: it is printed ततता — see the corrected Saṃhitā below.)*

*(Corrected Saṃhitā, as printed: the fifth word is तता.)*

> आ यस्मिन्त्सप्त रश्मयस्तता यज्ञस्य नेतरि ।
> मनुष्वद्दैव्यमष्टमं पोता विश्वं तदिन्वति ॥ २ ॥

> *ā yasmintsapta raśmayastatā yajñasya netari |*
> *manuṣvaddaivyamaṣṭamaṃ potā viśvaṃ tadinvati ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* In Agni, the guide of the sacrifice, the seven Hotṛs are spread like rays. As eighth, the Potṛ, Agni, like a human Potṛ, carries through the whole divine sacrifice.

*(The words after तत्संबंध्य (*tatsaṃbaṃdhya*) are printed ಷ್ಟಮುಷ್ಟೈತ್ರ್ವಿಕ್ಸಂಬಂಧಿ, written तत्संबंध्यष्टमर्त्विक्संबंधि (*tatsaṃbaṃdhyaṣṭamartviksaṃbaṃdhi*) [?]. The word before यज्ञं near the end is printed ತದ್ವದ್, written तद्वद् (*tadvad*) [?]. The tail तदित्यस्य लिंगव्यत्ययः (*tadityasya liṃgavyatyayaḥ*) is a remark on gender.)*

> यज्ञस्य नेतरि यागस्य निर्वाहके यस्मिन्नग्नौ सप्त रश्मयः सप्तसंख्याका रश्मिवद्व्याप्ता होत्रका आतताः । स्वस्वकर्मभिः सर्वतो व्याप्ता भवंति । स पोता पावको देवानां पोत्राख्य ऋत्विग्रूपो वाग्निर्मनुष्वत् मनुष्यपोतृवत् दैव्यं । देवो यज्ञः । तत्संबंध्यष्टमर्त्विक्संबंधि [?] तद्विश्वं कर्तव्यजातं सप्त होत्रकैः सह स्वयमष्टमः सन् इन्वति । व्याप्नोति । यद्वा तदित्यस्य लिंगव्यत्ययः । स पोतेति संबंधः । सप्तहोत्रकैः सहाष्टमो भूत्वा तद्वद्यज्ञं [?] निर्वहतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *yajñasya netari yāgasya nirvāhake yasminnagnau sapta raśmayaḥ saptasaṃkhyākā raśmivadvyāptā hotrakā ātatāḥ | svasvakarmabhiḥ sarvato vyāptā bhavaṃti | sa potā pāvako devānāṃ potrākhya ṛtvigrūpo vāgnirmanuṣvat manuṣyapotṛvat daivyaṃ | devo yajñaḥ | tatsaṃbaṃdhyaṣṭamartviksaṃbaṃdhi [?] tadviśvaṃ kartavyajātaṃ sapta hotrakaiḥ saha svayamaṣṭamaḥ san invati | vyāpnoti | yadvā tadityasya liṃgavyatyayaḥ | sa poteti saṃbaṃdhaḥ | saptahotrakaiḥ sahāṣṭamo bhūtvā tadvadyajñaṃ [?] nirvahatītyarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) यज्ञस्य नेतरि (*yajñasya netari*) — in the one who leads (conducts) the sacrifice; यस्मिन् (*yasmin*) — in which Agni; सप्त रश्मयः (*sapta raśmayaḥ*) — the seven Hotṛs (who are in the form of seven rays); आ तताः (*ā tatāḥ*) — as if they were spread everywhere with their respective duties; पोता (*potā*) — Agni, who is the ṛtvij called Potṛ for the gods; मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*) — like the Potṛ among human ṛtvijs; दैव्यं (*daivyaṃ*) — in the divine sacrifice; अष्टमं (*aṣṭamaṃ*) — joining (the other seven ṛtvijs) as the eighth ṛtvij; तत् विश्वं (*tat viśvaṃ*) — all that is to be done; इन्वति (*invati*) — pervades (carries through).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) In Agni, the conductor of the sacrifice, the seven Hotṛs, in the form of seven rays, are spread everywhere with their respective duties. That Agni, who is the Potṛ of the gods, like the Potṛ among men, carries through all the duties in the sacrifice.

*(Ṛk 2 is left open: its printed English and Special Topics follow on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 494 (PDF 515)

*(Header: "494", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 5", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 2)*

In whom, as conductor of the sacrifice, the seven rays are manifested and who, as a human Potri, officiates in the eighth place to perfect every divine (rite).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

*(The first word of the lemma is printed ಯೋಗಸ್ಯ, i.e. योगस्य (*yogasya*), as printed; the bhāṣya on p. 493 reads यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*). Written as printed.)*

> नेतरि—योगस्य निर्वाहके यस्मिन्नग्नौ ।

> *netari—yogasya nirvāhake yasminnagnau |*

"In which Agni, who conducts the sacrifice", is the commentator's meaning. In this Ṛk, the duties of the ṛtvijs called Netṛ and Potṛ are said to be performed by Agni.

> सप्त रश्मयस्तता—सप्तसंख्याका रश्मिवद्व्याप्ता होत्रका आ तताः । स्वस्वकर्मभिः सर्वतो व्याप्ता भवंति ।

> *sapta raśmayastatā—saptasaṃkhyākā raśmivadvyāptā hotrakā ā tatāḥ | svasvakarmabhiḥ sarvato vyāptā bhavaṃti |*

The meaning is: the Hotṛs, seven in number, like seven rays or like the seven flames of Agni, gather round Agni on every side and are engaged in their respective sacrificial duties. Who the seven Hotṛs are here: as the commentator has said before, the four Hotṛs of the Hotṛ-group and the three ṛtvijs of the Brahmā-group, seven in all, engage in the homa-work; this is the sense. Yāska, for the word सप्तहोतृ (*saptahotṛ*) (seven Hotṛs), gives "the seven rays of Agni" in the explanation of this Ṛk:

*(Reference numerals, 10-64-5, not zoomed. In the third pāda the printed word is आर्यमा, as it appears to be printed [?]; the first pāda is printed वादिते (*vādite*), as printed. The gloss is not given in the source.)*

> दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि व्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा विवाससि ।
> अतूर्तपंथाः पुरुरथो आर्यमा सप्तहोता विषुरूपेषु जन्मसु ॥

> *dakṣasya vādite janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi |*
> *atūrtapaṃthāḥ pururatho āryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-64-5, as printed.)

and in the explanation of this Ṛk he has said:

> सप्तहोता सप्तास्मै रश्मयो रसानभिसन्नामयंति । सप्तैनमृषयः स्तुवंतीति वा ।

> *saptahotā saptāsmai raśmayo rasānabhisannāmayaṃti | saptainamṛṣayaḥ stuvaṃtīti vā |*

(Ni. 11-23, as printed; the numerals not zoomed.) That is: because Agni's rays (flames) are seven, or because seven ṛṣis praise this Agni, Agni gets the name सप्तहोतृ (*saptahotṛ*); so he has explained the sense. In the Ṛk before us the meaning is: seven Hotṛs, or seven ṛtvijs, who are like the seven rays.

> मनुष्वत् दैव्यं अष्टमं पोता विश्वं तत् इन्वति—

> *manuṣvat daivyaṃ aṣṭamaṃ potā viśvaṃ tat invati—*

In this latter-half sentence, the meaning is explained that Agni, together with the seven ṛtvijs mentioned above, becomes himself the eighth ṛtvij, the Potṛ, in the sacrifice performed by men, and is a helper in carrying the sacrificial work to completion.

*(A short rule ":o:" is printed here, ending Ṛk 2.)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral, ೩ (the hooked glyph), not zoomed.)*

> द॒ध॒न्वे वा॒ यदी॒मनु॒ वोच॒द्ब्रह्मा॑णि॒ वेरु॒ तत् ।
> परि॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ काव्या॑ ने॒मिश्च॒क्रमि॑वाभवत् ॥ ३ ॥

> *dadhanve vā yadīmanu vocadbrahmāṇi veru tat |*
> *pari viśvāni kāvyā nemiścakramivābhavat ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> दधन्वे । वा । यत् । ईं । अनु । वोचत् । ब्रह्माणि । वेः । ऊं इति । तत् ।
> परि । विश्वानि । काव्या । नेमिः । चक्रंऽइव । अभवत् ॥ ३ ॥

> *dadhanve | vā | yat | īṃ | anu | vocat | brahmāṇi | veḥ | ūṃ iti | tat |*
> *pari | viśvāni | kāvyā | nemiḥ | cakraṃ 'iva | abhavat ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, being in every priest, himself carries out all: the oblations offered, the mantras recited; he knows and embraces all priestly acts like a wheel's rim.

> पूर्वे मंत्रे होत्रादिवत् स्वयमपि यज्ञं निर्वहतीत्युक्तं । अत्र तु सर्वं तत्तदात्मना स्थित्वा स्वयमेव निर्वहतीत्याह । वा अथवा ईमेनं यज्ञमनु लक्षीकृत्य यद्धविरादिकं दधन्वे धारयत्यध्वर्य्वादिरूपः । यानि ब्रह्माणि शस्त्रादीन्यनुवोचत् । अनुवक्ति होत्रादिरूपः । अत्र वान्वित्येतद्योज्यं । तत्सर्वं वेरु । वेरेव । कामयते जानाति वा स्वयमनुष्ठातुं । अयमग्निर्विश्वानि सर्वाणि काव्यानि । कवयो मेधाविन ऋत्विजः । तत्संबंधीनि कर्माणि पर्यभवत् । परिभवति । स्वायत्तानि करोति । व्याप्नोतीत्यर्थः । व्याप्तौ दृष्टांतः । नेमिः वहिर्वेष्टनवलयश्चक्रं रथांगं यथा कार्त्स्न्येन व्याप्नोति तद्वत् ॥

> *pūrve maṃtre hotrādivat svayamapi yajñaṃ nirvahatītyuktaṃ | atra tu sarvaṃ tattadātmanā sthitvā svayameva nirvahatītyāha | vā athavā īmenaṃ yajñamanu lakṣīkṛtya yaddhavirādikaṃ dadhanve dhārayatyadhvaryvādirūpaḥ | yāni brahmāṇi śastrādīnyanuvocat | anuvakti hotrādirūpaḥ | atra vānvityetadyojyaṃ | tatsarvaṃ veru | vereva | kāmayate jānāti vā svayamanuṣṭhātuṃ | ayamagnirviśvāni sarvāṇi kāvyāni | kavayo medhāvina ṛtvijaḥ | tatsaṃbaṃdhīni karmāṇi paryabhavat | paribhavati | svāyattāni karoti | vyāpnotītyarthaḥ | vyāptau dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | nemiḥ vahirveṣṭanavalayaścakraṃ rathāṃgaṃ yathā kārtsnyena vyāpnoti tadvat ‖*

*(In the bhāṣya the word वहिर्वेष्टन (*vahirveṣṭana*) is printed with व, as printed; the printed sentence "वा अथवा ईमेनं…" is as it stands. No grammatical tail beyond the sense is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) वा (*vā*) — or. ईं अनु (*īṃ anu*) — with reference to this sacrifice. यत् (*yat*) — which oblations. दधन्वे (*dadhanve*) — (the Adhvaryu and others) offer. ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*) — which mantras such as the śastras. वोचत् (*vocat*) — (the Hotṛ and others) recite. तत् (*tat*) — all that as well. वेरु (*veru*) — Agni remains knowing it (desiring it, this Agni). विश्वानि (*viśvāni*) — all. काव्या (*kāvyā*) — the actions of the ṛtvijs. नेमिः (*nemiḥ*) — the outer rim of the wheel. चक्रं इव (*cakraṃ iva*) — as pervading the wheel completely. परि अभवत् (*pari abhavat*) — has pervaded completely.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) Whatever oblations and the like the Adhvaryu and others offer, with reference to this sacrifice, and whatever mantras the Hotṛ and others recite, Agni knows all of them. As the outer rim of a wheel pervades the wheel completely, so this Agni, desiring them, has pervaded all the actions of all the ṛtvijs.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 3)*

Whatever (offerings the priest) presents, whatever prayers he recites, he, (Agni), knows them all : he comprehends all priestly acts, as the circumference (includes the spokes) of a wheel.

### Printed p. 496 (PDF 517)

*(Header: "496", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 5", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

In the preceding Ṛk it was only said that Agni, like the Hotṛ and other ṛtvijs, engages himself in the work of conducting the sacrifice. In this Ṛk it is described that Agni himself, being present in the several ṛtvijs, each in his own part, performs the work of all the ṛtvijs.

> वा ईं अनु दधन्वे—

> *vā īṃ anu dadhanve—*

The ṛtvijs such as the Adhvaryu offer in the sacrifice whatever oblations; Agni himself, knowing all this, in the form of the Adhvaryu offers the oblation in the homa; in the same way,

> ब्रह्माणि वोचत् तत् वेरु—

> *brahmāṇi vocat tat veru—*

whatever mantras, such as the śastras and stotras, the ṛtvijs of the Hotṛ-group recite, Agni knows them without fail, and he himself recites them.

> परि विश्वानि काव्या नेमिः चक्रमिव अभवत्—

> *pari viśvāni kāvyā nemiḥ cakramiva abhavat—*

Besides this, Agni himself does all the actions that the wise ṛtvijs do in the sacrifice, or is capable of doing them. An illustration is given here in this connection. The nemi of a wheel, that is, the band that goes round the outside (the tyre, as printed in English "Tyre"), pervades the wheel on every side; in the way it pervades the whole wheel, in that way Agni pervades all the actions carried on in the sacrifice; that is, taking part himself in all the actions of the sacrifice, he brings the sacrifice to completion; this is the meaning.

*(A short rule is printed here, ending the Special Topics of Ṛk 3.)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral, ೪ (the glyph like ಳ), not zoomed. In the Saṃhitā the first word of the second line is printed with a small mark above the first letter, which looks like an anunāsika: written विद्वाँ [?].)*

> सा॒कं हि शुचि॑ना॒ शुचिः॑ प्रशा॒स्ता क्रतु॒नाज॑नि ।
> वि॒द्वाँ अ॑स्य व्र॒ता ध्रु॒वा व॒या इ॒वानु॑ रोहते ॥ ४ ॥

> *sākaṃ hi śucinā śuciḥ praśāstā kratunājani |*
> *vidvā~ asya vratā dhruvā vayā ivānu rohate ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> साकं । हि । शुचिना । शुचिः । प्रशास्ता । क्रतुना । अजनि ।
> विद्वान् । अस्य । व्रता । ध्रुवा । वयाःऽइव । अनु । रोहते ॥ ४ ॥

> *sākaṃ | hi | śucinā | śuciḥ | praśāstā | kratunā | ajani |*
> *vidvān | asya | vratā | dhruvā | vayāḥ 'iva | anu | rohate ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 497 (PDF 518)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 26 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "497", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. Ṛk 4 continues from p. 496.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 4)**

*Gist:* Agni, self-pure and the regulator, was born together with the purifying rites; the sacrificer who knows his fixed rites performs them in order, like spreading branches.

> शुचिः स्वयं शोधकः प्रशास्ता देवानां एतन्नामक ऋत्विक् प्रशासिता वा यज्ञविघ्नानां शुचिना क्रतुना शोधकेनाग्निहोत्रादिकर्मणा साकं हि सहैवाजनि । उत्पन्नः । जातमात्र एव शुद्धः सर्वस्य प्रशास्ता च सन्नग्निहोत्रादिनिर्वोढाभवदित्यर्थः । अस्याग्नेर्ध्रुवा ध्रुवाणि फलपर्यवसायीनि व्रतानि कर्माणि विद्वान् जानन् यजमानो वयो इव विस्तृताः शाखा इवानुरोहते । क्रमेणानुतिष्ठति ॥

> *śuciḥ svayaṃ śodhakaḥ praśāstā devānāṃ etannāmaka ṛtvik praśāsitā vā yajñavighnānāṃ śucinā kratunā śodhakenāgnihotrādikarmaṇā sākaṃ hi sahaivājani | utpannaḥ | jātamātra eva śuddhaḥ sarvasya praśāstā ca sannagnihotrādinirvoḍhābhavadityarthaḥ | asyāgnerdhruvā dhruvāṇi phalaparyavasāyīni vratāni karmāṇi vidvān jānan yajamāno vayo iva vistṛtāḥ śākhā ivānurohate | krameṇānutiṣṭhati ‖*

*(No grammatical tail beyond the sense is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) — himself the purifier; प्रशास्ता (*praśāstā*) — the destroyer of the obstacles of the sacrifice; or, Agni who is the ṛtvij of that name (Praśāstṛ); शुचिना (*śucinā*) — the purifying; क्रतुना साकं हि (*kratunā sākaṃ hi*) — together with the rites such as the Agnihotra; अजनि (*ajani*) — was born; अस्य (*asya*) — of this Agni; ध्रुवा व्रता (*dhruvā vratā*) — the rites that end in their fruit; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — the sacrificer who knows; वयो इव (*vayo iva*) — like spreading branches; अनु रोहते (*anu rohate*) — following Agni's pattern (the Kannada word is printed ಮಾದರಿ, "model, pattern"), he ascends (carries them out) in order.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) Agni, himself the purifier and the destroyer of the obstacles of the sacrifice, was born together with the purifying rites such as the Agnihotra. The sacrificers who resort to the fruit-ending rites of this Agni, who is the root, as the branches of a tree spread following the tree that is their root, carry them out in order, following the pattern of Agni alone.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 4)*

The pure regulator (of the sacrifice) is born verily together with the holy act; the wise (worshipper) performs all his, (Agni's), prescribed rites in succession, as the branches spring (from a common stem).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated.)

In this Ṛk Agni is described as performing the work of the Praśāstṛ. The Praśāstṛ is one of the 16 ṛtvijs (the numeral printed, not zoomed). The duty of this ṛtvij is to prevent the obstacles that may arise in the sacrifice and to see that the sacrifice proceeds with all its parts complete. Therefore, "प्रशास्ता प्रशासिता वा यज्ञविघ्नानां शुचिना क्रतुना शोधकेनाग्निहोत्रादिकर्मणा (*praśāstā praśāsitā vā yajñavighnānāṃ śucinā kratunā śodhakenāgnihotrādikarmaṇā*)" — that is, he purifies the obstacles of the sacrifice by his command, or by rites of the nature of expiation such as the Agnihotra, and makes the sacrifice go forward. Therefore he is called Praśāstṛ — (the one who lays down that "the sacrifice must proceed in this way"; the text continues on p. 498).

### Printed p. 498 (PDF 519)

*(Header: "498", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 5", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) …the one who regulates, who commands, who orders: such is the name. It is described here that Agni was born from such a ṛtvij-form.

An illustration is given here for the rites carried out in the sacrifice. वयो इव अनु रोहते (*vayo iva anu rohate*) — as a tree grows, branches grow one above another all round its trunk; in the same way, in the sacrifice, as soon as one rite has been done according to an orderly rule, the rite that follows it is performed. The meaning is that the sacrificer, knowing these rites of Agni, which are of the nature of rules, performs them accordingly.

The word क्रतु (*kratu*) is read among the names of action (Ni. 3-2, as it appears [?]; numerals not zoomed). And for the word kratu the meaning "wisdom" (prajñā) is also given there: क्रतुं कर्म वा प्रज्ञां वा (*kratuṃ karma vā prajñāṃ vā*) (Ni. 3-28 [?]). Or the word kratu is read among the 11 names of wisdom beginning with केतः (*ketaḥ*) (Ni. 3-13 [?]).

व्रता (*vratā*) — वृतानि [?] (*vṛtāni [?]*): actions, rules. व्रतमिति कर्मनाम, वृणोतीति सतः (*vratamiti karmanāma, vṛṇotīti sataḥ*): "vrata" means karma. Because this karma (sin or meritorious action) always covers (surrounds) the doer who performs the action, karma is called vrata. Or,

> इदमपीतरत् व्रतमेतस्मादेव निवृत्तिकर्म वारयतीति सतः । अन्नमपि व्रतमुच्यते यदा वृणोति शरीरं ॥

> *idamapītarat vratametasmādeva nivṛttikarma vārayatīti sataḥ | annamapi vratamucyate yadā vṛṇoti śarīraṃ ‖*

(Ni. 2-13, as printed.)

Besides this, the abstention-rites (nivṛtti-karma) such as yama and niyama are also called vrata. This applies to Vedic rites done in the presence of Agni and to other rites as well. Therefore, वारयतीति सतः (*vārayatīti sataḥ*): because it keeps away from men the things, such as women, that cause obstacles to the rite of abstention, it is called vrata. And because food, as the support of the body, pervades the body and nourishes it, food too is called vrata: so the derivation of the word vrata has been given.

*(A short rule is printed here, ending the Special Topics of Ṛk 4.)*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral ೫, not zoomed.)*

> ता अ॑स्य॒ वर्ण॑मा॒युवो॒ नेष्टुः॑ सचंत धे॒नवः॑ ।
> कु॒वित्ति॒सृभ्य॒ आ वरं॒ स्वसा॑रो॒ या इ॒दं य॒युः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tā asya varṇamāyuvo neṣṭuḥ sacaṃta dhenavaḥ |*
> *kuvittisṛbhya ā varaṃ svasāro yā idaṃ yayuḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 499 (PDF 520)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 26.]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "499", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ताः । अस्य । वर्णं । आयुवः । नेष्टुः । सचंत । धेनवः ।
> कुवित् । तिसृभ्यः । आ । वरं । स्वसारः । याः । इदं । ययुः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tāḥ | asya | varṇaṃ | āyuvaḥ | neṣṭuḥ | sacaṃta | dhenavaḥ |*
> *kuvit | tisṛbhyaḥ | ā | varaṃ | svasāraḥ | yāḥ | idaṃ | yayuḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 5)**

*Gist:* The fingers, which carry out this rite, are the milch cows and sisters of Agni as Neṣṭṛ; they serve his excellent form, belonging to the three fires, in many ways.

> या वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणा या अंगुलय इदमनुष्ठीयमानं कर्म ययुः । अनुतिष्ठंति । ता आयुवो गंत्र्यो व्याप्ता धेनवः प्रीणयित्र्यः स्वसारः स्वयं सारिण्योऽंगुलयो नेष्टुर्विर्वाचितुर्भुक्षयितुः शोधयितुः पोषयितुर्नेतुर्वास्याग्नेः । यद्वैतन्नामकऋत्विग्रूपस्य । तिसृभ्य आ गार्हपत्यादिमूर्तीनामपि वरं वर्णं कुवित् बहुकृत्वः सचंते । सेवंते । परिचरंति ॥

> *yā vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇā yā aṃgulaya idamanuṣṭhīyamānaṃ karma yayuḥ | anutiṣṭhaṃti | tā āyuvo gaṃtryo vyāptā dhenavaḥ prīṇayitryaḥ svasāraḥ svayaṃ sāriṇyo 'ṃgulayo neṣṭurvirvāciturbhukṣayituḥ śodhayituḥ poṣayiturneturvāsyāgneḥ | yadvaitannāmakaṛtvigrūpasya | tisṛbhya ā gārhapatyādimūrtīnāmapi varaṃ varṇaṃ kuvit bahukṛtvaḥ sacaṃte | sevaṃte | paricaraṃti ‖*

*(In the bhāṣya the word group after अंगुलयो (*aṃgulayo*) is printed as नेष्टुर्विर्वाचितुर्भुक्षयितुः (*neṣṭurvirvāciturbhukṣayituḥ*); the middle word is doubtful [?]. No grammatical tail is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) याः (*yāḥ*) — which fingers; इदं (*idaṃ*) — this specified rite; ययुः (*yayuḥ*) — accomplish; ताः (*tāḥ*) — those same fingers; आयुवः (*āyuvaḥ*) — which spread out for the sake of the rite; धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) — which give pleasure; स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) — which are mutually of sister-nature; नेष्टुः (*neṣṭuḥ*) — of the one who is of Neṣṭṛ form; अस्य (*asya*) — of this Agni; तिसृभ्यः आ (*tisṛbhyaḥ ā*) — belonging to all three forms, Gārhapatya and the rest; वरं वर्णं (*varaṃ varṇaṃ*) — the excellent form; कुवित् (*kuvit*) — in many ways; सचंते (*sacaṃte*) — serve.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) The fingers which accomplish this specified rite, the same fingers, spreading out for the sake of the rite, giving pleasure, and being sisters to one another, serve in many ways the excellent form of this Agni, who is of Neṣṭṛ form, belonging to all three forms, Gārhapatya and the rest.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 5)*

The sister fingers, which are the milch cows of the Neshtri, are those which accomplish his, (Agni's), worship; and in various ways are combined for this purpose through the three (sacred fires).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated.)

स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) — Because the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) is read among the names of fingers (Ni. 3-8 as it appears [?]; numerals not zoomed), it means "fingers". For this word, formed from the root असु—क्षेपणे (*asu—kṣepaṇe*) together with the prefix सु (*su*), he gives: सुष्ठु अस्यते क्षिप्यते पदार्थः आभिः कार्येषु क्षेप्तव्या वा (*suṣṭhu asyate kṣipyate padārthaḥ ābhiḥ kāryeṣu kṣeptavyā vā*) — that is, which… (the sentence is cut off at the end of the page and continues on p. 500).

*(Ṛk 5 is left open in its Special Topics.)*

---

### Printed p. 500 (PDF 521)

*(Header: "500", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 5", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Special Topics of Ṛk 5 continue from p. 499; the first word is cut off at the left margin, so only its ending "…dāradū" is visible.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) …whatever work is done, things are placed in their proper places by these fingers. That is, because the fingers are used when work is done, these fingers are called स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*). Or the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) may also be formed from the root षद्ऌ [?]—विशरणे (*ṣadḷ [?]—viśaraṇe*) taken together with a word printed ಸ್ತೆ [?], which I take to be the prefix-word *sva*. In this connection the following is given:

> स्वं स्वं व्यापारं गच्छंति प्राप्नुवंति स्वस्मिन् स्वस्मिन् हस्ते सीदंतीति वा—

> *svaṃ svaṃ vyāpāraṃ gacchaṃti prāpnuvaṃti svasmin svasmin haste sīdaṃtīti vā—*

Kannada: these fingers, staying in their own hands, that is, the left or the right hands, engage in their own works (actions); therefore स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) means fingers. And again:

> अथवा परस्परं भगिनीव दृश्यंते, एकहस्तप्रभुत्वात् स्वसार उच्यंते—

> *athavā parasparaṃ bhaginīva dṛśyaṃte, ekahastaprabhutvāt svasāra ucyaṃte—*

That is: the fingers born in one hand are seen, one beside another, like elder and younger sisters; therefore the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) means fingers. In this way the etymological sense of the word can be given in three ways. In the Ṛgveda the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) is used in many places in the sense of fingers:

*Cited (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-62-10, numerals not zoomed):*

> पुरू सहस्रा जनयो न पत्नीर्दुवस्यंति स्वसारो अह्रयाणं ।

> *purū sahasrā janayo na patnīrduvasyaṃti svasāro ahrayāṇaṃ |*

In this Ṛk, for the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) the bhāṣyakāra gives:

> स्वयमेव सरंत्योंऽगुलयः—

> *svayameva saraṃtyoṃ 'gulayaḥ—*

That is, because their movement in the performance of works goes on of itself, the bhāṣyakāra explains this word as meaning fingers. And again:

*Cited (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-71-1, numerals not zoomed; the word after अजुष्र is doubtful):*

> स्वसारः श्यावीमरुषीमजुष्र [?] चित्रमुच्छंतीमुषसं न गावः ।

> *svasāraḥ śyāvīmaruṣīmajuṣra [?] citramucchaṃtīmuṣasaṃ na gāvaḥ |*

*Cited (Ṛg. Saṃ. 3-29-13):*

> दश स्वसारो अग्रुवः समीचीः पुमांसं जातमभि सं रभंते ।

> *daśa svasāro agruvaḥ samīcīḥ pumāṃsaṃ jātamabhi saṃ rabhaṃte |*

*Cited (Ṛg. Saṃ. 4-6-8):*

> द्विर्यं पंच जीजनन्त्संवसानाः स्वसारो अग्निं मानुषीषु विक्षु ।

> *dviryaṃ paṃca jījanantsaṃvasānāḥ svasāro agniṃ mānuṣīṣu vikṣu |*

In these Ṛks and others, the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) has been given the meaning "fingers" alone.

**कुवित्** (*kuvit*) — Among the twelve names of "many" beginning with उरु (*uru*), तुवि (*tuvi*) and so on, the word कुवित् (*kuvit*) is read (Ni. 3-13 [?], printed "ಸಿ. ೩-೧೩", the abbreviation ಸಿ. [sic] for Ni.); therefore कुवित् (*kuvit*) means "abundantly, many times".

**नेष्टुः** (*neṣṭuḥ*) — Sāyaṇa's words (the word is printed clearly here as हविर्याचितुः (*haviryācituḥ*) and भक्षयितुः (*bhakṣayituḥ*); this corrects the readings विर्वाचितुः (*virvācituḥ*) and भुक्षयितुः (*bhukṣayituḥ*) noted [?] on p. 499):

> नेष्टुः—हविर्याचितुर्भक्षयितुः पोषयितुर्नेतुर्वास्याग्नेः । यद्वैतन्नामकऋत्विग्रूपस्य ।

> *neṣṭuḥ—haviryāciturbhakṣayituḥ poṣayiturneturvāsyāgneḥ | yadvaitannāmakaṛtvigrūpasya |*

Kannada: Sāyaṇa explains this word as Agni who asks for the havis, who eats, who nourishes (promotes), and who leads (carries) the havis to the gods; or as Agni who has the form of the ṛtvij called Neṣṭṛ. That is, Agni who desires the havis, who eats it, who increases it, who takes to the gods the havis that the sacrificers offer in the fire; or who himself performs (the page ends in the middle of the sentence: …) the work of the ṛtvij named Neṣṭṛ. [The sentence runs over onto p. 501.]

### Printed p. 501 (PDF 522)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 26 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "501", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) …and who himself completes the rite of the ṛtvij called Neṣṭṛ; this is the intention.

**तिसृभ्य आ वरं** (*tisṛbhya ā varaṃ*) — This means the Agni who is in the three forms (fire-pits): Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni.

Here the word धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) is used as a qualifier of the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*), in the sense "giving pleasure like cows". The fingers in the hand of the ṛtvij Neṣṭṛ serve abundantly the three forms of Agni in the sacrificial rites. The chief intention is: as cows give milk and please, so the services and the like performed by the fingers of the Neṣṭṛ please Agni.

*(A short rule is printed here, ending the Special Topics of Ṛk 5.)*

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral ೬, the hooked glyph, not zoomed.)*

> यदी॑ मा॒तुरुप॒ स्वसा॑ घृ॒तं भरं॒त्यस्थि॑त ।
> तासा॑मध्व॒र्युराग॑तौ॒ युवो॑ वृ॒ष्टीव॑ मोदते ॥ ६ ॥

> *yadī māturupa svasā ghṛtaṃ bharaṃtyasthita |*
> *tāsāmadhvaryurāgatau yuvo vṛṣṭīva modate ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(In the Pada the avagraha mark is printed after वृष्टी and आ, as in वयाःऽइव (*vayāḥ 'iva*) of Ṛk 4; the first line has no visarga after वृष्टी in the print: written वृष्टीऽ इव, as printed.)*

> यदि । मातुः । उप । स्वसा । घृतं । भरंती । अस्थित ।
> तासां । अध्वर्युः । आऽगतौ । युवः । वृष्टीऽ इव । मोदते ॥ ६ ॥

> *yadi | mātuḥ | upa | svasā | ghṛtaṃ | bharaṃtī | asthita |*
> *tāsāṃ | adhvaryuḥ | ā 'gatau | yuvaḥ | vṛṣṭī ' iva | modate ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 6)**

*Gist:* When the ladles, sisters of the altar, stand near Agni full of ghee, Agni as Adhvaryu rejoices at their arrival, like barley at rain.

> यदि यदा मातुः सर्वस्य निर्मातुर्भूम्या वेदिलक्षणायाः स्वसा स्वसृस्थानीयो जुहूर्घृतं भरंती सत्युपास्थिते । उपतिष्ठेदग्निं । एकवचनमविवक्षितं । जुहूपभृद्ध्रुवा घृतं भरंत्यस्तिष्ठंतीत्यर्थः । तदा तासां जुहृादीनामागतौ यागाय प्राप्तौ सत्यामध्वर्युरेतन्नामक ऋत्विग्रूपोऽध्वरं कामयमानो वायुमग्निर्मोदते [?] । हृष्यति । युवो वृष्टीव वृष्ट्या यथा मोदते तद्वत् ॥

> *yadi yadā mātuḥ sarvasya nirmāturbhūmyā vedilakṣaṇāyāḥ svasā svasṛsthānīyo juhūrghṛtaṃ bharaṃtī satyupāsthite | upatiṣṭhedagniṃ | ekavacanamavivakṣitaṃ | juhūpabhṛddhruvā ghṛtaṃ bharaṃtyastiṣṭhaṃtītyarthaḥ | tadā tāsāṃ juhṛādīnāmāgatau yāgāya prāptau satyāmadhvaryuretannāmaka ṛtvigrūpo 'dhvaraṃ kāmayamāno vāyumagnirmodate [?] | hṛṣyati | yuvo vṛṣṭīva vṛṣṭyā yathā modate tadvat ‖*

*(Printed जुहृादीनाम् (*juhṛādīnām*) for जुह्वादीनाम् in one place is my reading of a doubtful conjunct; the word before अग्निर्मोदते (*agnirmodate*) is printed as वायुम् (*vāyum*) [?]. No grammatical tail beyond the sense is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) यदि (*yadi*) — when; मातुः (*mātuḥ*) — of the earth, the maker of the world and of the form of the altar; स्वसा (*svasā*) — the ladles that are of sister-nature; घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*) — the ājya (clarified butter); भरंति (*bharaṃti*) — filling; उप अस्थिते (*upa asthite*) — when Agni is placed near, (then); तासां (*tāsāṃ*) — of those ladles, Juhū and the rest; आगतौ (*āgatau*) — at the time of their coming; अध्वर्युः (*adhvaryuḥ*) — Agni who desires the sacrifice, or who is named Adhvaryu; युवः (*yuvaḥ*) — the barley grain (printed ಯುವ, "yuva"); वृष्टीव (*vṛṣṭīva*) — as it shows joy at the coming of rain; मोदते (*modate*) — rejoices.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) When the ladles Juhū and the rest, being sisters to the earth in the form of the altar, filled with ājya, Agni comes near, then Agni, who desires the sacrifice, rejoices exceedingly, as the barley grain shows joy at the time of the coming of rain.

### Printed p. 502 (PDF 523)

*(Header: "502", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 5", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Pratipadārtha and Bhāvārtha above run over from p. 501 to this page; the lines from "…ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಸಮೀಪದಲ್ಲಿ" onward are on p. 502.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 6)*

When the sister, (vessel), bearing the clarified butter, is placed near the maternal (altar), the Adhwaryu (Agni) rejoices at their approach, like barley (at the fall of) rain.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated.)

In this Ṛk the meaning of the words मातुः स्वसा (*mātuḥ svasā*) is not stated clearly, but the bhāṣyakāra has fitted the meanings "altar" and "Juhū" to them according to the context and explained them so. For the word मातृ (*mātṛ*) various meanings are given according to context: mother, maker, altar, world, earth. Here he gives the meaning "sacrificial altar", and for the word स्वसा (*svasā*) he explains "the Juhū, which is like a sister to the altar, the wooden ladle with which ājya is offered". Although the sense fits well with this explanation, there remains a doubt as to whether these words have really been used in these meanings.

अध्वर्युः घृतं भरंती आगतौ युवः वृष्टीव मोदते (*adhvaryuḥ ghṛtaṃ bharaṃtī āgatau yuvaḥ vṛṣṭīva modate*) — The comparison stated in this illustration fits well. When the ṛtvij called Adhvaryu, having filled the ladles used for offering with ājya (ghee) for the oblation in the fire, comes near Agni, the joy that arises in Agni is described thus: as the plants of barley welcome with great joy the rain that they need, so Agni too is gladdened.

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral ७ is the flat-footed glyph, not zoomed. In the first line the print shows what looks like a न् before ऋत्विग्, i.e. "कृणुतान्ऋत्विगृत्विजं"; the Pada has कृणुतां । ऋत्विक् । I give the Saṃhitā as printed [?].)*

> स्वः स्वाय॒ धाय॑से कृणु॒तान्ऋ॒त्विगृ॒त्विजं॑ [?] ।
> स्तोमं॑ य॒ज्ञं चादरं॑ व॒नेमा॑ ररि॒मा व॒यं ॥ ७ ॥

> *svaḥ svāya dhāyase kṛṇutānṛtvigṛtvijaṃ [?] |*
> *stomaṃ yajñaṃ cādaraṃ vanemā rarimā vayaṃ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्वः । स्वाय । धायसे । कृणुतां । ऋत्विक् । ऋत्विजं ।
> स्तोमं । यज्ञं । च । आत् । अरं । वनेम । ररिम । वयं ॥ ७ ॥

> *svaḥ | svāya | dhāyase | kṛṇutāṃ | ṛtvik | ṛtvijaṃ |*
> *stomaṃ | yajñaṃ | ca | āt | araṃ | vanema | rarima | vayaṃ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 7)**

*Gist:* Agni himself, as the divine ṛtvij, is asked to perform the priests' duties of this rite; we, by his favour, praise and offer oblations in full measure.

> अयमग्निः स्वः स्वयमेव स्वाय स्वकीयाय धायसे कर्मणे हविषां धारणाय वा ऋत्विक् होताजनिष्वेत्यादिनोक्तलक्षणो होतृपोतृप्रशास्त्राद्यृत्विग्रूपः सन् ऋत्विजमार्त्विज्यं ॥ भावप्रधानोऽयं निर्देशः ॥ देवर्त्विग्रूपः सन् ऋत्विजं मानुषमार्त्विज्यं कृणुतां । करोतु । वयं च तदनुग्रहात् अदनंतरमेव स्तोमं स्तोत्रं यज्ञं च तदाश्रयं योगमुप्यैरमलमत्यर्थं [?] वनेम । संभजेमहि । ररिम ददेमहि च हविः । यद्वा स्तोमं वनेम यज्ञं यज्ञयोग्यं हवी ररिम ॥

> *ayamagniḥ svaḥ svayameva svāya svakīyāya dhāyase karmaṇe haviṣāṃ dhāraṇāya vā ṛtvik hotājaniṣvetyādinoktalakṣaṇo hotṛpotṛpraśāstrādyṛtvigrūpaḥ san ṛtvijamārtvijyaṃ ‖ bhāvapradhāno 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ ‖ devartvigrūpaḥ san ṛtvijaṃ mānuṣamārtvijyaṃ kṛṇutāṃ | karotu | vayaṃ ca tadanugrahāt adanaṃtarameva stomaṃ stotraṃ yajñaṃ ca tadāśrayaṃ yogamupyairamalamatyarthaṃ [?] vanema | saṃbhajemahi | rarima dademahi ca haviḥ | yadvā stomaṃ vanema yajñaṃ yajñayogyaṃ havī rarima ‖*

*(The words योगमुप्यैरमलमत्यर्थं (*yogamupyairamalamatyarthaṃ*) are given as printed and are doubtful [?]; no grammatical tail beyond the sense is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated:) (अयमग्निः (*ayamagniḥ*) — this Agni.) स्वः (*svaḥ*) — himself; स्वाय (*svāya*) — for his own; धायसे (*dhāyase*) — for the rite, or for the holding (bearing) of the oblations; ऋत्विक् (*ṛtvik*) — as the ṛtvij of the form of the Hotṛ and the others described before; ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvijaṃ*) — the work to be accomplished by the Hotṛ and the others; कृणुतां (*kṛṇutāṃ*) — may he accomplish; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we also; आत् (*āt*) — immediately after that; स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*) — the stotra (praise); यज्ञं च (*yajñaṃ ca*) — and the sacrifice based on it; अरं (*araṃ*) — fully; वनेम (*vanema*) — we worship (resort to); ररिम (*rarima*) — we also offer the oblation.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated:) May this Agni, himself in the form of the ṛtvij, for his own rite, accomplish the work to be accomplished by the Hotṛ and the others. Immediately after that, we also fully resort to the stotra and to the sacrifice based on it, (accomplishing them), and we offer the oblation.

### Printed p. 504 (PDF 525)

*(Header: "504", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 5", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 7)*

May he, the ministering priest, discharge the office of priest at his own ceremony, and may we worthily repeat (his) praise, and offer (him) sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated.)

**सः ऋत्विक् ऋत्विजं कृणुतां (*saḥ ṛtvik ṛtvijaṃ kṛṇutāṃ*)** — In this sacrifice, which Agni himself accomplishes, the wish is stated here that, as said before, he himself should carry out the duties of the many ṛtvijs who take part in the sacrifice — Hotṛ, Potṛ, Praśāstṛ and the rest — and bring the sacrifice to completion. The use of the words ऋत्विक् ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvik ṛtvijaṃ*) here indicates all the ṛtvijs, Hotṛ and the others. That is, Agni himself (in the form of each respective ṛtvij) does the works that all of them do. The intention is that Agni, who is of the form of the divine ṛtvij, does the works that the human ṛtvijs do.

**स्तोमं यज्ञं चादरं वनेमा ररिमा वयं (*stomaṃ yajñaṃ cādaraṃ vanemā rarimā vayaṃ*)** — If, as said above, Agni himself does the sacrificial works that all the ṛtvijs do, what is it that we have to do? The answer: we also, in the sacrifice, recite the stotras and the like and praise the gods, and offer the oblations and the like; thus the works done by us (the sacrificers and the others) are also described.

*(A short divider line ":o:" is printed here, ending Ṛk 7.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral ८ is the "ಲ"-like glyph, not zoomed.)*

> यथा॑ वि॒द्वा अरं॒ कर॒द्विश्वे॑भ्यो यज॒तेभ्यः॑ ।
> अ॒यम॑ग्ने॒ त्वे अपि॒ यं य॒ज्ञं च॑कृ॒मा व॒यं ॥ ८ ॥

> *yathā vidvā araṃ karadviśvebhyo yajatebhyaḥ |*
> *ayamagne tve api yaṃ yajñaṃ cakṛmā vayaṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यथा । विद्वान् । अरं । करत् । विश्वेभ्यः । यजतेभ्यः ।
> अयं । अग्ने । त्वे इति । अपि । यं । यज्ञं । चकृम । वयं ॥ ८ ॥

> *yathā | vidvān | araṃ | karat | viśvebhyaḥ | yajatebhyaḥ |*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 8)**

*Gist:* Agni, grant that the knowing sacrificer may offer full worship to all the gods worthy of sacrifice, and that our sacrifice may be perfected in you also.

> हे अग्ने विद्वान् त्वन्माहात्म्याभिज्ञः प्रयोगज्ञो वा यजमानो यथा विश्वेभ्यो यजतेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो यजनीयेभ्यो देवेभ्योऽरं पर्याप्तं करत्

> *he agne vidvān tvanmāhātmyābhijñaḥ prayogajño vā yajamāno yathā viśvebhyo yajatebhyaḥ sarvebhyo yajanīyebhyo devebhyo 'raṃ paryāptaṃ karat*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated:) अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — the sacrificer who knows your greatness (or who is expert in the performance); यथा (*yathā*) — in whatever manner; विश्वेभ्यः (*viśvebhyaḥ*) — to all; यजतेभ्यः (*yajatebhyaḥ*) — to the gods who are worthy of sacrifice; अरं (*araṃ*) — so as to be full (complete); करत् (*karat*) — offers worship, (so favour him); वयमपि (*vayamapi*) — we also; यं यज्ञं (*yaṃ yajñaṃ*) — whatever sacrifice; चकृम (*cakṛma*) — we accomplish, (that sacrifice); त्वे अपि (*tve api*) — in you also, (may it obtain) fulfilment.

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, may you so favour that the worship offered by the sacrificer, who knows your greatness and knows the nature of the performance, reaches all the gods worthy of sacrifice together and brings them satisfaction. And do you, Agni, (grant), that this wise (worshipper) may worthily offer (worship) to all the adorable (divinities), and that the sacrifice which we offer may also be perfected in you.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated.)

This Ṛk is of the nature of a conclusion to this sūkta. The prayer is stated that the sacrifice we perform may bring satisfaction to the gods and also to you, Agni.

**विद्वान्—त्वन्माहात्म्याभिज्ञः प्रयोगज्ञो वा यजमानः (*vidvān—tvanmāhātmyābhijñaḥ prayogajño vā yajamānaḥ*)** — The sacrificer who performs the sacrifice is one who knows your greatness, Agni, and your extraordinary personality; or who knows the various programmes to be carried out in the sacrifice and the rules for performing them.

**विश्वेभ्यः यजतेभ्यः (*viśvebhyaḥ yajatebhyaḥ*)** — A prayer was made to Agni: "Favour that satisfaction may come to all those gods whom we invoke in this sacrifice and whom we intend to satisfy with stotras and the like and with the offering of oblations."

**अयं अग्ने त्वे अपि यज्ञं चकृमा वयं (*ayaṃ agne tve api yajñaṃ cakṛmā vayaṃ*)** — Not only favour that the gods concerned are satisfied, but also (favour) that in this sacrifice which we perform, joy may arise in you too (in Agni)… *(The sentence is cut off at the end of the page and continues on p. 506.)*

## Sūkta 6 (the sixth sūkta)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (introduction to Sūkta 6)**

*Gist:* Sūkta 6 has eight Ṛks, ṛṣi Somāhuti Bhārgava, deity Agni, metre Gāyatrī; it is used at the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra, and at the Upasad rite in the afternoon (as the Sāmidhenī verses).

> इमां म इत्यष्टर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं सोमाहुत्यार्षमाग्नेयं गायत्रं । इमां मे गायत्रं हीत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्गायत्रे छंदस्यस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । इमां मे अग्ने समिधमिमामिति त्रयाणामुत्तमामुद्धरेत् । आ. ४-१३ [?] । इति ॥ अपराह्णिक्यामुपसदीमां मे अग्ने समिधमिति तिस्र ऋचस्त्रिरभ्यस्ता नव सामिधेन्यः कृत्वा विनियोक्तव्याः । अथोपसदिति खंडे सूत्रितं । इमां मे अग्ने समिधमिमामिति तु सामिधेन्यः । आ. ४-८ । इति ॥

> *imāṃ ma ityaṣṭarcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ somāhutyārṣamāgneyaṃ gāyatraṃ | imāṃ me gāyatraṃ hītyanukrāṃtaṃ ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorgāyatre chaṃdasyasya viniyogaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | imāṃ me agne samidhamimāmiti trayāṇāmuttamāmuddharet | ā. 4-13 [?] | iti ‖ aparāhṇikyāmupasadīmāṃ me agne samidhamiti tisra ṛcastrirabhyastā nava sāmidhenyaḥ kṛtvā viniyoktavyāḥ | athopasaditi khaṃḍe sūtritaṃ | imāṃ me agne samidhamimāmiti tu sāmidhenyaḥ | ā. 4-8 | iti ‖*

*(The two Āśvalāyana-sūtra references are given as printed: "Ā. 4-13" [?] (the second numeral doubtful, not zoomed) and "Ā. 4-8".)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada, translated):** This sūkta beginning इमां मे (*imāṃ me*) is the sixth sūkta in the first Anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The ṛṣi is the same Somāhuti Bhārgava who was the ṛṣi of the preceding sūkta; the deity is Agni; the metre Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इमां मे गायत्रं हि (*imāṃ me gāyatraṃ hi*). The employment (viniyoga) of this sūkta, for the Gāyatrī-metre Ṛks at the time of the Prātaranuvāka and of reciting the Āśvina-śastra mantras, is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra: इमां मे समिधमिमामिति त्रयाणामुत्तमामुद्धरेत् (*imāṃ me samidhamimāmiti trayāṇāmuttamāmuddharet*) (Ā. 4-13 [?]). And at the Upasad rite performed at the afternoon time, the three Ṛks of this sūkta beginning इमां मे अग्ने समिधं (*imāṃ me agne samidhaṃ*), each recited three times, are to be used as nine Ṛks called Sāmidhenī; this is explained by the sūtra in the section of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra called अथोपसत् (*athopasat*): इमां मे अग्ने समिधमिमामिति तु सामिधेन्यः (*imāṃ me agne samidhamimāmiti tu sāmidhenyaḥ*) (Ā. 4-8).

**॥ ॐ ॥**

**सूक्त—६ (Sūkta 6)**

Maṇḍala 2 · Anuvāka 1 · Sūkta 6 · Aṣṭaka 2 · Adhyāya 5 · Varga 27 *(numeral read from the strip, not zoomed [?])* · Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8.

ऋषिः—सोमाहुतिभार्गवः (*Ṛṣi: Somāhuti Bhārgava*). देवता—अग्निः (*Devatā: Agni*). छंदः—गायत्री (*Chandas: Gāyatrī*).

### Printed p. 507 (PDF 528)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 27 ]" [numeral not zoomed [?]], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "507". The numeral file has no rows for this page. Accent marks are not reproduced.)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इ॒मां मे॑ अग्ने स॒मिध॑मि॒मामु॑प॒सदं॑ वनेः ।
> इ॒मा उ॒ षु श्रु॑धी॒ गिरः॑ ॥ १ ॥

> *imāṃ me agne samidhamimāmupasadaṃ vaneḥ |*
> *imā u ṣu śrudhī giraḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इमां । मे । अग्ने । सम्ऽइधं । इमां । उपऽसदं । वनेः इति वनेः ।
> इमाः । ऊं इति । सु । श्रुधि । गिरः ॥ १ ॥

> *imāṃ | me | agne | sam 'idhaṃ | imāṃ | upa 'sadaṃ | vaneḥ iti vaneḥ |*
> *imāḥ | ūṃ iti | su | śrudhi | giraḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 1)**

*Gist:* Agni, accept my fuel-stick and the oblation of the Upasad rite, and hear these praises well.

> हे अग्ने मे मदीयामिमामाधीयमानां समिधं इमामुपसदमुपसदनसाधनामाहुतिमुपसद्यागे क्रियमाणां वा वनेः । संभजेथाः । तथेमा उ इमा अपि गिरः स्तुतीः सु सुष्ठु श्रुधि । शृणु ॥

> *he agne me madīyāmimāmādhīyamānāṃ samidhaṃ imāmupasadamupasadanasādhanāmāhutimupasadyāge kriyamāṇāṃ vā vaneḥ | saṃbhajethāḥ | tathemā u imā api giraḥ stutīḥ su suṣṭhu śrudhi | śṛṇu ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) अग्ने (अग्ने (*agne*)) — O Agni; मे (मे (*me*)) — my (offered by me); इमां समिधं (इमां समिधं (*imāṃ samidhaṃ*)) — this fuel-stick too; इमां उपसदं (इमां उपसदं (*imāṃ upasadaṃ*)) — this oblation, which is an adjunct of the Upasad rite; वनेः (वनेः (*vaneḥ*)) — accept and enjoy; इमा उ गिरः (इमा उ गिरः (*imā u giraḥ*)) — these praises also; सु श्रुधि (सु श्रुधि (*su śrudhi*)) — listen with regard (abhimāna).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, accept this fuel-stick offered by me and this oblation which is an adjunct of the Upasad rite. Listen also to these praises with regard.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 1)*

Agni, accept this my fuel, this my oblation ; listen, well pleased, to my praises.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated.)

**उपसदं (उपसदं (*upasadaṃ*))** — उपसत् (*upasat*) is said to be an important part of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice.

**समिधं (समिधं (*samidhaṃ*))** — इंध् दीप्तौ (*iṃdh dīptau*) (the root *indh*, to shine). The word, formed from the root meaning "shine well, burn", is the name of the tips of certain dry trees that burn well. When offering into the fire, they are the small dry twig-ends that have fallen beneath certain trees fit for sacrifice, such as the aśvattha (peepal). They are thinner than about a little finger and four to six inches long. The tip (end) part of this is called the "front part" (agrabhāga). Samits furnished with such a front part are used for offering into the fire. While offering the samit certain prescribed Ṛks are recited; these are called Sāmidhenī mantras. They are seventeen in number. *(The passage runs over to p. 508 with "Agni-yalli / hōma-māḍuvāga".)*

### Printed p. 508 (PDF 529)

*(Header: "508", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 6", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue from p. 507; the Nirukta references below are read from the strip, not zoomed, and are doubtful [?].)*

**(Special Topics, Ṛk 1, continued)**

…(on p. 507 the text reads "in the fire"; here it continues:) while offering into the fire…, as described above.

**गिरः (गिरः (*giraḥ*))** — Hymns of praise in the form of sentences or in the form of Ṛks. Yāska has recorded the word गीः (*gīḥ*) among the names of speech (*vāṅnāmāni*) (Ni. 2-23 [?]). And गिरः—स्तुतयो गिरो गृणातेः (*giraḥ—stutayo giro gṛṇāteḥ*) (Ni. 1-10 [?], printed as "1 10"): the word गिरः (*giraḥ*) is formed from the root गृ शब्दे (*gṛ śabde*). गिरः (*giraḥ*) means praises. There is also the etymology गृणातिः स्तुतिकर्मा (*gṛṇātiḥ stutikarmā*) (Ni. 3-5 [?]). Besides, there is the etymology गिरा—गीत्या स्तुत्या (*girā—gītyā stutyā*) (Ni. 6-24 [?] and Ni. 10-5 [?]); hence गिरः (*giraḥ*) means hymns of praise. *(Kannada, translated.)*

*(A short rule is printed here, ending the Special Topics of Ṛk 1.)*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒या ते॑ अग्ने विधे॒मोर्जो॑ नपा॒दश्व॑मिष्टे ।
> ए॒ना सू॒क्तेन॑ सुजात ॥ २ ॥

> *ayā te agne vidhemorjo napādaśvamiṣṭe |*
> *enā sūktena sujāta ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अया । ते । अग्ने । विधेम । ऊर्जः । नपात् । अश्वंऽइष्टे ।
> एना । सुऽउक्तेन । सुऽजात ॥ २ ॥

> *ayā | te | agne | vidhema | ūrjaḥ | napāt | aśvaṃ 'iṣṭe |*
> *enā | su 'uktena | su 'jāta ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 2)**

*Gist:* Agni, we serve you with this oblation; you are the son of strength and lord of the swift sacrifice, well-born; we please you with this hymn.

> हे अग्ने ते त्वामयानयाहुत्या विधेम । परिचरेम । हे ऊर्जो नपात् बलस्य नस्तः [?] तस्य नपातयितर्वा हे अश्वमिष्टे व्यापकयज्ञ । यद्वा आशु क्रियमाणं कर्माश्वं । तदिच्छतीत्यश्वमिष्टिः । संत्वरमाणा ह्युपसदमाचरंति । ते कर्मभिः समुत्वरंत ते तिस्रः सामिधेनीरनूच्य तिस्रो देवता अयजन्निति ब्राह्मणं । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-४३ [?] । तादृशाग्ने ते त्वामयानयाहुत्या विधेम । परिचरेम । तथा हे सुजात शोभनजनन एना एतेन सूक्तेन स्तोत्रेण प्रीणयेमेति शेषः । यद्वा स्तुत्युपबृंहितेन विधेम ॥

> *he agne te tvāmayānayāhutyā vidhema | paricarema | he ūrjo napāt balasya nastaḥ [?] tasya napātayitarvā he aśvamiṣṭe vyāpakayajña | yadvā āśu kriyamāṇaṃ karmāśvaṃ | tadicchatītyaśvamiṣṭiḥ | saṃtvaramāṇā hyupasadamācaraṃti | te karmabhiḥ samutvaraṃta te tisraḥ sāmidhenīranūcya tisro devatā ayajanniti brāhmaṇaṃ | ai. brā. 3-43 [?] | tādṛśāgne te tvāmayānayāhutyā vidhema | paricarema | tathā he sujāta śobhanajanana enā etena sūktena stotreṇa prīṇayemeti śeṣaḥ | yadvā stutyupabṛṃhitena vidhema ‖*

*(The word नस्तः (नस्तः (*nastaḥ*)) is given as printed [?]; the sense requires "grandson/son" (नप्तः), but I do not alter the print. The Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa reference is read "3-43" [?], numerals not zoomed. Ṛk 2 is left open: its Pratipadārtha and the rest continue on p. 509.)*

### Printed p. 509 (PDF 530)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 27 ]" [numeral not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "509". The numeral file has no rows for this page. Ṛk 2 continues from p. 508.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) ऊर्जो नपात् (*ūrjo napāt*) — one who is the son of strength (śakti); अश्वमिष्टे (*aśvamiṣṭe*) — one who is swift (*tvarita*) and who desires the Upasad sacrifice performed with faith (*śraddhe*); अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; ते (*te*) — you; अया (*ayā*) — by this oblation; विधेम (*vidhema*) — we serve; सुजाते (*sujāte*) — O Agni, of excellent birth (as printed, the vocative form सुजाते (*sujāte*)); एना सूक्तेन (*enā sūktena*) — by this mantra, which is in the nature of a stotra (we serve).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, who are the son of strength, swift, and desirous of the Upasad sacrifice performed with faith, we serve you with this oblation. O Agni of excellent birth, we serve you also with this mantra, which is in the nature of a stotra.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 2)*

May we propitiate you, Agni, by this (oblation) ; grandson of strength, you are gratified by prompt sacrifice ; (my [sic] we please you), well-born, by this hymn.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated.)

**सूक्तेन—सुष्ठु उक्तेन (*sūktena—suṣṭhu uktena*)** — "Well-spoken", that is, a stotra or Ṛk that praises the qualities of the deities well. In the Ṛgveda a collection of many such Ṛks is called a *sūkta*. In sum, "sūkta" means a stotra.

**ऊर्जो नपात्—बलस्य नस्तः (*ūrjo napāt—balasya nastaḥ*)** *(as printed; the same reading as in the bhāṣya on p. 508)* — When fire is produced by churning in the two *araṇi* sticks, it arises only by churning with the use of much strength. Therefore Agni is addressed with the words सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*) ("son of might") and ऊर्जोनपात् (*ūrjonapāt*).

**अश्वमिष्टे—व्यापकयज्ञ (*aśvamiṣṭe—vyāpakayajña*)** — One who pervades the sacrifice. If the word अश्व (*aśva*) is regarded as formed from the root अशू व्याप्तौ (*aśū vyāptau*) (*aśū vyāptau*), the meaning given above is obtained. Or: **आशु क्रियमाणं कर्म अश्वं (*āśu kriyamāṇaṃ karma aśvaṃ*)** *(the print reads क्रियोमणं [?]; given here as the evident sense)* — the word अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*), derived from आशु (*āśu*), which means "quickly", also means a sacrifice that is performed quickly. Here room exists for both kinds of meaning.

**अया—अनया (*ayā—anayā*)** — For the convenience of the metre the letter न (*na*) of the word अनया (*anayā*) has been dropped, giving अया (*ayā*). Similarly the letter आ (*ā*) of the word आत्मना (*ātmanā*) has been dropped, and the word त्मना (*tmanā*) is used in many places. Such usages are numerous in the Ṛgveda.

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तं त्वा॑ गी॒र्भिर्गिर्व॑णसं द्रविण॒स्युं द्र॑विणोदः ।
> स॒प॒र्येम॑ सप॒र्यवः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

> *taṃ tvā gīrbhirgirvaṇasaṃ draviṇasyuṃ draviṇodaḥ |*
> *saparyema saparyavaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तं । त्वा । गीःऽभिः । गिर्वणसं । द्रविणस्युं । द्रविणःऽदः ।
> सपर्येम । सपर्यवः ॥ ३ ॥

> *taṃ | tvā | gīḥ 'bhiḥ | girvaṇasaṃ | draviṇasyuṃ | draviṇaḥ 'daḥ |*
> *saparyema | saparyavaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 3)**

*Gist:* O Agni, giver of wealth, we, your servers, serve you, who are worthy of praise and desirous of the oblation-wealth, with our praises.

> हे द्रविणोदो धनस्य दातरग्ने तं तादृशं गिर्वणसं गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्वननीयं द्रविणस्युं हविर्लक्षणधनेच्छुं त्वा त्वां सपर्यवः परिचरणकर्तारो वयं गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिः सपर्येम । परिचरेम ॥

> *he draviṇodo dhanasya dātaragne taṃ tādṛśaṃ girvaṇasaṃ gīrbhiḥ stutibhirvananīyaṃ draviṇasyuṃ havirlakṣaṇadhanecchuṃ tvā tvāṃ saparyavaḥ paricaraṇakartāro vayaṃ gīrbhiḥ stutibhiḥ saparyema | paricarema ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) द्रविणोदः (*draviṇodaḥ*) — O Agni, giver of wealth; गिर्वणसं (*girvaṇasaṃ*) — one who is served (*bhajisalpaḍuvavanu*) with praises; द्रविणस्युं (*draviṇasyuṃ*) — one who desires wealth in the form of the oblation; तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*) — you, who are well known and such; सपर्यवः (*saparyavaḥ*) — we, your worshippers; गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*) — with praises; सपर्येम (*saparyema*) — we shall worship.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, giver of wealth, we, your worshippers, worship you with praises: you who are served with praises, who desire wealth in the form of the oblation, and who are well known.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 3)*

Granter of riches, may we, your worshippers, propitiate you, who are desirous of (sacrificial) wealth, and deserving of laudation, by our praises.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated.)

**द्रविणोदः (*draviṇodaḥ*)** — A detailed explanation of this word has been given in this same volume, pages 407–409 (printed in Arabic numerals).

**गिर्वणसं—स्तुतिलक्षणैर्वचोभिः संभजनीयं (*girvaṇasaṃ—stutilakṣaṇairvacobhiḥ saṃbhajanīyaṃ*)** — "One who is attained (*hoṃdulpaḍuvavanu*) by praises", that is, one who is worthy of stotras, who is to be praised. Yāska has the etymology: **गिर्वणा देवो भवति गीर्भिरेनं वनयंति (*girvaṇā devo bhavati gīrbhirenaṃ vanayaṃti*)** (Ni. 6-14 [?], the numerals as printed "೬-೧೪" with a doubtful final glyph, not zoomed).

**सपर्यवः—परिचरणकर्तारो वयं (*saparyavaḥ—paricaraṇakartāro vayaṃ*)** *(continued on p. 511)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स बो॑धि सू॒रिर्म॒घवा॒ वसु॑पते॒ वसु॑दावन् ।
> यु॒यो॒ध्य१॒॑स्मद्द्वेषां॑सि ॥ ४ ॥

> *sa bodhi sūrirmaghavā vasupate vasudāvan |*
> *yuyodhyasmaddveṣāṃsi ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । बोधि । सूरिः । मघऽवा । वसुऽपते । वसुऽदावन् ।
> युयोधि । अस्मत् । द्वेषांसि ॥ ४ ॥

> *saḥ | bodhi | sūriḥ | magha 'vā | vasu 'pate | vasu 'dāvan |*
> *yuyodhi | asmat | dveṣāṃsi ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 4)**

*Gist:* You, who are wealthy, wise or the impeller, understand our stotra; and, Agni, separate our enemies from us.

> मघवान्धनवान् सूरिर्विद्वान् प्रेरको वा स उक्तलक्षणकस्त्वं बोधि । बुध्यस्वास्मदीयं स्तोत्रं । किंच हे अग्ने द्वेषांसि द्वेष्टॄनस्मदस्मत्तो [?] युयोधि । पृथक्कुरु ॥

> *maghavāndhanavān sūrirvidvān prerako vā sa uktalakṣaṇakastvaṃ bodhi | budhyasvāsmadīyaṃ stotraṃ | kiṃca he agne dveṣāṃsi dveṣṭṝnasmadasmatto [?] yuyodhi | pṛthakkuru ‖*

*(The words द्वेष्टॄनस्मदस्मत्तो (*dveṣṭṝnasmadasmatto*) are read from the strip as printed, with the glyph of द्वेष्टॄन् (*dveṣṭṝn*) doubtful [?].)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) वसुपते (*vasupate*) — O lord of wealth; वसुदावन् (*vasudāvan*) — O Agni, giver of wealth; मघवा (*maghavā*) — possessor of riches; सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) — who are wise, or who are the impeller to the rite; सः (*saḥ*) — that you; बोधि (*bodhi*) — know (our rite and our praise); द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*) — our enemies who hate us; अस्मत् (*asmat*) — from us; युयोधि (*yuyodhi*) — separate (drive far away).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, lord of wealth and giver of wealth, you who are rich, wise or the impeller to the rite, know our rite and our praise. Separate from us the enemies who hate us.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 4)*

Lord of wealth, giver of wealth, possessor of riches, Agni, you are wise, understand (our prayers), and scatter our enemies.

*(Ṛk 4 is left open: the page ends with the printed English; any Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu) would follow on p. 512.)*

### Printed p. 512 (PDF 533)

*(Header: "512", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 6". The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continue from p. 511.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated.)

**मघवा (*maghavā*)** — The word मघ (*magha*) is listed among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-9 [?], numerals not zoomed). There is also the etymology **मघमिति धननामधेयं महंतेर्दानकर्मणः** (Ni. 1-7 [?], numerals not zoomed). *(The Nirukta words are as printed, with महंते° [?].)* The word मघ (*magha*) is formed from the root that indicates the act of giving (a gift) and is named "wealth". मघवान् (*maghavān*) means "one who has wealth". The word is also used of other deities such as Agni and Indra. Because the word is used most often of Indra, in modern Sanskrit the word मघवत् (*maghavat*) has no meaning other than "Indra".

**सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)** — The word सूरि (*sūri*) is listed among the names of praisers (*stotṛ*) (Ni. 2-19 [?], numerals not zoomed). It has the meanings "intelligent", "learned", "wise", "impeller" and the like.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स नो॑ वृ॒ष्टिं दि॒वस्परि॒ स नो॒ वाज॑मन॒र्वाणं॑ ।
> स नः॑ सह॒स्रिणी॒रिषः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

> *sa no vṛṣṭiṃ divaspari sa no vājamanarvāṇaṃ |*
> *sa naḥ sahasriṇīriṣaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । नः । वृष्टिं । दिवः । परि । सः । नः । वाजं । अनर्वाणं ।
> सः । नः । सहस्रिणीः । इषः ॥ ५ ॥

> *saḥ | naḥ | vṛṣṭiṃ | divaḥ | pari | saḥ | naḥ | vājaṃ | anarvāṇaṃ |*
> *saḥ | naḥ | sahasriṇīḥ | iṣaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 5)**

*Gist:* The same Agni, for us, makes rain from the sky and gives abundant unfailing strength and thousandfold food.

> सः स एवाग्निर्नोऽस्मदर्थं दिवस्परि द्युलोकादंतरिक्षात् ॥ परीति पंचम्यर्थानुवादी ॥ वृष्टिं करोति च शेषः । स एव नोऽस्मदर्थमनर्वाणमविचलमनल्पं वाजं बलं ददातु । तथा सहस्रिणीरपरिमितप्रकाराणीषोऽन्नानि स एवाग्निर्ददातु ॥

> *saḥ sa evāgnirno 'smadarthaṃ divaspari dyulokādaṃtarikṣāt ‖ parīti paṃcamyarthānuvādī ‖ vṛṣṭiṃ karoti ca śeṣaḥ | sa eva no 'smadarthamanarvāṇamavicalamanalpaṃ vājaṃ balaṃ dadātu | tathā sahasriṇīraparimitaprakārāṇīṣo 'nnāni sa evāgnirdadātu ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) सः (*saḥ*) — that same Agni described above; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; दिवस्परि (*divaspari*) — from the sky (*antarikṣa*); वृष्टिं (*vṛṣṭiṃ*) — rain (he pours down); सः (*saḥ*) — he himself; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*) — (as if everlasting) abundant; वाजं (*vājaṃ*) — strength (let him give, likewise); नः (*naḥ*) — to us; सहस्रिणीः (*sahasriṇīḥ*) — unlimited; इषः (*iṣaḥ*) — foods; सः (*saḥ*) — that same Agni, let him give.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ईळा॑नायाव॒स्यवे॒ यवि॑ष्ठ दूत नो गि॒रा ।
> यजि॑ष्ठ होत॒रा ग॑हि ॥ ६ ॥

> *īḷānāyāvasyave yaviṣṭha dūta no girā |*
> *yajiṣṭha hotarā gahi ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ईळानाय । अवस्यवे । यविष्ठ । दूत । नः । गिरा ।
> यजिष्ठ । होतः । आ । गहि ॥ ६ ॥

> *īḷānāya | avasyave | yaviṣṭha | dūta | naḥ | girā |*
> *yajiṣṭha | hotaḥ | ā | gahi ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 6)**

*Gist:* O youngest, messenger, best of sacrificers, invoker Agni, come to me, who praise you and seek your protection, at our praise.

> हे यविष्ठ युवतम दूत देवानां यज्ञादिसूचक यजिष्ठातिशयेन यष्टव्य होतर्देवानामाह्वातरग्ने नो गिरास्मदीयया स्तुत्यैळानाय पूजयित्रेऽवस्यवे स्वरक्षणमिच्छते मदर्थमागहि । आगच्छ ॥

> *he yaviṣṭha yuvatama dūta devānāṃ yajñādisūcaka yajiṣṭhātiśayena yaṣṭavya hotardevānāmāhvātaragne no girāsmadīyayā stutyaiḷānāya pūjayitre 'vasyave svarakṣaṇamicchate madarthamāgahi | āgaccha ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*) — O very young one; दूत (*dūta*) — O messenger of the gods; यजिष्ठ (*yajiṣṭha*) — O one of surpassing worthiness of sacrifice; होतः (*hotaḥ*) — O Agni, who call the deities to the sacrifice; नः (*naḥ*) — our; गिरा (*girā*) — by the speech that takes the form of praise; ईळानाय (*īḷānāya*) — for me, who worship; अवस्यवे (*avasyave*) — who desire protection; आ गहि (*ā gahi*) — be gracious (come).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, very young, messenger of the gods, of surpassing worthiness of sacrifice, who call the deities to the sacrifice: be gracious to me, who worship you with speech in the form of praise and desire protection from you.

#### Ṛk 7

*(The Ṛk numeral is read as 7 from the strip, consistent with the sequence; not zoomed. The Saṃhitā reads दूते (*dūte*) as printed [?], but the Pada has दूतः (*dūtaḥ*); the Pada's जन्याऽ इव (*janyā ' iva*) is given as printed, with a sign after या read as ऽ.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अं॒तर्ह्य॑ग्न॒ ईय॑से वि॒द्वाञ्जन्मो॒भया॑ कवे ।
> दू॒ते जन्ये॑व॒ मित्र्यः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

> *aṃtarhyagna īyase vidvāñjanmobhayā kave |*
> *dūte janyeva mitryaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अंतः । हि । अग्ने । ईयसे । विद्वान् । जन्म । उभया । कवे ।
> दूतः । जन्याऽ इव । मित्र्यः ॥ ७ ॥

> *aṃtaḥ | hi | agne | īyase | vidvān | janma | ubhayā | kave |*
> *dūtaḥ | janyā ' iva | mitryaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 7)**

*Gist:* Agni, knowing the births of both sacrificers and gods, enters people's hearts and knows them, as a king's messenger knows his people's minds.

*(In the bhāṣya below: the Nirukta-like quotation is given as printed, with reference numerals read "4-8-4" [?], not zoomed; the word after हि (*hi*) seems to carry a visarga in the print; ज इभ्यो (*ja ibhyo*) in the print is probably जनेभ्यो (*janebhyo*) [?]; यष्टृणां (*yaṣṭṛṇāṃ*) [?].)*

> हे कवे मेधाविन्नग्ने अंतर्जनानां हृदये ईयसे हि । गच्छसि जानासि वा । हिः स होता सेदु दूत्यं चिकित्वाँ अंतरीयते । ४-८-४ [?] । इत्यादिमंत्रांतरप्रसिद्धिद्योतनार्थः । कीदृशस्त्वं । उभया उभयविधानि जन्म जन्मानि यष्टृणां [?] यजमानानां यष्टव्यानां देवानां च संबंधीनि विद्वान् जानन् सन् । ईयस इति संबंधः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जन्यो जनेभ्यो [?] हितो मित्र्यो विशेषेण मित्रेभ्यो हितो दूत इव । स यथा प्रजानां चित्तवृत्तिज्ञानाय राज्ञा प्रेरितस्तासां मनो जानाति तद्वत् त्वमप्यस्माकमंतरीयस इत्यर्थः ॥

> *he kave medhāvinnagne aṃtarjanānāṃ hṛdaye īyase hi | gacchasi jānāsi vā | hiḥ sa hotā sedu dūtyaṃ cikitvā~ aṃtarīyate | 4-8-4 [?] | ityādimaṃtrāṃtaraprasiddhidyotanārthaḥ | kīdṛśastvaṃ | ubhayā ubhayavidhāni janma janmāni yaṣṭṛṇāṃ [?] yajamānānāṃ yaṣṭavyānāṃ devānāṃ ca saṃbaṃdhīni vidvān jānan san | īyasa iti saṃbaṃdhaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | janyo janebhyo [?] hito mitryo viśeṣeṇa mitrebhyo hito dūta iva | sa yathā prajānāṃ cittavṛttijñānāya rājñā preritastāsāṃ mano jānāti tadvat tvamapyasmākamaṃtarīyasa ityarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated:) कवे (*kave*) — O wise one; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; उभया जन्म (*ubhayā janma*) — the births of the two kinds, namely the sacrificers and the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — knowing well; जन्यः (*janyaḥ*) — one who does good to the people; मित्र्यः (*mitryaḥ*) — and above all one who does service to friends; दूत इव (*dūta iva*) — as a messenger, knowing his master's mind, does what is good for him (so you also); अंतः (*antaḥ*) — in the hearts of people; ईयसे हि (*īyase hi*) — you enter and understand it surely.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated, begun:) O Agni, wise one, knowing well the births of the sacrificers and of the gods worthy of the sacrifice, doing good to the people, and above all rendering service to friends… *(the sentence continues on p. 515; Ṛk 7 is left open)*

### Printed p. 515 (PDF 536)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 27 ]" [numeral not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "515". The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 7 continues from p. 514.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 7, continued)**

(Kannada, translated:) …as a messenger, knowing his master's mind, does what is good for him, so you also enter into the hearts of people, know their several intentions (*iṅgita*), and fulfil their desires.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 7)*

Sage Agni, you penetrate the innermost (man) knowing the birth of both (the worshipper and the worshipped) ; like a messenger favourable to men, especially to his friends.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated.) **अंतः हि अग्ने ईयसे (*aṃtaḥ hi agne īyase*)** — "O Agni, you enter the hearts of people", that is, you know all the matters that are in people's hearts or minds: this is the sense intended. The same sense is indicated (by the following). The bhāṣyakāra has given as an example the Ṛk

> स होता सेदु दूत्यं चिकित्वाँ अंतरीयते ।

> *sa hotā sedu dūtyaṃ cikitvā~ aṃtarīyate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-8-4: printed ळ-ल-ळ.) *(This confirms the reference read "4-8-4 [?]" in the bhāṣya of p. 514.)* But in the bhāṣya on that Ṛk the idea "entering the hearts of people he knows what is in their minds" is not given. Instead, for the words अंतः ईयते (*aṃtaḥ īyate*) it explains:

> अंतर्द्यावापृथिव्योर्मध्य ईयते गच्छति

> *aṃtardyāvāpṛthivyormadhya īyate gacchati*

that is, "he goes (moves about) in the middle of heaven and earth (the earth and the atmosphere)". Therefore the Ṛk given here as an example does not establish the meaning of the Ṛk in hand.

**जन्म उभया विद्वान् (*janma ubhayā vidvān*)** — The bhāṣya gives:

> उभयविधानि जन्मानि यष्टृणां [?] यजमानानां यष्टव्यानां देवानां च संबंधीनि च जानन्

> *ubhayavidhāni janmāni yaṣṭṛṇāṃ [?] yajamānānāṃ yaṣṭavyānāṃ devānāṃ ca saṃbaṃdhīni ca jānan*

*(यष्टृणां (*yaṣṭṛṇāṃ*): the print is not clear to me [?]; not zoomed.)* Here Agni is described as knowing two kinds of births. The bhāṣyakāra explains this as knowing the birth, or order of origin, of the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice and of the gods who are worshipped in the sacrifice.

**दूतो जन्येव मित्र्यः (*dūto janyeva mitryaḥ*)** — A simile is given here. The bhāṣya:

> जनेभ्यो हितो विशेषेण मित्रेभ्यो हितो दूत इव । स यथा प्रजानां चित्तवृत्तिज्ञानाय राज्ञा प्रेरितस्तासां मनो जानाति तद्वत् त्वमप्यस्माकमंतरीयस इत्यर्थः ।

> *janebhyo hito viśeṣeṇa mitrebhyo hito dūta iva | sa yathā prajānāṃ cittavṛttijñānāya rājñā preritastāsāṃ mano jānāti tadvat tvamapyasmākamaṃtarīyasa ityarthaḥ |*

*(त्वमप्यस्माकम् (*tvamapyasmākam*): the print reads something like त्वमस्यस्माकम् (*tvamasyasmākam*) [?]; I give the sense-reading, not zoomed.)* Agni is praised: "you are like a messenger who is a well-wisher of people, and especially of those who are friends". For in the world a messenger sent by the king, to learn the minds of the subjects, moves among them, learns their intentions and reports them to the king; in the same way Agni too enters people's minds and, as a well-wisher, makes their wishes known to the deities for whom the sacrifice is intended.

#### Ṛk 8

*(The Ṛk numeral is read as 8 from the strip, not zoomed. In the Saṃhitā the print shows a sign above the द्वा (*dvā*) of विद्वा (*vidvā*), which I read as a candrabindu [?]; the same sign stands over चिकित्वा (*cikitvā*) in the Ṛk quoted on p. 515.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स वि॒द्वाँ आ च॑ पिप्रयो॒ यक्षि॑ चिकित्व आनु॒षक् ।
> आ चा॒स्मिन्त्स॑त्सि ब॒र्हिषि॑ ॥ ८ ॥

> *sa vidvā~ ā ca piprayo yakṣi cikitva ānuṣak |*
> *ā cāsmintsatsi barhiṣi ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । विद्वान् । आ । च । पिप्रयः । यक्षि । चिकित्वः । आनुषक् ।
> आ । च । अस्मिन् । सत्सि । बर्हिषि ॥ ८ ॥

> *saḥ | vidvān | ā | ca | piprayaḥ | yakṣi | cikitvaḥ | ānuṣak |*
> *ā | ca | asmin | satsi | barhiṣi ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 8)**

*Gist:* Omniscient Agni, fill us on all sides with desired things; wise one, worship the gods in order and sit on this strewn grass.

> हे अग्ने स त्वं विद्वान् विशेषाभिज्ञः सन् आ च पिप्रयुः । सर्वतोऽस्मान्पूरय च काम्यैः । हे चिकित्वश्चेतनावन् आनुषक् अनुक्रमेण यक्षि । यज देवान् । आसत्सि । आसीद चास्मिन् स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि ॥

> *he agne sa tvaṃ vidvān viśeṣābhijñaḥ san ā ca piprayuḥ | sarvato 'smānpūraya ca kāmyaiḥ | he cikitvaścetanāvan ānuṣak anukrameṇa yakṣi | yaja devān | āsatsi | āsīda cāsmin stīrṇe barhiṣi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated:) सः (*saḥ*) — (O Agni) you; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — being one who knows everything; आ च (*ā ca*) — in every way; पिप्रयुः (*piprayuḥ*) — fulfil our desires; चिकित्वः (*cikitvaḥ*) — you who are wise; आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*) — in order; यक्षि (*yakṣi*) — worship (the deities); अस्मिन् (*asmin*) — here, spread; बर्हिषि च (*barhiṣi ca*) — on the darbha seat too; आ सत्सि (*ā satsi*) — sit down.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, you who know everything, fulfil our desires in every way, and worship the deities in order. Sit also on the darbha seat spread here.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 8)*

Agni, you are all-wise ; fulfil (our desires) : you, who are intelligent, worship ( the gods) in order ; and sit down on this sacred grass.

### Printed p. 517 (PDF 538)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 28 ]" [numeral not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "517". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated.) **आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)** — the meaning is "in order". For this word Yāska gives *(as printed, the first words not zoomed [?])*:

> आनुषगिति नामानुपूर्वस्यानुषक्तं भवति । स्तृणंति बर्हिरानुषक् इत्यपि निगमो भवति

> *ānuṣagiti nāmānupūrvasyānuṣaktaṃ bhavati | stṛṇaṃti barhirānuṣak ityapi nigamo bhavati*

That is: आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*) is a synonym of अनुपूर्व (*anupūrva*) and अनुक्रम (*anukrama*) *(print: आनुक्रमु (*ānukramu*) [?])*, words that give the sense "one after another"; and he has given the example स्तृणंति बर्हिरानुषक् (*stṛṇaṃti barhirānuṣak*):

> आ घा ये अग्निमिंधते स्तृणंति बर्हिरानुषक् ।
> येषामिंद्रो युवा सखा ॥

> *ā ghā ye agnimiṃdhate stṛṇaṃti barhirānuṣak |*
> *yeṣāmiṃdro yuvā sakhā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-45-1 [?], printed ल-ळ५-१; numerals not zoomed.)

In this example it is said that first they kindle the fire; after that they spread the darbha grass called बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*) as a seat. Here kindling the fire is one act; spreading the darbha is another act. After the first act, kindling the fire, the second act, spreading the darbha, is carried out. Thus, when one act is done in order after another, the word आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*) is used to indicate that order. In the Ṛk in hand also there are three acts of Agni: fulfilling our desires, worshipping the deities, and sitting on the darbha. The word आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*) is used here so that they may be done in due order.

## Sūkta 7 (Seventh Sūkta)

*(Printed heading: "ಏಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು" — "The seventh sūkta".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Sūkta 7 (six Ṛks), seer Somāhuti Bhārgava, deity Agni, metre Gāyatrī; its use is as stated in the previous sūkta's introduction; the first Ṛk is used in the Śravaṇākarman.

> श्रेष्ठं यविष्ठेति षडृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं सोमाहुत्यार्षमाग्नेयं गायत्रं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्गायत्रे छंदस्यस्य विनियोगः पूर्वसूक्ते विवोक्तः [?] ॥ श्रवणाकर्मण्याद्या विनियुक्ता ॥

> *śreṣṭhaṃ yaviṣṭheti ṣaḍṛcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktaṃ somāhutyārṣamāgneyaṃ gāyatraṃ ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorgāyatre chaṃdasyasya viniyogaḥ pūrvasūkte vivoktaḥ [?] ‖ śravaṇākarmaṇyādyā viniyuktā ‖*

**अनुवाद (Anuvāda)**

(Kannada, translated:) The sūkta श्रेष्ठं यविष्ठ (*śreṣṭhaṃ yaviṣṭha*) is the seventh sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Somāhuti Bhārgava; the deity is Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. It was said earlier (in the introduction of the previous sūkta) that this sūkta is applied for the Gāyatrī-metre Ṛks at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvinaśastra mantras. In the Śravaṇākarman the first Ṛk of this sūkta has its application.

*(The Ṛks of Sūkta 7 begin on p. 518.)*
