#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> श्रेष्ठं॑ यविष्ठ भार॒ताग्ने॑ द्यु॒मंत॒मा भ॑र ।
> वसो॑ पुरु॒स्पृहं॑ र॒यिं ॥ १ ॥

> *śreṣṭhaṃ yaviṣṭha bhāratāgne dyumaṃtamā bhara |*
> *vaso puruspṛhaṃ rayiṃ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> श्रेष्ठं । यविष्ठ । भारत । अग्ने । द्युमंतं । आ । भर ।
> वसो इति । पुरुस्पृहं । रयिं ॥ १ ॥

> *śreṣṭhaṃ | yaviṣṭha | bhārata | agne | dyumaṃtaṃ | ā | bhara |*
> *vaso iti | puruspṛhaṃ | rayiṃ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 1)**

*Gist:* Agni, youngest, kinsman of the priests and giver of dwellings, bring us the best, shining, much-desired wealth.

> हे अग्ने यविष्ठ युवत्तम हे भारत । भरता ऋत्विजः । तेषां संबंधी भारतः । ते ऽध्वर्य्वादिभिर्मंथनहविःस्तोत्रादिना व्याप्रियमाणत्वात् । तादृश हे वसो वासक व्याप्त वा विवंरूपाग्ने [?] श्रेष्ठमतिप्रशस्यं द्युमंतं दीप्तिमंतं पुरुस्पृहं बहुभिरर्थिभिः स्पृहणीयं रयिमाभर । आहर ॥

> *he agne yaviṣṭha yuvattama he bhārata | bharatā ṛtvijaḥ | teṣāṃ saṃbaṃdhī bhārataḥ | te 'dhvaryvādibhirmaṃthanahaviḥstotrādinā vyāpriyamāṇatvāt | tādṛśa he vaso vāsaka vyāpta vā vivaṃrūpāgne [?] śreṣṭhamatipraśasyaṃ dyumaṃtaṃ dīptimaṃtaṃ puruspṛhaṃ bahubhirarthibhiḥ spṛhaṇīyaṃ rayimābhara | āhara ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*) — extremely youthful one; भारत (*bhārata*) — kinsman of the priests (ṛtvijas); वसो (*vaso*) — giver of a dwelling-place; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; श्रेष्ठं (*śreṣṭhaṃ*) — most excellent; द्युमंतं (*dyumaṃtaṃ*) — shining; पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*) — desired by many; रयिं (*rayiṃ*) — wealth; आ भर (*ā bhara*) — bring.

### Printed p. 519 (PDF 540)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 28 ]" [read from the strip, not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "519". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, you who are extremely youthful, kinsman of the priests, and giver of a dwelling-place, bring for us wealth that is most excellent, shining, and desired by many.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 1)*

Youngest (of the gods), Agni, descendant of Bharata, granter of dwellings, bring (to us) excellent, splendid, and enviable riches.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated.) **भारते (*bhārate*)** — The word भारत (*bhārata*) is read among the names of priests (ṛtvij) (Ni. 3-18 [?], as printed; the second numeral is doubtful, not zoomed). Bhārata means a priest. The word is formed from the root भृञ् भरणे (*bhṛñ bharaṇe*) and, according to the explanation of Skandasvāmin, the sense is:

> यज्ञद्वारेण नॄन् संभरतीति [?]

> *yajñadvāreṇa nṝn saṃbharatīti [?]*

— "by means of the sacrifice he upholds men (the sacrificers)", that is, by performing the sacrifice he thereby lifts up (saves) the people (the patrons). Therefore this priest is called Bhārata. Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, says:

> भ्रियंते दक्षिणाभिस्ते इति भारताः

> *bhriyaṃte dakṣiṇābhiste iti bhāratāḥ*

— "they are nourished (satisfied) by the dakṣiṇās and the like, so they are Bhāratas": having performed the sacrifice, they obtain satisfaction through sacrificial fees and so on, and so these priests are called Bhāratas. Thus the word भरत (*bharata*) has two kinds of etymological meaning. *(The first Skandasvāmin quotation: the print of नॄन् (*nṝn*) is not clear to me [?]; not zoomed.)*

#### Ṛk 2

*(The Ṛk numeral is read as 2, not zoomed.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मा नो॒ अरा॑तिरीशत दे॒वस्य॒ मर्त्य॑स्य च ।
> पर्षि॒ तस्या॑ उ॒त द्वि॒षः ॥ २ ॥

> *mā no arātirīśata devasya martyasya ca |*
> *parṣi tasyā uta dviṣaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मा । नः । अरातिः । ईशत । देवस्य । मर्त्यस्य । च ।
> पर्षि । तस्याः । उत । द्विषः ॥ २ ॥

> *mā | naḥ | arātiḥ | īśata | devasya | martyasya | ca |*
> *parṣi | tasyāḥ | uta | dviṣaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 2)**

*Gist:* Let no enemy, whether of gods or of men, overcome us; by your favour protect us from such enemies.

> हे अग्ने त्वदनुग्रहान्नोऽस्मानरातिरदानं शत्रुत्वं । यद्वा छंदस्यरातिशब्दः शत्रुवाची स्त्रीलिंगो भवति । अदाता शत्रुर्मीशत [?] । पराभवितुं शक्तो मा भूत् ।

> *he agne tvadanugrahānno 'smānarātiradānaṃ śatrutvaṃ | yadvā chaṃdasyarātiśabdaḥ śatruvācī strīliṃgo bhavati | adātā śatrurmīśata [?] | parābhavituṃ śakto mā bhūt |*

*(The bhāṣya continues at the top of p. 520.)*

### Printed p. 520 (PDF 541)

*(Header: "520", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 7". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

*(Bhāṣya of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 519:)*

> मा विषयीकुर्यात् । अरातिर्विशेष्यते । देवस्य च मर्त्यस्य च संबंधिनी त्रैः कारिता [?] । उत अपि च तस्या उभयविधाया द्विषोऽस्मदरातेः पर्षि । पूरय ॥

> *mā viṣayīkuryāt | arātirviśeṣyate | devasya ca martyasya ca saṃbaṃdhinī traiḥ kāritā [?] | uta api ca tasyā ubhayavidhāyā dviṣo 'smadarāteḥ parṣi | pūraya ‖*

*(The words त्रैः कारिता (*traiḥ kāritā*) are read as printed; I cannot make them out with certainty [?]; not zoomed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) (O Agni) देवस्य (*devasya*) — whether belonging to the company of the gods; मर्त्यस्य च (*martyasya ca*) — or belonging to the company of men; अरातिः (*arātiḥ*) — an enemy; नः (*naḥ*) — us; मा ईशत (*mā īśata*) — let him not be able to withstand and defeat; उत (*uta*) — and; तस्याः (*tasyāḥ*) — of those two kinds; द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*) — from enemies also; पर्षि (*parṣi*) — protect us.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, whether he belongs to the company of the gods or to the company of men, let the enemy not be able to withstand and defeat us; and protect us also from enemies of both those kinds.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 2)*

Let no enemy prevail against us, whether of god or man ; protect us from both such foes.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated.) **अरातिः (*arātiḥ*)** — the bhāṣya says:

> अरातिरदानं । यद्वा छंदस्यरातिशब्दः शत्रुवाची स्त्रीलिंगो भवति ।

> *arātiradānaṃ | yadvā chaṃdasyarātiśabdaḥ śatruvācī strīliṃgo bhavati |*

That is, a person who gives nothing to anyone, or who gives no oblations and the like to the deities, is called अराति (*arāti*). Or, in the Veda the word अराति (*arāti*) is used especially in the sense of "enemy"; in that case the bhāṣyakāra's explanation is that the word is feminine. Yāska in the Nirukta says:

> अरातयोऽदानकर्माणः

> *arātayo 'dānakarmāṇaḥ*

— "arātis are those who do not give" (Ni. 3-11, as printed), that is, those who make no gift are called arātis; or:

> अरातीः अमित्रानदानानिति वा

> *arātīḥ amitrānadānāniti vā*

— "arātis: enemies who are not friends, or those who do not give" (Ni. 11-1, as printed); thus he has given two kinds of meaning.

**देवस्य (*devasya*)** — For the word देव (*deva*) Yāska says:

> देवो दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा

> *devo dānādvā dīpanādvā dyotanādvā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā*

— he who gives, he who shines, he who illumines by radiance, or he who dwells in heaven; therefore he is called Deva. (Ni. 7-15, as printed; numerals not zoomed.)

**मर्त्यस्य (*martyasya*)** — This word is formed from the root

> मृज् [?] प्राणत्यागे

> *mṛj [?] prāṇatyāge*

(print: मृज् (*mṛj*) [?]; not zoomed), "to give up life", and from it:

> म्रियंत इति मर्त्याः

> *mriyaṃta iti martyāḥ*

— they are subject to death, therefore men are called Martyas. The gods are called Amartyas. The use of the words मर्त्य (*martya*) (मर्त (*marta*)) and अमर्त्य (*amartya*) is special in the Ṛgveda. *(The Special Topics of Ṛk 2 may continue on p. 521.)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वा॑ उ॒त त्वया॑ व॒यं धारा॑ उद॒न्या॑ इव ।
> अति॑ गाहेमहि॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

> *viśvā uta tvayā vayaṃ dhārā udanyā iva |*
> *ati gāhemahi dviṣaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विश्वाः । उत । त्वया । वयं । धाराः । उदन्याः ऽ इव ।
> अति । गाहेमहि । द्विषः ॥ ३ ॥

> *viśvāḥ | uta | tvayā | vayaṃ | dhārāḥ | udanyāḥ ' iva |*
> *ati | gāhemahi | dviṣaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 3)**

*Gist:* Through your favour may we cross over all our enemies easily, as people wade across streams that carry little water.

> उत अपि च हे अग्ने वयं त्वदनुग्रहाद्विश्वा द्विषः सर्वानपि द्वेष्ट्रॄन् [?] उदन्या धारा इव उदकसंबंधिनीर्धारा अल्पस्रुतीरिव त्मनात्मनैवान्यनिरपेक्षेणाति-गाहेमहि । अतिक्रम्य गच्छेम ॥

> *uta api ca he agne vayaṃ tvadanugrahādviśvā dviṣaḥ sarvānapi dveṣṭrṝn [?] udanyā dhārā iva udakasaṃbaṃdhinīrdhārā alpasrutīriva tmanātmanaivānyanirapekṣeṇāti-gāhemahi | atikramya gacchema ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) उत (*uta*) — and; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we; उदन्याः धाराः इव (*udanyāḥ dhārāḥ iva*) — like streams carrying only a little water, which people cross with ease; विश्वाः द्विषः (*viśvāḥ dviṣaḥ*) — all our enemies; त्वया (*tvayā*) — through your favour; अति गाहेमहि (*ati gāhemahi*) — may we be able to overcome and pass beyond.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, just as people easily cross over small streams or brooks that flow with only a little water, so may we too, through your favour, gain the power to overcome all our enemies easily.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 3)*

Let us, through your favour, overwhelm all our foes, like torrents of water.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated.) **धारा उदन्या इव (*dhārā udanyā iva*)** — People cannot easily cross rivers that are deep with water and flowing with force. But people walk across a small stream, in which there is only a little water and which creeps along slowly, without any trouble. In the same way, the prayer is made here that we may make our enemies yield without trouble.

#### Ṛk 4

*(The Ṛk numeral is read as 4, not zoomed.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> शुचिः॑ पावक॒ वंद्योऽग्ने॑ बृ॒हद्वि रो॑चसे ।
> त्वं घृ॒तेभि॒राहु॑तः ॥ ४ ॥

> *śuciḥ pāvaka vaṃdyo 'gne bṛhadvi rocase |*
> *tvaṃ ghṛtebhirāhutaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> शुचिः । पावक । वंद्यः । अग्ने । बृहत् । वि । रोचसे ।
> त्वं । घृतेभिः । आऽहुतः ॥ ४ ॥

> *śuciḥ | pāvaka | vaṃdyaḥ | agne | bṛhat | vi | rocase |*
> *tvaṃ | ghṛtebhiḥ | ā 'hutaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 4)**

*Gist:* O purifying Agni, being pure and worthy of homage, you shine greatly and in many ways, since you are sprinkled all around with ghee.

> हे पावक शोधकाग्ने शुचिः शुद्धो वंद्यो नमस्कार्य्यः सन् बृहत् महत् अत्यधिकं विरोचसे । विविधं दीप्यसे । यतस्त्वं घृतेभिर्घृतैराहुतः । समंतात्सिक्तः । अतो विरोचसे ॥

> *he pāvaka śodhakāgne śuciḥ śuddho vaṃdyo namaskāryyaḥ san bṛhat mahat atyadhikaṃ virocase | vividhaṃ dīpyase | yatastvaṃ ghṛtebhirghṛtairāhutaḥ | samaṃtātsiktaḥ | ato virocase ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) पावक (*pāvaka*) — O purifier; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) — being pure; वंद्यः (*vaṃdyaḥ*) — being worthy of homage; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; घृतेभिः (*ghṛtebhiḥ*) — by oblations of ghee; आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*) — sprinkled upon; बृहत् (*bṛhat*) — exceedingly; वि रोचसे (*vi rocase*) — you shine in many ways.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, the purifier, you who are pure and worthy of homage, being sprinkled with oblations of ghee you shine exceedingly and in many ways.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 4)*

Purifier, Agni, holy, adorable, you shine exceedingly when (you are) worshipped with (oblations of) butter.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated.) **पावक, शुचिः, वंद्यः (*pāvaka, śuciḥ, vaṃdyaḥ*)** — Many substances become pure by being burnt in fire. By boiling water, all the impurities in the water are destroyed and it becomes fit for drinking. In the same way, things or places infected with worms, insects and the like, or with disease-germs, can be purified by fire. Because many such purifying acts are accomplished by fire, Agni is praised with the epithets पावक (*pāvaka*) — *(the passage runs on to the next page)*

### Printed p. 523 (PDF 544)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 28" [read from the strip, not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "523". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued from p. 522:)* "…the purifier (पावक (*pāvaka*)), शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) — one who is himself pure, वंद्यः (*vaṃdyaḥ*) — and therefore worthy of homage": thus he is praised by these epithets.

**अग्ने बृहत् विरोचसे त्वं घृतेभिः आहुतः (*agne bṛhat virocase tvaṃ ghṛtebhiḥ āhutaḥ*)** — The meaning of this sentence is plain. Because ājya, samidhs, havis, firewood and the like are put into the fire as offerings, and especially because the flames of the fire, fed with the ājya-oblation (the pouring of ghee), grow and shine with great lustre; therefore Agni is praised thus: "O Agni, you shine greatly through the oblations of ghee."

#### Ṛk 5

*(The Ṛk numeral is read as 5, not zoomed.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं नो॑ असि भार॒ताग्ने॑ व॒शाभि॑रु॒क्षभिः॑ ।
> अ॒ष्टाप॑दीभि॒राहु॑तः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvaṃ no asi bhāratāgne vaśābhirukṣabhiḥ |*
> *aṣṭāpadībhirāhutaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । नः । असि । भारत । अग्ने । वशाभिः । उक्षऽभिः ।
> अष्टाऽपदीभिः । आऽहुतः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvaṃ | naḥ | asi | bhārata | agne | vaśābhiḥ | ukṣa 'bhiḥ |*
> *aṣṭā 'padībhiḥ | ā 'hutaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 5)**

*Gist:* O Agni, who stand as a son to the priests, you are ours and are propitiated with offerings of barren cows, bulls and pregnant animals.

> हे भारत ऋत्विजां पुत्रस्थानीयोऽग्ने नोऽस्मदीयस्त्वं वशाभिर्वंध्याभिर्गोभिः उक्षभिः सेक्तृभिर्बलीवर्दैः अष्टापदीभिर्गर्भिणीभिश्चाहुत आराधितोऽसि ॥

> *he bhārata ṛtvijāṃ putrasthānīyo 'gne no 'smadīyastvaṃ vaśābhirvaṃdhyābhirgobhiḥ ukṣabhiḥ sektṛbhirbalīvardaiḥ aṣṭāpadībhirgarbhiṇībhiścāhuta ārādhito 'si ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) भारत (*bhārata*) — one who stands in the place of a son to the priests; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; नः (*naḥ*) — belonging to us; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; वशाभिः (*vaśābhiḥ*) — with barren cows; उक्षभिः (*ukṣabhiḥ*) — with bulls; अष्टापदीभिः (*aṣṭāpadībhiḥ*) — with pregnant animals; आहुतः असि (*āhutaḥ asi*) — (by offering these) you are propitiated.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, you who stand in the place of a son to the priests, you who are ours: by offering barren cows, bulls and pregnant animals, in the form of oblations, you have been propitiated.

*(Ṛk 5 is left open: its printed English and Special Topics, if any, follow on p. 524.)*

### Printed p. 524 (PDF 545)

*(Header: "524", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 7". The numeral file has no rows for this page. Ṛk 5 continues from p. 523.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 5)*

Agni, descendant of Bharata, you are entirely ours, when sacrificed to with pregnant cows, with barren cows, or bulls.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated.) **भारत (*bhārata*)** — The word भारत (*bhārata*) is read among the names of priests [?] (Ni. 3-19, not zoomed). Here, for the word भारत (*bhārata*), the bhāṣyakāra gives the explanation ऋत्विजां पुत्रस्थानीयः (*ṛtvijāṃ putrasthānīyaḥ*), "O Agni, who are like a son to the priests". At the beginning of a sacrifice the priests churn in the aranis and produce Agni; therefore it is fitting to say that Agni stands in the place of a son to the priests.

**वशाभिः उक्षभिः अष्टापदीभिः आहुतः (*vaśābhiḥ ukṣabhiḥ aṣṭāpadībhiḥ āhutaḥ*)** — the bhāṣyakāra explains:

> वशाभिर्वंध्याभिर्गोभिः उक्षभिः सेक्तृभिर्बलिवर्दैः अष्टापदीभिर्गर्भिणीभिश्चाहुतः ।

> *vaśābhirvaṃdhyābhirgobhiḥ ukṣabhiḥ sektṛbhirbalivardaiḥ aṣṭāpadībhirgarbhiṇībhiścāhutaḥ |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) That is: "O Agni, you are propitiated with barren cows that we offer to you, with bulls capable of impregnating (cows), and with cows in calf." Sāyaṇa gives this explanation. Although there are these three kinds among cattle, the offering of cows into the fire as an oblation is nowhere seen. Alternatively, the words वशाभिः (*vaśābhiḥ*) and the like need not be given the meaning "cows"; other animals fit for sacrifice, goats and so on (अजादि (*ajādi*)), must be what is indicated here. The word अष्टापदीभिः (*aṣṭāpadībhiḥ*) means an animal together with eight feet: the four feet natural to an animal with young, and the four feet of the young in the womb, together make eight feet. Therefore the word अष्टापदीभिः (*aṣṭāpadībhiḥ*) is used to indicate a pregnant female animal.

#### Ṛk 6

*(The Ṛk numeral is read as 6, not zoomed.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> द्र्व॑न्नः स॒र्पिरा॑सुतिः प्र॒त्नो होता॒ वरे॑ण्यः ।
> सह॑सस्पु॒त्रो अद्भु॑तः ॥ ६ ॥

> *drvannaḥ sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ |*
> *sahasasputro adbhutaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> द्रुऽअन्नः । सर्पिःऽआसुतिः । प्रत्नः । होता । वरेण्यः ।
> सहसः । पुत्रः । अद्भुतः ॥ ६ ॥

> *dru 'annaḥ | sarpiḥ 'āsutiḥ | pratnaḥ | hotā | vareṇyaḥ |*
> *sahasaḥ | putraḥ | adbhutaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 525 (PDF 546)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 28 ]" [Varga numeral read from the strip, not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "525". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 6)**

*Gist:* Agni, whose food is fuel, who is sprinkled with ghee, ancient, the priest, to be chosen, son of strength, wonderful: may such an Agni favour us.

> द्र्वन्नः समिद्रूपान्नः । सर्पिरासुतिः सर्पिरासूयेत आसिच्यते यस्मिन् तादृशः प्रत्नः पुरातनो होता होमनिष्पादको वरेण्यो वरणीयः सहसस्पुत्रः सहसो बलस्य पुत्रस्थानीयः । बलेनोत्पन्नत्वात् । अद्भुत आश्चर्यभूतः । रमणीय इत्यर्थः । एवं महानुभावोऽग्निर्मामनुजानात्वित्यर्थः [?] ॥

> *drvannaḥ samidrūpānnaḥ | sarpirāsutiḥ sarpirāsūyeta āsicyate yasmin tādṛśaḥ pratnaḥ purātano hotā homaniṣpādako vareṇyo varaṇīyaḥ sahasasputraḥ sahaso balasya putrasthānīyaḥ | balenotpannatvāt | adbhuta āścaryabhūtaḥ | ramaṇīya ityarthaḥ | evaṃ mahānubhāvo 'gnirmāmanujānātvityarthaḥ [?] ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) द्र्वन्नः (*drvannaḥ*) — one who has food in the form of fuel; सर्पिरासुतिः (*sarpirāsutiḥ*) — one who is sprinkled with ājya; प्रत्नः (*pratnaḥ*) — the ancient; होता (*hotā*) — the accomplisher of the homa; वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*) — the desired; सहसस्पुत्रः (*sahasasputraḥ*) — the son of strength; अद्भुतः (*adbhutaḥ*) — the wonderful (may such an Agni favour us).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) May Agni, who has food in the form of fuel, who is sprinkled with ājya, the ancient, the accomplisher of the homa, desired by all, the son of strength, the wonderful, favour us.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 6)*

Feeder upon fuel, to whom butter is offered, (you are) the ancient, the invoker of the gods, the excellent; the son of strength, the wonderful.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated.) **द्र्वन्नः (*drvannaḥ*)** — द्रु अन्नः (*dru annaḥ*), समिद्रूपान्नः (*samidrūpānnaḥ*). For Agni the samidhs themselves are the food (āhāra). Since samidhs are connected with द्रु (*dru*) — trees — द्र्वन्नः (*drvannaḥ*) means: Agni, who has as his food the samidhs that are connected with trees.

**सर्पिरासुतिः (*sarpirāsutiḥ*)** — Although the word सर्पिः (*sarpiḥ*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24 [?], not zoomed), the bhāṣyakāra explains the word सर्पिः (*sarpiḥ*) as meaning ghee. In the Ṛks

> त्वं हि मानुषे जनेऽग्ने सुप्रीते इध्यसे ।
> स्रुचस्त्वा यंत्यानुषक्सुजाते सर्पिरासुते ॥

> *tvaṃ hi mānuṣe jane 'gne suprīte idhyase |*
> *srucastvā yaṃtyānuṣaksujāte sarpirāsute ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-21-2, as read; not zoomed)

> आ यस्ते सर्पिरासुतेऽग्ने शमस्ति धायसे ।

> *ā yaste sarpirāsute 'gne śamasti dhāyase |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-6-9, as read; not zoomed)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) he has explained the word सर्पिरासुते (*sarpirāsute*) in these Ṛks as "food mixed with ghee" (घृतयुक्तान्न (*ghṛtayuktānna*)). Since ghee is offered into Agni in sacrifices and the like, that ghee itself is said to be Agni's food. Therefore Agni is addressed in many places by the word सर्पिरासुति (*sarpirāsuti*).

### Printed p. 526 (PDF 547)

*(Header: "526", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 8" [numeral read as 8, not zoomed]. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Special Topics of Ṛk 6 continue.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) **प्रत्नः (*pratnaḥ*)** — The word प्रत्न (*pratna*) is read among the names of the ancient (Ni. 3-20, not zoomed); it means one who is ancient, who has existed from very long ago. Besides this ṛṣi who praises Agni, others more ancient than he were also praising for a very long time. Therefore Agni is said to be of a very ancient time.

**सहसः पुत्रः (*sahasaḥ putraḥ*)** — When producing fire by churning in the aranis, the ṛtvijas must use the strength of their arms greatly. Therefore it is very common in the Ṛgveda to say of Agni, who is produced by strength, that he is "born of strength", "the son of strength".

## ऎಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — The Eighth Sūkta

*(Printed heading: "ಎಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು" = "The eighth Sūkta".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sūkta 8)**

*Gist:* Sūkta 8 has six Ṛks; ṛṣi Gṛtsamada, devatā Agni, metre Gāyatrī, the last Ṛk Anuṣṭubh; its use in the morning recitation and the Āśvina śastra was stated earlier.

> वाजयन्निवेति षडृचमष्टमं सूक्तम् । सोमाहुतेर्[?]शब्दानुवृत्तेस्याभावान्मंडलद्रष्टा गृत्समद ऋषिः । अग्निर्देवता । हिंशब्दाद्गायत्री छंदः । अंत्यानुष्टुप् । वाजयन्निवांत्यानुष्टुबित्यनुक्रांतम् ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्तृतीयसूक्तत्वेनास्योत्तमावर्जितस्य विनियोग उक्तः ॥

> *vājayanniveti ṣaḍṛcamaṣṭamaṃ sūktam | somāhuter[?]śabdānuvṛttesyābhāvānmaṃḍaladraṣṭā gṛtsamada ṛṣiḥ | agnirdevatā | hiṃśabdādgāyatrī chaṃdaḥ | aṃtyānuṣṭup | vājayannivāṃtyānuṣṭubityanukrāṃtam ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayostṛtīyasūktatvenāsyottamāvarjitasya viniyoga uktaḥ ‖*

**अनुवाद (Anuvāda)**

(Kannada, translated:) This sūkta beginning वाजयन्निव (*vājayanniva*) is the eighth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada, the seer of the maṇḍala; the devatā is Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. Only the last Ṛk is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: वाजयन्निवांत्यानुष्टुप् (*vājayannivāṃtyānuṣṭup*). It was already said earlier that, at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras, the Ṛks of this sūkta (except the last Ṛk) are applied (viniyoga) as Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre.

**सूक्त—८**

### Printed p. 527 (PDF 548)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 29 ]" [numerals as read from the strip], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "527". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वा॒ज॒यन्नि॑व॒ नू रथा॒न्योगा॑ँ अ॒ग्नेरुप॑ स्तुहि ।
> य॒शस्त॑मस्य मी॒ळ्हुषः॑ ॥ १ ॥

> *vājayanniva nū rathānyogā~ agnerupa stuhi |*
> *yaśastamasya mīḷhuṣaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वाजयन्ऽइव । नु । रथान् । योगान् । अग्नेः । उप । स्तुहि ।
> यशःऽतमस्य । मीळ्हुषः ॥ १ ॥

> *vājayan 'iva | nu | rathān | yogān | agneḥ | upa | stuhi |*
> *yaśaḥ 'tamasya | mīḷhuṣaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 1)**

*Gist:* O inner self, quickly praise the horses (or chariots) of Agni, who is of widespread fame and a bestower of fruit, as one desiring food praises his horses.

> हे अंतरात्मन् नु क्षिप्रमग्नेर्योगानश्वानुपस्तुहि । कीदृशस्याग्नेः । यशस्तमस्य प्रवृद्धयशसः ॥ मत्वर्थो लुप्यते ॥ मीळ्हुषः सेक्तुः फलस्य । ईदृशस्य योगान् स्तुहि । होतरिति वा संबोध्यं । स्तुतौ दृष्टांतः । वाजयन्निव । अन्नमिच्छन् पुरुष इव । स यथाश्वान् गमनाय स्तौति तद्वत् । यद्वोक्तलक्षणस्याग्नेर्गमनसाधनान्रथान् स्तुहि ॥

> *he aṃtarātman nu kṣipramagneryogānaśvānupastuhi | kīdṛśasyāgneḥ | yaśastamasya pravṛddhayaśasaḥ ‖ matvartho lupyate ‖ mīḷhuṣaḥ sektuḥ phalasya | īdṛśasya yogān stuhi | hotariti vā saṃbodhyaṃ | stutau dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | vājayanniva | annamicchan puruṣa iva | sa yathāśvān gamanāya stauti tadvat | yadvoktalakṣaṇasyāgnergamanasādhanānrathān stuhi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) यशस्तमस्य (यशस्तमस्य (*yaśastamasya*)) — of him who has glory spread very widely; मीळ्हुषः (मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*)) — of him who is able to give fruits generously; अग्नेः (अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)) — of Agni; योगान् (योगान् (*yogān*)) — the horses; रथान् (रथान् (*rathān*)) — the chariots; वाजयन्निव (वाजयन्निव (*vājayanniva*)) — like one who desires food urging on the horses of his chariot; नु (नु (*nu*)) — quickly; उप स्तुहि (उप स्तुहि (*upa stuhi*)) — praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) O inner self, as one who desires food urges on the horses of his chariot, so you quickly praise the horses and the chariots of Agni, who has glory spread very widely and is able to give fruits generously.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 1)*

Praise quickly the yoked chariot of the glorious and munificent Agni, like one who is desirous of food.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated.) In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains the meaning of the Ṛk by addressing the inner self (अंतरात्मन् (*aṃtarātman*)), saying that Agni's horses and chariots are to be praised. Here there is no need to address the inner self at all. In a sacrifice one may address any one of the ṛtvijas who take part, or the yajamāna.

### Printed p. 528 (PDF 549)

*(Header: "528", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 8" [numerals as read]. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) **योगान् रथान् (योगान् रथान् (*yogān rathān*))** — the meaning may be made either "praise the horses and also the chariots", or "praise the chariots yoked with horses".

**वाजयन्निव (वाजयन्निव (*vājayanniva*))** — The word वाजः (*vājaḥ*) is read both among the names of food (Ni. 3-9 [?]; numerals not zoomed) and among the names of battle (वाजे (*vāje*)) (Ni. 3-9 [?]; as read, not zoomed). Here the meaning "food" is taken, and the illustration is given of a man who desires food.

**नु (नु (*nu*))** — नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा (*nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā*). The Nirukta (Ni. 1-4) explains the word नु (*nu*) as having many meanings:

> नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा । इदं करिष्यतीति हेत्वपदेशे । कथं नु करिष्यतीत्यनुपृष्टे ।

> *nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā | idaṃ kariṣyatīti hetvapadeśe | kathaṃ nu kariṣyatītyanupṛṣṭe |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) The particle नु (*nu*) has many meanings. When one says इदं नु करिष्यति (*idaṃ nu kariṣyati*), the word नु (*nu*) has the sense of "because of this", i.e. it indicates a reason (hetvartha). When one says कथं नु करिष्यति (*kathaṃ nu kariṣyati*), नु (*nu*) is interrogative. Likewise अथाप्युपमार्थे भवति (*athāpyupamārthe bhavati*): the word नु (*nu*) is used also to indicate comparison. For example:

> अक्षो न चक्र्योः शूर बृहन्प्र ते मह्ना रिरिचे रोदस्योः ।
> वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यूतयो रुरुहुरिंद्र पूर्वीः ॥

> *akṣo na cakryoḥ śūra bṛhanpra te mahnā ririce rodasyoḥ |*
> *vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vyūtayo ruruhuriṃdra pūrvīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-24-3 [?], as read; the first numeral not certain)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) The author of the Nirukta quotes this Ṛk and gives वृक्षस्येव ते पुरुहूत शाखाः (*vṛkṣasyeva te puruhūta śākhāḥ*) ("like a tree, O much-invoked one, the branches" or "like the branches of a tree") as the explanation of the word नु (*nu*) in the sense of comparison. Likewise:

> नू मर्तो दयते सनिष्यन्यो विष्णव उरुगायाय दाशत् ।
> प्र यः सत्राचा मनसा यजात एतावंतं नर्यमाविवासात् ॥

> *nū marto dayate saniṣyanyo viṣṇava urugāyāya dāśat |*
> *pra yaḥ satrācā manasā yajāta etāvaṃtaṃ naryamāvivāsāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-1, as read)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In Ṛks like this, नु (*nu*) has the meaning क्षिप्रम् (*kṣipram*) — "promptly, with alertness" (the Kannada gloss is जाग्रते (*jāgrate*) as printed ಜಾಗ್ರತೆಯಾಗಿ). And:

> नू इंद्र शूर स्तवमान ऊती ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधस्व ।
> उप नो वाजान्मिमीह्युप स्तीन्योयं [?] पाते स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

> *nū iṃdra śūra stavamāna ūtī brahmajūtastanvā vāvṛdhasva |*
> *upa no vājānmimīhyupa stīnyoyaṃ [?] pāte svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-11, as read; the word स्तीन्योयं (*stīnyoyaṃ*) is as read from the strip, not zoomed)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In Ṛks beginning like these, the word अद्य (*adya*) has the meaning "now, at once"; and as the author of the Nirukta says, नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा (*nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā*) (Ni. 1-4), the word नु (*nu*) is used in still other meanings. In the present Ṛk the meaning is "quickly, speedily".

#### Ṛk 2

### Printed p. 529 (PDF 550)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 29 ]" [as read], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "529". The numeral file has no rows for this page. At the foot: signature mark "Vol. 14. [34]".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यः सु॑नी॒थो द॑दा॒शुषे॑ऽजु॒र्यो ज॒रय॑न्न॒रिं ।
> चारु॑प्रतीक॒ आहु॑तः ॥ २ ॥

> *yaḥ sunītho dadāśuṣe 'juryo jarayannariṃ |*
> *cārupratīka āhutaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । सुऽनीथः । ददाशुषे । अजुर्यः । जरयन् । अरिं ।
> चारुऽप्रतीकः । आऽहुतः ॥ २ ॥

> *yaḥ | su 'nīthaḥ | dadāśuṣe | ajuryaḥ | jarayan | ariṃ |*
> *cāru 'pratīkaḥ | ā 'hutaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 2)**

*Gist:* The good leader, unageing, fair of aspect Agni, when well worshipped, destroys the foe of the yajamāna who gives oblations.

> सुनीथः शोभननयनोऽजुर्योऽजरणीयोऽनभिभाव्यः चारुप्रतीकः शोभनोपक्रमो योऽस्ति सोऽग्निर्ददाशुषे हविर्दत्त्रवते [?] यजमानाय तदर्थमरिं तस्य शत्रुं जरयन् नाशयन् आहुतः । समंतादाराधितो भवति ॥

> *sunīthaḥ śobhananayano 'juryo 'jaraṇīyo 'nabhibhāvyaḥ cārupratīkaḥ śobhanopakramo yo 'sti so 'gnirdadāśuṣe havirdattravate [?] yajamānāya tadarthamariṃ tasya śatruṃ jarayan nāśayan āhutaḥ | samaṃtādārādhito bhavati ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) सुनीथः (सुनीथः (*sunīthaḥ*)) — the excellent guide; अजुर्यः (अजुर्यः (*ajuryaḥ*)) — the unhindered; चारुप्रतीकः (चारुप्रतीकः (*cārupratīkaḥ*)) — one of a pleasing form; यः (यः (*yaḥ*)) — whichever Agni, when propitiated (he); ददाशुषे (ददाशुषे (*dadāśuṣe*)) — for the yajamāna who offers oblations; अरिं (अरिं (*ariṃ*)) — his enemy; जरयन् (जरयन् (*jarayan*)) — destroying; आहुतः (आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)) — becomes worshipped.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) The Agni who is an excellent guide, unhindered and of pleasing form, when he is propitiated, destroys the enemy of the yajamāna who offers oblations.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 2)*

Who, sagacious, invincible, and of graceful gait, destroys, when propitiated, his foe, for him who presents (offerings).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated.) **सुनीथः (सुनीथः (*sunīthaḥ*))** — शोभननयनः (*śobhananayanaḥ*). Sāyaṇa has explained it as "a good guide". Yāska reads the word सुनीथ (*sunītha*) in the list of ten laudable names beginning अस्रेमाः (*asremāḥ*), अनेमाः (*anemāḥ*) (Ni. 3-13 [?], not zoomed); therefore सुनीथः (*sunīthaḥ*) may mean "laudable, worthy of praise". Besides this, *(the discussion is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on p. 530)*.

*(Ṛk 2 is left open: Special Topics continue on p. 530.)*

### Printed p. 530 (PDF 551)

*(Header: "530", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 8" [numerals as read from the strip, not zoomed]. The numeral file has no rows for this page. This page continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 2; it opens directly with the quotation below, so the sentence that introduces it is not on this page.)*

#### Ṛk 2 (Special Topics, continued)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) The following Ṛk has the word सुनिथासः (*sunithāsaḥ*) (reference not printed here; the third pāda reads क्राणा (*krāṇā*) [?], as read):

> त्वामिंद्र मतिभिः सुते सुनिथासो वसूयवः । गोभिः क्राणा अनूषत ।

> *tvāmiṃdra matibhiḥ sute sunithāso vasūyavaḥ | gobhiḥ krāṇā anūṣata |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In his commentary on this mantra Durgācārya explains it thus:

> सुनीथासः सुष्ठु ये स्तोतुं शक्नुवंति ते सुनीथाः ।

> *sunīthāsaḥ suṣṭhu ye stotuṃ śaknuvaṃti te sunīthāḥ |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) That is, "those who are able to praise well". (Ni. 4-19 [?]; numerals not zoomed.)

**अजुर्यः (अजुर्यः (*ajuryaḥ*))** —

> अजुर्यः — अजरणीयोऽनभिभाव्यः ।

> *ajuryaḥ — ajaraṇīyo 'nabhibhāvyaḥ |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) This word is formed from the root ज्या वयोहानौ (*jyā vayohānau*) ("jyā, loss of vigour with age"). Because the prefix अ (*a*), which has a negative sense, is joined to it (the source prints उगसर्ग (*ugasarga*) [sic] for उपसर्ग (*upasarga*)), it means "one who is not aged"; that is, "one who is unobstructed, like a young man".

**चारुप्रतीकः (चारुप्रतीकः (*cārupratīkaḥ*))** — For the word प्रतीक (*pratīka*) Yāska has given this etymology (Ni. 2-13 [?]; numerals not zoomed):

> प्रतीकं प्रत्यक्तं भवति प्रत्यंचितं प्रतिगतं प्रकाशस्य ।

> *pratīkaṃ pratyaktaṃ bhavati pratyaṃcitaṃ pratigataṃ prakāśasya |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) On the strength of this etymology, चारुप्रतीकः (*cārupratīkaḥ*) means "one who has a charming form or shape".

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> य उ॑ श्रि॒या दमे॒ष्वा दो॒षोषसि॑ प्रश॒स्यते॑ ।
> यस्य॑ व्र॒तं न मीय॑ते ॥ ३ ॥

> *ya u śriyā dameṣvā doṣoṣasi praśasyate |*
> *yasya vrataṃ na mīyate ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । ऊं इति । श्रिया । दमेषु । आ । दोषा । उषसि । प्रशस्यते ।
> यस्य । व्रतं । न । मीयते ॥ ३ ॥

> *yaḥ | ūṃ iti | śriyā | dameṣu | ā | doṣā | uṣasi | praśasyate |*
> *yasya | vrataṃ | na | mīyate ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 3)**

*Gist:* Agni, endowed with flame, comes to the sacrificial houses and is praised by night, at dawn and by day; his rite is never impaired.

> योऽग्निः श्रिया ज्वालया युक्तः सन् दमेषु आ । आगत्य दोषा रात्रिषु उषस्यहःसु च प्रशस्यते । स्तूयते । यस्याग्नेर्व्रतं कर्म न मीयते । न हिंस्यते न क्षीयते वा ॥

> *yo 'gniḥ śriyā jvālayā yuktaḥ san dameṣu ā | āgatya doṣā rātriṣu uṣasyahaḥsu ca praśasyate | stūyate | yasyāgnervrataṃ karma na mīyate | na hiṃsyate na kṣīyate vā ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) यः उ (*yaḥ u*) — that same Agni; श्रिया (*śriyā*) — endowed with a flame full of radiance; दमेषु (*dameṣu*) — in the sacrificial houses; आ (*ā*) — having come; दोषा (*doṣā*) — in the nights; उषसि (*uṣasi*) — in the dawns (and by day, "ahaḥ"; the Kannada gloss reads ಅಹಸ್ಸ್ಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ); प्रशस्यते (*praśasyate*) — is praised; यस्य (*yasya*) — whose same Agni's; व्रतं (*vrataṃ*) — rite; न मीयते (*na mīyate*) — is not blunted (ಕುಂಠಿತವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, "does not become impaired").

### Printed p. 531 (PDF 552)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 29 ]" [as read from the strip, not zoomed], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "531". The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) The same Agni described above, endowed with a flame full of radiance, comes to the sacrificial houses and is praised in the nights, in the dawns and in the days. And the rite that worships that Agni is never impaired.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 3)*

Who, invested with radiance, is glorified, morning and evening, in (our) dwelling: whose worship is never neglected.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ यः स्व१॒॑र्ण भा॒नुना॑ चि॒त्रो वि॒भात्य॒र्चिषा॑ ।
> अं॒जा॒नो अ॒जरै॑र॒भि ॥ ४ ॥

> *ā yaḥ svarṇa bhānunā citro vibhātyarciṣā |*
> *aṃjāno ajarairabhi ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । यः । स्वः । न । भानुना । चित्रः । विभाति । अर्चिषा ।
> अंजानः । अजरैः । अभि ॥ ४ ॥

> *ā | yaḥ | svaḥ | na | bhānunā | citraḥ | vibhāti | arciṣā |*
> *aṃjānaḥ | ajaraiḥ | abhi ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 4)**

*Gist:* Agni of many hues shines all round with his mass of rays, like the sun with its ray, making all bright with his unageing flames.

> योऽग्निश्चित्रश्चायनीयो नानावर्णो वार्चिषा ज्वालया रश्मिसमूहेनाविभाति । सर्वतो भासते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । स्वर्भानुना । किरणेन सूर्य इव । स यथा विभाति तद्वत् । किं कुर्वन् । अजरैर्नित्यैर्ज्वालासमूहैरभि सर्वतोऽंजानो व्यंजयन् प्रकाशयन् ॥

> *yo 'gniścitraścāyanīyo nānāvarṇo vārciṣā jvālayā raśmisamūhenāvibhāti | sarvato bhāsate | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | svarbhānunā | kiraṇena sūrya iva | sa yathā vibhāti tadvat | kiṃ kurvan | ajarairnityairjvālāsamūhairabhi sarvato 'ṃjāno vyaṃjayan prakāśayan ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) स्वः (*svaḥ*) — the Āditya (sun); भानुना न (*bhānunā na*) — as he shines with his own rays; यः (*yaḥ*) — whichever same Agni; चित्रः (*citraḥ*) — being of many colours; अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*) — and being endowed with masses of rays; अजरैः (*ajaraiḥ*) — with eternal flames; अभि (*abhi*) — on all sides; अंजानः (*aṃjānaḥ*) — spreading radiance; आ विभाति (*ā vibhāti*) — shines fully.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) As the sun shines with his rays, Agni, of many colours and endowed with masses of rays, shines fully, spreading radiance on all sides with his eternal flames.

### Printed p. 532 (PDF 553)

*(Header: "532", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 8" [numerals as read, not zoomed]. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 4)*

Who, many-tinted, shines with radiance, like the sun with (his) lustre, spreading light over (all) by his imperishable (flames),

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated.) **स्वः न भानुना (*svaḥ na bhānunā*)** — the meaning is "as the Āditya shines with his rays". The word स्वः (*svaḥ*) is read in the common names स्वः पृश्निः नाकः (*svaḥ pṛśniḥ nākaḥ*) and so on. The Nirukta says (Ni. 2-13 [?], not zoomed):

> साधारणान्युत्तराणि षट् दिवश्चादित्यस्य च ।

> *sādhāraṇānyuttarāṇi ṣaṭ divaścādityasya ca |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) That is, the six words स्वः पृश्निः नाकः गौः विष्टपं नभः (*svaḥ pṛśniḥ nākaḥ gauḥ viṣṭapaṃ nabhaḥ*) are all common terms, both synonyms of the heaven-world and words for the Āditya, as the author of the Nirukta states. Then, explaining what the root of the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) is, in its sense of Āditya, and how the word is derived, he says:

> स्वरादित्यो भवति सु अरणः सु ईरणः स्वृतो रसान् स्वृतो भासं ज्योतिषां । स्वृतो भासेति वा ॥

> *svarādityo bhavati su araṇaḥ su īraṇaḥ svṛto rasān svṛto bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ | svṛto bhāseti vā ‖*

(Ni. 2-14 [?], not zoomed)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) The Āditya has this name either because he is very far away (सु अरणः (*su araṇaḥ*), "going well"), or because he scatters and destroys the darkness completely, or because he enters the juices (rasa) and goes inside them, or because he spreads his own light in the sphere of radiance and becomes one with it, or because he becomes all-pervading in the form of light. And by the words एतेन द्यौर्व्याख्याता (*etena dyaurvyākhyātā*) ("by this the sky is explained") the Nirukta-author shows that for this very reason the heaven-world also has the name स्वः (*svaḥ*).

> स्वरादित्यो भवति स एनानि सारयति [?] ।

> *svarādityo bhavati sa enāni sārayati [?] |*

(Ni. 5-4 [?], not zoomed; the word एनानि (*enāni*) is as read from the strip, not zoomed)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) The Āditya also has the name स्वः (*svaḥ*) because he makes the days (ಅಹಸ್ಸ್ಗಳು) move along. Where the word is used in the Ṛgveda:

> प्रत्यङ् देवानां विशः प्रत्यङ्ङुदेषि मानुषान् । प्रत्यङ् विश्वं स्वर्दृशे ॥

> *pratyaṅ devānāṃ viśaḥ pratyaṅṅudeṣi mānuṣān | pratyaṅ viśvaṃ svardṛśe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-5 [?], as read, not zoomed)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In Ṛks like this the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) has the name of the heaven-world (svargaloka). And:

> त्मना वहंतो दुरो व्यृण्वन्नवंत विश्वे स्वर्दृशीके ।

> *tmanā vahaṃto duro vyṛṇvannavaṃta viśve svardṛśīke |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-69-10 [?], as read, not zoomed)

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In Ṛks like this, the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) means नभसि (*nabhasi*), "in the sky, in the atmosphere". And:

> दानो अग्ने बृहतो दाः सहस्रिणो दुरो न वाजं श्रुत्या अपा वृधि ।
> प्राची द्यावापृथिवी ब्रह्मणा कृधि स्वर्ण शुक्रमुषसो वि दिद्युतुः ॥

> *dāno agne bṛhato dāḥ sahasriṇo duro na vājaṃ śrutyā apā vṛdhi |*
> *prācī dyāvāpṛthivī brahmaṇā kṛdhi svarṇa śukramuṣaso vi didyutuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-2-2 [?], as read, not zoomed)

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 4 are left open at the foot of the page, after this quotation; they continue on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 533 (PDF 554)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 29 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "533". The numeral file has no rows for this page. Header and reference numerals not zoomed.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued from the Special Topics of Ṛk 4.) In Ṛks like these the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) has been explained as "Āditya". In the same way, words that carry suffixes such as वत् (*vat*), e.g. स्वर्वत् (*svarvat*), are likewise to be explained according to the context. For example, (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-97-1 [?], numerals as read, not zoomed; the accent-like mark over स्वर्वा (*svarvā*) is as printed):

> या इंद्र भुज आभरः स्वर्वा असुरेभ्यः ।
> स्तोतारमिन्मघवन्नस्य वर्धय यो च त्वे वृक्तबर्हिषः ॥

> *yā iṃdra bhuja ābharaḥ svarvā asurebhyaḥ |*
> *stotāraminmaghavannasya vardhaya yo ca tve vṛktabarhiṣaḥ ‖*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In this Ṛk — the commentator says "सुखवान्, स्वर्गवान् वा" ("possessed of happiness, or possessed of heaven"):

*Gist:* The word स्वः (*svaḥ*) is a synonym of "all"; everything that is born is of one's own self, hence "possessed of all".

> अथवा स्वशब्दः सर्वपर्यायः । सर्वं भूतजातं आत्मन एवोत्पन्नत्वात्स्वान् [?] ।

> *athavā svaśabdaḥ sarvaparyāyaḥ | sarvaṃ bhūtajātaṃ ātmana evotpannatvātsvān [?] |*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) Since the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) has the meanings happiness, heaven or "all", स्वर्वान् (*svarvān*) means "one who has happiness", "a dweller in heaven", or "one who has obtained everything". All these meanings fit when it is an epithet of Indra. And again (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-40-11 [?], as read, not zoomed):

> तं शिशीता स्वध्वरं सत्यं सत्वानमृत्वियं ।
> उतो नु चिद्य ओहत आंडा शुष्णस्य भेदत्यज्मैः स्वर्वतीरपो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥

> *taṃ śiśītā svadhvaraṃ satyaṃ satvānamṛtviyaṃ |*
> *uto nu cidya ohata āṃḍā śuṣṇasya bhedatyajmaiḥ svarvatīrapo nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In passages like these, where स्वर्वतीः अपः (*svarvatīḥ apaḥ*) is an epithet of water, दिव्यानि (*divyāni*) means "water produced in the heaven-world". This epithet also describes the qualities of Agni and the other deities. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-3 [?], as read, not zoomed):

> ज्योतिष्मतीमदितिं धारयत्क्षितिं स्वर्वतीमा सचेते दिवे दिवे जागृवांसा दिवेदिवे ॥

> *jyotiṣmatīmaditiṃ dhārayatkṣitiṃ svarvatīmā sacete dive dive jāgṛvāṃsā divedive ‖*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) Here स्वर्वती (*svarvatī*) is an epithet of Aditi. In this place it is explained as the commentator has explained it — "yajñaniṣpatti-dvārā स्वर्गवतीं (*svargavatīṃ*)" (through the accomplishment of sacrifice, "possessing heaven"). (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-19-9 [?], as read, not zoomed; the words पश्चादोत्तरादधरादा [?] (*paścādottarādadharādā [?]*) and समोत्वर्वाजिंद्र [?] (*samotvarvājiṃdra [?]*) are as read from the strip, not zoomed):

> आ ते शुष्मो वृषभ एतु पश्चादोत्तरादधरादा पुरस्तात् ।
> आ विश्वतो अभि समोत्वर्वाजिंद्र द्युम्नं स्वर्वद्धेह्यस्मे ॥

> *ā te śuṣmo vṛṣabha etu paścādottarādadharādā purastāt |*
> *ā viśvato abhi samotvarvājiṃdra dyumnaṃ svarvaddhehyasme ‖*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) In Ṛks like these the meaning सुखयुक्तं धनं (*sukhayuktaṃ dhanaṃ*) ("wealth endowed with happiness") is also given. In the Ṛk in hand the meaning is "Āditya".

**भानुना (*bhānunā*)** — (Kannada, translated:) Since the word भानुः (*bhānuḥ*) is read in the twelve names of "day" (ahar-nāmāni) beginning with वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*), द्यौः (*dyauḥ*) and so on, it means the shining day. And भानुः भासते ह्येतत् ज्योतिषा (*bhānuḥ bhāsate hyetat jyotiṣā*) ("bhānu shines, for this shines by light") — since it shines by its own light, it is explained here as the rays of the sun.

### Printed p. 534 (PDF 555)

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अत्रि॒मनु॑ स्व॒राज्य॑म॒ग्निमु॒क्थानि॑ वावृधुः ।
> विश्वा॒ अधि॒ श्रियो॑ दधे ॥ ५ ॥

> *atrimanu svarājyamagnimukthāni vāvṛdhuḥ |*
> *viśvā adhi śriyo dadhe ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अत्रिं । अनु । स्वराज्यं । अग्निं । उक्थानि । ववृधुः ।
> विश्वाः । अधि । श्रियः । दधे ॥ ५ ॥

> *atriṃ | anu | svarājyaṃ | agniṃ | ukthāni | vavṛdhuḥ |*
> *viśvāḥ | adhi | śriyaḥ | dadhe ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 5)**

*Gist:* Our hymns magnify Agni, devourer of enemies or of oblations, self-shining; he holds all glories.

> अत्रिं शत्रूणामन्नानां वा भक्षकं स्वराज्यं स्वयमेव राजमानं स्वराज्यमनु अभिलक्ष्य वाग्निमुक्थानि शस्त्राणि ववृधुः । वर्धयंति । स चाग्निर्विश्वाः सर्वाः श्रियोऽधि दधे धारयति ॥

> *atriṃ śatrūṇāmannānāṃ vā bhakṣakaṃ svarājyaṃ svayameva rājamānaṃ svarājyamanu abhilakṣya vāgnimukthāni śastrāṇi vavṛdhuḥ | vardhayaṃti | sa cāgnirviśvāḥ sarvāḥ śriyo 'dhi dadhe dhārayati ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) अत्रिं (*atriṃ*) — the devourer of enemies, or one who eats food; स्वराज्यं (*svarājyaṃ*) — one who shines as a perfect lord by himself; अग्निं अनु (*agniṃ anu*) — chanted with Agni as the aim; उक्थानि (*ukthāni*) — our śastra-mantras; ववृधुः (*vavṛdhuḥ*) — make (him) grow strong (he); विश्वाः श्रियः (*viśvāḥ śriyaḥ*) — all riches; अधि दधे (*adhi dadhe*) — has obtained.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) Our śastra-mantras, chanted in praise of Agni, the devourer of enemies and the self-shining perfect lord, make him grow strong. He has obtained all riches.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 5)*

Our praises have increased the self-irradiating devouring Agni: he is possessed of all glory.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 5)**

**अत्रिं (*atriṃ*)** — (Kannada, translated:) For this word, derived from the root अद भक्षणे (*ada bhakṣaṇe*) ("ada, to eat"), the commentator explains two kinds of meaning. अत्रिं—शत्रून् अत्ति भक्षयति (दहति) ध्वंसयति इति अत्रिः (*atriṃ—śatrūn atti bhakṣayati (dahati) dhvaṃsayati iti atriḥ*) — he is called Atri because he devours enemies, or because he burns and destroys them; or

---

### Printed p. 535 (PDF 556)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 29.]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "535". The numeral file has no rows for this page. Header numerals not zoomed.)*

(Kannada, translated, continued.) The śruti sentence

> अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि [?] । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यते इति

> *adyate 'tti ca bhūtāni [?] | tasmādannaṃ taducyate iti*

(the form अद्यतेऽत्ति (*adyate 'tti*) is as read from the strip, not zoomed) says that a thing fit to be eaten is called अन्नं (*annaṃ*) ("food"). Since he eats (consumes by burning) such food, or food in the form of the oblation, he is called Atri: thus two kinds of meaning are given. The sense is, therefore, that Agni is the destroyer of enemies, or the eater of food in the form of the oblation.

**स्वराज्यं (*svarājyaṃ*)** — स्वयमेव राजमानं स्वराज्यमनु अभिलक्ष्य वा (*svayameva rājamānaṃ svarājyamanu abhilakṣya vā*). (Kannada, translated:) Two meanings are explained: Agni shines by his own power, without the help of another shining thing; or Agni is the lord who gives wealth and the like to men and creatures.

**उक्थानि (*ukthāni*)** — (Kannada, translated:) The word उक्थ्य (*ukthya*) is read among the names for praise (Ni. 3-13 [?], numerals as read, not zoomed). It means the hymns and the like that describe and recite the qualities of the deities.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒ग्नेरिंद्र॑स्य॒ सोम॑स्य दे॒वाना॑मू॒तिभि॑र्व॒यं ।
> अरि॑ष्यंतः सचेमह्य॒भि ष्या॑म पृतन्य॒तः ॥ ६ ॥

> *agneriṃdrasya somasya devānāmūtibhirvayaṃ |*
> *ariṣyaṃtaḥ sacemahyabhi ṣyāma pṛtanyataḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अग्नेः । इंद्रस्य । सोमस्य । देवानां । ऊतिभिः । वयं ।
> अरिष्यंतः । सचेमहि । अभि । स्याम । पृतन्यतः ॥ ६ ॥

> *agneḥ | iṃdrasya | somasya | devānāṃ | ūtibhiḥ | vayaṃ |*
> *ariṣyaṃtaḥ | sacemahi | abhi | syāma | pṛtanyataḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Ṛk 6)**

*Gist:* Unharmed by anyone, we are joined to the protections of Agni, Indra, Soma and the other gods, and may overcome enemies seeking battle.

> अरिष्यंतः केनाप्यहिंस्यमानाः वयमग्नेरिंद्रस्य सोमस्य देवानामन्येषामप्यूतिभी रक्षणाभिः सचेमहि । युक्ता भवेम । तथा रक्षायुक्ता वयं पृतन्यतः पृतनामात्मन इच्छतः शत्रूनभिष्याम । अभिभवेम ॥ पृतनाशब्दात्क्यचि कव्यध्वरपृतनस्यर्चि लोप इत्यवर्णलोपः ॥

> *ariṣyaṃtaḥ kenāpyahiṃsyamānāḥ vayamagneriṃdrasya somasya devānāmanyeṣāmapyūtibhī rakṣaṇābhiḥ sacemahi | yuktā bhavema | tathā rakṣāyuktā vayaṃ pṛtanyataḥ pṛtanāmātmana icchataḥ śatrūnabhiṣyāma | abhibhavema ‖ pṛtanāśabdātkyaci kavyadhvarapṛtanasyarci lopa ityavarṇalopaḥ ‖*

(Grammatical tail: formation of पृतन्यतः (*pṛtanyataḥ*) from पृतना (*pṛtanā*) with the suffix क्यच् (*kyac*) and the elision of the final अ (*a*); not explained.)

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated; the entry breaks off at the end of the page:) अरिष्यंतः (*ariṣyaṃtaḥ*) — not injured by anyone; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we; अग्नेः (*agneḥ*) — of Agni; इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*) — of Indra; सोमस्य (*somasya*) — of Soma (and); देवानां (*devānāṃ*) — of all the other gods; ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*) — protection

*(Ṛk 6 is left open in the Pratipadārtha, mid-sentence, at the foot of the page; it continues on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 536 (PDF 557)

*(Header: "536", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 8", numerals as read, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6, continued from the foot of p. 535)**

(Kannada, translated, continued: the word "protection" of the previous page continues as "…protections, with (them)".) सचेमहि (*sacemahi*) — let us be united (likewise); पृतन्यतः (*pṛtanyataḥ*) — also the enemies who have armies; अभिष्याम (*abhiṣyāma*) — let us obtain the power to defeat (them).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) Not falling under anyone's harm, let us be united with the protections of Agni, Indra and Soma, and likewise with the protections of all the other deities. Let us obtain the power to defeat the enemies who possess exceedingly great army strength.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 6)*

May we, uninjured, be secure in the protection of Agni, Indra, Soma, and the gods, and, confident in battle, overcome (our enemies).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) In this Ṛk, which forms the conclusion of the sūkta, prayer is made desiring the protection of Agni, Indra, Soma and all the other deities.

**पृतन्यतः (*pṛtanyataḥ*)** — (Kannada, translated:) Since the word प्रतना (*pratanā*) [sic, as printed; the Ṛk has पृतना (*pṛtanā*)] is read among the names of battle beginning with रणः (*raṇaḥ*) (the number-word printed in the Kannada is ಸಲವತ್ತಾರು [?]; Ni. 3-9 [?], numerals as read, not zoomed), पृतना (*pṛtanā*) means battle. पृतन्यतः (*pṛtanyataḥ*) means: the enemies who intend to fight a battle with an army — this is the sense.

**Close of the Fifth Adhyāya**

> वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् ।
> पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥

> *vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan |*
> *pumarthāṃścaturo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*

> इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्य-
> धुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे
> ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये द्वितीयाष्टके पंचमोऽध्यायः ॥ समाप्तः ॥

> *iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājya-*
> *dhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe*
> *ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye dvitīyāṣṭake paṃcamo 'dhyāyaḥ ‖ samāptaḥ ‖*

(Gist of the verse: "May Maheśvara, the 'Vidyātīrtha', removing the inner darkness by the light of the Veda's meaning, grant the four human aims." The colophon says: thus, in the Mādhavīya "Vedārthaprakāśa", the Ṛksaṃhitā-bhāṣya composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the fifth adhyāya of the second Aṣṭaka is ended.)

(Kannada closing line, translated:) Here the fifth adhyāya, in the second Aṣṭaka, of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with the Śrī Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and the Kannada translation, comes to completion. (The Kannada verb is printed ಸಮಾಪ್ತವಾಡುದು, as printed.)

> ॥ ओं तत्सत् ॥
> यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् ।
> तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
> ॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥
> ॥ मंगळं ॥

> *‖ oṃ tatsat ‖*
> *yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet |*
> *tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖*
> *‖ śubhaṃ bhūyāt ‖*
> *‖ maṃgaḷaṃ ‖*

(Gist: "Om, That is Real. Whatever is lacking in syllable or word, or short in measure — may all that be forgiven, O god, lord of speech; salutation to you. May there be auspiciousness. Blessing.")

### Printed p. 537 (PDF 558)

*(Half-title page of the Sixth Adhyāya of the Second Aṣṭaka; no header and no printed page number visible. The numeral file has no rows for this page. It carries an Om emblem and the following invocation, then the title and the adhyāya heading.)*

> ॥ श्री ॥
> ॥ श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः ॥

> *‖ śrī ‖*
> *‖ śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ ‖*

> वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे ।
> यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥
> यस्य निश्श्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् ।
> निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥
> द्वितीयाष्टकमध्यस्थः पंचमोऽध्याय आदरात् ।
> व्याख्यातः सायणार्येण षष्ठश्च व्याकरिष्यते ॥
> वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः ।
> तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥

> *vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame |*
> *yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*
> *yasya niśśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat |*
> *nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*
> *dvitīyāṣṭakamadhyasthaḥ paṃcamo 'dhyāya ādarāt |*
> *vyākhyātaḥ sāyaṇāryeṇa ṣaṣṭhaśca vyākariṣyate ‖*
> *vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ |*
> *tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*

(Gist: salutation to Gaṇeśa; to Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, whose breath was the Vedas; the fifth adhyāya has been expounded and the sixth will now be expounded; "the Veda is Śiva… therefore let one always recite the Veda".)

#### Sūkta 9 (Maṇḍala 2) — Sāyaṇa's introduction (begins here)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The ninth sūkta, of six Ṛks, is by Gṛtsamada; metre Triṣṭubh, deity Agni; it is used in the Prātaranuvāka, the Āśvina-śastra, the Agni-kratu and the Agnipraṇayana, with Āśvalāyana references.

> नि होतेति षडृचं नवमं सूक्तं गृत्समदस्यार्षं नि होतेत्यनुक्रांतत्वात् । अनुक्तत्वात् त्रिष्टुप् । मंडलादिपरिभाषयाग्निर्देवता ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोराग्नेये क्रतौ त्रैष्टुभे छंदस्यस्य विनियोगः । अथैतस्या इति खंडे सूत्रितं । नि होता होतृषदन इति सूक्ते । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥ अग्निप्रणयने आद्ये ऋचा विनियुक्ते । पंचम्यां पौर्णमास्यामिति खंडे सूत्रितं । नि होता होतृषदन इति द्वे । आ. २-१२ ॥

> *ni hoteti ṣaḍṛcaṃ navamaṃ sūktaṃ gṛtsamadasyārṣaṃ ni hotetyanukrāṃtatvāt | anuktatvāt triṣṭup | maṃḍalādiparibhāṣayāgnirdevatā ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorāgneye kratau traiṣṭubhe chaṃdasyasya viniyogaḥ | athaitasyā iti khaṃḍe sūtritaṃ | ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti sūkte | ā. 4-13 | iti ‖ agnipraṇayane ādye ṛcā viniyukte | paṃcamyāṃ paurṇamāsyāmiti khaṃḍe sūtritaṃ | ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti dve | ā. 2-12 ‖*

**अनुवाद (Anuvāda — Kannada, translated; Sūkta 9 introduction)**

(Kannada, translated:) This sūkta, नि होता (*ni hotā*), is the ninth sūkta in the first anuvāka of the second Maṇḍala. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada, the seer of the Maṇḍala; the deity is Agni; the metre is Triṣṭubh. At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra mantras, this sūkta is applied to the Triṣṭubh Ṛks belonging to the Āgneya sacrifice (*kratu*). This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning अथैतस्या (*athaitasyā*), by the sūtra नि होता होतृषदन इति सूक्ते (*ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti sūkte*) (Ā. 4-13 [?]). In the sacrificial-limb rite called Agnipraṇayana, the first two Ṛks of this sūkta are applied. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section पंचम्यां पौर्णमास्याम् (*paṃcamyāṃ paurṇamāsyām*), by the sūtra नि होता होतृषदन इति द्वे (*ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti dve*) (Ā. 2-12 [?]).

(The printed Āśvalāyana references are read as "Ā. 4-13" and "Ā. 2-12"; the numerals are not zoomed [?].)

**सायणभाष्यम् (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Ṛk 1)**

*Gist:* Gṛtsamada praises Agni with these epithets: invoker of the gods, wise, bright, strong, of unharmed rites, best giver of dwelling, bearer of many forms. He is to sit in the hotṛ's seat, the Uttaravedi. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa is cited.

> गृत्समदः स्तौति । होता देवानामाह्वाता विदानो विद्वान् त्वेषः प्रवृद्धो दीदिवान् दीप्यमानः सुदक्षः शोभनबलोऽदब्धव्रतप्रमतिः । अदब्धान्यहिंसितानि व्रतानि कर्माणि यस्याः सादब्धव्रता प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टा बुद्धिर्यस्य स तथोक्तः । वसिष्ठः सर्वस्य वासयितृतमः ॥ वासयतेस्तृजंतस्येष्ठनि रूपं ॥

> *gṛtsamadaḥ stauti | hotā devānāmāhvātā vidāno vidvān tveṣaḥ pravṛddho dīdivān dīpyamānaḥ sudakṣaḥ śobhanabalo 'dabdhavratapramatiḥ | adabdhānyahiṃsitāni vratāni karmāṇi yasyāḥ sādabdhavratā pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭā buddhiryasya sa tathoktaḥ | vasiṣṭhaḥ sarvasya vāsayitṛtamaḥ ‖ vāsayatestṛjaṃtasyeṣṭhani rūpaṃ ‖*

> सहस्रंभरः सहस्रस्यानेकविधस्य भर्ता । विहरणेन नानाविधरूपस्य धारक इत्यर्थः । यद्वा सहस्रस्य सर्वस्य भर्ता । तथा च वाजसनेयं । सर्वं वै सहस्रं सर्वंभर इत्येव तदाहेति । शुचिजिह्वः । शुचिर्दीप्ता जिह्वा ज्वाला यस्य स तथोक्तः । एवंभूतोऽग्निर्होतृषदने । होतात्र सीदतीति होतृषदनमुत्तरा वेदी ॥ अधिकरणे ल्युट् ॥ तत्र न्यसदत् । नितरां सीदतु ॥ उक्तार्थे ब्राह्मणं । नि

> *sahasraṃbharaḥ sahasrasyānekavidhasya bhartā | viharaṇena nānāvidharūpasya dhāraka ityarthaḥ | yadvā sahasrasya sarvasya bhartā | tathā ca vājasaneyaṃ | sarvaṃ vai sahasraṃ sarvaṃbhara ityeva tadāheti | śucijihvaḥ | śucirdīptā jihvā jvālā yasya sa tathoktaḥ | evaṃbhūto 'gnirhotṛṣadane | hotātra sīdatīti hotṛṣadanamuttarā vedī ‖ adhikaraṇe lyuṭ ‖ tatra nyasadat | nitarāṃ sīdatu ‖ uktārthe brāhmaṇaṃ | ni*

> होता होतृषदने विदाद इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैतद्धोतृषदनं यदुत्तरवेदीनाभिस्त्वेषो दीदिवा असदत्सुदक्ष [?] इत्यासन्नो हि स तर्हि भवत्यदब्धव्रतप्रमतिर्वसिष्ठ इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां वसिष्ठः सहस्रंभरः शुचिजिह्वो अग्निरित्येषा वा अस्य सहस्रंभरता यदेनमेकं संतं बहुधा विहरंति । ऐ. ब्रा. १. २८ [?] । इति ॥

> *hotā hotṛṣadane vidāda ityagnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaitaddhotṛṣadanaṃ yaduttaravedīnābhistveṣo dīdivā asadatsudakṣa [?] ityāsanno hi sa tarhi bhavatyadabdhavratapramatirvasiṣṭha ityagnirvai devānāṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ sahasraṃbharaḥ śucijihvo agnirityeṣā vā asya sahasraṃbharatā yadenamekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā viharaṃti | ai. brā. 1. 28 [?] | iti ‖*

(The grammatical remarks "वासयतेस्तृजंतस्येष्ठनि रूपं" and "अधिकरणे ल्युट्" are transcribed without explanation. The bhāṣya reads "असपत्सदक्ष" or "असदत्सुदक्ष" in the Brāhmaṇa quotation, which is doubtful [?]. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa reference "१. २८" is read, not zoomed [?].)

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha, Ṛk 1; Kannada, translated)**

- होता (*hotā*) — one who is fit to call the deities to the sacrifice.
- विदानः (*vidānaḥ*) — the wise one.
- त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*) — the fully grown one (the Kannada word is *pravṛddha*).
- दीदिवान् (*dīdivān*) — the shining one.
- सुदक्षः (*sudakṣaḥ*) — one with excellent strength.
- अदब्धव्रतप्रमतिः (*adabdhavratapramatiḥ*) — one with a distinguished knowledge, that his own rite cannot be harmed.
- वसिष्ठः (*vasiṣṭhaḥ*) — one with an excellent dwelling-place.
- सहस्रंभरः (*sahasraṃbharaḥ*) — one who bears (holds) thousands of forms.
- शुचिजिह्वः (*śucijihvaḥ*) — one whose tongue is shining and of the form of flame.
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*) — Agni.
- होतृषदने (*hotṛṣadane*) — in the Uttaravedi, the place of the hotṛ.
- नि असदत् (*ni asadat*) — let him sit down.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha, Ṛk 1; Kannada, translated)**

May Agni sit down in the Uttaravedi, the place of the hotṛ. He is fit to call the deities to the sacrifice. He is wise, fully grown, shining and of excellent strength. His knowledge is distinguished, so that his rite cannot be harmed. He has an excellent dwelling-place and bears thousands of forms. He is shining, and his tongue is of the form of flame.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 1; it breaks at the foot of this page)*

May Agni, the invoker (of the gods), the intelligent, the resplendent, the radiant, the very powerful; he who knows (how to maintain) his rites

undisturbed; who is steady in (his own) place, and is the cherisher of thousands, sit in the station of the invoking priest.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) In this Ṛk the seer Gṛtsamada praises Agni, describing him by various epithets.

**होता (*hotā*)** — (Kannada, translated:) One who invokes the deities. That is, the Agni who brings to the sacrificial altar the deities who have been invoked in the sacrifice. The word होतृ (*hotṛ*) is used in three senses. It means the human *hotṛ* priests in the sacrifice. It means Agni as the accomplisher of the oblation, that is, the Agni who carries out the oblation. And it means Agni as the one who invokes the deities. Here it is said to be the Agni who invokes the deities.

**त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*)** — (Kannada, translated:) *Pravṛddha*, that is, the Agni who blazes and crackles, flaming up with samit (kindling sticks), kāṣṭha (wood) and the like. When Agni is produced by churning in the two *araṇis* (fire-drills), he is very small, and so he is said to be in the form of an infant. The same Agni, established in the Āhavanīya and other fires and burning large with wood and with oblations of ghee (*ājya*) and the like, is called *pravṛddha*. The word त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*) is formed from the root त्विष् (*tviṣ*) ("to shine"), and indicates the sense "one who shines brilliantly".

**सुदक्षः (*sudakṣaḥ*)** — (Kannada, translated:) The word दक्षः (*dakṣaḥ*) is read among the twenty-eight names of strength beginning with ओजः (*ojaḥ*) and पाजः (*pājaḥ*) (Ni. 2-9 [?], numerals as read, not zoomed). Therefore सुदक्षः (*sudakṣaḥ*) means "one with exceedingly great strength".

**अदब्धव्रतप्रमतिः (*adabdhavratapramatiḥ*)**

> अदब्धान्यहिंसितानि व्रतानि कर्माणि यस्याः सादब्धव्रता प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टा बुद्धिर्यस्य स तथोक्तः ।

> *adabdhānyahiṃsitāni vratāni karmāṇi yasyāḥ sādabdhavratā pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭā buddhiryasya sa tathoktaḥ |*

(Kannada, translated:) That is, Agni's acts (*karma*), the invocation of the deities, the carrying out of the oblation and the other subsidiary acts of the sacrifice, are unharmed. They are by nature such that they do harm to no one. The sense is that Agni has a distinguished knowledge that the acts he performs are of such a nature. In the Ṛgveda, compound words (compound words, in English as printed) of more than two members are very rare. In this word three words, अदब्ध (*adabdha*) + व्रत (*vrata*) + प्रमति (*pramati*), join to form one compound. Such usages are extremely scarce.

**वसिष्ठः (*vasiṣṭhaḥ*)**

> सर्वस्य वासयितृतमः ।

> *sarvasya vāsayitṛtamaḥ |*

(Kannada, translated:) The best among those who give a dwelling-place to everyone. Or, one who has an excellent dwelling-place.

**सहस्रंभरः (*sahasraṃbharaḥ*)**

> सहस्रस्यानेकविधस्य भर्ता । विहरणेन नानाविधरूपस्य धारक इत्यर्थः । यद्वा सहस्रस्य सर्वस्य भर्ता ।

> *sahasrasyānekavidhasya bhartā | viharaṇena nānāvidharūpasya dhāraka ityarthaḥ | yadvā sahasrasya sarvasya bhartā |*

(Kannada, translated, continuing at the foot of the page:) Here the word सहस्र (*sahasra*) has the meaning "many"; Agni

**शुचिजिह्वः (*śucijihvaḥ*)**

> शुचिर्दीप्ता जिह्वा ज्वाला यस्य ।

> *śucirdīptā jihvā jvālā yasya |*

(Kannada, translated:) *Śuci* means shining; *jihvā* means tongue. "One who has a shining tongue" means one who has flames that burn brightly. The flames of Agni are said to be Agni's tongues (*jihvā*).

**होतृषदने (*hotṛṣadane*)**

> होतात्र सीदतीति होतृषदनमुत्तरा वेदी ।

> *hotātra sīdatīti hotṛṣadanamuttarā vedī |*

(Kannada, translated:) The place where the ṛtvij called *hotṛ* sits down in the sacrificial altar is called होतृषदन (*hotṛṣadana*) (होतृ (*hotṛ*) + सदन (*sadana*)). The sense is the place called the Uttaravedi. On this matter the bhāṣyakāra has cited a sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 1-28 [?], not zoomed). The first two Ṛks of this sūkta are the last two (the 7th and 8th Ṛks [?]) of the eight Ṛks to be recited when, in the sacrifice, the rite called Agnipraṇayana is performed. Agnipraṇayana means setting Agni in the Uttaravedi. This rite is an important one performed in the animal sacrifice (*paśuyāga*) and in the Soma sacrifices. The rite of taking the fire from the Āhavanīya fire to the Uttaravedi (this sentence is carried over to the next page of the print)

(Kannada, translated, continuing the bracket:) "… Afterwards this Agni says: 'May he carry to the deities the oblations and the like that we offer.']. The Ṛk spoken above is of the Gāyatrī metre. Why should a Ṛk of this metre be recited? —"

*(Brāhmaṇa passage in bold in the print; the first word reads गायत्रो as printed.)*

> गायत्रो वै ब्राह्मणस्तेजो वै ब्रह्मवर्चसं गायत्री तेजस्यैवैनं तद्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन समर्धयति ॥

> *gāyatro vai brāhmaṇastejo vai brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī tejasyaivainaṃ tadbrahmavarcasena samardhayati ‖*

(Kannada, translated:) If the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice is a Brāhmaṇa, a Ṛk of the Gāyatrī metre must be recited. The reason is that the Brāhmaṇa has the nature of the Gāyatrī. Because the Brāhmaṇa is born from the mouth of Prajāpati (Parabrahman) (ब्राह्मणोऽस्य मुखमासीत् (*brāhmaṇo 'sya mukhamāsīt*) Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-12 [?], numerals read, not zoomed), the *tejas* (radiance) of Prajāpati is in the Brāhmaṇa. In the Gāyatrī too there is such *brahmavarcas* (the radiance of sacred knowledge). Therefore the Brāhmaṇa must carry this rite through with a Ṛk of the Gāyatrī metre, which is endowed with *brahmavarcas*. On the question which metres' Ṛks the Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya and Vaiśya should recite in order to carry the sacrificial rites through, the Brāhmaṇa passage of the Taittirīya (Yajurveda) reads thus—

*(In the Brāhmaṇa quotation: the printed त्रिष्टुग्भी is kept as printed. The word प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय, read from the strip and not zoomed, is doubtful [?].)*

> गायत्रीभिर्ब्राह्मणस्याद्ध्यात् । गायत्रच्छन्दा वै ब्राह्मणः । स्वस्य छन्दसः प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय [?] । त्रिष्टुग्भी राजन्यस्य । त्रिष्टुप्छन्दा वै राजन्यः । स्वस्य छन्दसः प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय [?] । जगतीभिर्वैश्यस्य । जगतीछन्दा वै वैश्यः । स्वस्य छन्दसः प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय [?] ॥

> *gāyatrībhirbrāhmaṇasyāddhyāt | gāyatracchandā vai brāhmaṇaḥ | svasya chandasaḥ pratyayanastvāya [?] | triṣṭugbhī rājanyasya | triṣṭupchandā vai rājanyaḥ | svasya chandasaḥ pratyayanastvāya [?] | jagatībhirvaiśyasya | jagatīchandā vai vaiśyaḥ | svasya chandasaḥ pratyayanastvāya [?] ‖*

(Printed reference: Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 1-1-9-6, 7 [?], numerals read, not zoomed.)

(Kannada, translated:) That is, the Brāhmaṇa must carry through the *agnyādhāna* (the rite performed afresh) only with mantras of the Gāyatrī metre, because the Brāhmaṇa has the nature of the Gāyatrī metre. For that very reason, to obtain *brahmavarcas*, the sacrificial rites must be performed using Ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre. In the same way it is said that Kṣatriyas must carry the sacrificial rites through with Ṛks of the Triṣṭup metre, and Vaiśyas with Ṛks of the Jagatī metre. Because it is so said, if the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice is a Kṣatriya, then in the Agnipraṇayana rite—

> इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषमिति त्रिष्टुभं राजन्यस्यानुब्रूयात् त्रैष्टुभो वै राजन्य ओजो वा इन्द्रियं वीर्यं त्रिष्टुबोजस्यैवैनं तदिन्द्रियेण वीर्येण समर्धयति ।

> *imaṃ mahe vidathyāya śūṣamiti triṣṭubhaṃ rājanyasyānubrūyāt traiṣṭubho vai rājanya ojo vā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ triṣṭubojasyaivainaṃ tadindriyeṇa vīryeṇa samardhayati |*

(Kannada, translated:) the Ṛk of the Triṣṭup metre beginning इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं (*imaṃ mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṃ*) must be recited. The reason is that the Kṣatriya is born from the arm of Prajāpati (बाहू राजन्यः कृतः (*bāhū rājanyaḥ kṛtaḥ*) Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-12 [?]). The arm is the sign of *ojas* (strength), *indriya* and *vīrya* (strength, valour, power and capacity). Because *ojas* and the rest are obtained from the Triṣṭup metre, the one who is a Kṣatriya must carry the sacrificial rite through with Ṛks of the Triṣṭup metre. For that very reason the hotṛ—

*(The words त्रिष्टुभं and त्रैष्टुभो in the Brāhmaṇa quotation are read from the strip and not zoomed [?].)*

(1) The Ṛk (the Triṣṭup recited for the Kṣatriya):

> इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं शश्वत् कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुः ।
> शृणोतु नो दम्येभिरनीकैः शृणोत्वग्निर्दिव्यैरजस्रः ॥

> *imaṃ mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṃ śaśvat kṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruḥ |*
> *śṛṇotu no damyebhiranīkaiḥ śṛṇotvagnirdivyairajasraḥ ‖*

(Printed reference: Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-1 [?]; numerals read, not zoomed.)

(Kannada, translated:) he recites this Ṛk of the Triṣṭup metre. The explanation of the meaning of this Ṛk is likewise given in the Brāhmaṇa passage itself—

> शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्रजभ्रुरिति स्वानामेवैनं तच्छ्रैष्ठ्यं गमयति शृणोतु नो दम्येभिरनीकैः शृणोत्वग्निर्दिव्यैरजस्र इति अजरसं हास्मिन्नोजसो दीदाय य एवं वेद ॥

> *śaśvatkṛtva īḍyāya prajabhruriti svānāmevainaṃ tacchraiṣṭhyaṃ gamayati śṛṇotu no damyebhiranīkaiḥ śṛṇotvagnirdivyairajasra iti ajarasaṃ hāsminnojaso dīdāya ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Kannada, translated:) The meaning of the Ṛk beginning इमं महे (*imaṃ mahe*) is as follows. The ṛtviks brought Agni, the cause of happiness, to the Uttaravedi (for the success of the kings' sacrifice). Agni is always to be praised. The hotṛ makes the yajamāna the chief (so that he stands in front of his kinsmen) and leads him, calling him. This is the meaning of the first half of the Ṛk. The meaning of the second half is: in order to keep the yajamāna's enemy armies under control, may Agni, helping the yajamāna with his troops in the form of flames, listen to our stotras and the like. May Agni know the sacrificial rites that the yajamānas perform well. And may this Agni, endowed with enjoyments fit for the world of the gods and staying in our houses, always, that is to say throughout their lifetime, go on protecting our yajamānas. This is the chief meaning. Now the mantras that Vaiśyas must recite are these—

*(In the first word of the Brāhmaṇa quotation the initial vowel looks like आ, but the Ṛk below has अ. It is written अयमिह and flagged [?].)*

> अयमिह [?] प्रथमो धायि धातृभिरिति जगतीं वैश्यस्यानुब्रूयात् । जागतो वै वैश्यो जागताः पशवः पशुभिरेवैनं तत्समर्धयति । वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशेविश इत्यभिरूपा यद्यज्ञोऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धम् ॥

> *ayamiha [?] prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhiriti jagatīṃ vaiśyasyānubrūyāt | jāgato vai vaiśyo jāgatāḥ paśavaḥ paśubhirevainaṃ tatsamardhayati | vaneṣu citraṃ vibhvaṃ viśeviśa ityabhirūpā yadyajño 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddham ‖*

(Kannada, translated:) The Vaiśya is born from the middle region or the thigh of Prajāpati (ऊरू तदस्य यद्वैश्यः (*ūrū tadasya yadvaiśyaḥ*) Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-12 [?]). This matter is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā thus—

> मध्यतः सप्तदशं निरमिमीत तं विश्वे देवा देवता अन्वसृज्यंत जगतीछंदो वैरूपं साम तस्माद्वैश्यो वै मनुष्याणां ।

> *madhyataḥ saptadaśaṃ niramimīta taṃ viśve devā devatā anvasṛjyaṃta jagatīchaṃdo vairūpaṃ sāma tasmādvaiśyo vai manuṣyāṇāṃ |*

(Kannada, translated:) The Vaiśya has the nature of the Jagatī metre. For the animals too (wealth of cattle) have the nature of the Jagatī metre. If the Vaiśya is to be made endowed with this wealth of cattle, he must recite Ṛks of the Jagatī metre and carry the sacrificial rite through. Therefore, if the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice is a Vaiśya, the hotṛ recites—

*(In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā quotation the word निरमिमीत is split across a line break in the print. The reading निरमि-मीत is not zoomed [?]. The bhāṣya reference "तै. सं." is not given in the print for this passage.)*

(1) The Ṛk (the Jagatī recited for the Vaiśya):

> अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यः ।
> यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशेविशे ॥

> *ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhirhotā yajiṣṭho adhvareṣvīḍyaḥ |*
> *yamapnavāno bhṛgavo virurucurvaneṣu citraṃ vibhvaṃ viśeviśe ‖*

(Printed reference: Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-7-1 [?]; numerals read, not zoomed.)

### Printed p. 544 (PDF 566)

*(Header: **544**, "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 9". The task labelled this page 545. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

(Kannada, translated:) he recites this Ṛk of the Jagatī metre. The reason is that, as said before, the Vaiśya belongs to the Jagatī metre. The animals (wealth of cattle) too belong to the same class. Therefore the Vaiśya recites the mantra of the Jagatī metre in order to grow endowed with wealth. In the last pāda of this Ṛk there is a word that points to the word *vaiśya*, namely विशेविशे (*viśeviśe*). In sacrifices, if one recites Ṛks that are joined with words suited to each context, the desired fruit is obtained in a special degree. Therefore the recitation here of this Ṛk of the Jagatī metre, which carries a word pointing to the Vaiśya, is in accordance with this context. In this way, according to the fruit that the Brāhmaṇa, the Kṣatriya and the Vaiśya each desire, the hotṛ recites one first mantra (Ṛk) in each of the three different metres, the Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭup and the Jagatī. Now he recites the second Ṛk (mantra), which people of all the varṇas must recite in common in this Agnipraṇayana rite—

*(In the Brāhmaṇa quotation the words यो (before पुरा) and वाचैव are read from the strip and not zoomed [?].)*

> अयमु ष्य प्र देवयुरिति अनुष्टुभि वाचं विसृजते । वाग्वा अनुष्टुब्वाचैव [?] तद्वाचं विसृजते । अयमु ष्य इति यदाहायमु स्यागमं यो [?] पुरा गंधर्वेष्ववाक्समित्येव तद्वाक्ब्रूते ॥

> *ayamu ṣya pra devayuriti anuṣṭubhi vācaṃ visṛjate | vāgvā anuṣṭubvācaiva [?] tadvācaṃ visṛjate | ayamu ṣya iti yadāhāyamu syāgamaṃ yo [?] purā gaṃdharveṣvavāksamityeva tadvākbrūte ‖*

(Kannada, translated:) At the time of Somakrayaṇa too, in the rites performed from then up to now, the mantras were recited in the *upāṃśu* manner, that is, in a low voice. According to the injunction that mantras are to be recited in a soft sound, they were recited in a low sound. Now, that is, from here onwards, that rule is released (*visarjana*). That is, the soft speaking is given up and the mantras are recited in a loud sound. This procedure is called *vāco-visarjana* (the release of speech). It is well known that this is begun with a Ṛk of the Anuṣṭup metre. The reason is that speech (*vāk*) itself has the nature of the Anuṣṭup metre. Therefore, with a mantra of that very metre the soft speaking is released. So the hotṛ—

(2) The Ṛk:

> अयमु ष्य प्र देवयुर्होता यज्ञाय नीयते ।
> रथो न योरभीवृतो घृणीवाञ्चेतति त्मना ॥

> *ayamu ṣya pra devayurhotā yajñāya nīyate |*
> *ratho na yorabhīvṛto ghṛṇīvāñcetati tmanā ‖*

(Printed reference: Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-176-3 [?]; numerals read, not zoomed. The word घृणीवाञ्चेतति is as read from the strip.)

(Kannada, translated:) he recites this Ṛk loudly. This speech (the goddess of speech, Vāgdevatā) was formerly among the Gandharvas. Now it speaks thus (the Kannada word is printed ಬೇಳುವುದು, [sic], presumably for ಹೇಳುವುದು): "Formerly, at the time of Somakrayaṇa, I was among the Gandharvas. Now I have come back." Since it is so said, the hotṛ recites the mantra loudly accordingly.

In the matter of the goddess of speech having been among the Gandharvas and now having come back, an *upākhyāna* (story) is told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The print gives the passage with dots for omitted words—

> तेग्ं सोममाह्रियमाणं गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुः पर्यमुष्णात् स ………………… तेभ्य इव ददति ॥

> *tegṃ somamāhriyamāṇaṃ gandharvo viśvāvasuḥ paryamuṣṇāt sa ………………… tebhya iva dadati ‖*

(Kannada, translated:) While the Soma was being brought from the heavenly world, on the way (in the middle of the path) the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu stole it, and—

*(The sentence runs on to the next page of the print; it is left open at the word ಕದ್ದು, "stole".)*

### Printed p. 545 (PDF 567)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 6 V. 1" (Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 1), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", and the printed number **545**. The signature mark "[35]" and "Vol. 14" at the foot of the page are printer's marks.)*

(Kannada, translated, continuing the sentence left open at the foot of printed p. 544:) … stole it and hid it for three nights. Even now, after the Somakrayaṇa (the purchase of Soma), keeping it (the Soma) in the same way for three nights has come into custom. Then all the deities together deliberated how to get the Soma back from that Gandharva, and an idea suddenly flashed in their minds. Gandharvas are greatly infatuated when they see women. Therefore they decided to give the Gandharvas an exceedingly beautiful young woman and to take the Soma in exchange for her. Thereupon the deities called Vāgdevatā (the goddess of speech) and said: "O Vāgdevatā, take the form of an exceedingly beautiful young woman; we shall exchange you with the Gandharvas, bring the Soma, and carry the sacrifice through." Vāgdevatā agreed to this. Then they exchanged that beautiful young woman with the Gandharva king named Viśvāvasu and brought the Soma. After the deities' work was done, Vāgdevatā, who had been in the form of a beautiful young woman, took the form of a "reddish deer" (as printed ಕೆಂಪುಜಿಂಕೆ) and ran from the Gandharvas' side to the deities' presence. It is this matter that is stated here as "Vāgdevatā has come back". The Somakrayaṇa (purchase of Soma) that went on until Vāgdevatā, in the form of a beautiful young woman, stayed with the Gandharvas and came again to the deities, and the work done in the Agnipraṇayana up to now, all these they say in the *upāṃśu* manner (in a low voice), because Vāgdevatā was not near. After Vāgdevatā has come back, the hotṛ begins to recite the mantras fearlessly and firmly (loudly): this is the main intention.

(Kannada, translated:) Now the hotṛ proceeds and recites the third Ṛk.

*(Gist of the bhāṣya: the Ṛk says Agni is "as if from immortality", beyond all fear; by reciting it the immortality of the yajamāna is established, for Agni is a deity made for long life.)*

> अयमग्निरुरुष्यतीति अयं वा अग्निरुरुष्यति अमृता दिव जन्मन इत्यमृतत्वमेवास्मिंस्तद्दधाति सहसश्चित्सहीयान्देवो जीवातवे कृत इति देवो ह्येष एतज्जीवातवे कृतो यदग्निः ॥

> *ayamagniruruṣyatīti ayaṃ vā agniruruṣyati amṛtā diva janmana ityamṛtatvamevāsmiṃstaddadhāti sahasaścitsahīyāndevo jīvātave kṛta iti devo hyeṣa etajjīvātave kṛto yadagniḥ ‖*

(Kannada, translated:) The text of the third Ṛk is as follows—

(3)

> अयमग्निरुरुष्यत्यमृतादिव जन्मनः ।
> सहसश्चित्सहीयान् देवो जीवातवे कृतः ॥

> *ayamagniruruṣyatyamṛtādiva janmanaḥ |*
> *sahasaścitsahīyān devo jīvātave kṛtaḥ ‖*

(Printed reference: Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-176-4 [?]; numerals read from the strip, not zoomed.)

(Kannada, translated:) The main intention of this Ṛk is this: because this Agni gives the yajamānas a birth of divine form, he protects them by warding off the fear that comes from men and the fear that comes from the deities. This Agni is mightier even than strength itself. Here the hotṛ says that he has been fashioned for the sacrifice, or for granting long life. By reciting the first half of the Ṛk he makes the yajamāna free from death, that is, long-lived. By reciting the second half the power of this Agni becomes of great capacity. Therefore, by reciting this Ṛk, Agni becomes favourable to protect our life.

> जातवेदो नि धीमह्यग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे ॥

By इळायाः पदे (*iḷāyāḥ pade*) (the place of Iḷā) is meant the navel-region of the Uttaravedi where the feet of the cow, made excellent by ghee-pressing and other rites, have been set; this is what the word इळायास्पदं (*iḷāyāspadaṃ*) describes. By the sentence जातवेदो निधीमहि (*jātavedo nidhīmahi*) the meaning is indicated that we, the ṛtvijs, place Agni in the Uttaravedi. The sentence in the last pāda, अग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे (*agne havyāya voḷhave*), indicates that he has been established here in order to carry the oblations and the like to the deities.

> कुलायिनं घृतवंतं सवित्रे यज्ञं नय यजमानाय साधु ॥

> *agne viśvebhiḥ svanīka devairūrṇāvaṃtaṃ prathamaḥ sīda yonim |*

(Printed reference: Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-15-16 [?]; numerals read from the strip, not zoomed.)

The use of the word विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*) here indicates that all the deities have been established together with Agni. That is to say, Agni, together with all the deities, sits in the Uttaravedi, which is like the nest of a bird that has made a soft bed by spreading strands of wool. Remaining in the navel-place called the Uttaravedi, which is rich with sticks and the like and sprinkled with ghee, carry through the yajamāna's sacrificial acts … *(the sentence runs on to the next page of the print)*
